What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee is $30.00 per document; additional $3.00 for each additional instrument assigned/discharged (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Office hours: closed daily 12-1 p.m.; recording hours 8:30 a.m.-4 p.m. (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Who handles deed recording in Alcona County, and what is the number?

Deeds and mortgages for Alcona County property are filed with the Register of Deeds in Harrisville, reachable at 989-724-9450 (fax 989-724-9459). The office page describes the job as the official recording point for every legal paper touching real estate, run under a uniform state system.

That page lists the papers it takes: warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, liens and releases, easements, rights of way, oil and gas leases, plats, surveys, land corners and court orders. Passport applications are accepted there too.

Counter staff cannot draft your deed or weigh in on legal questions, so lean on a lawyer or the closing agent for that. The county also keeps a closure list that includes Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, so phone ahead before you carry a signed original to the courthouse.

What fees apply when you file a deed at the Alcona County counter?

Filing runs $30.00 per paper regardless of length, the figure fixed in MCL 600.2567 and printed on the Alcona page. A few add-ons exist:

  • $3.00 extra for every further instrument when one document assigns or discharges several.
  • $1.00 a page for photocopies of the record, with $5.00 on top to certify.
  • $5.00 for the treasurer's tax certificate, which spans up to five property descriptions, then 20 cents per added description.

Mailing it in has quirks. Enclose a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. If your check overshoots the fee by $10.00 or less, the county keeps the difference, so total the charges before you send anything.

Which Alcona County papers need the treasurer's certificate first?

Warranty deeds, land contracts and their assignments, condominium master deeds, subdivision plats and any deed that conveys with a warranty must arrive with a certificate from the Treasurer's Office, 989-724-9420. The register's page states this directly.

Make this stop first on your errand list, since the certificate travels with the deed to the register. Holding a different deed form, such as a quitclaim? Ask the register if the same rule reaches it.

The same counter can tell you whether any tax is still unpaid on the parcel. Knowing that number before you pick a closing date avoids a last-minute surprise.

How is the Michigan transfer tax figured on an Alcona County sale?

Two levies stack on the seller. The county charges $0.55 for each $500 of value (MCL 207.504) and the state charges $3.75 for each $500 (MCL 207.525), rounding any leftover amount up to a full $500.

Try the math on $162,800, the 2020 to 2024 median value for an Alcona County owner-occupied home in Census Bureau data. It contains 326 blocks of $500.

Transfer tax on a $162,800 Alcona County sale, computed from the rates in MCL 207.504 and 207.525
LevelPer $500Total
County$0.55$179.30
State$3.75$1,222.50
Both levels$4.30$1,401.80

The county treasurer collects within 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). Put the full price on the face of the deed, or file a value affidavit with it.

Can an Alcona County family transfer avoid the transfer tax?

Often yes. MCL 207.526 carves out gifts inside a family, which is the usual case for heirs and aging owners.

  • Parent to child, including a stepchild or adopted child.
  • Grandparent to grandchild, including step and adopted grandchildren.
  • Spouses creating or ending a tenancy by the entireties.
  • Any instrument carrying consideration under $100.
  • A corrective deed that confirms title the grantee already holds.

If you paid and then learn an exemption applied, the state Treasury Department takes refund requests.

Why might Alcona County turn a deed away?

Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, gives a register grounds to refuse papers that break its layout rules. Four checks cover most trouble:

  • Leave a clear top margin of 2 1/2 inches on page one.
  • Open with a single line that names the event, such as "Warranty Deed."
  • Use 10-point or larger type in black ink on white 20-pound stock.
  • Print the drafter's name and business address on the paper.

Keep one event per sheet. A first line claiming two recordable events, such as a deed plus a release, bars recording.

Which other Alcona County offices matter when a house sells?

Several county desks can touch a sale, and the directory on the county home page gives each one's line.

  • Treasurer, 989-724-9420: tax certificates and balances.
  • Equalization, 989-724-9430: assessed and taxable values.
  • Building Department, 989-724-9440: permits.
  • County Clerk, 989-724-9410, and Probate Court, 989-724-9490: records and estate matters when the owner has died.

Alcona County sits in Michigan's 23rd Circuit, shared with Arenac, Iosco and Oscoda counties. An heir selling an inherited house should ask Probate Court what paperwork the deed needs before anything goes to the register.

What should an owner know about Alcona County itself?

Alphabetically first among Michigan's 83 counties, Alcona was created in 1840 and organized in 1869. Of its 1,791 square miles, 62 percent is water, mostly Lake Huron and inland lakes such as Hubbard Lake, one of the state's twenty largest. The Au Sable River crosses the southwest, with the Alcona Dam in Curtis Township, and part of the Huron National Forest lies within the borders.

Harrisville is the sole city and the county seat, and Lincoln is the village. Townships on the county list are Alcona, Caledonia, Curtis, Gustin, Greenbush, Harrisville, Haynes, Millen and Mitchell.

About 10,556 people lived here in mid-2025, roughly 15 per square mile. Older adults are 37.4 percent of the population, 89.6 percent of housing is occupied by its owner, the median household earns $54,993 and the average worker travels 27.9 minutes, against 17.5 in neighboring Alpena County.

Zoning, permits and assessments sit with townships and the county, not with the register. The Building Department is at 989-724-9440 and Equalization at 989-724-9430. Call them if a permit or valuation question could hold up your sale.

How has Alcona County grown, and what do homes cost to carry?

The county was first named Negwegon and took the Alcona name in 1843. Its 2010 census count was 10,942 and its 2020 count was 10,167, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 10,556 is a 3.9 percent rise over the April 2020 base.

Housing figures for 2020 to 2024 show 5,305 households averaging 1.94 people, which fits a county where more than a third of residents are 65 or older. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,096, owners without one $441, and median gross rent is $867.

Work is thin on the ground. The county had 182 employer establishments and 1,126 paid jobs in 2023, and retail sales of $91.7 million in 2022, or $8,820 per person. Only 42.7 percent of people 16 or older are in the labor force.

More questions about Alcona County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing price for a deed in Alcona County?

It is $30.00 a document. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra, and copies of records cost $1.00 a page.

Who must pay the transfer tax in an Alcona County sale?

The seller must, since MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor. The county treasurer expects payment inside 15 days from delivery of the deed.

Is a treasurer's certificate required before an Alcona County warranty deed is recorded?

Yes. The Treasurer's Office issues it at 989-724-9420 for $5.00 per document with up to five descriptions.

Can a deed go to the Alcona County register by mail?

Yes, if you add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Any mailed overpayment of $10.00 or under becomes county revenue.

Is there an online search for Alcona County land records?

Yes, two fee-based tools: Laredo, which works by subscription, and Tapestry. Ask the register at 989-724-9450 how to sign up for Laredo.

The Allegan County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Allegan County

  • Allegan County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • E-recording via CSC, Simplifile, ePN (E-Recording Partners Network) listed on county page (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Statutory recording fee $30 per document regardless of pages; certify $5; copies $1/page (MCL 600.2567; state law, not county page) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Allegan County?

Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page not searched/opened
  • Millage rates not researched
  • Allegan register of deeds address/hours not seen

Allegan County by the numbers

Allegan County has about 120,913 residents and 52,262 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 18 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $247,000, 32% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $80,255, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 86% of occupied homes and renters in 14%. The median home was built in 1981, about 42 years ago.

What are the options for filing a deed with Allegan County?

Paper and electronic filing both work. The register's page lists three e-recording vendors with direct lines: CSC (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and ePN, the E-Recording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Title companies normally use one of these, which spares most sellers any contact with them.

The same page links a land records search portal, the state recording requirements and county clerk and register annual reports. After filing, the register enters the paper in a book called a liber and stamps that reference on the document. An image becomes the permanent record, and the office does not keep the original deed or mortgage.

Counter staff do not prepare documents or answer legal questions, and they refer people to an attorney or title company. One protection for senders comes from MCL 565.201: a register may not refuse a compliant paper over its wording, and a paper already recorded is presumed to comply. The format rules are the real hurdle, so let the title agent look over the deed before signing.

What are Allegan County's recording and copy fees?

One flat $30 covers a recording of any length, as MCL 600.2567 provides. The remaining items on the statutory list are short.

  • $3 on top for every further instrument that a single paper assigns or discharges.
  • $1 per page of copies, and a $5 certification charge.
  • Grantor and grantee searches at 50 cents per year examined, minimum $5.
  • $1 for filing or looking up any other paper.

Fees are due when the paper is left. For electronic filings the fee can follow electronically, up to one business day after receipt. For copy purposes, a "page" is one side of a sheet measuring 8 1/2 by 11 up to 14 inches, in paper of 20 pound weight or more.

How much transfer tax is due on an Allegan County sale?

A median Allegan County home is worth $267,100 by Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024, well above Alcona County's $162,800 and Alpena County's $153,900. Across the two taxes the seller pays $4.30 for each $500 of value, rounding a partial $500 upward.

Transfer tax at three Allegan County sale prices, from the $0.55 county rate (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 state rate (MCL 207.525)
Sale priceCountyStateCombined
$200,000$220.00$1,500.00$1,720.00
$267,100 (median)$294.25$2,006.25$2,300.50
$350,000$385.00$2,625.00$3,010.00

The seller carries liability under MCL 207.523, although a buyer may pay on the seller's behalf. Payment reaches the county treasurer no later than 15 days after the instrument is delivered.

Which Allegan County transfers can skip the tax?

MCL 207.526 exempts a list of transfers, and a few come up often with houses in a lake or farm county like this one.

  • A deed that only straightens a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • A quitclaim deed given to confirm a title the grantee already holds, such as one that corrects a flaw.
  • A transfer between a limited liability company and its members when ownership shares are unchanged.
  • A transfer between a partnership and its partners on the same terms.
  • A deed in which the grantor is a government body or officer acting officially.

Anyone relying on one of these should say so to the title agent before closing. A refund request goes to the Department of Treasury.

What other services does the Allegan County register offer owners?

The office runs a free Property Fraud Alert. An owner or business enters a name and gets a notice whenever a recorded document matches it, which gives early warning of a forged deed or a lien filed against you.

The register also posts Plat Board public notices, which matter to anyone splitting a parcel before a sale. A related treasurer form covers tax certification for land divisions and lot line adjustments, with its own instructions.

U.S. passport applications are taken at the office by appointment only, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays. The number to call is 269-673-0390.

What does the Allegan County Treasurer handle in a sale?

The Treasurer's Office certifies deeds, keeps tax histories, and collects delinquent real estate tax for the 35 townships, cities and villages in the county. The county chose to run the whole tax reversion process in-house, including title searches, court hearings, foreclosure and sale.

A seller with delinquent tax should talk to the treasurer's staff first, because the office advances delinquent amounts to the local units through its revolving fund. The page links to pay delinquent taxes, search tax records and foreclosure sales.

The treasurer also describes how former owners can claim leftover foreclosure proceeds. For foreclosures starting in 2021, a person with title or equity must file Form 5743 with the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 after the auctions with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow between February 1 and May 15. These steps come from MCL 211.78t.

Who sets and bills property tax in Allegan County?

Assessing happens at the township or city level, with the county Equalization Department publishing property records, a township and city assessor list, equalization reports and a tax levies and millages page. The county treasurer's page describes accounting for tax collections of the 35 local units and collecting delinquent real estate tax.

Because 24 townships, 9 cities and 2 villages each act as their own unit, the correct office depends on the parcel. The county's directory lists addresses and phone lines for all of them, such as Allegan Township at 269-673-5051, Otsego City Hall at 269-692-3391 and Holland City Hall at 616-355-1300.

Ask your township or city for the current tax balance before you list the house.

What is Allegan County like for a seller?

Allegan County was laid out in 1831 and organized in 1835. The county seat is the city of Allegan, and Holland is the largest city. It covers 825 square miles of land and counts as the Holland micropolitan area, part of the Grand Rapids combined area. The area is mostly agricultural and is urbanizing as Grand Rapids and Kalamazoo spread toward it.

The Lake Michigan shore draws vacation homes, especially around Saugatuck and Douglas. The Allegan State Game Area covers about 45,000 acres, Saugatuck Dunes State Park has dune trails and a swim beach, and Lake Allegan is another destination. A Pottawatomi band, the Match-e-be-nash-she-wish Band, has a reservation in the county.

The 2025 Census estimate is 123,188 residents, up 2.2 percent from April 2020. Owners live in 87.4 percent of homes, median household income is $83,283, and the mean commute is 24.2 minutes. The county issued 399 building permits in 2025.

What do household and business numbers show for Allegan County?

For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau counts 45,522 households averaging 2.64 people. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,523, owners with none $575, and median gross rent is $1,100. About 92.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 4,920 residents are veterans.

The county had 2,571 employer establishments and 38,899 jobs in 2023, a 5.8 percent drop in employment from 2022. Retail sales reached about $1.68 billion in 2022, or $13,863 per resident, and the poverty rate is 8.2 percent.

More questions about Allegan County, MI Register of Deeds

Which e-recording services does Allegan County accept?

It accepts CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Their phone lines are 866-652-0111, 800-460-5657 and 888-325-3365.

How much does a deed cost to record in Allegan County?

A recording costs $30 per document. Add $3 per further instrument assigned or discharged, $1 a page for copies and $5 for certification.

What is the state share of transfer tax on a $267,100 Allegan County house?

The state share is $2,006.25, computed on 535 units of $500 at $3.75. With the $294.25 county share, the seller owes $2,300.50.

Will the Allegan County register prepare my deed?

No. The office neither drafts documents nor answers legal questions, so an attorney or title company must do that.

How does a former owner claim surplus from an Allegan County foreclosure sale?

Send Form 5743 to the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow.

Alpena County, MI Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Michigan
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Alpena County, MI Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alpena County, MI Register of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Alpena County, MI Register of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Alpena County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Alpena County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

The Alpena County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Alpena County

  • Alpena County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Michigan flat recording fee $30 per recordable event; tax certification $5; copies $1/page (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Alpena County?
We buy Alpena County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

When does the Alpena County recording desk take your deed?

The register works out of 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, and answers at 989-354-9547. According to the county office page, hours run 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

Recording cutoffs come sooner than closing time. An e-filing must land by 3:30 p.m. to count that day, and paper has until 4:00 p.m. at the window. Anything later joins the next business day's pile, so a Friday 4:15 delivery waits for Monday.

The register insists on originals. Once indexed, the original is returned to the sender, normally inside seven days of recording. No blank deeds are given out, and staff cannot coach you through completing one; the page sends people to an office supply store, a lawyer or a title company.

Which fees does Alpena County collect for recording and copies?

Most Michigan counties follow MCL 600.2567, which prices a recording at one flat sum no matter the number of pages. A charter county can override that by ordinance, so phone the register for the exact total before a check goes in the mail.

  • $30 for every recorded paper, and $3 more for each extra instrument it assigns or discharges.
  • Copies at $1 per page and certification at $5.
  • Index searches at 50 cents a year for grantor and grantee names, never less than $5.
  • A tax certification fee on certain deeds. Ask the Alpena County treasurer whether yours qualifies.

Links on the office page lead to a fee sheet, a recording requirements sheet and e-recording instructions.

What search and alert tools does the Alpena County register run?

Researchers can choose Laredo or Tapestry. Per the county, Tapestry fits someone who needs a copy or two, and Laredo suits title companies and frequent searchers.

Two free services cover Alpena County only: a property fraud alert and a notary fraud alert. Each sends a call, text or email when a recorded paper carries your name.

The same office is a certified passport agent and takes passport photos,, so some visitors are there for a passport.

What will state and county transfer tax cost on an Alpena County house?

A typical Alpena County house, valued at $153,900 in the 2020 to 2024 Census estimate, holds 308 units of $500. On each unit the seller pays 55 cents to the county (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 to the state (MCL 207.525).

Transfer tax on a $153,900 Alpena County sale (308 units of $500), worked from MCL 207.504 and 207.525
PartMathResult
County308 x $0.55$169.40
State308 x $3.75$1,155.00
Both308 x $4.30$1,324.40

Remit it to the Alpena County treasurer inside 15 days after delivery. When furniture or equipment rides along, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an attached affidavit lists the values separately.

Which distress and court transfers escape the Alpena County transfer tax?

Distressed owners and heirs should read MCL 207.526, because several exemptions fit their situations.

  • A deed handed to a lender in foreclosure or in place of it. The lender's own resale is still taxed.
  • A court of record's order moving title, when no price is set.
  • An installment land contract, while legal title sits with the seller.
  • Husband and wife moving property into or out of a tenancy by the entireties.

Paid in error? Treasury takes refund requests.

What details on a deed trip up an Alpena County recording?

Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, lets a register refuse a paper that skips basic identification steps. Returns usually trace to one of these:

  • A signer's printed name that differs from the name in the notary's certificate.
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue.
  • No notary name printed next to the notary's signature.
  • No street address for the buyer, or no drafter name and address.
  • A full Social Security number left visible.
  • Foreign-language text without an English version attached.

Once a paper satisfies the act, the register has no right to refuse it over what it says.

How should you time a deed against the Alpena County cutoffs?

Start the e-record by early afternoon, because the 3:30 p.m. cutoff arrives half an hour before the counter's 4:00. Before signing, run through a short list:

  • The buyer's mailing address appears on the deed.
  • The notary's name is printed beside the signature.
  • The full sale value is stated, or a value affidavit is attached.
  • The original, not a copy, goes to the register.
  • Any tax certification step has been cleared with the county treasurer.

Miss the cutoff and your record date moves to the next business day.

What is Alpena County like for someone selling a home?

In the northeast of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, Alpena County fronts Lake Huron and Thunder Bay, and the Thunder Bay River drains most of its land. Lawmakers drew the county in 1840 as Anamickee, changed the name in 1843, and set up local government in 1857. The 45th parallel cuts across the county, and Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary lies offshore, with automated lighthouses on Middle Island and Thunder Bay Island.

Alpena is the county seat and its only city. Hillman is a village that straddles the county line, and Alpena Charter Township and the Ossineke area fill out the list. U.S. 23 hugs the shoreline, M-32 ends in downtown Alpena, and M-65 offers a quicker way south.

The Census Bureau puts mid-2025 headcount at 28,853, down 0.2 percent from 2020, and seniors make up 27.9 percent. Four of every five homes are lived in by their owners. The typical household earns $53,950, workers spend 17.5 minutes getting to work, and gross rent has a median of $673. Employers in 2023 numbered 822, jobs 10,141, and shoppers spent roughly $616 million in 2022.

Assessments are a local matter, so a seller with a parcel question should call the city or township assessor, not the register.

How have Alpena County's population and housing changed over time?

Population topped out at 32,315 in 1980, then slid to 30,605 by 1990, 29,598 by 2010 and 28,907 by 2020.

The 2020 to 2024 Census data counts 13,019 households with 2.17 people each and 15,768 housing units as of 2025. Owners with a mortgage carry median monthly costs of $1,096, and owners without one pay $455. Poverty affects 16.7 percent of residents, and 18.3 percent of adults 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree.

The land itself is part of the story. Glaciers left a Grayling outwash plain of sandy ridges, jack pine barrens and hardwood forest, and large inland lakes such as Long Lake and Grand Lake sit north of the city along U.S. 23.

What do the work and household numbers say about Alpena County?

Alpena County recorded 72 building permits in 2025, a small figure beside its 15,768 housing units. Census data shows 89.4 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier.

Some 53.7 percent of people 16 and older are in the civilian labor force. Employers number 822, with 817 firms counted in the 2023 reference year and a further 1,849 nonemployer businesses in 2024. Annual payroll for employer establishments came to about $476.6 million in 2023, and employment grew 3.4 percent between 2022 and 2023.

The county has 2,310 veterans, and 85.1 percent of households have a broadband subscription. The original residents of the area were the Thunder Bay Band of Chippewa and Ottawa, who later merged with the Mackinac Bands, and offshore islands in Thunder Bay belong to the Michigan Islands National Wildlife Refuge.

More questions about Alpena County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alpena County?

Paper filings are taken until 4:00 p.m. and e-recordings until 3:30 p.m. A deed that arrives later is recorded on the next business day.

How can I contact the Alpena County Register of Deeds?

Phone 989-354-9547 or fax 989-354-9646, or visit 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena.

Will my original deed come back from the Alpena County register?

Yes. The office indexes the paper and then returns the original, usually within a week of the recording date.

How much transfer tax applies to a $153,900 sale in Alpena County?

The total is $1,324.40, which splits into $1,155.00 for the state and $169.40 for the county. Each rate applies to every $500 or fraction thereof.

Can Alpena County staff write or advise on my deed?

No. They do not complete documents, give legal advice or provide blank deeds. A title company, an attorney or an office supply store can help instead.

The Antrim County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Antrim County

  • Antrim County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30.00 per document (real estate records); copies $1.00/page; plat copies $2.00/page (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • E-recording encouraged via Simplifile or EPN; mail/courier and drop box also accepted (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

Where do Antrim County property records live, and how far back do they go?

Deeds, mortgages and liens on Antrim County land are filed with the Register of Deeds at the county building in Bellaire, which keeps a grantor and grantee index and serves weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. The register also chairs the County Plat Board, the body that reviews new subdivisions before they can be sold off in lots.

Antrim's own office page says its filings reach back to 1856. Computer images start in January 1990, and older entries sit in bound books. The name index covering the whole life of the county can be searched without charge at a public terminal, though you reserve a slot by appointment.

The register's page also explains why timing matters. Michigan runs a race-notice system, so a recorded deed puts every later buyer on notice, and the office stamps and numbers each paper in the order it lands on the counter. A lake cottage that changes hands in July should have its deed filed the day the money moves.

What does the Antrim County fee schedule list for recording?

Antrim charges a flat $30.00 for each document it records, whether the deed runs one page or twelve. The county fee schedule adds a few other items that matter at a sale.

  • When one paper handles more than one assignment or discharge, add $3.00 for every instrument past the first.
  • Warranty deeds, any deed carrying a covenant of warranty, and land contracts (plus assignments or amendments that touch the legal description) need a $5.00 treasurer's certificate.
  • Photocopies cost $1.00 a page, plat copies $2.00 a page, and a certified copy costs $5.00 for its first page.

The office accepts a check, cash or a credit card. Make checks out to the Antrim County Register of Deeds, and expect the certificate to be handled through the treasurer's window.

Charges listed on the Antrim County Register of Deeds fee schedule

How much transfer tax comes due on an Antrim County sale?

The tax is charged per $500 of the price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full block, and it is paid at recording. Other Michigan register offices post a state share of $3.75 per block plus a county share of $0.55, which adds up to $4.30. Antrim's office can confirm its county share.

As a worked example, Census figures for 2020 through 2024 put a typical owner-occupied Antrim home at $255,500. That price spans 511 blocks, so the combined tax would be about $2,197. Your own bill follows the real sale price on the deed.

The state act lists transfers that owe nothing. The exempt group in MCL 207.526 includes:

  • a gift deed running to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild;
  • transfers by foreclosure or by a deed in lieu of foreclosure;
  • court orders that move title without naming a money amount;
  • a quitclaim that repairs a title flaw by confirming what the grantee already holds;
  • any instrument where the price is below $100.

The deed text itself must name the exemption claimed, or the office will collect the tax.

Can an Antrim County deed be filed electronically or dropped off?

Yes to both. The register recommends e-recording through Simplifile or EPN, and still accepts the post office, FedEx, UPS and similar carriers. A drop box at the southeast corner of the county building takes hand deliveries, but the office says it is only checked periodically, so a deed on a closing deadline should go another way.

Slip a return envelope with postage into anything you mail, and the original comes back once it is indexed. Staff can say what a filing needs, yet drafting a deed or picking a form is outside their role.

At a normal sale none of this lands on the seller. The closing agent signs the deed with you, adds the transfer tax and the treasurer's $5.00 certificate, and sends the package in electronically. Owners handling an inherited cabin by hand can call the office before they file.

Which office bills property tax in Antrim County, and how is an old balance paid?

Your village or township bills the year in progress. The County Treasurer takes only earlier years and delinquent accounts. Summer bills go out in July and are due to the village or township on September 14. Township winter tax is billed in December and due February 14.

To pay a past-year balance, the treasurer accepts a check by mail at PO Box 544, Bellaire, MI 49615, a card online or by phone at 231-533-6720, or a visit to the secure drop box outside the public entrance. Card payments add 2.95 percent, with a $3.99 minimum. The treasurer's page also points to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services for people who may qualify for help.

If the parcel carries an unpaid balance, call the treasurer for a payoff figure before the house goes on the market. The closing agent deducts that sum from what you receive.

What should a seller know about Antrim County's land and housing?

Antrim covers 602 square miles of northwest lower Michigan, and 126 of them are water. Torch Lake, which Wikipedia calls the deepest and second-largest inland lake in the state, lies here, and most of the Chain of Lakes does too. Grand Traverse Bay marks the western edge, and Bellaire is the seat.

Five villages anchor the map: Bellaire, Central Lake, Elk Rapids, Ellsworth and Mancelona. Alba, Alden, Eastport and Lakes of the North are census-designated places. A shoreline lot at Elk Rapids and a woodland house near Mancelona sit in different markets, so get comparable sales from the immediate area.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 24,698, a gain of 5.4 percent over the 2020 estimates base.
  • Owner-occupied homes: 86.4 percent of 11,100 households.
  • Median household income: $72,054 in 2020 to 2024 dollars.
  • Residents 65 or older: 30.7 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 105.
  • Median gross rent: $902 a month, and median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,462 a month.
  • Average household size: 2.15 people.

Many houses in the county are seasonal or came through an estate, and a place closed up through several winters can need roof, plumbing or septic work before a financed buyer will go ahead. A buyer who takes the house in its current condition skips that repair list, and that draws some owners to a cash sale.

More questions about Antrim County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing fee for an Antrim County deed?

The fee is $30.00 for a document of any length. Each extra assignment or discharge on the same paper adds $3.00, and warranty deeds and land contracts also need the $5.00 treasurer's certificate.

Does the Antrim County office take deeds by e-recording?

Yes, through Simplifile or EPN, which the register encourages. Paper still works by mail, by carrier, or through the box at the building's southeast corner.

Which office collects this year's tax on an Antrim County house?

The village or township holds the current year's tax roll. The county treasurer steps in for prior years and delinquent bills, and the due dates for summer and winter township tax are September 14 and February 14.

Will the register's staff prepare my deed?

No. They can describe what the office needs, but writing the deed is left to a preparer you hire. Heirs and sellers working without a closing agent should line one up first.

Is a deed to my daughter taxed as a sale in Antrim County?

MCL 207.526 exempts a parent's conveyance to a child from the state tax, provided the deed names the exemption in its text. The county side has its own wording, so confirm the exact language with the register before you sign.

What we confirmed on the official page

Why would an Arenac County seller deal with the Register of Deeds?

The deeds office in Standish files the paper trail of Arenac County real estate: deeds, mortgages, discharges and the other instruments that move or burden land. For a seller, it is the office that turns a signed deed into a public record, and it is also the counter where state and county transfer tax get collected. You can reach the office at (989) 846-9201.

Its web page invites owners to sign up for land notifications, an alert service that sends an email when a new document is recorded against a property. A person who inherited a house, or who owns a place that sits empty for part of the year, may want that watch in place before listing.

Arenac is small. It is the third-smallest county in Michigan by land area, and the register's workload follows: an estimated 9,615 housing units spread along the Saginaw Bay shore and the inland river valleys.

What are Arenac County's recording charges?

Every document filed in Arenac County pays $30.00, however many pages it has. The county cites MCL 600.2657 and says the flat fee took effect on October 1, 2016.

When one document assigns or discharges more than a single instrument, the office adds $3.00 for each instrument beyond the first. A payoff release that clears two recorded mortgages, for example, would cost $36.00 to file.

What would transfer tax run on an Arenac County house?

Add the county's 55 cents to the state's $3.75 and a sale pays $4.30 per $500 of price, with a leftover partial $500 counted as a whole one. The middle-priced owner-occupied home in Arenac County was valued at $150,600 in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates. That is 302 blocks of $500, so the tax would come to $1,298.60. Your sale will be taxed on its own price.

The register's page lays out the paperwork. The deed should show the property's value. A real estate valuation affidavit can be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says an affidavit is being filed. The statutes the office cites for this are MCL 207.511 and 207.525.

  • The office collects the tax unless the deed qualifies for a state exemption, a county exemption, or both.
  • The deed has to name the exemption, with the statute behind it (MCL 207.505 for the county, MCL 207.526 for the state).
  • Exemptions under the state act reach gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure transfers, and deeds that only confirm title the buyer already holds.

Can you search Arenac County deeds online?

Yes, with two separate tools. The county's online records site covers documents from February 11, 1991 forward, and it lets you search and buy copies of filings from 1992 to the present. Older index books are handled differently.

For anything before 1992, the office points researchers to RECORDhub. You make an account, pick one of the subscription plans Arenac County offers, and then view and print pages from deed books 1 through 214. That archive is how a family finds the chain of ownership on a farm or a lakeshore lot that has not changed hands for decades.

Online searching tells you what is on file, but it does not replace a title search. If a seller spots an old easement, a lien or a name that does not match the deed, a title company can sort out what it means before a buyer's lender does.

Who handles property tax bills in Arenac County?

Ask the treasurer of the city, village or township where the parcel sits for the current tax bill, and ask the Arenac County Treasurer about any amount that has fallen behind. Each can give you a written figure to hand the closing agent.

At a sale, an unpaid tax balance is normally paid from the seller's side of the closing statement. On an older or inherited house, request the payoff early, so the number you plan around matches the one the closing agent sees.

Arenac's register does not handle tax collection, so questions about assessments or exemptions go to the local assessor or treasurer rather than to the deeds counter.

How do Arenac County's geography and past shape a house sale?

Arenac County covers 681 square miles, and 47 percent of that is water, mostly Saginaw Bay on Lake Huron. Standish, the seat, is the largest of three cities along with Au Gres and Omer and Sterling, Turner and Twining as villages. The county has a start-and-stop past: the Michigan Territory created it in 1831, it was attached to Saginaw County for administration in 1836, and the creation of Bay County legally erased it in April 1857. It came back on April 21, 1883, carved from Bay County's northern townships. Anyone tracing an old Arenac farm deed should expect the records to reflect that history.

Several rivers cross the county, including the Au Gres, the Rifle and the Pine. I-75 and US 23 are the main routes, along with M-13, M-33, M-61 and M-65. Off-reservation trust land of the Isabella Indian Reservation sits in three small parcels inside Standish Township.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 15,068, a rise of 0.5 percent over 2020.
  • Households: 6,552, with 86.2 percent in owner-occupied homes.
  • Median household income: $58,811, and median gross rent: $761.
  • People 65 or older: 30.0 percent of residents.
  • Residential and other building permits in 2025: 43.

Against a median home value near $150,600, repair costs weigh heavily on a sale. A place needing a roof, a furnace or a cleanout may suit a cash buyer who accepts it as it stands.

What does the Arenac County economy look like around a house sale?

Arenac County is a place of small employers and long commutes. The Census Bureau counts 355 employer establishments with 3,619 workers in 2023, a gain of 6.9 percent over 2022, and an annual payroll of about $169 million. Workers who travel to a job spend a mean of 26.6 minutes getting there.

The shoreline adds a visitor trade. Accommodation and food service sales came to roughly $128.6 million in 2022, and retail sales reached about $268 million, or $17,724 for each resident. For a seller, that background matters mostly at the margins: buyers who want a getaway near Saginaw Bay and buyers who need a year-round home bring different budgets.

  • Residents past age 25 holding at least a high school diploma: 88.2 percent, and holding a four-year degree: 16.0 percent.
  • Persons in poverty: 11.7 percent.
  • Per capita income: $32,082, in 2024 dollars.

More questions about Arenac County, MI Register of Deeds

How do I contact the Arenac County deeds office by phone?

The office lists (989) 846-9201 on its web page. Call that line with questions about recording, transfer tax or the online records subscription.

What does a deed filing cost at the Arenac office?

A deed pays $30.00 whatever its length. A paper that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each one beyond the first.

What are the Arenac County transfer tax rates?

The county takes 55 cents per $500 and the state takes $3.75 per $500, rounded up for a partial block. A transfer worth $100 or more owes both unless the deed states an exemption.

Do I have to put the sale price on the deed?

Not if you file a real estate valuation affidavit instead. There is no fee for the affidavit, and the deed must say that one is being filed.

Where can I look at old Arenac County deed books?

Deed books 1 through 214 can be viewed on RECORDhub with a subscription plan from the county. Documents from 1992 forward are on the county's online records site.

Who records deeds in Barry County

  • Barry County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • All documents $30.00 recording fee regardless of page count; e-recording providers page exists (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Barry County?

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page not searched/opened

Barry County by the numbers

Barry County ranks 32 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 62,982 people in 27,617 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $243,700, the median home value sits 30% above the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Barry County reports $77,873. Owner-occupancy is 86%, so renters hold about 14% of occupied homes.

Where do you take a deed in Barry County, and what is staff allowed to help with?

Go to Room 102 at the Barry County Courthouse, 220 W State Street, Hastings, MI 49058. The office posts Monday to Friday hours from 8:15 to 4:45, shuts for the noon hour, and answers at 269-945-1289 or bcrod@barrycounty.org. Its page offers a useful reminder: filing a deed puts it in the public record without vouching for its legality.

Clerks record, index and preserve what arrives. They do not search titles, hand out blank forms or coach anyone on wording, so the deed itself comes from your closing agent or a lawyer. Nothing already on file can be altered, and a name added to or dropped from ownership means a brand-new deed gets signed and filed.

People sometimes ask for the "title" to a house. The county answers that most homes have none, since the recorded deed covers whatever is permanently fixed to the land. Certain mobile homes are the exception and may keep a separate title with the Secretary of State.

What are the Barry County recording charges, and who pays what?

A flat $30.00 covers any document, and each added instrument number that a paper assigns or discharges brings another $3.00. Sale deeds and similar transfers owe state and county transfer tax on top, collected during recording. One payment to the Register of Deeds can cover the fee and the tax together.

One item travels separately. Land contracts, their assignments, warranty deeds and any deed with a warranty covenant require a Tax Certification from the Barry County Treasurer, priced at $5.00, written as its own check to the treasurer.

Barry County charges posted on the register's recording and FAQ pages
ItemAmount
Recording a document$30.00
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3.00

State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or fraction
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 or fraction
Copy by mail or email$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 search fee if no document number

The counter takes cash, checks, and debit or credit cards; cards add a small service fee.

What transfer tax goes with a Barry County sale?

In the register's FAQ, the seller carries the tax, set at $4.30 for every $500 of consideration, and it is due the moment the deed is recorded. Take $264,100, the 2020 to 2024 Census median for homes in Barry County. It holds 529 blocks of $500 after rounding up, so the tax lands at $2,274.70.

Some transfers escape the tax, though staff will not choose an exemption on your behalf. A deed claiming one must show MCL 207.505 (county) or MCL 207.526 (state) plus the exemption's letter, and the county posts separate lists for each. Have your closing agent make that call.

  • Family gifts to a son, daughter or grandchild sit among the state exemptions.
  • Foreclosure transfers, and deeds given to avoid foreclosure, are exempt from the state tax.
  • Deeds that fix a title flaw by confirming what the grantee already owns are exempt, along with any instrument priced under $100.

The full state list sits in MCL 207.526.

What does the Barry County office require on a deed?

State statutes set recording standards, and Barry posts a checklist drawn from them. Run through it before filing. These are the main points from the county's page.

  • Ink signatures in black or dark blue, original rather than copied, with each name typed or printed under it.
  • An acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary in Michigan, with the notary's name typed on the signature page.
  • A street or post office address for each grantee, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A blank 2.5 inch strip at the top of page one, and half an inch of white space around the rest.
  • Readable black print no smaller than 10 point, on white 20 pound paper sized from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • The property's full value stated in the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit attached.
  • A certified death certificate recorded alongside, or ahead of, any deed that conveys by survivorship.

Photocopies are rejected. Court orders must carry the clerk's seal, and all other documents need original signatures.

What are the ways to file in Barry County, and when does the paper come back?

Walk it in, mail it, or route it through an e-recording company. Barry names five: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, Nationwide Title Clearing, EPN and CSC. A document sent by ordinary email is not recorded.

A paper that meets the standards is recorded the day it is received, according to the FAQ, and walk-in filers take the recorded copy home. Mail and drop-offs usually return in 2 to 4 business days. Enclose a stamped return envelope, or the office keeps the original for 90 days at least. Digital PDF returns through Swift are free and arranged with staff.

One catch from the county's page: the treasurer issues electronic tax certifications only via Simplifile and CSC. Confirm that your closing agent's provider fits before signing day.

Does the register handle property tax or foreclosure questions?

Property tax is outside the register's job. Its FAQ points owners to the city or township for current bills and to the Barry County Treasurer for delinquent amounts. If the parcel has back tax, get a payoff figure from the treasurer first.

Foreclosures reach the office only after the sale occurs, so staff cannot say whether a house is set for sheriff's sale. After a sheriff's deed is recorded, the office takes the redemption payment but does not compute it. Open liens show up in a title search, run at the public workstations or through a title firm.

For ownership questions the county suggests starting with its GIS property map. It follows the tax roll and shows the listed taxpayer, while the recorded deed settles who actually owns the parcel.

What is Barry County like for a seller?

The county spans 577 square miles, 553 of them land. Hastings serves as its lone city and its seat, with Freeport, Middleville, Nashville and Woodland as villages and Delton, Dowling and Hickory Corners as census-designated places. Neighbors include Kent and Allegan counties on the west and northwest, Kalamazoo to the southwest, Eaton to the east and Calhoun to the southeast.

No passenger trains run here, and the lone remaining line is a two-mile CSX stretch through Woodland Township. Drivers rely on M-37 to reach Hastings from the north and south, M-43 through Delton and Hastings, M-79 from Nashville toward Hastings, M-66 along the eastern side and M-89 and M-179 in the west and southwest.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 63,991, a 2.5 percent increase over 2020.
  • Housing units in 2025: 28,284, and 24,480 households.
  • Homeownership: 87.3 percent, and a median home value of $264,100.
  • Household income at the median: $77,500, with gross rent at the median of $972.
  • Mean commute: 27.7 minutes, and building permits in 2025: 157.

With a mean commute near 28 minutes, buyers here weigh drive time and condition. A house with deferred repairs can be hard to finance, and a cash buyer who purchases as-is offers a way to close without fixing them first.

More questions about Barry County, MI Register of Deeds

When is the Barry County deeds counter open?

It posts weekdays from 8:15 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., with a closure from noon to 1:00. Occasional adjusted hours are announced on its page, so call 269-945-1289 before a long drive.

Can I email a deed to Barry County for recording?

No. Plain email cannot be recorded. Send it through an approved provider such as Simplifile, EPN or CSC, or deliver the signed original.

Who is responsible for transfer tax in a Barry County sale?

The seller, per the register's FAQ, and payment falls due at recording. The rate is $4.30 per $500, split as $3.75 to the state and $0.55 to the county.

Can Barry County staff tell me who owns a parcel?

Not directly. Staff can only retrieve the latest deed under a given name. Check the GIS property map for the listed taxpayer, then search that name at a public workstation.

How can I order a copy of a recorded Barry County deed?

The office will mail or email a copy at $1.00 a page, with a $5.00 search charge when you lack the document number. A check has to reach them first, because payment is not taken by email or phone.

  • eRecording offered via partners Simplifile, Indecomm, ePN, CSC Global (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Bay County by the numbers

Bay County ranks 20 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 103,235 people in 48,620 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $135,100, the median home value sits 28% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Bay County reports $60,523. Owner-occupancy is 76%, so renters hold about 24% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1962, about 61 years ago.

What can the Bay County Register of Deeds office do for a seller?

Think of this office as the county's land filing cabinet. Deeds, mortgages, notices of pending suits and certified copies all land here to be indexed, and the resulting public record is what every title company reads before a Bay County closing.

The counter opens Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m. Hands on research with staff wraps up a half hour sooner, and nobody locks the door at midday. Beginning January 1, 2018, each instrument receives a single Document Number in place of the old Liber and Page pair.

The office page also gathers links that sellers and heirs find handy, including a Bay County cemetery directory, contact details for local city and township officials, and state forms from Michigan.gov. Tax certifications carry their own $5 charge, paid to the Treasurer.

  • Doxpop offers search any hour of the day. Its help line, 1-866-369-7671, assists with account sign up.
  • Doxpop Property Watch emails you free of charge whenever someone attempts to transfer title to your land.
  • Approved eRecording partners are listed on the office page for electronic delivery.
  • A package sent by USPS, UPS or FedEx should include postage paid return packaging addressed to you.

What will recording a deed in Bay County set me back?

Bay County's statutory fee schedule sets a single price, $30.00 per document, for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or any similar instrument. Out of each $30, four dollars move on to the state's survey and remonumentation program. Liens held by the state or federal government, fixture filings, plats, state deeds and tax reversion papers are not charged that four dollar share.

What the Bay County office charges. Source: county recording fee page.
ItemAmount
A deed, mortgage or comparable instrument$30.00 apiece
Assignment or discharge naming several instrumentsAdd $3.00 per extra instrument
Tax certificate, paid by separate check to the Treasurer$5.00
UCC financing statement or fixture filing$30.00
State transfer tax$7.50 for each $1,000
County transfer tax$1.10 for each $1,000

The certificate comes from MCL 211.135 and covers deeds with a warranty clause, land contracts, land contract assignments that carry a warranty, and condominium master deeds.

Why might Bay County reject my deed?

The office publishes sixteen rules taken from Michigan recording statutes. If a paper fails any of them it is sent back, and several lost days can upset a closing schedule. These are the flaws that catch sellers most.

  • Signatures must be live originals, with each signer's name typed or printed beneath the line and matching the notary's certificate exactly.
  • A deed has to give the grantee's street or post office address, and it also needs the name and address of the person who prepared it.
  • Any paper that conveys or burdens land needs an acknowledgment from a Michigan notary, judge or court clerk.
  • Page one needs a 2.5 inch empty band along the top, with half an inch of margin on all remaining sides. Print in black ink, 10 point or bigger, on white paper.
  • Paper size runs from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches, and the first line should say what kind of instrument it is.
  • If a deed refers to a surviving owner, pair it with a certified death certificate unless one is already of record.
  • A court order must be certified and sealed by the clerk, and any Social Security number has to have its first five digits removed.

One more rule on the list asks conveyances to give the marital status of male grantors, citing MCLA 565.221.

What is the transfer tax math for a Bay County sale?

Two levies arise at recording, one county (MCL 207.505) and one state (MCL 207.526). Either the deed states the total price on its front, or the filer hands in a Real Estate Transfer Affidavit with that number. Both taxes are due unless an exemption applies, and the instrument itself has to claim it.

Try a house priced at the Census median of $152,200. At $7.50 per thousand, the state share lands near $1,141. At $1.10 per thousand, the county share is near $167. The recorder would collect about $1,309 in all.

The two exemption lists overlap but are not identical. Each excludes consideration below $100, security instruments, leases, court orders that set no price, land contracts whose title has not passed, and foreclosure transfers involving government backed loans. Only the state act goes on to name gifts from a parent or grandparent to a child or grandchild. Ask the title agent or the office which section covers your paper.

Which state fee rules stand behind the Bay County schedule?

The Revised Judicature Act, at MCL 600.2567, governs what a register may charge, and the Bay County page cites it. The statute also prices the services that sellers and heirs request most often.

  • Copies run $1.00 per page. Certifying a recorded paper adds $5.00.
  • Index searches by grantor and grantee cost 50 cents per year covered, with a $5.00 minimum.
  • Filing a miscellaneous paper costs $1.00.
  • Fees are paid on delivery of the paper, with exceptions for electronic filers and for government filers that have a payment agreement.

A charter county can pass its own schedule by ordinance, so confirm any copy or search fee with Bay County staff before you write a check.

In what order should a seller handle recording in Bay County?

Work in this order and you save a trip. Settle who must sign and whether a survivor appears on the deed, so the death certificate is on hand. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the tax certificate from the County Treasurer. Have the deed drafted with the full price written in, or complete the transfer affidavit. Have it notarized in Michigan, then hand the original to the title agent or post it with a return envelope.

Once the paper is recorded, you receive a Document Number, which is how the instrument turns up in the online index. File it with your closing papers. Anyone who holds other land in the county should also enroll in Property Watch.

When a paper bounces, the cause usually sits on the sixteen item list: a mismatched name, a narrow margin, an unsealed court order or an exposed Social Security number. Correct that single defect and resubmit instead of redrafting everything.

Which other Bay County offices does a deed touch?

A sale crosses several counters. The Treasurer, upstairs at 515 Center Ave., writes the tax certificate and collects late tax. Equalization answers parcel and description questions. The assessor in your city or township keeps the value record, while the Register preserves the chain of title.

Bay County borders Saginaw Bay and counts 14 townships and 4 cities. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owned home worth $152,200, 77.0 percent owner occupancy, 45,103 households and a median household income of $61,763. New construction is slight: 67 building permits were counted for 2025.

More questions about Bay County, MI Register of Deeds

What does a Bay County recording cost?

It is $30.00 per document, with $4.00 of the total sent to the state survey fund. A paper that assigns or discharges multiple instruments adds $3.00 for each additional one.

Are Bay County land records searchable on the web?

Yes. Doxpop offers searching at any hour, and the office suggests its free Property Watch alert so you learn of any attempt to move your title.

Is eRecording available in Bay County?

It is. The office page names the approved partners that deliver title documents electronically to the county.

What does the Bay County tax certificate cost on a warranty deed?

Five dollars, on its own check, payable to the Bay County Treasurer instead of the Register.

What transfer tax rates does Bay County list?

The Register shows $7.50 per $1,000 of consideration for the state and $1.10 per $1,000 for the county. An exempt transfer must say why on the instrument.

The Benzie County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Benzie County

  • Benzie County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Statewide: recording fee $30.00 per document regardless of pages (MCL 600.2567); copies $1/page; certification $5 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Benzie County?

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Where do I find the Benzie County Register of Deeds?

Go to Suite 202 of the Government Center, 448 Court Place, Beulah, MI 49617. The counter staffs weekdays from half past eight in the morning to five in the afternoon, and callers reach it at 231-882-0016.

Benzie County hugs Lake Michigan on the northwest side of the state, and its website advertises more than 100 lakes and several square miles of state forest. Every deed, mortgage and easement for land in those townships and in the city of Frankfort lands in the same index at this one counter.

  • Clerks cannot supply blank forms or weigh in on legal questions. People who need a deed written are told to see an attorney or a title company.
  • A filing can arrive over the counter, by post, via UPS or FedEx, or by electronic submission.
  • If you request copies by mail, enclose your own return envelope with postage.

What is the price of recording at the Benzie County office?

The county page quotes $30.00 per filing however many pages it runs. Michigan's MCL 600.2567 sets that same $30 and includes the survey fee inside it. If one paper assigns or discharges multiple instruments, each instrument after the first brings a $3.00 surcharge.

Benzie County recording office charges. Source: Benzie County Register of Deeds page and MCL 600.2567.
ServicePrice
File one document$30.00
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Copy of a recorded real estate record$1.00 a page
Certification of a document$5.00 extra
Tax certificate covering up to five descriptions$5.00 per instrument
Every description beyond five20 cents

Certain papers need a County Treasurer certificate first: warranty deeds, any deed that promises warranty, land contracts and assignments of them, and condominium master deeds. Under MCL 211.135 the proof covers five years of taxes before the instrument date.

Can I record electronically in Benzie County, and is there a surcharge?

Four vendors handle electronic submissions: Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm. Every one sets a price of its own, and the county Register adds nothing more, so the vendor's charge is the only extra cost to budget for.

If your deed also calls for county tax certification, the office recommends ePN because a document router links the two. A single electronic package can then serve both offices.

Searching is its own service. Names are indexed by seller and buyer, and scans reach back to the mid 1800s. The public Tapestry link charges for use, and title professionals may take a Laredo subscription arranged by phone.

What transfer tax applies to a Benzie County deed?

Michigan's state transfer tax is collected by this office as the deed goes on record, and its page links the county act (MCL 207.505) and the state act (MCL 207.526). The state charge is $3.75 on each $500 of price, a partial block rounding up, or $7.50 per $1,000. Call the office to learn the county amount for your instrument.

Take Benzie's Census median value of $285,700: state tax alone comes to $2,145, because the price spans 572 blocks of $500 after rounding up. That amount deserves a line in any shoreline seller's net sheet.

Some transfers escape the state tax, and the instrument has to say which exemption it claims.

  • A price below $100, loan security papers, leases and mineral interests.
  • A deed passing from a person to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild.
  • A court order that sets no dollar price, a boundary adjustment, or a corrective quitclaim.
  • A land contract in which the seller still holds title, and foreclosure deeds, including deeds given to avoid foreclosure.

What kinds of instruments does Benzie County record?

The office lists its services as the recording of land related paper, and the list is broad. A seller or an heir will meet several of these during a sale or estate settlement.

  • Warranty, quit claim and mineral deeds, as well as administrator, tax and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, along with assignments and discharges of them.
  • Liens for state and federal tax, circuit court orders, and probate orders.
  • Certificates of trust, master deeds, rights of way, restrictions and subdivision plats.
  • Surveys, land corner records and remonumentation records.

Payoff paperwork matters most with an older loan. A lender files a discharge once a mortgage is satisfied, and the buyer's closer checks this index for it before title is cleared.

What should a Benzie County seller do before filing a deed?

Sequence matters at a small counter. Begin with the title commitment, so you know which liens need a discharge. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the Treasurer's certificate next, or send the deed through ePN so certification travels with it. After that, check that the deed states the complete price, because transfer tax follows the stated price.

Last, choose how it gets there. Carry it in on a weekday, post it with a return envelope, or let the closing agent send it through one of the four vendors. A family transfer should name its exemption right on the instrument, so the tax is not collected in error.

Which neighbors of the Register of Deeds should a seller call?

Upstairs in that building is the Treasurer, at 231-882-0011, on the same weekday schedule. The office administers delinquent tax under Public Act 206 and keeps the tax rolls. Online payments of delinquent tax cost 2.49 percent by card (minimum $1.50) or $1.00 by e-check.

Downstairs, Equalization works from Suite 130 at 231-882-0015. It supplies parcel maps, descriptions, values, sales data, tax maps and millage rates, and its page also links a parcel search and FEMA map change forms, handy for lakefront owners.

The Register's page also carries identity crime guidance. A free Property Fraud Alert service emails you when any document is recorded under your name, which helps an owner who lives elsewhere catch a forged deed early. The office keeps related handouts on preventing identity theft, and the Register collects the state remonumentation fee as part of each filing.

Separately, the Register leads the county Plat Board that reviews new subdivisions and processes U.S. passport applications.

How do Benzie County housing numbers look?

Benzie is small and growing. Census puts it at 18,568 people in 2025, up 3.3 percent from the 2020 base, on 319.7 square miles of land. Nearly a third of residents, 31.1 percent, are 65 or older.

The county counts 12,682 housing units against only 7,708 households, and 87.8 percent of occupied homes belong to their occupants. The 2020 to 2024 median value is $285,700, with household income near $74,834 a year. Builders pulled 136 permits in 2025. Median gross rent is $1,026 a month, a useful benchmark if the house you are selling has a tenant living in it. Because units outnumber households so widely, ask the title agent early whether any owner or heir lives out of the area, since that changes where papers are signed and mailed.

More questions about Benzie County, MI Register of Deeds

What is Benzie County's fee for filing a deed?

Thirty dollars a document, no matter how long it is. A paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds three dollars for each one after the first.

Does the Benzie County Register of Deeds add a surcharge for electronic filing?

No. Only the vendor you pick bills a fee, and the approved list is Simplifile, ePN, CSC and Indecomm.

When is a tax certificate required in Benzie County?

Warranty deeds, land contracts and condominium master deeds need one. Up to five descriptions cost $5.00, and each further description is 20 cents.

Will Benzie County staff write my deed for me?

No. Staff do not prepare blank documents or give legal advice, so engage an attorney or a title company.

When can I visit the Benzie County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon, in Suite 202 of the Government Center in Beulah. Phone 231-882-0016 first if you have a question.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Michigan flat recording fee of $30 effective Oct 1, 2016 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Address 701 Main Street, St. Joseph; beginning Nov 9, 2026 office closed to public and stops recording at 4:00 p.m. daily (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Berrien County?
We buy Berrien County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Berrien County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 153,411 people and 77,127 housing units in Berrien County, which ranks 16 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $211,400, which is 13% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $63,152; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 27% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 73% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1966, about 57 years ago.

Where do I take a deed in Berrien County, and when is the counter open?

The office occupies the Berrien County Administration Center, 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085. Staff are present on weekdays that are not county holidays, with doors open from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. The window for taking in documents is shorter, ending at 4:30 p.m., and the public search computers go dark at 4:45 p.m.

Questions go to 269-983-7111, extension 8562. The county's own roster of local governments names 8 cities, 9 villages and 22 townships, so paper reaches this one counter from Benton Harbor, New Buffalo, Niles, Three Oaks and many places in between.

  • Deliver the original in person, by courier, or by USPS, UPS or FedEx to 701 Main Street.
  • Slip in a self addressed return envelope, since the recorded paper travels back to whoever you name on it.
  • Photocopies get turned away because the office only records originals with live signatures.
  • Pay the whole amount up front. Checks should name the Register of Deeds, because a check meant for another county department will bounce the whole packet back.

What does the Berrien County office charge to record a deed?

Berrien's fee page posts $30 for any document, however long, and its FAQ describes that as the flat Michigan charge per recordable event. Certification and transfer tax can be added when the paper is a deed.

Fee schedule posted by the Berrien County Register of Deeds. Source: county fee page.
ItemCharge
Record a single document of any size$30
Extra instrument named in an assignment or discharge$3 each
Tax certification covering up to 25 parcel descriptions$5
Each further parcel description20 cents
Ordinary copy$1 per page
Oversize copy, larger than tabloid paper$3 per page
Certifying a recorded document$5 plus $1 per page

The treasurer's certificate has to accompany a warranty deed, any deed with a warranty covenant, a land contract or its assignment, and a master deed for a condominium.

What will a Berrien County seller pay in transfer tax?

Berrien's fee page applies two taxes to a non exempt deed of $100 or more. The county levy is 55 cents for each $500 of the price and the state levy is $3.75 for each $500, and a leftover fraction counts as a whole block. Added up, that is $4.30 per block. A rate chart posted by the county turns sale prices into dollar amounts.

State the whole price on the deed or attach a real estate valuation affidavit. Name any exemption on the instrument itself.

A worked example: Census lists $224,300 as the median value of an owned home here. Rounded up, that price fills 449 blocks of $500. The state share is 449 times $3.75, which is $1,683.75, and the county share is 449 times 55 cents, which is $246.95. At recording the sum due is $1,930.70. The purchase contract assigns who pays, so confirm with the title agent.

The two statutes differ on exemptions. MCL 207.526, the state act, excuses a gift of a home to a child or grandchild, court orders with no stated price, and a transfer made through a mortgage foreclosure. MCL 207.505, the county act, shares many exemptions but has no family transfer item, so settle which tax applies before anyone signs.

What must a Berrien County deed have before staff will accept it?

Berrien keeps a recording requirements page and a question list. These items show up most with house sales and estates.

  • Bring a certified death certificate, sealed by the clerk, to record that a joint owner has died (MCL 565.48). Recording it does not change the earlier deed, which stays the most current deed of record until someone files a new one.
  • A court paper must show the court's certification and seal.
  • For a notary, try the County Clerk by appointment on the main number, extension 8233, or a bank, municipal office or title company, some of which charge a fee.
  • Employees do not write deeds for the public. The county points people to a lawyer or title insurer, and notes that templates can be found online or in office supply stores.
  • Mortgage survey reports do not go on file here. Only a certified survey that was actually recorded appears in the index.

Every recorded paper turns into a public record, and any member of the public may buy a copy for $1 per page. Once a loan is repaid, the lender files a discharge of mortgage at this office, and a buyer's closer checks for it.

Where can I search Berrien County records online?

Berrien's website has a Land Records Search page for lookups and an e-Recording page for electronic filing. Its property and taxes page also links to online Register of Deeds services, the transfer tax chart and a flowchart on splitting or combining parcels.

Ahead of a closing, search by name for the chain of title, open mortgages and recorded liens. Counter searches by staff run 50 cents per year covered. Owners who intend to hold back a piece of their lot should read the split and combine flowchart first, since that process runs through other offices.

Keep the county's departments straight when you chase a payoff. The Register of Deeds is an elected office that reviews and records papers moving or burdening land, and the county describes it as a land historian. The County Treasurer is a separate elected office with a four year term, and the Equalization Department prepares the report that sets the equalized tax base for the Board of Commissioners. Tax payoff questions belong with the treasurer, not here.

An heir preparing to list should pull the earlier deed and any recorded death certificate before the listing goes live, so the title agent can tell exactly who holds the interest.

How do Berrien County's housing numbers read for a seller?

The July 2025 population estimate is 152,444, which is 1.3 percent under the 2020 base, across 567.78 square miles of land. Housing stock totals 78,132 units and 63,999 households. Owner occupancy sits at 72.8 percent.

Over the 2020 to 2024 survey period the typical owned home was worth $224,300 and the typical household earned $65,425. Monthly costs for owners paying a mortgage averaged out to a median of $1,462, and gross rent had a median of $942. Roughly 7.9 percent of people use another language at home, which can affect interpreter and notary planning for a closing. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 372.

Among three neighboring Michigan counties surveyed together, Bay has a median value of $152,200 and Benzie has $285,700. Berrien lands between them, so a median priced sale here carries more transfer tax than one in Bay and less than one in Benzie.

More questions about Berrien County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is the Berrien County recording fee?

Thirty dollars flat per recordable document, regardless of how many pages it has. When a paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each one past the first adds $3.

What are Berrien's transfer tax numbers?

The county tax is 55 cents per $500 and the state tax is $3.75 per $500, with each block rounded up. That adds to $4.30 per block, unless the deed is exempt.

Is mailing a deed to Berrien County allowed?

Yes. Send the signed original to 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085, along with complete payment and a return envelope that carries postage. A photocopy cannot be recorded.

What is the cutoff for recording in Berrien County?

Documents are taken until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office itself stays open to 5:00 p.m. and the public search computers close at 4:45 p.m.

Does the Berrien County recording office offer a notary?

No. Book a notary at the County Clerk through 269-983-7111, extension 8233, or visit a bank, municipal office or title company. Some of them charge a fee.
