Branch County by the numbers

Branch County ranks 38 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 44,914 people in 20,879 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $147,500, the median home value sits 21% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Branch County reports $61,958. Owner-occupancy is 77%, so renters hold about 23% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1969, about 54 years ago.

Where does Branch County record deeds and mortgages?

Branch County land records are kept in the Courthouse Annex, 23 East Pearl Street, Coldwater. Weekday counter hours are 7:30 to 4:30, lunch hour included, and the office phone is 517-279-4320.

A document that arrives after the 4:30 close still gets that day's date stamp, and the clerks record it first thing the following morning. E-recording is accepted, which suits lenders and title agents closing a Coldwater, Bronson or Quincy sale from a distance. Frequent researchers can pay monthly for remote access, and occasional ones pay per search.

An owner checking for back taxes before listing can use the treasurer's free delinquent tax search at bsaonline.com. Under Online Services choose Delinquent Tax Search, then enter a surname, a parcel number or a street address.

What does the Branch County Register of Deeds charge?

Each recording costs $30 flat. The county forwards $4 of every fee to the state survey and remonumentation fund, with carve-outs for fixture filings, liens filed by the state or federal government, state deeds, plats and tax reversion documents. The governing fee statute is MCL 600.2567.

  • $30 each for a deed, a mortgage, a lien notice or release, and a UCC fixture filing.
  • $3 for every instrument past the first on a combined assignment or discharge.
  • $1 per page for copies of recorded real estate documents, and $5 to certify a document.
  • Name searches at 50 cents per year searched, never less than $5, and $3 per name for a lien search.
  • $5 to have a document faxed or emailed.

Mailed submissions must include a stamped envelope addressed to you, since that is how the recorded original comes back.

Why would Branch County reject a deed?

Returned paper usually fails one of the formatting tests in MCL 565.201. Check these points first.

  • A typed or printed name beneath each signature, which should be dark ink and must spell the name the way the notary block does.
  • The notary's printed name sitting near the notary signature on the same sheet.
  • Grantee mailing addresses, plus who drafted the paper and where to reach them.
  • An unprinted strip of 2 1/2 inches on top of page one, and 1/2 inch along all remaining edges.
  • A heading line that states the single recordable event, for example warranty deed.
  • Dark print of at least 10 points on white stock weighing 20 pounds, no smaller than letter and no longer than legal.
  • Social Security numbers cut to their last four digits, and a written English translation for foreign-language text.

Once a document meets these tests, the register cannot refuse it over what it says.

Does a Branch County deed need a tax certificate first?

That turns on the kind of deed. Warranty deeds, deeds with a warranty covenant, land contracts and land contract memoranda with a warranty clause all go through the Branch County Treasurer first. MCL 211.135 is the source, and the certificate has to show that the parcel carries no tax liens or tax titles and that five years of taxes before the deed date are settled.

The treasurer charges $5 a document for as many as five descriptions and 20 cents for each one beyond five. That money goes on its own check made out to the Treasurer's Office.

A quitclaim with no warranty covenant sits outside the rule, so family transfers and title fixes tend to move quickly. If you owe back taxes, expect a warranty deed to sit until the balance is paid.

How much transfer tax does a Branch County sale cost?

A sale draws two levies. The county takes 55 cents for every $500 of value or fraction (MCL 207.504), and the state takes $3.75 per the same unit (MCL 207.525). Added together, that is $4.30 per $500 and $8.60 per $1,000. The deed should state the full value on its face, or an affidavit of value goes with it.

The Register of Deeds collects the tax on any transfer of $100 or more and publishes a rate schedule on its resources page. Who pays is settled in the purchase agreement.

Branch County transfer tax by price; $162,500 is the 2020-2024 Census median value
PriceCounty (0.55)State (3.75)Combined
$90,000$99.00$675.00$774.00
$162,500$178.75$1,218.75$1,397.50
$240,000$264.00$1,800.00$2,064.00

A house at the county median thus carries about $1,400 of combined tax at the recorder's window.

Which Branch County transfers escape transfer tax?

County and state exemptions overlap without matching exactly. Both let through nominal deals under $100, mortgages and other security papers, leases, court orders that name no price, boundary corrections, title-confirming quitclaims, and land contracts whose legal title has not yet passed.

  • A parent or grandparent deeding to a descendant, including step and adopted relations, is exempt only in the state act, MCL 207.526.
  • Foreclosure is treated differently too. The state exempts any mortgage foreclosure or deed in lieu, while MCL 207.505 reaches only government-made, guaranteed or insured loans.
  • The county list carries no gift-to-child entry, so ask in Coldwater whether the county's 55 cents still hits a family deed.

Which Branch County towns does the Coldwater office serve?

The Coldwater office records land for every parcel in the county, wherever it sits. The two cities are Bronson and Coldwater. Quincy, Sherwood and Union City are villages. The sixteen townships are Algansee, Batavia, Bethel, Bronson, Butler, California, Coldwater, Gilead, Girard, Kinderhook, Matteson, Noble, Ovid, Quincy, Sherwood and Union.

Unincorporated places on the county's list include Canada Shores, Crystal Beach, East Gilead, Girard, Hatmaker, Hodunk, Lockwood, Pearl Beach, Ray and Sans Souci Beach. A deed for a lot in any of them goes to the same counter in Coldwater.

What should a seller know about Branch County?

County government in Branch is centered on Coldwater, the seat and biggest city. The county dates to 1829, with local government organized four years later, and its 520 square miles of total area make it the third smallest in the state. Bronson is the second city, Quincy, Sherwood and Union City are villages, and sixteen townships make up the balance. Farming is still the foundation of the local economy, and the county forms the Coldwater micropolitan area.

Census figures give 44,862 residents in 2020 and an estimated 45,993 in 2025, spread over 506 land square miles at roughly 89 people each. There are 21,287 housing units and 16,906 households. Owners occupy 77.7% of units, the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $162,500, and gross rent in the middle of the range is $959. Median household income is $63,724; 13.2% of residents are in poverty and 21.1% are over 65. Workers commute 22.7 minutes on average.

Against a U.S. median home value of $332,700, those prices mean the recording fee, the tax certificate and the transfer tax weigh heavily on a Branch County closing statement.

More questions about Branch County, MI Register of Deeds

How much will I pay to put a deed on record in Branch County?

Budget $30 for the recording itself, no matter how many pages the deed has. Add $3 per extra instrument if one document assigns or discharges several, and at least $5 for the treasurer's certificate when the deed carries a warranty.

What are the street address and hours of the Branch County recorder?

Go to the Courthouse Annex at 23 East Pearl Street in Coldwater between 7:30 and 4:30 on a weekday. The number to call is 517-279-4320.

Does Branch County take electronic filings?

It does. Electronic submissions are accepted, and whatever lands after 4:30 in the afternoon is date stamped that day and entered in the books the next morning.

Is a tax certificate needed to record a quitclaim in Branch County?

Usually not. The tax certificate statute, MCL 211.135, carves out a quitclaim or any deed lacking a covenant of warranty. Warranty deeds and land contracts still need the county treasurer's sign-off.

What happens with transfer tax when I deed the house to my son or daughter?

The state tax does not apply, because MCL 207.526(j) and (k) exempt a transfer to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild. The county statute lists no such exemption, so ask the Register of Deeds about the county's 55 cents per $500 before you record.

Calhoun County by the numbers

Calhoun County ranks 17 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 133,846 people in 59,626 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $151,500, the median home value sits 19% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Calhoun County reports $60,385. Owner-occupancy is 72%, so renters hold about 28% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1961, about 62 years ago.

Where are Calhoun County land records filed?

Calhoun County accepts land documents in one place only: the Marshall County Building at 315 West Green Street, home of the Clerk and Register of Deeds. The second office, at 161 East Michigan Avenue in Battle Creek, deals with circuit court filings and personal protection orders, so a deed taken there goes nowhere. Call the Marshall counter at 269-781-0718.

Title researchers and genealogists use the research room, open on business days and shutting at 4:45 p.m., a quarter hour ahead of the office itself. The Marshall building also issues marriage licenses, vital records and notary commissions, so expect a mixed crowd at the counter. A drop box at the west edge of the parking lot behind the County Building takes completed documents with payment enclosed. The county also provides an online land record search and a property alert tool.

Clerks do not give legal advice about completing a land record form, and the office stocks no blank forms. Questions go to a lawyer; the county suggests the State Bar of Michigan referral line, 1-800-968-0738, or Michigan Legal Help.

What are the recording fees at the Calhoun County office?

A flat $30 buys the recording of any document, long or short. The list the county gives includes deeds, mortgages, certified copies, lis pendens, timber, oil and gas leases, UCC filings, Land Division Act filings, discharges and terminations, and federal, state and employment security liens. Land record payments are taken as cash or check, nothing else.

  • Add $3 for each additional liber and page referenced on a discharge or assignment.
  • Pay $5 to the treasurer for the tax certification a warranty deed or land contract requires.
  • Copies cost $1 a page for real estate records, $2 for UCC filings, and at least $2 a page for plats.
  • Certification of a recorded instrument is $5.

The statute behind the base fee is MCL 600.2567: $30 to enter and record a document, with $3 added for each further instrument assigned or discharged.

Can I record a Calhoun County deed electronically?

Yes, with one carve-out. Every document type can be e-recorded except those that require a real estate transfer tax valuation affidavit, which have to be mailed or brought to the Marshall counter. The process runs through a vendor: you scan and upload, the register reviews, and anything with errors comes back for correction before it is stamped and returned by electronic delivery.

Four vendors work with the county: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. Sign up as a customer with one of them; each offers demonstrations and training. Where a document needs tax certification, the system routes it to the County Treasurer's Office, so no separate trip is needed for the certificate.

What does the Marshall office check on a Calhoun County deed?

The county's posted checklist rests on MCL 565.201 and adds items that catch people who draft their own deeds.

  • Signatures in original ink, each with a typed or printed name below it that agrees with the notary block.
  • Street or post office addresses for grantees, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A Michigan acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary.
  • For any deed that names a survivor, a certified death certificate that was recorded earlier and is cited by liber and page.
  • Court orders bearing the court clerk's certification and seal.
  • A first line stating one recordable event, black type of 10 points or more on white 20-pound paper, and a 2 1/2 inch blank band above the first line of page one and 1/2 inch on the other edges.
  • The land's total value shown on the deed or in an attached valuation affidavit. The county bars the stock phrase "and other good and valuable consideration."
  • Any transfer tax exemption spelled out on the instrument, and a trust document recorded as a separate paper.

Who certifies taxes before a Calhoun County warranty deed is recorded?

The Calhoun County Treasurer signs off. A warranty deed, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract or any deed with a warranty covenant must carry the treasurer's certification before the register accepts it, and the fee is $5. Call 269-781-0807 with questions about deed certification. When you e-record, the system forwards the paper to the treasurer for you.

The rule comes from MCL 211.135: the parcel must be free of tax liens and tax titles, and the five years of taxes before the deed date must be paid. A plain quitclaim lacking a warranty covenant is outside it.

An owner who has fallen behind will run into the balance at this step, so clear it before the closing date and keep the recording on schedule.

How much transfer tax applies to a Calhoun County sale?

Stack the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) on the state's $3.75 (MCL 207.525) and you get $4.30 for each $500 of value, with any remainder counted as one more block. The law counts a fraction of a block as a whole one, so a $162,800 home, the county's Census median, becomes 326 blocks instead of 325.6.

Calhoun County transfer tax by sale price; $162,800 is the 2020-2024 Census median value
PriceCounty (0.55)State (3.75)Combined
$95,000$104.50$712.50$817.00
$162,800$179.30$1,222.50$1,401.80
$275,000$302.50$2,062.50$2,365.00

Owners selling a troubled property care most about three exemptions. A deed in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure on any mortgage is exempt under the state act, while the county act covers only government-backed loans. A court order that sets no price escapes both taxes. A transfer to a child or grandchild appears on the state list in MCL 207.526. Whatever you claim should be written on the instrument.

How big is Calhoun County, and who lives in its homes?

Calhoun County has 718 square miles of area, 706 of it land, centered on Battle Creek, the largest city, and Marshall, the seat. Albion and Springfield are the other cities. Athens, Burlington, Homer, Tekonsha and Union City are villages, and sixteen townships fill the rest. Established in 1829 and organized in 1833, the county is the core of the Battle Creek metropolitan area and sits inside the wider Kalamazoo-Battle Creek-Portage combined statistical area.

The Census Bureau estimates 133,408 residents for 2025 in 59,808 housing units. Owners live in 72.7% of homes, the typical owner-occupied value is $162,800, typical gross rent is $968, and the county has 53,333 households earning a median $63,177. Households average 2.44 people, 91.4% of adults 25 and older finished high school, and 22.9% hold a bachelor's degree or more. About 89.6% of households have broadband, a point worth knowing when a buyer will sign closing papers online.

At that typical value, a sale triggers roughly $1,400 of transfer tax, and the rates are the same in every Michigan county.

More questions about Calhoun County, MI Register of Deeds

What will I owe the Calhoun County recorder for a deed?

Thirty dollars per document, paid in cash or by check. A discharge or assignment adds $3 per additional liber and page it references, and a warranty deed needs the $5 treasurer tax certification as well.

Will the Battle Creek office record my deed?

No. Land document recordings are filed only at the Marshall office, 315 West Green Street. Battle Creek handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders.

Is e-recording available for Calhoun County deeds?

Yes, through CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A document with a transfer tax valuation affidavit is the exception and must be mailed or delivered to Marshall.

What commonly gets a Calhoun County deed returned?

Typical reasons are a missing grantee address, no drafter name, signer names that disagree with the acknowledgment, no stated property value, and margins or type size outside the statute. The office returns rejected paper with the reasons checked off.

Who is responsible for the Calhoun County transfer tax in a sale?

The statutes tax the written instrument and leave payment to the parties, so the purchase agreement governs. A $162,800 sale carries $1,401.80 in combined county and state tax.

Who records deeds in Cass County

  • Cass County Clerk/Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30 per document regardless of pages (since Oct 1, 2016); $3 per additional instrument for multi-instrument assignments/discharges (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Cass County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 51,606 people and 25,543 housing units in Cass County, which ranks 35 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $205,200, which is 9% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $68,011; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 19% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 81% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1972, about 51 years ago.

Which office handles Cass County land records?

In Cass County one elected official, on a four-year term, fills both the Clerk and Register of Deeds roles. Besides land records, that office serves as clerk to the circuit court, the board of commissioners, the plat board and the jury board, as registrar of vital records, and as the county's chief election officer. The same counter handles marriage licenses, concealed pistol permits, assumed business names and notary commissions. Find it at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, Cassopolis. The phone is 269-445-4464 and the fax is 269-445-4406. Call to confirm counter hours before you drive in with an original deed.

For occasional users, the county runs a basic deed search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number. The index search costs nothing. Looking at, printing or saving an image runs $1 a page plus a processing fee. Staff searches are done as time permits, so allow extra days. Clerks will pull a single document you identify, but the office has no authority to search real property records or draw up a list of recorded instruments.

What does Cass County bill for recording?

The price of a recording has been $30 since October 1, 2016, however many pages the document runs. Where one paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each additional instrument costs $3. MCL 600.2567 is the state basis. Keep staples away from checks.

  • A treasurer's tax certification, $5, is required for warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of them, and may be added to the recording check.
  • UCC terminations and fixture filings: $30 each. Financing statements go to the State of Michigan only.
  • Copies: $1 a page, $5 for a plat of record, $5 by fax; certifying a copy is $5.
  • Staff searches: half a dollar for each year covered with a $5 floor, $3 per name for state or federal tax lien certificates, and $6 for a financing statement certificate on one debtor name.

What does the Cass County checklist demand of a deed?

The county posts twenty requirements. Many echo MCL 565.201, and several are more explicit than other counties' lists.

  • The land's complete legal description.
  • A notary block giving the notary's signature, commission expiration date, the county and state of certification, the names of those acknowledging, and where the paper was signed.
  • A notary seal if the notary is out of state.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits, unless a law or court order calls for more.
  • An affidavit explaining the correction whenever an original is recorded a second time.
  • A recorded death certificate, attached or cited by liber and page, wherever a grantor is described as survivor.
  • The consideration stated on the deed itself. Wording such as "other good and valuable consideration" is accepted only with an affidavit.

Layout follows the statewide rule: a blank 2 1/2 inches above the first line of page one, half an inch on other edges, black print of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, and a sheet no smaller than letter or larger than legal.

What does a Cass County tax certification actually cover?

MCL 211.135 sets up a two-part certificate. First, the county or state treasurer says whether any tax liens or tax titles are held on the parcel and whether taxes are paid for the five years preceding the instrument's date. Second, the treasurer of the city, village or township where the land lies reports on tax titles and tax sale certificates, and on whether those titles, certificates and sold special assessments were redeemed over the same five years.

Timing can matter. Paper presented from March 1 on, before the local treasurer has filed the year's delinquent return, receives a county treasurer notation that the return could not be checked. That gap is not a reason for the register to turn the deed away.

Where a tax certificate or special assessment has been sold against your parcel, redeem it through the village or township and collect written proof ahead of closing, because the statute requires evidence of redemption.

How is transfer tax figured on a Cass County closing?

The same rates apply here as elsewhere in Michigan: 55 cents for the county per MCL 207.504 and $3.75 for the state per MCL 207.525, each applied to every $500 of price or any leftover part of $500, so a price of $218,001 would count as 437 blocks. The Cass County Census median of $218,000 divides into 436 blocks.

Cass County transfer tax by price; $218,000 is the 2020-2024 Census median value
PriceCounty (0.55)State (3.75)Combined
$120,000$132.00$900.00$1,032.00
$218,000$239.80$1,635.00$1,874.80
$350,000$385.00$2,625.00$3,010.00

When a deal includes personal property, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an affidavit states the two values apart.

Which Cass County transfers are exempt from transfer tax?

MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526 share most of their exemptions. The ones most likely to matter in Cass County are below.

  • Land contracts, while legal title waits for the final payment.
  • Quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • Boundary-line deeds with no payment attached.
  • A joint tenancy among people when at least one already owned the land.
  • A husband's or wife's deed that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entireties.
  • On the state list alone: deeds from a parent or grandparent to a descendant, including step and adopted relations, and a dissolving company's transfer to its owners.

An exempt deed still has to meet every format rule, so ask the Clerk/Register how to word the exemption before you sign.

Which Cass County communities send deeds to Cassopolis?

Every parcel in the county records in Cassopolis. The cities and villages are Dowagiac, Cassopolis, Edwardsburg, Marcellus and Vandalia, and unincorporated places include Adamsville, Calvin Center, Glenwood, Jones, La Grange, Penn, Pokagon, Sumnerville, Union and Wakelee. Library districts give a handy map of the townships: Cass District Library serves Calvin, Howard, Jefferson, LaGrange, Mason, Milton, Newberg, Ontwa, Penn, Pokagon, Porter and Volinia, Dowagiac District Library serves the city of Dowagiac and Wayne Township plus parts of three others, and Marcellus runs its own.

Where is Cass County, and what does its housing look like?

Cass County belongs to the South Bend-Mishawaka metropolitan area, the Michiana corner of southwest Michigan. Cassopolis, platted in 1831 at the geographic center of the county, is the seat; Dowagiac is the largest city. Villages include Cassopolis, Edwardsburg, Marcellus and Vandalia. Cass dates from 1829 and filled in quickly because its prairie land needed less clearing than nearby areas. Pennsylvania Quakers settled Penn Township that same year, and it became a station on the Underground Railroad. Southwestern Michigan College is in Dowagiac.

The 2025 Census estimate is 51,677 residents, with 490 square miles of land under them, which works out near 105 per square mile. There are 26,087 housing units and 21,207 households. Owner occupancy reaches 81.6%. The half-way owner-occupied value is $218,000, half-way gross rent is $916, and half of households earn more than $70,443. Residents 65 or older make up 24.0% of the county, and the typical commute takes 24.4 minutes.

At $218,000, the median here sits well above the $162,800 reported for Calhoun County, so a typical Cass County sale carries a larger transfer tax bill in dollars.

More questions about Cass County, MI Register of Deeds

What will a deed cost to record in Cass County?

Thirty dollars per document, whatever its length, plus $3 for each extra instrument on a combined assignment or discharge. A warranty deed also needs the $5 treasurer tax certification, which the county lets you include in the same check as the recording fee.

What is the address of the Cass County Register of Deeds?

The Clerk/Register office is at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, Cassopolis, MI 49031. Call 269-445-4464, and do not staple your check to the document.

Is searching Cass County deeds free?

The index is free to search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number. Viewing, printing or saving a document image costs $1 a page plus a processing fee.

What does the transfer tax come to on a $218,000 sale in Cass County?

The total is $1,874.80, made up of $239.80 for the county and $1,635.00 for the state, using 55 cents and $3.75 per $500.

Do I need a treasurer's certificate to record a Cass County quitclaim?

Generally not. The county asks for one on warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a covenant of warranty, and MCL 211.135 excludes conveyances without a warranty covenant.

Who records deeds in Charlevoix County

  • Charlevoix County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30.00 per document; $5.00 certified (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

Where is the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?

The Charlevoix County Register of Deeds sits at 13513 Division Street in the city of Charlevoix, MI 49720. The state treasury list of registers of deeds gives the phone as 231-547-7204 and the fax as 231-237-0106, and the office takes email at rod@charlevoixcounty.org. Call before you drive in, because the office page does not post public counter hours.

The city of Charlevoix is the seat, while Boyne City is the largest city. Anyone selling a house here, whether it is a Lake Charlevoix cottage, a place in East Jordan, or a home on Beaver Island, finishes the transfer at this one office. The county Register of Deeds page describes the office as a constitutional office created in 1835 that records, indexes and preserves land documents.

What happens to my deed once Charlevoix County receives it?

Staff stamp the time on it, give it a liber and page, scan it and add it to the searchable index. That sequence is what puts the buyer's name on the public record for the property.

The office is plain about its limits. Its page says recording does not make a document legal; it makes the document public. Counter staff have no blank deed forms to hand out and cannot draft or coach, because MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from legal advice. The deed itself comes from your closing attorney or the title agent, and the register of deeds only checks it against the recording rules.

  • Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and discharges are recorded here.
  • The computer image index reaches back to January 1984, and older records are still being indexed.
  • Documents can be walked in or mailed with the fee and a prepaid return envelope.

What are the Charlevoix County recording charges?

Filing one document costs $30.00 whatever its length. That amount follows MCL 600.2567, and the county fee page notes that $4.00 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund.

Charlevoix County Register of Deeds statutory fees (county fee page)
ItemCharge
Recording one document$30.00
Each extra liber and page on an assignment or discharge covering several instruments$3.00
Tax certification$5.00
Copies of documents$1.00 a page
Plat copies$4.00 a page
Certified copy$5.00

One check payable to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds can cover the recording fee, any transfer tax and the tax certification together. Since January 2, 2025, the office adds $3.00 per document for return postage when you send a document in without a prepaid return envelope, and it holds the document unrecorded until that amount arrives.

What transfer tax comes due at a Charlevoix County closing?

Most sales carry two taxes, both counted in $500 slices of the price with any leftover treated as a full slice. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a slice for counties under 2,000,000 people. MCL 207.525 puts the state rate at $3.75 a slice.

Take a sale at $276,800, the Census median value for homes that owners live in here. That is 554 slices, so roughly $305 in county tax and $2,078 in state tax. The full value has to appear on the deed itself, or an affidavit stating it travels with the deed.

Some transfers escape the county tax. MCL 207.505 lists instruments with consideration under $100, security instruments such as mortgages, leases, and deeds that only fix a title flaw. Check with the office on how your own deed is treated well before the closing date.

Which layout rules can bounce a deed at the Charlevoix counter?

A deed must satisfy the page rules in MCL 565.201, and the office may not take one that misses them. Formatting causes most returns, so inspect the sheet before it goes in the mail.

  • Margin: 2.5 inches of clear space at the head of page one and half an inch around the rest of every page.
  • Print: 10-point type or bigger, black ink, white paper of 20-pound stock or heavier.
  • Size: letter or legal sheets only, from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • First line: one statement naming the recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Only one recordable event per instrument.

The statute also wants a legible printed name under every signature that matches the acknowledgment, and the name and workplace address of whoever drafted anything signed after 1964.

Why do I need a tax certificate before a warranty deed is recorded in Charlevoix County?

Michigan law makes the office ask for proof that no tax liens attach to the parcel. Under MCL 211.135 the county treasurer certifies that taxes for the five years leading up to the deed date are paid, and Charlevoix charges $5.00 for that certification.

The county fee page names the deeds that trigger this step: warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, and trustee, fiduciary or personal representative deeds with a warranty clause. It reaches master deeds for condominiums as well. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excluded by MCL 211.135(6)(e), so it moves through without the certificate. Start at the County Treasurer's Office first, then bring the certificate with the deed.

How can I search records or guard my title in Charlevoix County?

The county offers three search routes and a free fraud alert. Webtecs is the free portal for taxpayers and occasional users, and images can be bought document by document. Laredo Anywhere is a subscription service for people who run title searches regularly, and the office asks for an email to rod@charlevoixcounty.org to request an agreement. Tapestry is a web search that needs no subscription.

Homeowners can also enroll in Property Fraud Alert, which sends the owner an alert whenever a filing appears under their name. That helps after a sale too, since a seller can watch for a deed or lien appearing against a property they believed they had cleared.

How does Charlevoix County's housing stock look in federal data?

Charlevoix County is one of the pricier corners of northern Michigan. The Census Bureau counts 26,036 residents in 2025 and 18,026 housing units. Owners live in 83.5% of occupied homes, median rent is $949, and the typical household brings in $76,531 (five-year survey ending 2024).

In the 2020 count, 35.4% of housing units sat vacant, which points to plenty of seasonal and second homes. Builders took out 111 permits in 2025. Water covers 70% of the county's 1,390 square miles, and the 416 square miles of land make it the fourth smallest county in Michigan by land area, so waterfront parcels and island properties often carry details that the deed and title search have to capture accurately.

More questions about Charlevoix County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing charge for one deed in Charlevoix County?

One document costs $30.00 whatever its length. A tax certification adds $5.00 when the deed type calls for one, and a mailed document with no prepaid return envelope adds $3.00 for postage. Transfer tax is separate and follows the sale price.

Can the Charlevoix County office prepare my deed for me?

No. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from it, and the office keeps no blank deed forms. Have an attorney or the title agent prepare the deed first.

Do I need a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed in Charlevoix County?

Usually not. MCL 211.135(6)(e) exempts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty from the certificate rule. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and certain fiduciary deeds do need the County Treasurer's certification first.

How do I pay the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County sale?

Pay when you hand in the deed. The fee page asks that transfer tax and tax certification checks be made out to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds, and one check can cover them together with the recording fee. Rates are 55 cents (county) and $3.75 (state) per $500 slice.

Where can I buy a copy of a recorded Charlevoix deed?

Search the free Webtecs portal and buy the image, or ask the office. The fee page lists plain copies at $1.00 a page and certified copies at $5.00, so request the exact total on a long document.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • 870 South Main St, Rm 204, Cheboygan, MI 49721 (PO Box 70); Register of Deeds hours 8:30am-4:30pm Mon-Fri (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Which Cheboygan County office takes my deed?

Take it to the County Clerk/Register of Deeds in the county building, 870 South Main Street, Room 204, Cheboygan, MI 49721. Letters go to PO Box 70, and the main line is 231-627-8808. In Cheboygan County the clerk and the register of deeds are the same office, so the same counter handles court filings, marriage licenses and land records.

The Register of Deeds side keeps weekday hours that open at 8:30 in the morning and close at half past four, half an hour after the rest of the clerk's office starts. The county closes on a fixed list of holidays that includes Good Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, so a closing planned near those dates needs an earlier recording plan.

What is the Cheboygan County Register of Deeds responsible for?

It is the repository of official real property records for Cheboygan. The office page says any document that affects real property is recorded there, and it lists warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, wills, mortgages and divorces as examples.

After your sale, this is where the chain of title for the house continues. The county website also offers recording packets: a general recording requirements sheet, a warranty deed with recording requirements, a land contract form and a quit claim deed with recording requirements. Pull those sheets before a drafter starts work, because they show the layout the office expects.

  • Payment is accepted by cash, check and debit or credit card.
  • Coins above $5.00 are not accepted.
  • Card payments can be taken by phone for most services.

What should I bring when I take a deed to the Cheboygan County office?

Carry the signed original deed, payment for the fee and transfer tax, and any tax certificate the deed type needs. For a mailed package, add a return envelope and a note with a daytime phone number so staff can reach you about a problem.

  • The original deed with every signature and notary block complete.
  • A stated total value on the deed or an attached affidavit of value.
  • A check, cash or a card for the recording fee and the transfer tax.
  • The treasurer's certification if the deed carries warranty covenants.

The county was set off in 1840 from land that had belonged to Michilimackinac County, and the name Cheboygan comes from the river, though the precise meaning is no longer known. Mackinaw City, Tuscarora Township and the city of Cheboygan each run their own police departments, which is a reminder that most day to day local rules, from building permits to zoning, sit with the city, village or township rather than the county recording office.

How much is the recording fee in Cheboygan County?

State law puts the usual price of entering and recording a document at $30.00, with no extra charge for length. MCL 600.2567 also lists $3.00 for each added instrument on a multi-instrument assignment or discharge, $1.00 a page for copies and $5.00 to certify a recorded document.

A charter county may adopt its own schedule by ordinance, so confirm the total with the Cheboygan office before you write the check. Payment is expected on the day the document is left at the counter, with narrow exceptions for electronic filings and government agencies. A short call to 231-627-8808 gets the exact amount.

What will the state and county transfer tax add up to in Cheboygan County?

Both taxes run on the full sale price, counted in $500 steps with a partial step counted whole. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a step and MCL 207.525 sets the state rate at $3.75 a step.

Combined county and state transfer tax at sample prices, worked from the statutory rates
Sale price$500 unitsCounty taxState taxTotal
$100,000200$110$750$860
$192,500385$211.75$1,443.75$1,655.50
$300,000600$330$2,250$2,580

The middle row uses $192,500, which is the Census figure for the county's middle-priced home across the five-year survey ending 2024. The deed must print the total value, or carry an affidavit of value. When a sale bundles in a boat or furniture, stating real and personal values apart keeps the tax on the real property only.

Which deeds need a tax certificate in Cheboygan County?

A deed carrying warranty promises needs county treasurer certification first. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that the parcel's taxes are paid for the five years ahead of the deed date, plus a statement of any tax liens or titles.

Subsection (6)(e) excuses a quitclaim deed that has no warranty covenants, and subsection (6)(c) excuses a sheriff's deed from a court proceeding. If a deed is presented after March 1 and before the local treasurer has filed the current delinquent tax return, the certificate carries a note that the return was not available, and the register of deeds may not refuse the deed for that reason alone.

What formatting mistakes get a Cheboygan County deed rejected?

Mismatched names, missing addresses and cramped signature blocks cause most trouble. MCL 565.201 sets the rules that every Michigan register of deeds applies.

  • Each signer's name is printed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the name in the acknowledgment.
  • A notary's name is printed or stamped on the same page near the notary signature.
  • Every grantee's address appears on the deed, using the street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The person who drafted it is named, with a workplace address.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed or obscured.

A deed written in another language needs an English translation attached. A returned deed goes back to your drafter for repair.

What should a Cheboygan County seller know about the local housing picture?

Cheboygan County is big, thinly settled and full of seasonal homes. Its 885 square miles split into 715 of land and 170 of water, and the Census Bureau counts 35.8 residents per square mile.

The 2025 estimate is 25,793 people, and 30.6% of them are 65 or older. Owners hold 85.6% of homes, the middle rent is $773, and the typical household earns $62,875 (five-year survey ending 2024). The 2020 count found 36.0% of the 17,631 housing units vacant, and the Census lists 74 building permits for 2025. County government was organized in 1853 after a merger with the former Wyandot County.

How do I protect my Cheboygan County property from deed fraud?

Sign up for Property Activity Alert, a service that watches for recordings under your name. The office explains that it cannot stop fraud, but the alert warns an owner early so they can act. Call 231-627-8866 and the staff will enter your name and email address.

This is useful for sellers who keep another parcel in the county, and for anyone who inherited land and has not yet recorded a transfer into their own name.

More questions about Cheboygan County, MI Register of Deeds

When can I reach the Cheboygan register of deeds counter?

The Register of Deeds window runs Weekdays, opening at 8:30 and closing at half past four. Other clerk services start at 8:00. Closures follow the county holiday list, which includes Good Friday and the day after Thanksgiving.

Can I pay recording fees by card in Cheboygan County?

Yes. Cash, checks and debit or credit cards all work at the office, and most services can be paid by card over the phone. Coin payments above $5.00 are refused.

Is a quitclaim deed taxed differently in Cheboygan County?

A quitclaim deed does not need the treasurer's tax certificate, but transfer tax can still apply if money changes hands. MCL 207.505 exempts deeds that only confirm a title already held, and deeds with consideration under $100.

How is the county transfer tax calculated in Cheboygan County?

Divide the price by $500, round up, and multiply by $0.55. The state tax rounds the same way at $3.75. A $200,000 sale gives 400 steps, so $220 county tax and $1,500 state tax.

Does the Cheboygan office help me write a deed?

No. Hire an attorney or the title agent to draft it. The county posts a general recording requirements sheet and sample warranty and quit claim deed layouts that show what the register of deeds expects.

Who records deeds in Chippewa County

  • Chippewa County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee all documents $30.00; $3.00 per instrument for assignments/discharges of more than one; $5 treasurer tax certification for warranty clause docs (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Chippewa County?
We buy Chippewa County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where is the Chippewa County Register of Deeds?

The office is at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783. The state treasury directory lists the phone as 906-635-6312, the fax as 906-635-6855 and the email as rod@chippewacountymi.gov. Call ahead for counter hours, since none are posted on the land records site.

Chippewa County is in the eastern Upper Peninsula, and Sault Ste. Marie is the county seat. A seller on Drummond Island, in the Sault, or anywhere along the St. Marys River records the deed here. Mail works as well as a visit, as long as the document, the fee and the return envelope go in together.

How is Chippewa County organized, and who answers tax questions?

Chippewa County government was set up in 1826 and once reached across most of what is now the Upper Peninsula and parts of Minnesota. The Act of March 9, 1843 cut that vast area down, and the county now follows the Canadian border along the St. Marys River. Sault Ste. Marie anchors the Sault Ste. Marie micropolitan area, and Drummond Island is part of the county.

The county itself operates the jail, maintains rural roads, runs the major local courts and keeps the deed and mortgage records. Police, fire, building and zoning, tax assessment and street maintenance belong to the cities and townships. A seller with a question about an assessed value or a building permit therefore calls the local township or city office, not the register of deeds. The register of deeds answers questions about what has been recorded against the parcel, and it can tell you whether an older mortgage was ever discharged on the record before your buyer's lender asks.

  • Recording, indexing and copies: the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street.
  • Assessment and local zoning: the city or township where the house sits.
  • Tax certificates for warranty-type deeds: the treasurer offices named in MCL 211.135.

Why does a Chippewa County house sale end at the Register of Deeds?

Only a recording here puts the new deed into the county's land record. The office also holds the mortgages, discharges and liens that a title agent hunts for when clearing your title.

The online land records system shows how deep the file goes. Its indexes start on May 16, 1865, which gives a title examiner well over a century of names to search. Sellers who inherited a Chippewa County house can use that index to find the deed that put the family on title.

  • Guests search the index free of charge.
  • Members log in with a group, user ID and password, and login charges may apply.
  • PDF copies are bought by credit card after the search.

What do recording and copy charges look like in Chippewa County?

Under MCL 600.2567 the recording fee is $30.00 a document unless a charter county has adopted a different schedule. The same section prices copies at a dollar a page and certifying a recorded document at $5.00.

Chippewa County land record charges drawn from the statute and the online system
ServiceChargeWhere it comes from
Recording a document$30.00, any page countMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00 eachMCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Certifying a recorded document$5.00MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
Online PDF copy$1.00 per pageChippewa land records site
Online order fee$5.00 per orderChippewa land records site

Five dollars of the $30.00 is set aside for the register of deeds' automation fund. Send payment together with the deed, because the office wants it at the time of filing.

Which Chippewa County deeds escape transfer tax?

MCL 207.505 carves out a list of instruments, and a few of them come up often here. A mortgage or other security instrument is carved out. So is a lease, and so is a deed whose stated consideration is under $100.

  • A deed where the grantor is the federal government, the state or a local government.
  • A deed given to settle, or in place of foreclosing, a government-backed or insured loan.
  • A corrective deed that repairs a defect in title the buyer already holds.
  • A boundary-straightening deed when no money changes hands.
  • A transfer between husband and wife that sets up or dissolves an entireties tenancy.

Everything else owes the county 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 slice. Phone the office to learn which exemption, if any, fits your deed.

For a taxable sale, work it out on paper before closing. A house that sells at $161,900, the Census median value for the county, covers 324 slices of $500. County tax comes to $178.20 and state tax to $1,215.00, which makes $1,393.20 together. The deed has to show the full consideration, or an affidavit with the value goes on top of it, so the clerk can check your arithmetic.

What else must a Chippewa County deed carry besides the legal description?

MCL 565.201 requires details about the people named in the deed, and one missing item stops the recording. Every grantee's address must be printed, using the street number where street numbers are normal and a post office address where they are not.

Any Social Security number must have its first five digits removed or blacked out. A deed in a foreign language needs an English translation stapled on. Anything signed after January 1, 1964 must show who drafted it, with a business address. A notary's printed name belongs on the same page as the notary's signature.

Do I need a tax certificate to record a Chippewa County deed?

For most warranty-type deeds, yes. MCL 211.135 directs the office to demand certification that no taxes are unpaid for the five years preceding the deed, together with a statement of any liens or tax titles on the parcel.

Certificates come from the county treasurer and from the treasurer of the local city, village or township. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds are among the exceptions. Skipping the step is a misdemeanor for a register of deeds, with a fine up to $100, so the office does not bend on it.

How do Chippewa County homes measure up in the Census data?

By land area Chippewa is Michigan's second largest county, with 1,558 square miles of dry ground inside 2,698 total. It touches both Lake Huron and Lake Superior, and the Census puts density at only 23.6 residents per square mile.

The 2025 estimate is 36,081 people, down 1.9% from the 2020 base. Three of every four homes are owner-held (75.0%), and the middle rent is $797. A typical home is valued at $161,900, and a typical household takes in $62,217. The county has 20,556 housing units, and builders pulled 86 permits for them in 2025. In the 2020 count, 31.7% of units stood vacant and 27.5% of occupied homes were rented.

More questions about Chippewa County, MI Register of Deeds

What is Chippewa County's price to record one deed?

The state fee under MCL 600.2567 is $30.00 a document whatever the page count. Add transfer tax where it applies and any certification charge the treasurer sets. The office at 906-635-6312 can quote the final total.

Can I search Chippewa County land records for free?

Yes. Guests can search the online index at no charge. A PDF of a document is $1.00 a page plus a $5.00 online fee per order, paid by credit card.

How far back do the Chippewa County records go?

The online indexes begin May 16, 1865. The system posts its own index range and upload date on its welcome screen, so you can see how current it is before you search.

Is a mortgage subject to transfer tax in Chippewa County?

No. MCL 207.505 exempts instruments given as security, and an assignment or discharge of them. You pay the recording fee, but not the transfer tax, when you record a mortgage.

Who handles a recording problem with a Chippewa County deed?

Reach the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, phone 906-635-6312, email rod@chippewacountymi.gov. A question about what the deed should say belongs with an attorney or the title agent.

Which Harrison office takes a Clare County deed?

The combined County Clerk and Register of Deeds office sits at 255 W. Main Street, Harrison, MI 48625. Mail goes to PO Box 438. Reach staff at 989-539-7131 or by fax at 989-539-6616, and the county site gives clerk@clareco.net as the email address.

In Clare County one elected office holds both jobs, so the person who files circuit court papers and issues marriage licenses also keeps the land records. Harrison has been the county seat since 1877, when the seat moved from Farwell. A seller in Clare, Farwell, Harrison or any lake community around them sends the deed to the same counter. Phone first for counter hours.

How did Clare County and its records come about?

The Michigan Legislature created the county from part of Michilimackinac County in 1840 under the name Kaykakee County, and renamed it Clare County in 1843. A series of other counties administered it until its own government was organized in 1871. Farwell served as the first county seat before the seat moved to Harrison in 1877.

That history explains why older Clare County property descriptions may trace back through several jurisdictions. The county covers 564 square miles of land and is counted as part of both Northern and Central Michigan. The Clare-Gladwin Regional Education Service District serves students in the county, and the county is served by several public school districts, so a buyer's questions about schools go to the district the house sits in.

As in other Michigan counties, the county records deeds and mortgages, while cities and townships handle tax assessment, building and zoning, and street maintenance. Ask the township or city office about assessments, and ask the Harrison office about what is on the record.

Wooded acreage and lake cottages make up much of the housing stock around Harrison and Farwell, and the Census counted 22,209 housing units in the county in 2025 against 12,521 households. That gap tells a seller that many neighbors are part-year owners, which can matter when a deed has several co-owners who sign in different states. Each signer's printed name must match the acknowledgment, so gather every signature page before the package goes to the recorder.

What does the Clare County Register of Deeds handle in a home sale?

It records the deed that moves ownership to your buyer and the mortgage that goes with it. The same office holds earlier deeds, land contracts, discharges and liens, so a title search on a Clare County house begins and ends in these books.

The county's homepage also lists the clerk as the official abstractor, a role that matters when a seller needs a title history on an older parcel. Clare County sits among large state forests, and a seller with an older wooded parcel can ask for the deed history early so closing is not held up.

  • Bring the original signed deed, not a photocopy.
  • Include the fee, a return envelope and any certificate the deed type requires.
  • Keep a copy of the recording stamp for your closing file.

What does Clare County bill for recording a deed?

The base charge set by Michigan is $30.00 a document, with page count irrelevant. MCL 600.2567 sends $5.00 of that fee into the register of deeds' automation fund and adds $3.00 for each additional instrument an assignment or discharge covers.

Copies run a dollar a page and a certification is $5.00. A requested records search costs 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 floor, and filing some other paper is $1.00. Charter counties may use a different schedule, so verify the total with the Clare office by phone.

How is Michigan transfer tax shown on a Clare County deed?

The deed must print the total value of the real property, or an affidavit of value goes with it. Both the county act (MCL 207.504) and the state act (MCL 207.525) say so.

With the value printed, the arithmetic is short. The county takes 55 cents and the state takes $3.75 on every $500 slice of price, partial slices counted whole. A $133,800 sale, which matches the Census median home value in Clare County, spans 268 slices: $147.40 for the county and $1,005 for the state. If real and personal property sell together, naming each value separately confines the tax to the real property. Ask the office how it collects the tax so payment arrives with the deed.

What belongs on page one of a Clare County deed?

The first printed line must name the recordable event in a single statement, such as warranty deed or quit claim deed. MCL 565.201 bars recording an instrument signed after April 1, 1997 when that statement points to more than one event.

  • Keep 2.5 inches clear at the head of page one.
  • Keep half an inch clear on every other side, on every page.
  • Print in 10-point type or larger, black ink, on white stock of 20-pound weight or more.
  • Attach nothing that falls outside letter or legal dimensions.

Once an instrument is received and recorded, the statute presumes it complies, so a clean first page protects you later.

When does a Clare County deed need treasurer certification?

A deed that conveys title with warranty covenants, and a land contract, needs county treasurer certification under MCL 211.135. The certificate says whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirms payment of the taxes for the five years that precede the deed.

If the register of deeds refuses to receive a deed for lack of certificates, the office notes that fact on the instrument, and the person presenting it must obtain the certificate before trying again. Plan for that trip to the treasurer when you are scheduling a closing, because the deed cannot be recorded without it.

What do Census figures say about Clare County homes?

Clare County is a lower-priced market. The table lists the Census Bureau's figures.

Clare County at a glance, from federal survey data

Housing units, 2025 estimate22,209
Share of homes held by owners86.9%
Median home value$133,800
Median gross rent$765
Median household income$49,384
Building permits, 202523

Population rose 2.2% from the 2020 base to the 2025 estimate. In the 2020 count, 39.1% of the 21,818 housing units stood vacant. Workers spend 29.9 minutes getting to work on average, the longest commute among the four counties compared, and the county is nearly all land, with 564 square miles of ground and 11 of water. A typical home sells for less here than in the lakefront counties to the north.

More questions about Clare County, MI Register of Deeds

Is the Clare County Register of Deeds a separate office from the clerk?

No. The County Clerk and Register of Deeds offices are combined in Clare County, and both operate from 255 W. Main Street in Harrison.

How do I phone the Clare County office?

Dial 989-539-7131, or fax 989-539-6616. Letters go to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Ask about counter hours before you deliver a deed.

What is the standard recording fee in Clare County?

The statutory fee is $30.00 per document, long or short. Add $3.00 for each extra instrument on an assignment or discharge, and $5.00 if you want a certified copy.

How do I figure the transfer tax on a Clare County sale?

Divide the price by $500, round up, then multiply by $0.55 for the county and by $3.75 for the state. A $150,000 sale is 300 slices, so $165 county tax plus $1,125 state tax, or $1,290 together.

Can I mail a deed to the Clare County Register of Deeds?

Yes. Send the signed original, the exact fee and a return envelope to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Confirm the amount by phone first so the deed is not held for a short payment.

  • Clinton County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • 100 E State Street Suite 2500, St. Johns, MI 48879; 989-224-5270; hours Mon-Fri 8-noon and 1-5 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Online records via vendor domain clintoncountymi-recorder.tylerhost.net (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

  • Clinton County MI sheriff Facebook post on Sept 1 / March 1 halves was not used (not clearly MI treasurer source)

Clinton County by the numbers

Clinton County ranks 25 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 79,419 people in 33,123 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $243,700, the median home value sits 30% above the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Clinton County reports $85,928. Owner-occupancy is 83%, so renters hold about 17% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1981, about 42 years ago.

Where in Clinton County are deeds filed?

Head for the courthouse at the county seat. The land records for Clinton County are kept by an office that combines the county clerk and the register of deeds, found at 100 E State Street, Suite 2500, with a phone line at 989-224-5270.

The doors are open on weekdays from eight until noon, then again from one until five. Staff ask that you walk in by 4:30 so a transaction is not rushed at closing time, and holiday schedules can shift. Passport services run from the same office by appointment only.

Do not expect the counter to help you write anything. Employees do not prepare or alter documents, do not give legal advice, and keep no blank deeds in stock. For a sale, a title company or attorney writes the deed and sends it over.

What will recording a Clinton County deed cost me?

Thirty dollars flat, whatever the page count. The same figure covers a mortgage or a lis pendens, and the county's recording fees page repeats it next to the add-ons below.

Charges the Clinton County office may add to a closing package
ItemChargeSource
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30 eachMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Release or assignment naming extra instruments$3 per extra instrument namedMCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Stamp certifying a recorded paper$5MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
Photocopy$1 a pageMCL 600.2567(1)(c)
Treasurer's tax certificate$5 for 25 descriptions, 20 cents more for each beyondClinton County Register of Deeds

If you ask staff to search the index for you, the statutory rate is fifty cents per year covered, never less than $5.

Which formatting mistakes get a Clinton County deed sent back?

The county posts a sixteen-point checklist drawn from Michigan's recording statutes, and the office will look over a draft before you file it. Common reasons for rejection, in the county's own words, are an incorrect fee, no drafter named, names not typed under the signatures, a male grantor's marital status left out, and an unfinished notary block.

  • Page one needs a blank band 2.5 inches deep along its top, and a half-inch gutter elsewhere.
  • Use black ink, type at 10 points or larger, and white paper of at least 20-pound weight cut to letter or legal dimensions.
  • Open the first printed line with a statement naming the single event the paper records, such as a warranty deed. A paper that combines two events is refused.
  • List every party's street address, and put the drafter's name and address on the instrument.
  • Truncate any Social Security number to its final four digits.
  • Lift the legal description from the previous deed or a fresh survey instead of the abbreviated wording on an assessment notice.

A survivor deed must come with a certified death certificate, unless the certificate is already recorded and the deed cites its liber and page. A court order has to arrive as a certified copy bearing the court clerk's seal.

Who owes transfer tax on a Clinton County sale, and how much?

The seller does, in two layers. State layer: $3.75. County layer: 55 cents. Each is charged on every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts as a whole one (MCL 207.504 and 207.523).

Work it through for a $250,000 house. That price holds 500 slices, so the state takes $1,875 and the county $275, for $2,150 total. Typically the title company deducts it from the seller's proceeds. Fifteen days after the deed is delivered is the statutory deadline, and the county treasurer is the collector.

  • Outside both taxes: any deed carrying less than $100 of value, and deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Outside the state tax only: foreclosure transfers and deeds in lieu, plus conveyances down a family line to a child or grandchild (MCL 207.526).
  • The county statute lists no family exemption of its own, so ask the register how the county layer is treated on a family transfer.

Print any exemption claim on the deed itself. If none appears, the clerk charges the tax at the window.

When does a Clinton County deed need the treasurer's certificate?

Any time the instrument is a warranty deed, a land contract, or a land contract assignment with a warranty clause. Under MCL 211.135 the register may not record those papers until the county treasurer has certified the parcel's tax status.

It looks back five years from the date on the instrument and flags tax liens or tax titles. A quitclaim without warranty covenants skips the step. For a seller who is behind on taxes, request a payoff letter from the Clinton County Treasurer early, so the balance can be paid at closing and the certificate comes back without a lien.

What does the Clinton County housing picture look like?

This is Lansing's northern commuter belt. QuickFacts values the typical owner-occupied house at $259,500, with $88,210 as the typical household income. Owners live in 82.2% of occupied homes. Renters pay $1,092 at the median, and the county issued 197 building permits during 2025.

The county dates to 1831, was organized in 1839 and honors DeWitt Clinton. It spans 566 square miles of land and holds the cities of St. Johns, DeWitt, and parts of Ovid, Lansing, East Lansing and Grand Ledge. Interstate 69 crosses the south, US 127 passes through St. Johns and DeWitt, and M-21 links Fowler, St. Johns and Ovid.

The 2020 count was 79,128 people. By July 2025 it was estimated at 80,432, a 1.6% rise. Residents tend to stay: 89.7% lived at the same address a year earlier, which means a house for sale often draws buyers from outside the neighborhood rather than from next door.

Why does Clinton County's growth matter to a seller?

Growth is the story here. The county counted 37,969 people in 1960, 57,883 in 1990 and 75,382 in 2010 before reaching 79,128 in 2020. Most of that came as Lansing's suburbs pushed north, and DeWitt Township holds Capital Region International Airport, just off I-69.

Statistically the county is part of the Lansing-East Lansing metro area. The 2020 census put 48.7% of residents in urban areas and 51.3% in rural ones. Census-designated places such as Bath, Eureka, Lake Victoria and Wacousta sit alongside the cities, so a Clinton County address can mean anything from a subdivision lot near DeWitt to farmland beyond St. Johns.

Those differences matter at sale time. A house on a rural parcel may involve a private well and septic system, a legal description that spans acreage, and a survey, while a city lot usually comes with a short platted description. In either case the register of deeds only needs the recorded instrument to meet the format list above. Education and work figures from QuickFacts: 95.3% of adults hold a high school diploma, 35.4% a bachelor's degree, and 63.8% of people 16 and older are in the labor force.

What happens at closing when a Clinton County owner sells for cash?

The paperwork matches a financed sale. The closing agent submits the signed deed to the register with the $30 fee, adds a treasurer's certificate if the deed warrants title, and attaches either the transfer tax or the exemption wording.

Before you sign, ask who is ordering the certificate, whether the deed recites the full price or relies on a valuation affidavit, and what exemption, if any, is claimed. If you mail originals yourself, enclose a stamped return envelope so the recorded deed comes back to you.

One more errand sits outside the register's counter. Within 45 days, the buyer sends the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit. A seller who claimed the principal residence exemption files to end it effective on the closing date.

More questions about Clinton County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is the Clinton County filing fee for a deed?

Thirty dollars, charged per document. Expect an extra $5 for the treasurer's certificate on a warranty deed, which covers up to 25 legal descriptions.

Who is liable for transfer tax when a house in St. Johns or DeWitt sells?

The seller. The statutes name the grantor as the liable party, and the title company usually withholds the tax from what the seller receives.

Will courthouse staff prepare my deed?

No. They review drafts against the recording rules but leave the writing to an attorney, a lender or a title company.

Can I drop off a deed over the lunch hour?

Not in person. The office shuts from noon to one on weekdays. Phone 989-224-5270 to check holiday schedules.

Why did the register send my deed back?

The usual culprits are a wrong fee, a missing drafter name, signatures with no typed names beneath, a half-finished notary block, thin margins, or two recordable events on one paper.

Which office handles Crawford County deeds?

The Register of Deeds Office at 200 W. Michigan Avenue in Grayling takes every deed for land in the county. Crawford County is among the 31 Michigan counties that merge the clerk's job with the register's, and the register's line is (989) 348-2841.

Walk-ins are welcome without an appointment, weekdays from 8:00 until 4:30, with a closure for lunch between 12:00 and 1:00. The counter takes cash, checks, money orders and cards, and cards add a service charge.

Mail works too. Send the document, a return envelope with postage, and a check or money order made out to Crawford County or Crawford County ROD. Three vendors handle e-recording here: CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile. Only Simplifile can submit a paper that needs the treasurer's certification, so a home sale deed usually goes through that one.

What are the Crawford County register's fees?

One flat $30 covers any document, however many pages. The register's page credits Public Acts 224 through 232 of 2016, in force since October 1, 2016, and notes that $4 of each fee feeds the state's survey and remonumentation fund.

Crawford County register charges that often show up in a house sale
ServiceAmount
Recording, any document$30.00
Extra instrument on a release or assignment$3.00 apiece
Treasurer's certification before a warranty deed is recorded$5.00
Certifying a recorded copy$5.00
Paper copies$1.00 a page
Tapestry online search$8.95 each name or legal description

Fold the $5 certification into the same payment as the recording fee. The treasurer does not need a second check.

How is transfer tax calculated for a Crawford County sale?

Divide the price into $500 slices, round a partial slice up, and multiply: $3.75 per slice for the state, 55 cents per slice for the county. The register posts both rates, and MCL 207.504 backs the county figure for counties under 2,000,000 people.

Try $160,000. That is 320 slices, giving $1,200 to the state and $176 to the county, $1,376 combined. The example is not far from the $163,000 median owner-occupied value that QuickFacts reports here.

  • The seller carries the bill, and the stamps must be bought in Crawford County itself.
  • Land that straddles a county line needs the price allocated between the counties, with each one taxed on its share.
  • Show the full consideration on the deed, or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which costs nothing to file.
  • Write any exemption into the deed. Examples: value under $100, foreclosure transfers, and quitclaims that merely repair a title defect.

Michigan's state act, MCL 207.526, also exempts gifts to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The county act's list holds no such item, so ask Grayling how the county portion is handled.

When does the Crawford County Treasurer have to certify a deed?

Four kinds of paper need it: warranty deeds, other deeds that include a warranty covenant, land contracts, and land contract assignments with warranty wording. MCL 211.135 tells the register to hold such papers until the certificate arrives.

The treasurer sits at the same address, 200 W. Michigan Ave, on the same weekday schedule, and answers at (989) 344-3231. The certificate reports liens and tax titles and confirms five years of paid taxes. Quitclaims lacking warranty covenants are exempt.

Delinquent taxes in the county moved to a new payment platform on November 4, 2025, offering online payment, text-to-pay, digital wallets, ACH and autopay, all with fees. Request a payoff figure first, then choose the closing date. The treasurer's page also described a class action settlement over surplus proceeds from tax foreclosure auctions held from 2013 to 2020, whose claims deadline of July 16, 2026 has passed.

What sets Crawford County apart for a seller?

Land ownership does. Of roughly 360,000 acres, over three quarters belong to the State of Michigan, the U.S. Forest Service or the Department of Military Affairs. The county has six townships and one city, Grayling, which is its only incorporated community, and its water drains toward the Au Sable, Manistee and Muskegon rivers.

QuickFacts counted 12,988 residents in 2020 and 13,722 by July 2025, a 5.7% rise from a small base. Only 23.3 people live on each square mile. Seniors make up 28.6% of the population, owners occupy 79.6% of occupied homes, rent is $862 at the median, and builders took out 27 permits in 2025.

The area began as Shawono County in 1840 and took its present name in 1843, and local government formed in 1879. Logging ended in the 1800s and tourism, built on trout fishing in the Au Sable, took over. Household income here has a median of $60,392 and 14.4% of residents fall below the poverty line.

What do Crawford County's history and daily life say about its homes?

Fishing put Grayling on the map in the 1870s. Anglers came for the Michigan grayling in the Au Sable, and the county's weekly paper, the Crawford County Avalanche, opened in 1879 with a fishing story on page one. The native grayling disappeared by century's end, overfishing, logging damage and introduced brown trout all taking a toll, and the river now holds brown and rainbow trout.

A 1912 regional history described the Michigan Central railroad as the main transport line and noted a Detroit and Charlevoix line reaching Frederic, in the northwest.

QuickFacts lists 1,196 veterans, 89.9% of households with broadband, and a labor force participation rate of 49.5%. The mean commute is 25.7 minutes, longer than in Delta County. Be ready to describe internet service at the property when a buyer asks.

How can a Crawford County owner guard against deed fraud?

Sign up for the register's free alert service. It sends an email or phone notice when a document is filed under your name, which is the fastest way to learn that someone has recorded a bogus deed against your property.

The office's files reach back to 1879. It keeps an image of each document rather than the original deed, which is stamped with a liber number after recording. Visitors can search on public computers at the counter, and Tapestry (occasional users) and Laredo (subscribers) offer remote search.

Staff will not draft documents or answer legal questions. They point owners toward a real property attorney, a title company, or a blank deed from an office supply store, with a warning that forms found online might not satisfy Michigan's format rules.

What belongs on a Crawford County pre-closing checklist?

Before the deed travels to Grayling, run through these points with your closing agent.

  • Does the deed warrant title? If so, order the treasurer's certification.
  • Who buys the transfer tax stamps, and for what amount?
  • Does the legal description copy the previous deed, and does the deed name its drafter with an address?
  • Are delinquent taxes outstanding, and will proceeds clear them?
  • Is the transfer paperwork headed to the local assessor, along with a rescission of any principal residence exemption effective on closing day?

Rural parcels raise extra questions about wells, septic systems and private roads. Those belong with the county's health and road authorities, because the register of deeds only deals with the recorded paper.

More questions about Crawford County, MI Register of Deeds

What does it cost to file a Crawford County deed?

Thirty dollars flat. A warranty deed also needs the treasurer's $5 certification, and a release that names several instruments adds $3 for each additional one.

What transfer tax rates apply in Crawford County?

The seller pays $3.75 to the state and 55 cents to the county for each $500 slice of price, with stamps bought in Crawford County itself.

Does the Grayling register close for lunch?

Yes, daily from 12:00 to 1:00. Otherwise the counter serves walk-ins on weekdays until 4:30, no appointment needed.

Can a deed be e-recorded in Crawford County?

Yes, through CSC, Indecomm or Simplifile. Simplifile is the one the county names for papers needing tax certification.

Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim?

Not when the quitclaim has no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts do need it under MCL 211.135.

Where in Delta County are deeds recorded?

Everything goes through Escanaba. The Register of Deeds works from the county building at 310 Ludington Street, open from eight to four, and the county line is (906) 789-5100, with a fax at (906) 789-5179.

That holds whether the house stands in Escanaba, in Gladstone, in the village of Garden, or out in a township near Rapid River or Rock. The county's own register page is brief, so phone ahead about anything unusual, bring the original signed deed and the fee, and ask whether cards are accepted.

Delta County lies on the Upper Peninsula's Lake Michigan side, and the Wisconsin line runs through the water to its south. Menominee County borders it to the southwest, Marquette to the northwest, Alger to the north and Schoolcraft to the east.

What fee schedule does the Delta County register follow?

The statewide schedule in MCL 600.2567, which applies unless a charter county sets its own. Under it a deed is $30 to record whatever the page count.

Fees from MCL 600.2567 as they apply to an Escanaba closing
ServiceFee
Recording one document$30.00

Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00
