Filing another paper$1.00

Pay when you hand the document over. The statute lets a document that is both filed and paid for electronically settle within one business day, so ask whether the office accepts e-recording and from which vendors.

What transfer tax comes out of a Delta County seller's proceeds?

Two charges: $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500 slice of price, a partial slice counting as whole. MCL 207.504 sets the county charge, and MCL 207.523 puts liability on the seller.

A $150,000 sale sits just below the $157,100 median owner-occupied value on QuickFacts. It holds 300 slices, so the state share is $1,125 and the county share $165, a $1,290 total. The county treasurer collects, and the clock runs 15 days from the buyer's receipt of the deed.

  • State tax does not apply to transfers under $100, instruments given as security, land contracts that hold back title until paid, or conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • If tax was paid on a sale that later proves to have qualified for an exemption, the seller, or a buyer who paid for the seller, may request a refund from the Department of Treasury.
  • The deed must state its value, or an affidavit declaring the value must travel with it.

The county statute, MCL 207.505, carries a shorter exemption list. A family transfer can therefore escape the state share and still owe the county share, so ask the register before you sign.

Which Delta County deeds need a treasurer's certificate?

Most sale deeds do. Under MCL 211.135 the register must hold a deed, plat or land contract until the treasurer certifies tax liens and tax titles and confirms that five years of taxes are paid.

Quitclaims and other conveyances without warranty covenants are excused, as are sheriff's deeds and some state tax deeds. On the county's treasurer page, the office describes itself as keeper of county money and collector of delinquent property taxes, certifier of deeds and operator of the annual tax sale for the State Treasury.

Ask the treasurer what the certificate costs and how quickly it is issued before you pick a closing date. If back taxes exist, obtain a written payoff so they can be satisfied from the seller's proceeds.

Which records does the Delta County Equalization office sell?

Title agents and appraisers lean on it. A price list effective April 10, 2026 shows a $5 Equalization Report, a $15 Apportionment Report listing millage rates, and $15 for taxable value broken out by school district or township.

The rest of the list: database copies at $1 a page, simple maps at $2, top-taxpayer lists at $15, miscellaneous totals and statistics at $25, and a digital copy of the current assessment roll at $2,000. Owner names and addresses and current assessed and equalized values are among the data the office keeps.

A single house is different. For its assessed and taxable value, contact the assessor in the city or township where it sits. A buyer estimating the first tax bill will want those two numbers and the millage rate.

What does QuickFacts say about Delta County homes and residents?

The median owner-occupied house is valued at $157,100, rent at the median is $692, and household income at the median is $57,809. Owners live in 82.0% of occupied homes. Poverty touches 12.1% of residents, and 28.2% of people are 65 or older.

Delta spans 1,991 square miles, though 820 are water. Its 1,171 square miles of land make it Michigan's fifth-largest county by that measure. It had 36,903 people in 2020 and an estimated 36,582 in July 2025, a 0.9% slide. Its census-day population peaked at 38,947 in 1980.

US 2 runs along the southern tier and US 41 climbs the middle and hugs the shore. M-35, M-69 and M-183 branch off, the last serving the Garden Peninsula and Fayette State Park. Hiawatha National Forest takes in part of the county, and Delta County Airport, southwest of Escanaba, offers scheduled service to Detroit and Minneapolis. Recreation and forest products anchor the economy, and the 2022 receipts of health care and social assistance firms came to about $234 million.

How did Delta County come to look the way it does?

The name is a geometry lesson. The county was surveyed in 1843 and organized in 1861, and it takes its name from the Greek letter delta because the original county was triangular, with pieces that later went to Menominee, Dickinson, Iron and Marquette counties.

Growth came fast once logging and shipping arrived. Delta had 1,172 residents in 1860, 6,812 in 1880 and 23,881 by 1900, then passed 30,000 by 1910. The count has stayed between about 31,000 and 39,000 since 1920. Soils here support hay, corn, small grains, potatoes and strawberries, which is why some Delta parcels are farms rather than house lots.

For a seller the practical upshot is variety. A lakeside cottage near Escanaba, a house in Gladstone and forty acres near Garden call for different disclosures, surveys and legal descriptions, but all three travel to the same counter on Ludington Street for recording.

What formatting does a Delta County deed need?

Michigan applies a single recording format everywhere, found in MCL 565.201 and summarized on the Clinton County recording page. Expect Delta County to enforce the same items.

  • Ink signatures, with the name printed beneath each, and names that agree from body to notary block.
  • Street addresses for each party, plus who drafted the deed and where they can be reached.
  • An acknowledgment by a notary, judge or court clerk for a deed signed in Michigan.
  • A blank 2.5 inches at the head of page one for the recorder's stamp.
  • No more than four trailing digits of a Social Security number.

Counter staff neither write deeds nor give legal advice. For an inherited house, ask the title company whether a death certificate or court order must be recorded ahead of the deed.

More questions about Delta County, MI Register of Deeds

How much does the Delta County register charge to record a deed?

Thirty dollars a document, per MCL 600.2567. A release naming several instruments adds $3 for each extra, and certifying a recorded paper costs $5.

Who pays transfer tax on a Delta County house sale?

The seller does. The state rate is $3.75 and the county rate 55 cents for every $500 slice, payable to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

Do deeds for Gladstone and Garden homes go to Escanaba?

Yes. The register at 310 Ludington Street records for the entire county, including both cities and the village.

Is a quitclaim deed exempt from the treasurer's certificate in Delta County?

Yes, when it has no warranty covenants. A warranty deed or land contract must carry the certificate before the register will accept it.

What are the register's hours in Escanaba?

The county lists eight to four. Telephone (906) 789-5100 to confirm holiday closures.

Eaton County by the numbers

Eaton County ranks 19 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 109,000 people in 47,650 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $206,700, the median home value sits 10% above the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Eaton County reports $78,025.

What does the Eaton County Register of Deeds actually do?

Eaton County's register keeps the county's land title file: deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and any other paper that touches real estate between Charlotte, Grand Ledge, Eaton Rapids and the townships around them. Each filing is checked against Michigan's recording rules and then stored as a digital image.

Nobody at the counter will write a deed for you. The county page puts responsibility for wording and purpose on the person who prepared the paper, and it sends legal questions to an attorney. If a deed still has to be written, a title company or real estate lawyer can do it, and the signed original comes here afterward.

The counter opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, with the staff away from noon until 1:00. Courthouse holidays interrupt that schedule, as the notice about Veterans Day on the register's page shows. Anything sent by mail should include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, because the office requires one before it sends documents back.

What does it cost to file papers in Charlotte?

A flat $30 covers each deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified real estate copy. The extras are itemized on the county's fees page.

Eaton County register charges, copied from the posted schedule
ItemCharge
Filing one deed, mortgage or similar paper$30
Each further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges$3 each
Tax certificate, first 25 legal descriptions$5
Each description past that$0.20
Ordinary copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 a page
Certified copy of a recorded document$1 a page plus $5 for the seal

The website does not sell certified copies. Ask at the counter or write to the office.

When does a deed need the treasurer's certificate?

A warranty deed, a land contract or an assignment of one cannot go on the record until the county treasurer's office has certified the parcel. The county cites MCL 211.135, which wants proof that nobody holds a tax lien or tax title on the land and that five years of taxes before the instrument date are settled.

The statute excuses quitclaim deeds and other conveyances without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds. Closers usually order the certificate while escrow is open, so sellers seldom chase it themselves.

  • The treasurer's certificate stapled to a warranty deed or land contract.
  • The full price printed on the deed, or a value affidavit attached.
  • An addressed envelope with postage when the package travels by mail.
  • The $30 filing charge plus $5 for the certificate where one is required.

Incomplete packages return to the sender, which can delay a closing by days. A parcel with unpaid taxes does not get a clean certificate until the balance is cleared.

How much Michigan transfer tax does an Eaton County seller owe?

Two levies attach to the deed. The state's is $3.75 on every $500 slice of price (MCL 207.525). The county's is 55 cents on each slice, the rate for counties below two million residents (MCL 207.504). A fraction of a slice counts as a whole one.

Both fall on the grantor (MCL 207.502 and 207.523). The treasurer must receive the state portion within 15 days of the deed changing hands.

A sale at $216,900, the median value QuickFacts reports for Eaton County, works out to 434 slices. That means $1,627.50 to the state and $238.70 to the county, $1,866.20 in all. A purchase contract can push the cost onto the buyer, yet the statute still names the seller.

Which Eaton County transfers owe nothing?

Michigan excuses many transfers, as long as the instrument says which exemption applies. The county list is MCL 207.505 and the state list is MCL 207.526. Most entries match, apart from the family item at the end.

  • Price below $100.
  • Mortgages and other security papers, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Leases and leasehold transfers.
  • Court orders that move title without naming a price.
  • Quitclaim deeds fixing a flaw in title the grantee already holds.
  • Land contracts until legal title actually passes.
  • State tax only: a gift deed running from parent to child or stepchild, or grandparent to grandchild.

If tax was paid on a deal that qualified, MCL 207.523(4) lets the seller, or a buyer who paid in the seller's place, ask the state Department of Treasury for the money back.

How far back can you search Eaton County land records?

The search link on the register's page reaches every record from 1836 up to the most recent proof date, so a whole chain of title can be traced from home. A link for electronic filing sits beside it.

Electronic filing lets a title company submit the signed deed the same day with no courier. Ask your closer whether the file goes in that way and when the recorded copy will reach you. Money owed on a parcel is a separate matter, and the county treasurer runs its own search for it.

What is the Eaton County landscape like?

Eaton County covers 579 square miles, 575 of them land, beside Ingham County, and part of the city of Lansing falls inside its lines. Lawmakers organized it on December 29, 1837 and named it for John H. Eaton, a secretary of war under President Jackson. Charlotte holds the courthouse. Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet and Potterville are the other cities.

Interstates 69, 96 and 496 run through the county, joined by M-43, M-50 and M-99. Fitch H. Beach Airport in Charlotte handles general aviation, while airline service is at Capital Region International Airport across the line in Clinton County. Eleven school districts serve it, among them Charlotte, Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet, Potterville, Maple Valley, Bellevue and Waverly, and a few edges send children to schools in neighboring counties. The road commission looks after more than 1,170 miles of county roads, most of them outside city limits.

  • QuickFacts lists 109,581 residents as of July 2025 and 48,090 housing units.
  • About three in four homes are lived in by their owners, 74.2% to be exact.
  • Median household income is $79,597 across 45,428 households.
  • Half of renters pay at least $1,092 a month.

What happens when Eaton County taxes go unpaid?

Delinquent bills are the county treasurer's job, and the same office is the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay behind. Its page says over 2,000 foreclosures have been prevented since 2016 and links a chart of Michigan's foreclosure deadlines.

Payment can be made online once the parcel number and amount are found in the county's tax search. A 2.49% fee applies to cards, and parcels inside Lansing use their own link. A county land bank deals with vacant and foreclosed property.

An owner in that spot can still sell. The payoff comes out of the sale money, and the treasurer's certificate tells the closer what must clear first.

More questions about Eaton County, MI Register of Deeds

Where is a deed filed in Eaton County?

At the Register of Deeds in Charlotte, the county seat. The register's page on eatoncounty.org gives the counter location. Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:30, except for the noon hour.

How much does Eaton County ask for a filing?

It is $30 for each document. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments adds $3 per extra instrument, and a tax certificate is $5 for 25 descriptions or fewer.

Can an Eaton County deed be filed online?

Yes, through the e-record link on the register's page. Paper filings by mail need a stamped envelope addressed back to the sender.

Who pays the transfer tax on an Eaton County sale?

The seller, by statute. A purchase agreement can assign the cost to the buyer. The state share reaches the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

How old are the records online?

They start in 1836 and run to the latest proof date. Certified copies are not sold on the website, so contact the register's office for those.

Where are Emmet County deeds recorded?

Emmet County's Register of Deeds works from 200 Division Street, Suite 150, in Petoskey, MI 49770, and answers at 231-348-1761. Every deed for land in the county, from Harbor Springs to Pellston, ends up in this one office.

It handles more than 240 kinds of paper, including deeds, mortgages with their assignments and discharges, land contracts, leases, liens, probate orders, condominium documents and plats. The register also chairs the county plat board, which reviews new subdivisions.

Land records start in 1852. Images exist from that year forward, yet the name index only runs from 1922 on, with earlier years being added a little at a time. For older searches the county invites people in to use the index books at the counter.

What are the fees at the Petoskey recording counter?

Recording starts at $30 per document, collected at the counter by cash or check only. The register's page supplies the remaining numbers.

Emmet County register fee schedule, taken from the county's posted fee list
ServiceFee
Entering and recording any document$30
Warranty deeds, land contracts, covenant deeds and similar$35
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3 per instrument
Certification of a document$5

The $35 line applies to any deed carrying a warrant or covenant clause, and the $5 tax certification has to be added to that payment. By mail, write the check to the Emmet County Register of Deeds.

What makes an Emmet County filing bounce?

Every filing is measured against Michigan's recording statutes, and anything short is mailed back. The county prints the rules with citations. These entries cause the most returns.

  • Signatures have to be originals with typed names under them, and the notary block must repeat those names exactly.
  • Keep a clear band of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch along every other edge.
  • Type in black ink, 10-point or bigger, on white stock of at least 20 pounds, cut anywhere from letter size to 8.5 by 14.
  • Put the name and address of whoever drafted the paper on anything signed in Michigan.
  • Show nothing beyond the final four digits of a Social Security number.
  • One instrument may cover only one recordable event.
  • Court orders come certified with the clerk's seal. A survivorship deed needs a certified death certificate recorded already.

Pack a return envelope with the filing. A paper is usually recorded the day it arrives, held for a day and mailed back the next business day, unless the title company or lender asked for something else.

How does Emmet County figure Michigan transfer tax?

Michigan layers two taxes on the price. The state takes $3.75 for every $500 or part of $500 (MCL 207.525), and a county with under two million residents takes 55 cents on the same measure (MCL 207.504). The deed has to show the whole price, or carry an attached affidavit of value.

The register's downloads include a transfer tax table, a list of exemptions and a state refund application. Under MCL 207.502 and 207.523 the seller carries the bill.

Take $315,700, the QuickFacts median for Emmet County. It spans 632 slices of $500, which gives $2,370.00 for the state and $347.60 for the county, or $2,717.60 combined. Gifts running from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild escape the state tax under MCL 207.526, so long as the instrument states it.

Why does the recording order matter under Michigan law?

Under Michigan's race-notice system, as the Emmet County register puts it, a recorded deed warns every later buyer, and papers rank in the order they were first handed in. First in time, first in line.

After closing, the deed and the buyer's mortgage should go straight to the register, since a delay lets a later filing cut ahead. Title companies know this and typically file the same day. In a private sale you would carry the deed in yourself or use an e-recording provider the county names: CSC, EPN or Simplifile.

The county page carries a ROD Alert about outside companies that offer certified copies of a deed for $50 or more. Copies cost as little as $1 a page at the register, and the office asks residents to call 231-348-1761 before paying a third party.

Can you search Emmet County records without paying?

Yes, after a free registration. Searches work by liber and page, by name or by document type, and a low-resolution preview shows before you pay $1.05 a page by card for a copy. The county also runs Fraud Notify, which sends an email each time a paper is recorded in your name.

Tax details sit in a separate property search on the county website that accepts a name, an address or a parcel number. Anyone buying or inheriting a house here should run both searches.

What sets the Emmet County market apart from other counties?

Emmet County sits at the tip of the Lower Peninsula, with Lake Michigan to the west and the Straits of Mackinac to the north. It measures 882 square miles, but only 467 are land. Little Traverse Bay and the inland lakes account for the other 47%. Petoskey holds the county seat and is the biggest city. Harbor Springs is the second city, with the Tunnel of Trees scenic stretch of M-119 running north of it, and the villages are Alanson, Pellston and part of Mackinaw City.

QuickFacts gives a quick read on the people and housing:

  • 15,190 households, with owners occupying 77.0% of the homes.
  • A median household income of $78,112.
  • 28.5% of residents past age 65, more than a quarter of the county.
  • 33,775 people sharing 22,395 housing units, per the July 2025 estimate.

Petoskey was chosen as county seat in a county-wide election, and most of present-day Charlevoix County began as part of Emmet. The Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians hold at least 13 scattered reservation areas in the county, among them parts of Petoskey and several townships, so a buyer or seller with a parcel near one should ask the title company how that land is treated.

McLaren Northern Michigan Hospital in Petoskey employs about 950 people, and the Odawa Casino Resort in Resort Township is one of the county's major attractions. Moeller Aerospace Technology is in Harbor Springs, and Kilwins, the candy and ice cream company founded in 1947, is based in Petoskey.

What if the Emmet County house has back taxes?

Overdue taxes go through the county treasurer's office, which also issues the tax certification a deed needs before it can be recorded. The register will take redemption payments while the redemption period runs. After it ends, only the foreclosing unit can help.

A sale can wipe out the debt. The closer pays it from the proceeds and then orders the certification, so ask the treasurer for an exact payoff before you choose a closing day.

More questions about Emmet County, MI Register of Deeds

Where is the Emmet County register's office?

200 Division Street, Suite 150, Petoskey, MI 49770, phone 231-348-1761. Recording fees are paid in person by cash or check only.

What does a warranty deed cost to record in Emmet County?

$35. The county lists $30 as the base fee and puts warranty deeds, land contracts and other covenant-language deeds at $35, with the $5 tax certification folded into the payment.

Does Emmet County accept electronic recording?

Yes, through three providers: CSC, EPN and Simplifile. Contact one of them for guidance on sending a deed in electronically.

How old are Emmet County land records?

They start in 1852. Images are indexed from 1922 forward and earlier indexing continues, so some older searches mean a trip to the index books.

Do Michigan deeds still need witnesses?

No. Emmet County's register says witnesses are no longer required, though most documents still need a notary acknowledgment.

Genesee County by the numbers

Genesee County ranks 5 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 404,087 people in 183,729 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $172,900, the median home value sits 8% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Genesee County reports $60,673. Owner-occupancy is 71%, so renters hold about 29% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1969, about 54 years ago.

Which Genesee County office keeps recorded deeds?

The County Clerk and Register of Deeds does, from the Genesee County Administration Building at 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. Hours on the county page run weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, with holiday closings.

One elected office oversees vital records, elections and the register of deeds. The register's collection covers deeds, mortgages, liens and other papers touching Genesee land. The county page puts it bluntly: filing makes a paper public and does not make it legal. Staff index each filing into a searchable database and preserve it, so a flawed deed stays flawed after it is on file.

What are the recording fees in Genesee County?

The statewide default is a flat $30 per recorded document, whatever its length. Charter counties can pass their own schedule, so get the current sheet from the office before you mail payment.

Service (MCL 600.2567)Charge
Record one document$30
Extra instruments covered by one discharge or assignment$3 apiece
Photocopies$1 per page
Certification of a recorded paper$5
Index search by request$0.50 per year, $5 floor
Other filings$1

Reference: MCL 600.2567. The $30 already includes the state remonumentation share, and $5 of each recording goes to the register's automation fund.

Fees are due at drop-off. If the register takes electronic filings and you pay electronically, the statute gives one business day after receipt. Ask whether Genesee takes e-filing before you plan a closing around it.

Which taxes does the deed trigger when it is recorded in Genesee County?

A sale deed brings two levies, and the seller owes both. Michigan's rate is $3.75 per $500 of price, rounded up by $500 block, and the county adds 55 cents on each block because its population is under two million.

The deed must carry the total value in its text, or a value affidavit goes with it. When land and personal property sell together with separate stated values, only the land is taxed. Remit to the county treasurer within 15 days of handing over the deed. At $120,000 there are 240 blocks, so $900 goes to the state and $132 to the county.

  • Tiny deals: instruments under $100.
  • Loan paper: mortgages and other collateral documents, with their assignments and discharges.
  • Gifts to descendants: deeds from a parent to a child or grandchild avoid the state levy.
  • Lender foreclosure: transfers made through foreclosure or in place of it, though a resale afterward is taxed.
  • Land contracts: exempt until legal title passes.

A seller who overpaid on an exempt transfer may request a refund from the Department of Treasury.

Which papers does a Genesee County house sale put on record?

A typical sale records a deed and, where a mortgage existed, a discharge. Each is filed separately with its own fee.

  • Deed: warranty, quitclaim or personal representative form.
  • Mortgage discharge or assignment: $30, plus $3 for every extra instrument it covers.
  • Tax foreclosure papers: forfeiture and redemption certificates, notices of judgment and auction deeds. Their fees may be settled within 30 days after the sale or transfer.
  • Transfer affidavit: kept with the local assessor, which in Flint is the city Assessments Division, so it never reaches the register.

The county page does not list electronic options, so ask what the office accepts for each paper.

What does a tax foreclosure judgment do to recorded title?

It clears most of what is on the books. When the judgment takes effect on March 31, title vests in the foreclosing unit, which in Genesee is the county treasurer, and liens and interests on the parcel are extinguished. The state timeline names what survives: future installments of special assessments, environmental liens filed by government agencies, severed or leased oil and gas interests, visible or recorded easements and private deed restrictions.

The paper trail lands at the register's desk. A notice of judgment goes on record, and later so does the deed from an auction. Redemption stays open through March 31. After that date the former owner has no claim, and the buyer at the county auction relies on the recorded deed.

How far back do Genesee County's land descriptions go?

Genesee County's land history starts in the 1830s, which is why old deeds can describe parcels by township surveys that no longer match current boundaries. The Legislature created the county on March 28, 1835 from land taken from Lapeer, Shiawassee and Saginaw counties, and for a time it was attached to Oakland County for court purposes. Grand Blanc, organized in 1833, was the only township at first.

Flint Township followed on March 2, 1836, and the county was fully organized that April 4. More townships were carved out over the next two decades, among them Genesee, Fenton, Flushing, Thetford, Gaines, Clayton and Mount Morris, and in 1843 a column of townships along the eastern edge, including Davison and Atlas, was added from Lapeer County. An old legal description may therefore cite a township that has since been split.

For a seller, the lesson is practical. If a deed in your chain uses an older description, or a township that was later renamed or split, tell the title company early so any correction deed can be recorded before the sale closes.

Where do the other Genesee County property records sit?

Four offices hold the records a seller is likely to need, and only the register holds the recorded documents.

  • Register of Deeds, Suite 1A: deeds, mortgages, discharges, liens and foreclosure notices.
  • Equalization, Suite 8B: parcel descriptions and land records for every municipality except Flint, with assessment data left to the local assessor.
  • Flint Assessments Division: Flint's own parcel records, transfer affidavits, splits and combinations.
  • County Treasurer, Suite 2A: payoffs on delinquent tax and foreclosure information.

Before closing, order a payoff from the treasurer if tax is overdue, and confirm with the assessor that the parcel description matches the deed.

Why does the Genesee County record matter to a seller?

Title companies and buyers read it as the public chain of ownership. A discharge nobody filed, or a misspelled grantor name, has to be corrected before a closing can finish.

The Census Bureau counts 185,007 housing units and 167,334 households in Genesee, with owners in 70.7% of homes and a midpoint owner-occupied value of $182,400, against $53,500 in Flint. Six counties ring it: Tuscola, Lapeer, Oakland, Livingston, Shiawassee and Saginaw. I-75, I-69 and I-475 cross its middle.

A seller with a house that needs work or carries back tax can sell as-is for cash, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds when the deed is recorded.

More questions about Genesee County, MI Register of Deeds

What does the register charge to file a deed in Genesee County?

The state's baseline in MCL 600.2567 is $30 per document of any length. Because charter counties can set their own amounts, confirm the current Genesee County figure with the office before you pay.

Where do I find the Genesee County Register of Deeds?

The office is in the County Administration Building, 324 S Saginaw St, Suite 1A, Flint, MI 48502. The county page lists weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:00, excluding holidays.

Is a recorded deed automatically valid?

No. The county's own page says recording makes a document public and does not make it legal. The deed still needs proper signatures, a correct description and a grantor who owns the land.

Who writes the transfer tax check when a Genesee County house sells?

The seller does, to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. The two levies are $3.75 and 55 cents on each $500 block of price.

Do I owe transfer tax on a deed to my child?

A deed to a child, stepchild, adopted child, grandchild or step-grandchild escapes the state tax. The deed is still recorded, and the usual filing fee applies.

What we confirmed on the official page

Where do you file a deed for Gladwin County land?

At the Register of Deeds in the county building at 401 West Cedar Avenue in the city of Gladwin, the same address as the commission chambers. The office keeps weekday hours from half past eight until half past four.

ItemDetail from the county page
Address401 W Cedar Ave, Gladwin, MI 48624
Telephone989-426-7551
Recording a document$30 flat, any number of pages
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3, added to the flat fee
Certification$5
Copies$1 a page
Searches50 cents per year, $5 minimum

Source: Gladwin County Register of Deeds, which points readers to MCL 600.2567 for questions. The flat charge already covers the state's remonumentation and automation shares.

Does Gladwin County offer online land records?

Yes. The register's page links an online land records search and a free fraud alert sign-up, and it says the office takes electronic recording through three vendors. Paper filings still come in by hand or mail.

The office also handles passports, which have nothing to do with land. New applications are taken by appointment, renewal forms are on hand, and photos cost $10. Call before a trip that combines a deed and a passport.

An alert suits any owner who lives elsewhere. The 2020 census counted 16,862 housing units in Gladwin County, of which 34.7% were vacant, and an owner who is rarely on site is the last to notice a paper recorded against the parcel.

What does the state ask a seller to pay at recording?

Mainly transfer tax. The seller owes two levies that together equal $4.30 on every $500 of price: $3.75 to the state and 55 cents to the county, the rate for counties under two million people. A $100,000 sale therefore costs $860. The deadline to pay the county treasurer is 15 days from delivery.

The deed carries its value in the text, or an affidavit does. Several transfers sit outside the state levy, among them gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds and mortgages. Electronic filings may be paid for within one business day of receipt, and all other documents must be paid for when left at the counter.

What kind of county is Gladwin?

Gladwin is a rural, low-density county in the middle of the Lower Peninsula with 26,077 people in the 2025 estimate. It was set off in 1831 and organized in 1875, and its name honors the British commandant at Detroit during Pontiac's War in 1763.

Of its 516 square miles, 502 are land, and, as a headwaters area it sends most of the water leaving the county on the Tittabawassee River. M-18 follows the west side and links the cities of Gladwin and Beaverton, M-30 cuts through the center, and M-61 crosses from east to west through Gladwin and White Star. Ogemaw, Arenac, Bay, Midland, Clare, Isabella and Roscommon counties border it. Local government is two cities, Gladwin and Beaverton, and 15 townships: Beaverton, Bentley, Billings, Bourret, Buckeye, Butman, Clement, Gladwin, Grim, Grout, Hay, Sage, Secord, Sherman and Tobacco. Each has its own treasurer for current bills, so first confirm which township or city your parcel is in.

  • Housing: 17,329 housing units, 11,280 households and an owner-occupancy rate of 86.1%.
  • Rent and value: median gross rent is $690, and the midpoint home value is $162,300.
  • Age: residents 65 and older make up 28.9%.
  • Income: $55,349 for the median household.
  • Permits: 93 building permits in 2025.

Figures: Census QuickFacts.

How did Gladwin County's land come to be settled?

Gladwin's land was surveyed under the Northwest Ordinance in the 1830s, but settlement came much later. The surveyors reportedly doubted the area would ever be settled, and the first census to mention residents was the 1860 count, which listed 14 people, most tied to lumbering camps. County government was organized in 1875.

Population then climbed from 1,127 in 1880 to 4,208 in 1890 and 8,413 in 1910. It reached 19,957 in 1980 and 26,023 in 2000, then eased to 25,386 in 2020. Some of the early survey work was faulty, so a seller holding an old legal description should ask the title company to check it against the parcel before closing.

The equalization department's GIS viewer helps locate a parcel on a map.

How does Gladwin County's tax calendar touch a sale?

Township and city treasurers bill and collect first. The county treasurer's page lists summer bills going out on July 1 and due without interest by September 14, with a different summer schedule for Gladwin City, and winter bills going out December 1 and due by February 14.

Whatever remains unpaid on March 1 passes to the county, with a 4% charge and one percent interest for each month. The county's own timeline then shows a $15 mailing fee in October, forfeiture on the next March 1, a personal visit fee, a publication fee in the fall and a last payment date of March 31. Foreclosed parcels go to auction at tax-sale.info. The office does not honor postmarks: the date of payment is the day the county receives and processes it.

The treasurer also certifies deeds, plat maps and tax histories, so order a payoff and history before a sale. For principal residence, taxable value, hardship and veteran questions, the page points owners to the township or city assessor.

Who checks assessments in Gladwin County?

The county equalization department does. It reviews local assessments for the Board of Commissioners and is responsible for keeping each property class in each local unit between 49% and 50% of true cash value, based on an annual study. The local assessor stays responsible for fairness between individual parcels.

  • April: equalization report of values.
  • June: millage reduction fractions for each taxing authority.
  • October: apportionment report of allowable millage rates.
  • December 31: the sales and appraisal study.

The department also maintains the countywide database of values, descriptions, title changes, owner addresses and exemption status, plus a GIS viewer for locating land records and principal residence exemption forms. A deed recorded at the register shows up there as a title change, so a buyer should send in a change of address form after closing.

What if tax is still owed when a Gladwin County house sells?

A sale can proceed. The closing agent settles the overdue amount out of the seller's proceeds, based on a payoff that runs to the day of closing.

Timing matters because costs step up. Once a parcel forfeits, monthly interest goes from 1% to 1.5% retroactive to the original delinquency date, and a personal visit and publication fee follow. Redemption rights end at the close of business on March 31, so a seller near that date should request the payoff first. Buyers paying cash as-is can often close quickly when repairs or an inheritance stall a listing.

More questions about Gladwin County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the flat recording charge at the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?

It is $30 per document, whether the document runs one page or many. A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3 for each extra one.

When can I visit the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?

The office is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon at 401 West Cedar Avenue. The listed telephone number is 989-426-7551.

Does the Gladwin office take e-filings?

Yes. The county says it works with three e-recording vendors. Call the office to learn which vendors it uses before you submit anything online.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Gladwin County sale?

The seller owes it. The combined state and county rate is $4.30 per $500 of price, paid to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

When does overdue Gladwin County tax go to the county?

On March 1 of the following year. A 4% fee and monthly interest of one percent start then, and the parcel can forfeit a year later.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

The Grand Traverse County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Grand Traverse County

  • Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30.00 per document regardless of pages (additional fees may apply) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • E-recording accepted for all document types including warranty deeds from major vendors (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Grand Traverse County by the numbers

Grand Traverse County has about 95,757 residents and 46,435 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 22 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $296,200, 58% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $79,486, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 77% of occupied homes and renters in 23%.

What is kept at the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds in Traverse City?

Land paperwork for the whole county lands here: warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages, land contracts, liens and releases. The public can search every file. Scanned images are indexed back to 1966, and a clerk can pull older papers, some dating to 1853, when given a liber and page.

The clerks hand out no blank forms and cannot coach a seller through the wording. The county's own advice is to hire a Michigan real property lawyer, call a title agent, or complete a deed yourself, with the warning that forms downloaded from the web sometimes fail the recording rules.

The county spans 601 square miles, nearly a quarter of it water, and shares its name with the bay at Traverse City. A mission at Old Mission, founded in 1839, was the first permanent settlement. The territory was cut out in 1840 as Omeena County and renamed in 1851. A 2025 federal estimate of 96,729 residents is the largest count of any county in the northern Lower Peninsula.

Where do sellers find homes in Grand Traverse County?

Traverse City is the only city and the county seat. The villages of Fife Lake and Kingsley sit to the south and east, and Interlochen, Grawn and Chums Corner are unincorporated communities. Interlochen is home to the Interlochen Center for the Arts, a boarding school.

Water shapes the map. Long Lake is the biggest inland lake, the Boardman River runs west into West Bay at Traverse City, and the Old Mission Peninsula juts 17 miles into Grand Traverse Bay inside Peninsula Township. Part of the Pere Marquette State Forest lies within the county. A parcel on the peninsula, by a lake or in town is recorded at the same counter. Seven counties touch this one (Antrim, Kalkaska, Missaukee, Wexford, Manistee, Benzie and Leelanau), and a deed for land across the line goes to that county's own register.

Population climbed from 86,986 in 2010 to 95,238 in 2020 and 96,729 in the 2025 estimate, a gain of about 10,000 residents in fifteen years.

What does a seller pay at the Grand Traverse County recording counter?

Filing a deed, mortgage or lis pendens costs $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. Mailed checks go to Register of Deeds or GTROD, with a stamped return envelope or $3.00 to cover postage.

Grand Traverse County recording price list
ItemCharge
One deed, mortgage or similar instrument$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Treasurer certification, warranty deeds$5 for up to 25 parcels, then $0.20 each
Counter photocopies$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 to certify

The $30 figure traces to MCL 600.2567. The county's posted schedule is dated October 1, 2016, so phone the office before sending a large package.

How is the Grand Traverse County transfer tax worked out?

Clerks round the price up to the next $500 step and charge each step twice. The county levy is $1.10 for each $1,000, the 55 cents per $500 fixed by MCL 207.504 for a county this size. The state levy is $7.50 for each $1,000, which is the $3.75 per $500 in MCL 207.525. Together they take $8.60 from every $1,000 of rounded price.

The county's worked case is a $110,100 sale. Rounded to $110,500, it owes $828.75 to the state and $121.55 to the county, for $950.30. Add one dollar to the price and the base jumps to $111,000, producing $954.60. A house valued at the county median of $339,400 would round to $339,500 and owe about $2,919.70.

The deed either states the full price or comes with a value affidavit, and an exemption is written into the instrument. The exemption lists sit in MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax. They cover small transfers under $100, foreclosure deeds and gifts from parents to children or grandchildren, among others.

Why does the County Treasurer certify a warranty deed in Grand Traverse County?

Under MCL 211.135 a deed with a warranty covenant, or a land contract, cannot be recorded until the treasurer certifies two points: no tax liens are outstanding, and five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim with no covenant escapes this rule.

The Treasurer's office is at 400 Boardman Avenue, Suite 104, Traverse City, telephone 231-922-4735. Order the certification before the closing, because the register will hold the deed until it arrives.

The same elected official keeps the county's money, chairs the County Land Bank Authority, and runs the delinquent tax revolving fund that advances unpaid township and city taxes while the county pursues the owner. Each March the office starts collecting delinquent real property taxes. After a court order it can sell parcels that are more than 24 months behind, so a buyer or seller who sees an old balance on a parcel should get a written payoff first.

A seller who plans ahead can bring the following to the title company:

  • The Treasurer's certification, ordered ahead of the closing date.
  • A written payoff for any unpaid year, since the Treasurer collects delinquent bills from March 1 on.
  • The deed, drafted by a lawyer or title agent, because the register offers no drafting help.
  • A check for the $30.00 recording fee, the transfer tax and the $5 certification.

How quickly can unpaid tax cost an owner the property in Grand Traverse County?

Current bills go to the township, city or village treasurer from July 1 through February. When March arrives, whatever is still owed shifts to the County Treasurer.

Two years of delinquency end the owner's rights. In year one the county adds a 4% fee plus 1% interest each month. After forfeiture the rate rises to 1.5% monthly, counted back to the first missed date, and a $175 title search and notice costs join the total. The county files a certificate of forfeiture with the register, so any buyer's title search will find it. On March 31 a year after forfeiture the county forecloses, and it calls that step final.

  • Partial payments slow the interest, provided the last one arrives before foreclosure.
  • Owners get five notices: two ordinary letters, two certified letters and one hand delivery.
  • If an auction brings more than the debt, a former owner files a Notice of Claim by July 1 and asks the court for the surplus the following February.

The county adds a caution for people with escrow accounts: lenders occasionally miss a bill, especially right after a refinance, yet the owner stays liable.

What do the housing numbers look like in Grand Traverse County?

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 lists a typical owned home at $339,400, with owners living in 77.2% of homes. Household income runs $81,647 at the median, rent $1,288, and one resident in four is 65 or older. The county has 40,287 households on 464 square miles of land.

Values at that level make transfer tax a noticeable line on a settlement statement. A seller with tenants, repairs or back taxes should order the treasurer's certification and a payoff letter first, so the title company can hand the register a clean deed.

More questions about Grand Traverse County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing fee for a deed in Grand Traverse County?

$30.00 per document, whatever the page count. A sale adds transfer tax, and a warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer certification.

How much transfer tax does a Grand Traverse County sale pay?

$8.60 for every $1,000 of price rounded up to the next $500: $7.50 to the state and $1.10 to the county. A $110,500 base owes $950.30.

Can a deed be mailed to the Grand Traverse County register?

Yes. Enclose a check payable to Register of Deeds or GTROD plus a stamped, self addressed envelope, or add $3.00 for postage and handling.

When do overdue taxes move to the Grand Traverse County Treasurer?

March 1 after the bill year. The county then adds a 4% fee and 1% interest each month, and forfeiture follows a year later.

Will the Grand Traverse County register help me write a deed?

No. The office provides no blank deeds and no drafting advice, so turn to an attorney or a title company.

Gratiot County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 41,478 people and 16,051 housing units in Gratiot County, which ranks 39 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $136,800, which is 27% below the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $61,128; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 21% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 79% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1966, about 57 years ago.

Where do you take a deed in Gratiot County?

The counter is inside the Gratiot County Courthouse at 214 E Center Street in Ithaca, and the phone is 989-875-5217. Weekday hours run from 8:00 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon. Special closures are announced on the department page, such as the late-morning closing of November 10, 2026.

This is a constitutional office, and its counter handles more than 200 kinds of paper. Seller-side examples include warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, land contracts and mortgage releases, and the shelves also hold powers of attorney and oil and gas leases. Filings stretch back to the 1800s. Anyone may inspect a recorded document during business hours. The same window takes passport applications until 3:30 p.m., after a call to confirm availability.

Staff do not draft paperwork or give legal answers, so the deed itself is a job for an attorney or a title agent. Free public terminals sit on the courthouse's lower level and in the Treasurer's office.

What are the recording charges in Gratiot County?

One $30 charge covers a document of any length. Cash, check or card all work. Transfer tax and a tax certificate are added where they apply, and the $30 base is set in MCL 600.2567.

Gratiot County recording and copy charges
ServiceFee
Record one deed, mortgage or instrument$30
Every added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Warranty deed or land contract tax certificate$5
Copy of a real estate record$1 per page
Certifying a copy$5 per document plus $1 per page
Name search of the real estate record$0.50 per year, minimum $5

Parcel research is priced through the Treasurer's side. Terminal printouts run $1 per page, phone lookups $3, and a written property tax and assessment report $5 per parcel. A new online account gets one free parcel lookup, and later searches on records with the same owner name stay free.

How much transfer tax does a Gratiot County sale owe?

Think in $500 blocks, rounding the price up. Each block pays 55 cents to the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 to the state under MCL 207.525, for $4.30 a block.

Try a $140,000 sale. It holds 280 blocks, which means $1,050.00 for the state, $154.00 for the county and $1,204.00 altogether, apart from the $30 filing. Raise the price by a dollar and the count moves to 281 blocks. Show the whole price on the deed or attach a value affidavit.

  • County exemptions: MCL 207.505. State exemptions: MCL 207.526.
  • No state tax on a deed issued in a foreclosure or in lieu of one.
  • No state tax on a conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or grandchild.
  • No tax of either kind on a corrective quitclaim that confirms title already held.

When does tax in Gratiot County become the county's problem?

The county sends bills July 1 and December 1. A current tax is paid locally, at the township, city or village office, until the first of March next year, and from that day it is the Gratiot County Treasurer's to collect. Payoff amounts come by phone.

The county's published schedule shows how years stack up. Open balances turn delinquent that first March 1. They become forfeited one year later. They are foreclosed on the March 31 after that. For 2025 bills that means forfeiture on March 1, 2027 and foreclosure on March 31, 2028. The online foreclosure auction for 2026 ran through tax-sale.info on a date set for August 7.

  • Cards work for delinquent balances through Graphite, which bills 2.75% with a $1 floor and turns away American Express.
  • Neither the county nor a local treasurer answers for an escrow company that skipped a payment on a mortgaged home.
  • A class settlement over surplus auction proceeds, which Gratiot County joined, covered tax foreclosure sales between 2013 and 2020. Its claim deadline of July 16, 2026 has gone by.
  • Since December 24, 2025 the Postal Service stamps the day mail is processed instead of the day it was dropped off, which can make a last-day envelope late.

What certificate does Gratiot County require for a warranty deed?

A $5 tax certificate from the Treasurer's office goes with warranty deeds, deeds containing a warranty covenant, land contracts and assignments of land contracts with a warranty clause. In MCL 211.135 the treasurer vouches that the last five years are paid and that no tax liens or tax titles hang over the land.

A quitclaim without covenants skips the step. For anything else, request the certificate early in the closing window and ask what an unpaid year would cost, because the register waits for it.

What happens to a deed after Gratiot County records it?

Clerks screen each document against Michigan law first. A deed that clears is given the next number, stamped with the time, scanned whole and cross indexed, and its legal description plus buyer and seller are keyed into the search system. A title company later leans on that index to follow ownership.

Township and city offices, Equalization and the Treasurer each learn of a sale from this register and use it to prepare valuations for the next tax roll. After recording, any member of the public may read or copy the deed. The office suggests double-checking a document against recording requirements before submitting it.

Where is Gratiot County and who lives there?

The county lies in central Michigan and was organized in 1855, named for Captain Charles Gratiot. Ithaca is the seat, Alma is the largest city, and St. Louis is the third city. Ashley, Breckenridge and Perrinton are villages. US 127 runs through Alma, Ithaca and St. Louis, while M-46 and M-57 cross it east and west. Seven counties border it, including Isabella, Saginaw and Montcalm. The Gratiot-Isabella Regional Education Service District is based in Ithaca.

The county covers about 572 square miles, mostly farmland and small towns. The courthouse is a classical revival building listed on the National Register, and the 212.8 MW Gratiot County Wind Project, opened in June 2012, is the largest wind installation in Michigan.

Population has hovered near 42,000 since 2000 (42,285 then, 42,476 in 2010, 41,761 in 2020), and the 2025 estimate of 41,190 is 1.4% under the 2020 base. The median age in the 2020 census was 39.7. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports a median home value of $147,500, 78.9% owner occupancy, household income of $63,556 and median rent of $834. A sale at the median value of $147,500 would owe $1,268.50 in combined transfer tax.

More questions about Gratiot County, MI Register of Deeds

$30 per document, no matter the page count. Transfer tax is extra on a sale, and a warranty deed needs a $5 tax certificate.

Is there a card option for delinquent tax in Gratiot County?

Yes. The Treasurer takes cards for delinquent taxes through Graphite, which adds 2.75% with a $1 minimum. American Express is not accepted, and online payments are processed in the morning and afternoon.

Will the Gratiot County register write my deed?

No. The office prepares nothing and answers no legal questions, so hire a lawyer or title agent. Before you submit, review the deed against the recording requirements so the clerks do not have to send it back.

When do Gratiot County tax bills go out?

July 1 and December 1. If one never shows up, call the township, city or village treasurer, because the tax is still owed. Current-year tax stays payable at that local office until March 1.

Who records deeds in Hillsdale County

What we confirmed on the official page

Hillsdale County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 45,658 people and 21,490 housing units in Hillsdale County, which ranks 37 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $170,500, which is 9% below the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $60,869; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 19% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 81% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1970, about 53 years ago.

How do you file a deed with the Hillsdale County Register of Deeds?

Walk in to Room 212 of the County Office Building, 33 McCollum St., Hillsdale 49242, or phone (517) 437-2231. The window is staffed Monday to Friday from 8:30 in the morning until 5:00 in the afternoon. E-filings can be transmitted at any hour, but clerks work them only during posted hours and not on holidays.

Four e-recording vendors are approved: Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile and CSC/Ingeo. They are paid by ACH, may add charges of their own, and return the recorded document electronically. Any e-filing that violates the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected.

A personal check will not pay for a paper filing, though certified funds are fine (cashier's checks and money orders). Staff do not draft documents, supply templates, or say anything that could be read as legal advice.

What does Hillsdale County charge for recording?

Recording a document costs a flat $30.00 under MCL 600.2567, as amended by PA 224 of 2016, with side charges listed below.

Statutory deed fees posted by Hillsdale County, effective October 1, 2016
Charge forPrice
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 total
Each extra instrument released$3.00
Treasurer's tax certificate (five descriptions)$5.00
Name search$5.00 floor, then 50 cents per year
Page of a real estate record$1.00
Certifying a copy$5.00

Lien searches at the state or federal level cost $3.00 per name, and plats copy at $2.00 per page. A transfer tax calculator is posted on the register's page for planning, with the final amount settled when the deed is presented.

What transfer tax applies to a Hillsdale County sale?

Start by counting $500 blocks in the price, rounding up, and multiply the count by $4.30. The number is 55 cents for the county, from MCL 207.504, plus $3.75 for the state, from MCL 207.525.

Take a $175,000 sale: 350 blocks, $1,312.50 for the state, $192.50 for the county, $1,505.00 in all. A house at the county median of $176,100 rounds to $176,500, making 353 blocks and $1,517.90.

  • The deed shows the price, or an affidavit does.
  • A claimed exemption is stated on the instrument.
  • Statutory exemptions: MCL 207.505 (county) and MCL 207.526 (state).
  • A land contract is exempt while title stays with the seller, and the deed that completes it must reference the contract.

Which 2018 law changes still matter for a Hillsdale County deed?

A notice dated June 22, 2018 went from the register to title companies, attorneys and lenders about Public Acts 191 to 200, signed two days before. Most of the changes started on September 19, 2018.

  • A deed from a surviving owner must be backed by a certified death certificate recorded earlier, cited by liber and page, or filed alongside as a separate recording. Attaching a copy no longer meets MCL 565.48.
  • Documents signed outside Michigan follow Michigan's recording rules too, except for page layout (MCL 565.203).
  • Anything partly in a foreign language comes with an English translation (MCL 565.201).

Court orders need the clerk's certification and seal, an acknowledgment cannot omit its date, and fees are collected when a document is handed over.

What does the Hillsdale register check on every deed?

A checklist from the register spells out what a deed must contain, and a deed lacking one item can be bounced.

  • Ink signatures, each with a printed name that agrees with the notary's wording (MCL 565.201).
  • A mailing address for the grantee, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledging any deed signed in the state.
  • Readable black type of 10 points or more on white 20 pound sheets, leaving 2.5 inches blank at the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere, under a line naming what the paper records.
  • Property value stated on the deed or in an attached affidavit.
  • Social Security numbers cut back to four digits.
  • Trust certificates that meet MCL 565.432 and 565.433.

Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 also had to say whether any male grantors were married or single, a rule that no longer reaches newer deeds.

How do you search Hillsdale County deed records?

The register's page offers search by full text, using optical character recognition, and by name, date, and liber and page. Tract books are linked through Kofile. An owner who wants a deed corrected should know that the office cannot change or alter a document already recorded or in the middle of recording.

Title companies do much of the research for a sale. The register's page names three in the city of Hillsdale: Public Title, Midstate Title and Bell Title Tri County. Ask whichever one handles your closing to confirm the transfer tax figure, since the register collects it with the recording fee.

What does the Hillsdale County Treasurer require before and after a closing?

MCL 211.135 calls for a certificate from the Treasurer on any warranty deed, land contract, or land contract assignment carrying a warranty clause. Five descriptions cost $5.00, and the office answers at (517) 437-4700.

A yearly delinquent tax notice from the Treasurer describes the closing stage of Michigan's foreclosure process. One cutoff date decides whose name is printed in a two week newspaper ad before the Show Cause Hearing in Circuit Court. A little later the office refuses partial payments and personal or business checks, taking only cash, cashier's checks, money orders and credit cards (3% convenience fee). The notice presses owners to pay before a valuable property is lost.

Anyone with an old balance should ask for a payoff before listing the house, because the deed cannot move until the certificate issues.

What is Hillsdale County like?

Territorial lawmakers described the county in 1829 and it was organized in 1835. Its name refers to rolling terrain. The city of Hillsdale is both seat and largest city, and Hillsdale College is based there. At 607 square miles, the county is the only one in Michigan bordering both Indiana and Ohio, and it holds Michigan's southernmost point. Two separate St. Joseph Rivers begin here, one flowing toward Lake Michigan and one toward the Maumee. McCourtie Park and Slayton Arboretum are local parks. Jackson, Calhoun, Lenawee and Branch counties border it in Michigan, with Fulton and Williams counties in Ohio and Steuben County in Indiana to the south.

Winter highs in January average 29 degrees and July highs 82, and June brings the most rain, about 4.3 inches.

Headcount is flat. The 2025 estimate is 45,738, against 45,746 in 2020 and 46,688 in 2010. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show 17,860 households, a $176,100 median home value, 82.0% of homes owner-occupied, $64,242 median household income, $832 median rent and 23.2% of residents aged 65 or more. Owners live in more than four of five homes, so a typical recording here is a home sale.

A free Property Alert service from the register warns landowners of possible property fraud.

More questions about Hillsdale County, MI Register of Deeds

What does a Hillsdale County deed cost to file?

$30.00 buys the filing of a whole document. Transfer tax comes on top for a sale, and a warranty deed also needs a $5.00 certificate from the County Treasurer.

Can I e-record a deed in Hillsdale County?

Yes, through Indecomm, ePn, Simplifile or CSC/Ingeo. Payment goes by ACH, and the vendors may add fees of their own.

Is a personal check good for a Hillsdale County filing?

No. The office takes certified funds, such as a cashier's check or a money order, in its place.

When is the Hillsdale County register open?

Weekdays, from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., in Room 212 at 33 McCollum St. Electronic filings may be transmitted at any hour but are handled only during those hours.

What would a $175,000 Hillsdale County sale owe in transfer tax?

$1,505.00. That is 350 blocks of $500 at $4.30 each, split into $1,312.50 for the state and $192.50 for the county.

Where do Keweenaw Peninsula deeds get filed, and until what hour?

Houghton County deeds go to the courthouse in the city of Houghton, second floor, 401 E. Houghton Avenue (ZIP 49931). Call 906-482-1311. Staff are in from 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, yet the recording day closes at 3:30, so a deed delivered after 3:30 misses that day's recording.

The Register of Deeds page on the county site describes the job as keeping an index plus a copy of every recorded instrument tied to land here. The shelves hold deeds, mortgages, plats, surveys, land corners and a miscellaneous category. Anyone with a nagging boundary question can request the survey or the land corner record for the parcel before the listing goes live.

What will the courthouse charge me to file a deed?

One flat $30.00 covers a document of any length. The county says the figure already includes the state remonumentation charge and the register automation charge. The check goes to the office by name. The fee comes from MCL 600.2567.

  • Add $3.00 for every instrument beyond the first named in an assignment or discharge.
  • Add $5.00 when a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract or land contract assignment is certified.
  • Copies of real estate records are priced by the page at $1.00, and plat copies at $2.00.
  • A lien certificate search, state or federal, runs $3.00 for each name.

Transfer tax is billed separately and is not part of any of these numbers.

How big is the transfer tax bill on a Houghton County closing?

Michigan stacks a state tax and a county tax on the sales price. The county half, set at 55 cents in counties under two million people by MCL 207.504, governs here because Houghton County has under 40,000 residents. The deed must show the full consideration, or a sworn statement of value must ride along with it.

Charges on a Houghton County deed, with a sample $160,000 price
ItemRateStatute
State transfer tax$3.75 for each $500 or part of $500MCL 207.525
County transfer tax$0.55 for each $500 or part of $500MCL 207.504
Recording$30.00 flatMCL 600.2567
Sample sale at $160,000: 320 units, $4.30 per unit$1,376 in transfer taxArithmetic from the rates above

Some transfers escape the state tax under MCL 207.526:

  • Paper that carries consideration below $100.
  • A deed delivered through foreclosure or in place of it.
  • Court-ordered transfers where the judge sets no price.
  • A gift deed to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • A land contract, until title actually moves to the buyer.

The county statute's exemption list, MCL 207.505, contains no child or grandchild entry. Ask the office how the county portion works for a family deed.

Which formatting slips get a Houghton County deed bounced?

Under MCL 565.201 the register must refuse paper that breaks the layout rules. Check the draft against this list before it leaves your hands:

  • Black or dark blue ink for signatures, with a printed name under each one.
  • A grantee mailing address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A blank strip of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere.
  • 10 point type or larger, on white stock of 20 pounds or heavier, sized 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • One opening line naming the single recordable event.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits, and any foreign language text translated.

Once a conforming instrument is in, the statute bars the register from refusing it over its content.

Can a Houghton County deed be filed or searched without driving to the courthouse?

Yes on both counts. Four vendors send electronic filings here: CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Indecomm. They may submit at any hour, and the office works the queue between 8:30 and 3:30. The county advertises same day recording and fewer lost papers, while warning that some document types cannot go electronic.

On the search side, the county points to Tapestry, an occasional-user tool covering September 1993 to the present. A search costs $8.75, viewing images is free and each printed page is $1.00. Professionals who search constantly can subscribe to Laredo. The in-office tract index is billed at $400.00 a month, $20.00 an hour or $5.00 per quarter hour. Owners can also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert, which pings them when their exact name shows up on a newly recorded paper.

What shapes a house sale in the Copper Country?

The county covers 1,502 square miles of the Keweenaw Peninsula, 33 percent of it water. Created in 1843, bounded in 1845 and organized in 1846, it honors Douglass Houghton, Michigan's first state geologist. Keweenaw County split off in 1861 and Baraga County in 1875. Copper mining pushed the 1910 count to 88,098; the 2020 count was 37,361, and the 2025 estimate is 37,842.

Hancock and the county seat, Houghton, face each other across Portage Lake and are joined by the Portage Lift Bridge. US 41 and M-26 are the major roads, and Michigan Technological University is in the county. Its two charter townships are Calumet and Portage. From the Census Bureau:

  • Owners live in 71.8 percent of the 19,308 housing units.
  • The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $159,900, and the typical rent is $840.
  • Median household income is $58,899.
  • The average trip to work takes 15.6 minutes.

Does Houghton County's history leave marks on old titles and parcels?

It does, in a few ways. The mining boom drew people from dozens of countries. At the 1910 census 40.6 percent of residents were foreign-born, and the 2010 census shows about 32.5 percent of residents with Finnish ancestors. A name search on a very old Houghton County deed is worth running under several spellings, which is a point to raise with the title company.

The land itself has changed as well. After the Depression-era job losses in mining and timber, the area turned to potato farming for a time in the 1930s and 1940s. In June 2018 a flash flood left sinkholes and washouts in Chassell, Houghton, Ripley, Lake Linden and Hubbell. A seller in one of those places should gather repair invoices and permits and keep them with the sale file, since a buyer will ask what was fixed.

Which county desks handle taxes before a Houghton County sale?

The Treasurer is on the courthouse second floor too, at 906-482-0560, and keeps the same weekday schedule of 8:00 to 4:30. That desk collects delinquent real estate tax, certifies deeds and plats, prints tax histories and arranges partial payment plans. It also hosts the tax sale and foreclosure timeline pages.

Equalization supports 16 assessing jurisdictions and sends their taxable values to the State Tax Commission annually. Write to equalization@houghtoncounty.net or to Attn: Equalization, 401 E Houghton Ave, Houghton MI 49931. Calling the Treasurer ahead of closing shows the title company whether anything is owed.

More questions about Houghton County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is the deed filing fee at Houghton County?

A single $30.00 charge applies no matter how long the document is. A $5.00 certification is added for warranty deeds and land contracts, and $3.00 for each further instrument in an assignment or discharge.

Is 3:30 really the last call for recording in Houghton?

Yes. Doors stay open until 4:30 p.m., though the day's recording ends at 3:30 p.m. E-files may arrive overnight and get worked during the 8:30 to 3:30 window.

Who covers transfer tax when a Houghton County home is sold?

The county page does not say, so confirm with the title company or the register. Rates are $3.75 state plus $0.55 county for each $500, due when the deed is submitted.

Is there a way to look up Houghton deeds from home?

Yes. Tapestry has records from September 1993 forward at $8.75 a search with free image viewing, and Laredo suits frequent searchers. For earlier material, call 906-482-1311.

Whom do I ask about back taxes on a Houghton parcel?

The Treasurer at 906-482-0560, courthouse second floor, is the contact. The desk handles delinquent taxes, tax histories, payment plans and tax sale information.
