What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Which Bad Axe office takes Huron County deeds?

Room 203 of the county building, 250 East Huron Avenue in Bad Axe (48413), is the recording desk. Phone 989-269-9941; fax 989-269-8786. The counter runs 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, holidays excepted, and nobody locks the door at noon.

The county's own page for the office says the land record indexes are searchable online back to 1947, with older land records going back to 1848 kept in the office. Documents can be delivered by hand or mailed. Correct fees have to arrive with the paper, and payment can be a check, a money order, cash or a card.

Why do older Huron County records get thin around 1865?

A courthouse fire explains it. The Legislature created Huron County on April 1, 1840, and it was fully organized January 25, 1859. Sand Beach, today's Harbor Beach, hosted the county seat until the courthouse burned in 1865 and took most of the records with it. Government moved to Port Austin, and in 1873 the Board of Supervisors picked Bad Axe.

Farm and shoreline parcels held by one family for generations may therefore show gaps in the earliest paper. Ask the title company early how it plans to deal with the oldest links in the chain, and look through the paper books in Room 203 where the online index stops.

How do I check the record before listing a Huron County home?

Begin with the online index and write down the book and page, or the document number, of your own vesting deed. The county page also links to Laredo search details and to Property Fraud Alert enrollment. Laredo is the program title searchers use on the official record, and the alert tells an owner when a filed paper carries the exact name entered.

  • Pull the deed that put the property in your name, plus every mortgage, so you know what must be released at closing.
  • Scan the index for easements, land contracts and assignments touching the parcel.
  • Enroll your name as it appears on title, and add a second entry for any variant.
  • Call 989-269-9941 about anything older than 1947.

If a recorded paper surprises you, staff in Room 203 can help you find it in the index.

What does a Huron County filing cost?

Michigan sets a $30.00 charge for each recorded document, however many pages it has, in MCL 600.2567. Smaller items from that statute may also appear on a seller's bill:

  • An extra $3.00 for each added instrument that a single assignment or discharge reaches.
  • $5.00 to certify a document on record.
  • $1.00 per page for photocopies.
  • 50 cents per year searched in a grantor or grantee search, with a $5.00 floor.

The charge is due as the paper is left for recording; for an electronic filing the statute gives one business day. Huron County names two e-recording firms: Simplifile, 1-800-460-5657, and CSC, 1-866-652-0111. For an unusual instrument, call the register to learn the exact amount.

What transfer tax follows a Huron County sale?

Two levies run on the price: $3.75 for each $500 or part of $500 as the state's share in MCL 207.525, and 55 cents per $500 as the county's share in MCL 207.504, which applies to a county under 2,000,000 residents. Huron County estimated 30,530 in 2025. The instrument must state the whole value, or an affidavit of value is attached.

Transfer tax if a Huron County house sells at the county median
LineBasisResult
Median owner-occupied value, Census 2020 to 2024$154,300, rounded up to 309 blocks of $500309 blocks
State portion309 x $3.75$1,158.75
County portion309 x $0.55$169.95
TotalBoth portions added$1,328.70

That total is arithmetic from the rates, and no quote. The two acts diverge on family deeds. The state list in MCL 207.526 excuses a conveyance to a child or grandchild, yet the county list in MCL 207.505 has no such line. Ask the register before a parent signs a house over to a son or daughter.

What trips up a deed headed for Bad Axe?

The recording statute, MCL 565.201, lists what a register of deeds may insist on. Walk through it with the drafter:

  • The typed name under every signature should match the name the notary wrote in the acknowledgment.
  • The notary's printed or stamped name belongs on the same page, near the notary signature.
  • A deed signed after January 1, 1964 carries its drafter's name and business address.
  • Cover or remove the first five digits of any Social Security number.
  • Attach a written English translation to any paper in another language.

When a paper is accepted and recorded, the statute treats it as conforming, and a compliant instrument cannot be refused for what it says.

What is it like to sell in the Thumb's northern tip?

Huron County has Saginaw Bay on the west and Lake Huron on the north and east, with over 90 miles of shoreline. Land makes up 836 of its 2,137 square miles. Farming leads the economy, and weekend visitors from Detroit, Flint and Saginaw concentrate around Port Austin and Caseville. Bad Axe is both seat and largest city; Caseville and Harbor Beach are the other cities, Bay Port is a census-designated place, and M-19, M-25, M-53 and M-142 carry the state highway traffic.

  • The estimated 2025 population is 30,530, which is 2.8 percent below the 2020 base of 31,411.
  • Nearly 30 percent of residents (29.7) are 65 or older.
  • Owners occupy 81.8 percent of homes across 14,150 households.
  • A typical owner-occupied home is worth $154,300, and a typical household earns $58,870.
  • The county issued 69 building permits in 2025.

The long view is a plateau followed by slow decline. Huron County had 34,162 people in 1900, reached 36,459 in 1980 and 36,079 in 2000, then dropped to 33,118 in 2010 and 31,407 in 2020. The median age at the 2020 census was 49.6 years. To look up a parcel, the county's home page links an Assessing and Tax Search tool and a FetchGIS map, both handy for checking acreage and the parcel number before a deed is drafted.

Who else in the Huron County building matters at closing?

The Treasurer's Office is in Room 204 of that building at 989-269-9238, open 8:30 to 4:30 with no lunch closure. Equalization is in Room 306 at 989-269-6497, sharing the room with Tax Mapping and GIS at 989-269-9421. Ask the Treasurer about the parcel's tax standing before the closing date so any balance is cleared out of the proceeds. The Huron County Land Bank operates from that same Treasurer's office. If the owner has died and the house passes through an estate, Probate Court is in Room 206 at 989-269-9944, and the County Clerk is in Room 201 at 989-269-9942.

More questions about Huron County, MI Register of Deeds

When can I reach the Huron County Register of Deeds?

Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays, with no break at noon. The office is Room 203 at 250 East Huron Avenue, Bad Axe.

Can a Huron County deed be e-recorded?

It can. The county lists Simplifile and CSC as e-recording providers, so contact one of them and the office receives the document electronically.

How far back can I search Huron County deeds?

Online indexes begin in 1947, and land records from 1848 forward are held in the office. The 1865 courthouse fire at Sand Beach destroyed most early records.

Does a gift deed to my daughter owe transfer tax in Huron County?

The state tax exempts conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, while the county act's list shows no matching item. Call 989-269-9941 before counting on it, and state the exemption on the deed.

How do I pay the Huron County register of deeds?

Use a check, money order, cash or credit card, and include the correct fees with each recording. Checks may be made out straight to the Register of Deeds.

Fees

Selling in Ingham County?

Ingham County by the numbers

Ingham County has about 282,015 residents and 125,812 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 8 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $187,500, 0% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $64,354, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 60% of occupied homes and renters in 40%. The median home was built in 1971, about 52 years ago.

Why do Lansing sellers record deeds in Mason?

Mason holds the county seat, even though most of Lansing, the state capital, sits inside Ingham County. No other state capital in the country lacks the county seat. The recording desk is the Register of Deeds, 2nd Floor, 341 S. Jefferson Street, Mason, MI 48854. Mail goes to PO Box 195 at the same town, and the phone is 517-676-7216.

According to the office contact page, the front counter is staffed weekdays from 8 until 5. Older books live in the vault, which is open 8:30 to 4 by appointment only. A seller coming from East Lansing or Okemos should phone before making the drive.

What will an Ingham County closing cost at the recording desk?

The county fee schedule sets $30.00 for any deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified court paper or similar real estate instrument, however many pages it runs. Smaller charges stack up when several papers file on the same day.

  • $3.00 for every liber and page or instrument number named in an assignment or discharge covering more than one instrument.
  • 50 cents a page for a time-stamped copy, available only at the moment the original is submitted.
  • $1.00 a page for a copy of anything already recorded.
  • $5.00 per document plus $1.00 a page for a certified copy of the whole recorded document.

Payment is expected at recording, following MCL 600.2567.

Does the Treasurer have to sign off before an Ingham County warranty deed is recorded?

Yes. A tax certificate from the County Treasurer is a precondition for recording a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract, or an assignment of land contract that carries a warranty clause. The same gate covers an affidavit fixing the legal description in one of those papers, and condominium master deeds, amendments that alter the legal description included.

The certificate is $5.00 for five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each one after that, citing MCL 211.135. A seller with a split or multi-parcel property should count the tax IDs first. Treasurer telephone: 517-676-7220. Ask for the certificate before the closing date, so it is already in hand when the title company sends the deed to Mason for recording.

Who owes the transfer tax on an Ingham County sale, and how much?

The county's fee page puts the burden on the seller or grantor, payable when the instrument arrives for recording. The rates are $3.75 per $500 (state) and $0.55 per $500 (county). The deed shows total consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit comes with it, and any claimed exemption has to be written on the instrument.

Seller's transfer tax at Ingham County's median home value
StepFigure
Median owner-occupied home (Census 2020 to 2024)$198,800
Blocks of $500, rounding up398
State charge, 398 x $3.75$1,492.50
County charge, 398 x $0.55$218.90
Seller's total$1,711.40

The page ties the county tax to MCL 207.501 through 207.513 and the state tax to MCL 207.521 through 207.537. In the table, $198,800 divided by $500 is 397.6, and the fraction rule lifts it to 398 blocks. Three odd cases from the same page:

  • Land spanning two counties needs the price divided by parcel, and each county taxes its piece.
  • County tax applies to the price named in a foreclosure instrument.
  • A deed of easement or right of way is taxable as well.

Exemptions sit in MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526.

What does the Mason office look for when it reviews a deed?

The recording requirements page warns that its list is only the common problems. Even so, it is a useful pre-flight check:

  • Original ink signatures, typed or printed names beneath, black or dark blue.
  • An acknowledgment with the notary's signature, county and state of commission, expiration date and the place of signing.
  • A certified death certificate recorded as a separate document and cross-referenced when a survivor is named.
  • Court orders certified under the clerk's raised seal.
  • No correction fluid or tape.
  • A top margin of 2.5 inches on page one, and Social Security numbers cut to four digits or fewer.

The underlying rules are in Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, and neighboring sections.

How far back do Ingham County's online records reach?

The index goes to 1956, and images start in 1960. Choose among three tools: Direct Search, a free index lookup that leaves out the latest seven days; Tapestry, at $8.95 a search with $1.00 per printed page; and Laredo, a subscription aimed at regular title searchers. County staff are still auditing indexed data for 1956 to 1981 for conversion errors, so that stretch is best checked in the vault by appointment. Laredo subscription questions go to 517-676-7294. Pre-1960 copies are $1.00 a page at the Mason office or by mail to Register of Deeds Copies, P.O. Box 195, Mason, MI 48854.

Which other offices does an Ingham County seller phone?

The county home page publishes direct lines for the offices a sale tends to touch. Gather paperwork from them ahead of the closing date.

  • Treasurer, 517-676-7220: tax certificates and parcel tax status.
  • Register of Deeds, 517-676-7216: recording, copies, vault appointments.
  • Probate Court, 517-483-6300: estates, when an owner has died and the house passes through probate.
  • County Clerk, 517-676-7201: listed beside the Register of Deeds among the county's elected officials.
  • 30th Judicial Circuit Court, 517-483-6500: judgments and orders that may need recording against the property.

The courthouse is at 341 S. Jefferson, Mason, MI 48854, and the county's department list also shows an Equalization office for valuation questions.

What is Ingham County like beyond the capital?

The Michigan Territorial Legislature created Ingham County on October 29, 1829, and Washtenaw County ran it until 1838. It takes its name from Samuel D. Ingham, a Treasury secretary under Andrew Jackson. Of 561 square miles, 556 are land, rolling at 800 to 1,000 feet. The Grand River bends along the west edge and the Red Cedar crosses the north. Michigan State University, Lansing Community College and the Lansing Lugnuts all call it home.

Municipalities include East Lansing and Lansing (each partly), Leslie, Mason and Williamston, plus the villages of Dansville, Stockbridge and Webberville. Haslett, Holt and Okemos are census-designated places. By Census Bureau figures the 2025 estimate is 289,709 people and 127,510 housing units, with 59.5 percent owner-occupied. Typical values: a $198,800 home, $1,084 rent and a $65,526 household income. Among adults 25 and over, 41.2 percent hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The county has grown steadily, from 2,498 residents in 1840 to 211,296 in 1960, 261,039 in 1970 and 284,900 in 2020, when the median age was 33.4 years and density ran 512 people per square mile.

More questions about Ingham County, MI Register of Deeds

When is the Ingham County recording counter open?

Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The vault closes earlier, with appointment hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Call 517-676-7216 to book.

Who writes the check for transfer tax in Ingham County?

The seller or grantor, per the county fee page. Payment comes due as the deed is presented, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county.

Must I visit the Treasurer before my Ingham County deed is recorded?

Only for warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts, which need a tax certificate first. It costs $5.00 for up to five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each extra one.

Is there a free way to search Ingham County deeds?

Yes, Direct Search is free and covers the index from 1956 forward, minus the most recent seven days. Seeing images through Tapestry costs $8.95 a search, and printing adds $1.00 a page.

Is the Ingham County Register of Deeds located in Lansing?

No. The office is in Mason at 341 S. Jefferson Street, 2nd Floor, because Mason is the county seat although Lansing lies mostly within the county.

Who records deeds in Ionia County

  • Ionia County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Courthouse, 100 W. Main St., Ionia, MI 48846 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Accepts e-recording; $5 fee combinable with recording check; copies $1/page (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Ionia County?
We buy Ionia County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page not searched/opened
  • Millage rates not researched
  • Ionia recording fee/hours not seen

Ionia County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 66,706 people and 24,746 housing units in Ionia County, which ranks 29 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $189,400, which is 1% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $73,436; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 23% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 77% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1972, about 51 years ago.

Who files the deed after an Ionia County home sale?

The Ionia County Register of Deeds files it. That office keeps the land records for the whole county, and a sale becomes public only once the deed is stamped, indexed and filed there. Staff will not help you draft or repair paperwork, so the papers should arrive complete, drafted by a lawyer or the closing company.

Land area in Ionia County is roughly 571 square miles. The seat is the city of Ionia, and the county counts as part of the Grand Rapids-Kentwood metro area. Filing can happen at the counter, through the mail, or through an approved electronic provider. Counter filings are handed back on the spot. Mailed packets come back only if you include a self-addressed return envelope, and anything sent without one is held 90 days. For questions, call (616) 527-5320 or write deeds@ioniacounty.org.

What will the Ionia County deed filing cost me?

Thirty dollars covers each document, however long. Payment can be cash, check or card, and card payments add a service fee that depends on the amount. One check can cover the filing charge and both transfer taxes.

Ionia County Register of Deeds charges
ItemAmount
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 per document
Document that assigns or discharges several instruments$3.00 for each one past the first
Treasurer tax certification (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5.00
Name lookup by staff$5.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 added

Source: Ionia County Register of Deeds pages on fees and on searching and copies.

How is transfer tax figured on an Ionia County sale?

Ionia County publishes two rates that apply to a deed conveying real estate for money. The state takes $3.75 for every $500 of price, counting any partial $500 as a full one, and the county takes $0.55 on the same basis. A $200,000 price therefore produces $1,500 state tax and $220 county tax, $1,720 combined. That is simple arithmetic on the posted rates; your closing agent will confirm the final number.

Any claimed exemption goes in writing on the deed itself. The two Michigan statutes do not match, and the gap matters for family transfers:

  • MCL 207.526 (state tax) exempts a deed from a parent or grandparent to a child, stepchild or grandchild, along with foreclosure deeds and deeds in place of foreclosure.
  • MCL 207.505 (county tax) exempts instruments valued under $100, security instruments, leases, and court orders that name no price, and it omits the child and grandchild category.
  • Both statutes exempt a land contract until the full contract price has been paid and title passes.

So a gift deed to a daughter can owe county tax while owing nothing to the state. Ask the office how your transfer is classified before you sign.

Which sales need a treasurer certification first?

Warranty deeds, any deed with a covenant of warranty, land contracts, and assignments of land contracts must carry a Tax Certification from the Ionia County Treasurer. The $5 charge can sit on the same check as the filing charge. A quitclaim deed has no warranty covenant, so it usually avoids this step, and the Register of Deeds can say whether yours does.

If back taxes are owed on the parcel, raise it with your closing agent early, because the certification is part of the package that gets filed. Ask the County Treasurer what the office requires before it will issue one.

Why would the office send my deed back?

Clerks check each document against Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201 and related sections. A deed that misses a rule comes back, and a closing can stall for days. The county's own checklist covers the usual trouble spots:

  • Signatures are originals in dark ink, black or dark blue, with each name printed below.
  • The notary block repeats the same printed names, and the notary's name sits on the page that holds the notary signature.
  • The buyer's mailing address appears, as does the drafter's name and address as well.
  • Page one leaves a 2 1/2 inch blank band at the top, with half an inch clear on the remaining edges.
  • The first printed line names the one recordable event the paper covers.
  • Print is black, 10 point or larger, on white stock of at least 20 pound weight, in letter or legal size.
  • A deed to a surviving owner needs a certified death certificate recorded with it or earlier.
  • The full property value is stated on the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit goes with it.

Can I look up Ionia County land records myself?

Yes. Public workstations in the office let you search by grantor or grantee for free, with copies at $1 a page. Searching those machines by legal description or parcel number runs $1 per minute. If you ask staff to find your last deed, the fee is $5 plus copies, and the lookup works by name rather than by property.

Remote searching comes in two forms. Tapestry charges $8.95 per search and suits a single visit. Laredo bills monthly and fits agents, investors and anyone searching often; call the office to open an account. If either service gives you trouble, the county asks that you contact the vendor's support team (Fidlar) first and the Ionia filing counter after that. A title company search digs deeper than either tool when you need the full ownership chain behind your house.

How do Ionia County housing numbers compare for a seller?

Census QuickFacts puts the population at 66,557 in July 2025, slightly under the April 2020 count of 66,804. About 77.3 percent of households own, with a typical owned home worth $198,500 (2020 to 2024 survey years). Typical household income of $75,611 is the highest among the four Michigan counties researched alongside this one.

Commuters average 27.1 minutes each way to work, the longest of those four counties, which fits a county that feeds the Grand Rapids job market. Rent runs $884 a month at the median, and builders pulled only 100 permits in 2025. Resale houses supply most of what buyers see, and your listing joins that pool.

Will the next property tax bill look different after I sell?

A transfer of ownership uncaps taxable value. Under Proposal A, the new figure takes effect in the calendar year after the transfer, so the buyer's bill can climb toward the assessed value. Michigan Treasury posts the Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, which the buyer files with the local assessor. Ask the assessor for your city or township about the filing deadline.

Transfers listed in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act do not uncap. Assessment is a local job in Michigan, handled by the city or township where the house stands, so the assessor there is the person to call about taxable value. Current bills come from that same local unit, and the County Treasurer takes over delinquent ones.

More questions about Ionia County, MI Register of Deeds

Does Ionia County bill by page count?

No. Each document costs $30 to file. Documents that assign or discharge several instruments add $3 for each extra one.

May I email a deed to the Ionia County Register of Deeds?

No. Email filings are refused. Electronic recording runs through accredited servicers named on the county page: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, EPN and CSC. Only a scanned original signed document is accepted.

Who covers transfer tax in Ionia County?

Neither buyer nor seller is named on the county page. Payment comes with the deed at filing, so read your purchase agreement and watch the settlement statement for the amount.

Will paying off my mortgage give me a new deed?

No. Your lender files a discharge of mortgage, which carries the same $30 filing charge, and your original deed remains the proof of ownership.

Is a quitclaim to a relative taxed in Ionia County?

It may be taxed by the county. The state list exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, and the county list leaves them out. The deed has to state the exemption, so ask the office first.

What does the Iosco County Register of Deeds do for a home seller?

The Iosco County Register of Deeds files and keeps every deed, mortgage, survey, land contract, condominium and subdivision document for real estate in the county. The office dates to Michigan's first state constitution in 1835, and the county's own records begin in 1858. All of them have been digitized, and the online index reaches back to the early 1970s. Anything older is searched in person at the office, or by a title company you hire.

Iosco County is a lakeshore county in northern Michigan, with Tawas City as the seat and Lake Huron along its eastern border. Selling a house here means the closing deed gets filed with this office. The office says it has no forms, is not staffed by attorneys, and will not advise on legal questions or prepare papers, so line up a lawyer or title company for that part.

What fees apply to filing a deed in Iosco County?

A deed costs $30 to file. Some documents, such as a discharge of mortgage, an assignment of mortgage or an oil and gas paper, cross-reference other instruments, and each cross-reference after the first adds $3. Two payees are involved, so write two checks when a treasurer certification is needed.

Tax certification$5 per documentIosco County Treasurer

Source: Iosco County Register of Deeds, Fees and Charges page.

Which Iosco County documents need a tax certification?

Warranty deeds, land contracts, assignments of land contracts, and any other paper containing a Warrant and Defend or Covenant clause need a tax certification. The $5 payment goes to the Iosco County Treasurer, not to the Register of Deeds. Ask your closing agent to add it to the settlement statement.

Quitclaim deeds carry no covenant of warranty. Whether yours needs a certification is a question for the Register of Deeds before you submit it.

How does Michigan transfer tax apply to an Iosco County sale?

Michigan taxes deeds that convey property for money twice, once for the state and once for the county. The Resources page of the Iosco Register of Deeds carries three PDFs: a Transfer Tax Chart, a county exemption list and a state exemption list. Ask the office, or open that chart, for the exact dollar amount at your sale price.

Both statutes (MCL 207.505 for the county tax, MCL 207.526 for the state tax) shield some transfers entirely. Examples that come up in house deals:

  • An instrument with consideration under $100.
  • A deed used to confirm a title already held, such as a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.
  • A deed that creates a joint tenancy when one of the people already owns the property.
  • A transfer in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a government-backed or government-made loan under the county act, and any mortgage foreclosure under the state act.

If one fits your sale, the deed has to cite it on its face.

What Michigan filing rules should an Iosco County deed meet?

The state recording statutes, chiefly MCL 565.201 and 565.8, govern the format of every deed, and the Iosco office insists on an original with original signatures. Court orders and death certificates must carry a certified raised seal. Beyond that, county offices across Michigan flag these points:

  • Signatures are typed or printed beneath, and the notary acknowledgment matches those names.
  • The paper lists who drafted it, with name and address.
  • A deed to survivors comes with a certified death certificate on record.
  • A trust agreement that accompanies an instrument is recorded as its own document.
  • Anything in a language other than English has a written English translation attached.

A rejected deed pushes a closing back, so have the preparer check the document against the Iosco office's own requirements page before it goes in.

What are the steps from closing to a filed deed in Iosco County?

Most of the sequence happens before anyone walks into the Tawas City office, and a short checklist keeps the file complete:

  • Have the deed drafted by an attorney or title company, since the office will not prepare it.
  • Sign it in front of a Michigan notary, using original signatures only.
  • Add the tax certification request if the deed has warranty language, with a separate $5 check to the County Treasurer.
  • Calculate the transfer tax from the county chart, or note the exemption on the deed.
  • Submit the deed with a $30 check to the Register of Deeds, adding $3 for each extra cross-reference where one applies.
  • Confirm the filing later through the DoxPop search to see that the document shows up in the index.

The search index reaches back only to the early 1970s, but a deed from this closing will be in it, so a quick lookup afterward confirms the record is complete.

How do I search Iosco County property records?

Search recorded documents through the county's DoxPop link, or visit the office. Staff will not run genealogy searches on your behalf, though visitors may use the records themselves. A Property Watch service from DoxPop sends a notice when a new document is recorded against a property you name.

If you want a copy of your deed, you can get one online or at the counter for $1 a page. Paying off a mortgage does not produce a new deed, since your lender records a discharge and your original deed remains the proof of title.

What is the Iosco County housing picture for sellers?

Of Iosco County's 1,890 square miles, 1,341 are water, which leaves about 549 of land. Most residents live along the US-23 shoreline in East Tawas, Tawas City and Oscoda. The legislature first created it in 1840 under the name Kanotin County, renamed it in 1843, and county government was organized in 1857. Gypsum mining around Alabaster, south of Tawas City, began in 1862 and still operates.

QuickFacts estimates 25,266 people for July 2025, and a third of them (33.0 percent) are 65 or older. It counts 20,221 housing units against only 11,713 households, and the 2020 census found that 41.3 percent of the units were vacant, a sign of the cottages and seasonal houses common here. Owners hold 82.1 percent of the occupied homes. A typical owned home is valued at $142,200 for 2020 to 2024, the lowest of the four Michigan counties studied together here. Rent at the median is $719 a month, household income at the median is $50,066, and builders pulled just 47 permits in 2025.

How will a sale change the property tax on an Iosco County house?

A change of ownership lifts the cap on taxable value the following calendar year, as Michigan Treasury explains in its guidance on Proposal A. The affected buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the local assessor. Which exemptions avoid uncapping is spelled out in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act.

Iosco County has an Equalization department and a Treasurer's Office listed among its departments. Ask them how a specific parcel is assessed and billed.

More questions about Iosco County, MI Register of Deeds

What does the Iosco office charge to file a deed?

$30, with $3 more for each additional cross-referenced instrument on documents such as mortgage discharges. Copies are $1 a page and certified copies are $5 plus $1 a page.

Do I need a new deed after paying off my Iosco County mortgage?

No. Your lender sends you a discharge of mortgage to record. The deed you received at purchase continues to prove ownership.

Who writes the check for the $5 tax certification in Iosco County?

You do, payable to the Iosco County Treasurer only. Recording fees and copy charges go on a separate check payable to the Iosco County Register of Deeds.

Will Iosco staff add a name to my deed?

No. The office tells people to consult an attorney for that kind of change, because each situation differs. Staff do not prepare documents or give legal advice.

Can I record a photocopied court order in Iosco County?

No. Recording needs an original document with original signatures, and court orders and death certificates have to be certified with a raised seal.

Who records deeds in Isabella County

What we confirmed on the official page

Selling in Isabella County?

What we could not confirm

Isabella County by the numbers

Isabella County has about 64,475 residents and 28,600 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 31 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $165,100, 12% below the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $53,759, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 61% of occupied homes and renters in 39%.

Where does an Isabella County deed get filed?

Filing happens in Room 220 of the county building at 200 N. Main Street, Mount Pleasant, MI 48858. The office phone is (989) 317-4089. Land records here reach back to the mid-1800s, and a recorded document is open for anyone to review or copy. Staff neither draft documents nor answer legal questions, so a lawyer or closing company should finish the paperwork first.

The county seat and biggest city is Mount Pleasant. Territorial lawmakers described the county in 1831, it was organized in 1859, and its name honors Queen Isabella I of Castile. When your Isabella County house sells, the closing deed lands at this counter, and the county urges a careful read against the recording rules before anything is handed in.

What do Isabella County statutes set as the filing charge?

State law sets a flat $30.00 for each document. If a document lists several liber and page references, each one beyond the first costs $3.00. Mail-in filers who want the original back should send a prepaid return envelope.

Isabella County recording and certification charges
ServiceCharge
Recording, per document$30.00 flat
Each additional liber and page listed$3.00 (first one free)
Tax certificate, up to 5 descriptions$5.00
Tax certificate, each description past 5$0.20
Name search by the office$0.50 per year searched, $5.00 minimum

Source: Isabella County Register of Deeds, Recording Information and Fees. Tax certificate checks are payable to the Isabella County Treasurer. Copies from a search carry the statutory copy fee, which the office will quote.

As a worked example, a name search covering 12 years comes to $6.00 at 50 cents a year, while any search of ten years or fewer is billed the $5.00 minimum.

Which sales in Isabella County need a tax certificate first?

Section 211.135 of Michigan law requires a treasurer certificate before the office will file any of these:

  • Warranty deeds, plus any other deed with a covenant of warranty written into it.
  • Land contracts, and their assignments when a warranty clause is attached.
  • Condominium master deeds.

The treasurer issues it, so the check goes to the Isabella County Treasurer. Parcels with many descriptions pay 20 cents for each one after the fifth. Have your closing agent request the certificate before signing day so it cannot delay the filing.

What recording rules do Isabella County deeds have to meet?

The county posts a summary of the Michigan recording rules people ask about most, and refers readers to the legislature's website for the full text. Highlights from that list:

  • Original signatures only, each name typed, stamped or printed below, and no mismatch among the body text, the signature and the acknowledgment.
  • Every party's address is shown on any instrument that conveys, assigns or encumbers title.
  • A deed signed in the state is acknowledged by a notary and names its drafter with an address.
  • If the grantor section names a survivor, a certified death certificate is filed as a separate document.
  • A trust agreement attached to an instrument is filed on its own under Public Act 194 of 2018.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the clerk of the court.
  • Page one leaves 2 1/2 inches blank at the top, other margins run 1/2 inch, and the type is black, 10 point or larger, on white paper.
  • Any part written in another language needs an English translation attached.

A county news item says Public Acts 191 through 200 of 2018 changed some of these rules and sends readers to the legislature's site for details.

How much is Michigan transfer tax on an Isabella County sale?

Two Michigan laws tax real estate transfers: Act 330 of 1993 at the state level and Act 134 of 1966 for counties. The dollar amount at your sale price comes from the Register of Deeds, and the settlement statement will show it.

A few statutory exemptions come up with house transfers, and the deed must carry the claim:

  • Spouses moving property into or out of entireties ownership.
  • Boundary-line adjustments made without payment.
  • Corrective quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • New joint tenancies where one of the co-owners already had the property.

Gifts to a child or grandchild are exempt only in the state act, so a family gift needs a question to the office first.

What should I gather before a deed goes to the Isabella County office?

A complete package avoids a second trip to Mount Pleasant. Pull these items together with your closing agent:

  • The signed, notarized original deed, with the drafter's name and address on it.
  • A check for $30.00 to cover the recording, plus $3.00 for each extra liber and page.
  • The treasurer's tax certificate and its separate check, when the deed has warranty language.
  • The transfer tax payment or a stated exemption.
  • A return envelope, stamped and addressed, if the package goes by mail.

Once the office records the deed, it becomes a public record, and any buyer, lender or neighbor can pull a copy. That is why a clean filing matters.

Does a university town change how a house sale works?

Paperwork is identical, yet the buyer pool differs. Central Michigan University sits in the county, and the 2020 census recorded a median age of 31.7, far below the other three counties in this set. QuickFacts lists a 61.8 percent ownership rate, the lowest among the four counties, and the 2020 census counted renters in 39.9 percent of occupied units.

For a landlord selling a rental near campus, that means a deed from an investor-owned property that may have tenants in place. Read any lease before you fix a closing date. Part of Mount Pleasant also lies within the Isabella Indian Reservation, which spans 217.67 square miles and is the main land base of the Saginaw Chippewa Tribal Nation. Your title company can tell you whether your parcel sits inside the reservation and whether that changes the paperwork.

What do the housing statistics show for Isabella County?

Census estimates put Isabella County at 64,691 residents in mid-2025, half a percent above the April 2020 base. Midpoint figures for 2020 to 2024 include a $170,400 owned home, $913 monthly rent and $55,237 in household income, while 19.0 percent of people live in poverty. College graduates are 31.3 percent of adults, the best share of the four counties, and the average trip to work takes 19.6 minutes.

The county issued 90 building permits in 2025. Just 78.5 percent of residents had stayed put for a full year, a lower share than in the other three counties in this set.

How is the next tax bill affected after an Isabella County sale?

Selling resets taxable value, according to Michigan Treasury: under Proposal A the cap lifts in the calendar year following the transfer. Form 2766, the Property Transfer Affidavit, is the paper the new owner sends to the local assessor. Some transfers are carved out of uncapping in subsection (7) of MCL 211.27a.

In Michigan, assessing is largely handled by cities and townships. The local assessor can tell you your taxable value and when the affidavit is due.

More questions about Isabella County, MI Register of Deeds

How much does a deed cost to file in Isabella County?

Thirty dollars flat per document, with $3.00 added for every extra liber and page reference past the first. When a tax certificate is required, it runs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

Who issues the tax certificate for an Isabella County warranty deed?

The county treasurer's office. Your check for the certificate is payable to the Treasurer, and it must be obtained before the Register of Deeds records a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed.

How do I get my filed deed returned by mail?

Include a self-addressed, stamped return envelope with the package. Without it the office has no way to mail the recorded paper back.

Will Isabella County staff review my deed for legal problems?

No. Reviewing for legal problems is outside the office's role, because it neither drafts papers nor answers legal questions. An attorney handles that, and the county advises checking the recording requirements before you submit.

What does a name search cost at the Isabella County office?

Fifty cents for every year searched, set by MCL 600.2567, with a $5.00 floor. Copies pulled from a search are billed at the statutory copy rate.

Jackson County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 160,187 people and 69,188 housing units in Jackson County, which ranks 13 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $182,900, which is 2% below the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $65,004; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 25% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 75% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1966, about 57 years ago.

Where in Jackson do I bring a signed deed?

Take the signed deed to the Register of Deeds at 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th Floor, Jackson, MI 49201. Posted hours run 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays without a lunch break, and the phone is 517-788-4350. County holidays are days off.

The closing agent usually files the deed and pays the office, so few sellers visit. Transfer tax is still deducted on the seller's side of the settlement statement, which makes the counter's rules worth a look.

Jackson County has 702 square miles of land, per Wikipedia, with the city of Jackson as its seat and only city. Villages include Brooklyn, Concord, Grass Lake, Hanover, Parma and Springport, with Cement City partly inside the line. A parcel in any of those places is recorded at this same twelfth floor office.

What fees does the Jackson County counter collect on a deed?

A flat $30 buys the recording of one document at any length. The statutory fee page dates this to October 1, 2016, and notes that $4 of it goes toward survey monument upkeep. The authority is MCL 600.2567.

The county's fee page also lists smaller items you may run into:

  • $3 for each further instrument a paper assigns or discharges.
  • Page copies at $1, and $5 for a certified document.
  • Name searches at 50 cents a year covered, $5 minimum.
  • Tax lien name searches, state or federal, at $3 each.

Cash, checks and cards are accepted. Make the check out to the Register of Deeds, and the county lets you include transfer tax in that same check.

How do I figure the Jackson County transfer tax?

The county levies 55 cents per $500 and the state $3.75 per $500, both listed on the Jackson County transfer tax page. A partial $500 step is charged as a full one. The seller is the taxpayer under MCL 207.523, and the county's share is set by MCL 207.504.

Show the full price on the deed, or file a valuation affidavit and say so on the deed. The affidavit has no filing fee. An exemption claim also belongs on the deed.

The middle row starts from the Census median value of $193,700 for the county and rounds it up to $194,000.

Which Jackson County conveyances owe no transfer tax?

Several, though the two lists are not the same. A deed given as security, a transfer under $100, and a spouse to spouse deed that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties are exempt from both. For the state tax, a deed from an owner to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild is also exempt, and so is a deed made through a mortgage foreclosure or in place of one. See MCL 207.526.

The county list in MCL 207.505 is shorter, so a gift to a daughter or son can be free of state tax while county tax still applies. Phone the register of deeds with the exact deed type before the paperwork is signed.

A seller who paid on a deed that turns out to be exempt can ask the state treasury department for a refund.

When does a Jackson County deed need a treasurer's certificate?

If it carries warranty language, yes, and the same goes for land contracts and their assignments with a warranty clause. The county treasurer first certifies the tax history that MCL 211.135 covers, five years back from the date of the deed.

Jackson County charges $5 for this certificate and wants it on a separate check payable to the Jackson County Treasurer, handed in with the recording. A quitclaim deed without warranties is excepted by the statute.

If tax is owed on the house, get a payoff figure from the treasurer early, and the title company will pay it out of your proceeds.

Why would the Jackson County office send a deed back?

Paper that breaks MCL 565.201 comes back unrecorded, and the county prints that statute on its Recordings page. Typical causes are layout slips and missing names:

  • Sheets outside the legal size range, faint ink, or type below 10 point.
  • A top band on page one that is under 2.5 inches.
  • A first printed line that fails to name the one event being recorded.
  • No printed name beneath a signature, a notary name on a different page from the notary's signature, or no grantee address.
  • No drafter's name and business address.
  • Unredacted social security numbers.

Per the county FAQ, a photocopy is refused because only original signatures qualify. Court papers need the court seal, and a death certificate needs the clerk's seal. Staff neither draft deeds nor sell forms, so hire an attorney or title agent for that.

What does Census data show about Jackson County homes?

Owner occupants dominate here. QuickFacts lists 159,552 residents for mid 2025 and 69,801 housing units, with 75.0 percent of homes lived in by their owners. A household with a mortgage carries a median $1,377 in monthly owner costs, one without a mortgage $557, and the median rent is $985.

  • Middle home value, 2020 to 2024: $193,700.
  • Household income, middle point: $66,073 in 2024 dollars.
  • Residents aged 65 and up: 21.5 percent.
  • Density: roughly 228 people per square mile.

With over one resident in five past 65, sales that follow a death or a move into care come up often. A clean deed history helps those close, and the county records show it.

QuickFacts also records 303 building permits for 2025, 2,991 employer establishments with 50,612 jobs in 2023, 8,520 veterans, and a mean commute of 22.5 minutes. Only 23.4 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree, and 62,540 households share the county.

Geography matters to a few sellers too. Wikipedia notes that the Grand River runs through the city of Jackson and that the north branch of the Kalamazoo River begins in Hanover Township. A lot near either water course may carry easements or flood questions that show up in the recorded chain of title, so ask for a records search if yours does.

How do I search Jackson County's recorded documents?

An online grantor and grantee name search covers deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers, and heavy copy buyers can ask the office for an escrow account. You can also carry your parcel's legal description to the counter and staff will help you start a records search. Easement or lake right questions are often answered by the title insurance policy you got at purchase.

Owners can enroll in the free alert that reports any filing made under their name, a no cost way to spot a forged deed.

If a buyer raises a title question, pull together your recorded deed, the loan payoff statement and any lien notices. Those answer most of what a purchaser wants to see.

More questions about Jackson County, MI Register of Deeds

Does the Jackson County recording fee go up with extra pages?

No. A long deed costs the same $30 as a short one. The only add on is $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

Who owes transfer tax on a Jackson County sale?

The grantor does. The recorder takes 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on each $500 of price, unless the deed states a valid exemption.

Will Jackson County record a copy of my deed?

No. Only the original signed paper is taken. Court orders carry the court seal, and death certificates carry the clerk's seal.

Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim deed in Jackson County?

Usually no, since the statute exempts quitclaim deeds that carry no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts are the ones needing it.

When can I visit the Jackson County Register of Deeds?

Come Monday to Friday between 8 and 4, noon hour included. Legal holidays are days off, so check 517-788-4350 first.

Kalamazoo County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 261,437 people and 114,463 housing units in Kalamazoo County, which ranks 9 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $227,500, which is 21% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $70,525; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 36% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 64% owner-occupied.

Which office files Kalamazoo County land records?

Land records for Kalamazoo County are kept by the Register of Deeds in the County Administration Building, 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49007, phone 269-383-8970. The county calls the register of deeds a constitutional office dating from 1835, and says recording makes a document public without making it legally valid.

Staff index and preserve the records. Title searches and legal advice are off limits to them. In most sales a title company makes the trip or e-records the deed. A seller filing alone should read the checklist below, since the counter turns away papers that miss a formatting rule.

Kalamazoo County has four cities (Galesburg, Kalamazoo, Parchment and Portage) and five villages (Augusta, Climax, Richland, Schoolcraft and Vicksburg), according to Wikipedia. All of them record at this single office.

What does filing a document cost at the Kalamazoo County counter?

The county fee schedule sets recording at $30 a document under MCL 600.2567. A few extras can apply:

  • $3 more for each added instrument on a paper that assigns or discharges several.
  • Copies at $1 a page, plus $5 a document if certified.
  • $5 per search when staff look something up.
  • A $5 treasurer certificate for up to 20 tax ID numbers on one document, and 20 cents for each description after that.

The counter takes cash, checks, money orders and cards. Recording checks go to the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds, and certificate checks to the treasurer involved. No online pay portal exists for counter filings, so card payers phone the office or come in. The full list is on the county fee schedule.

How do Kalamazoo County sellers calculate transfer tax?

The seller's transfer tax is paid at the counter when the deed goes on record. The schedule gives $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, applied to a price rounded up to the next $500, so $100,000.01 becomes $100,500.

Those amounts are the statutory 55 cents and $3.75 per $500 restated per thousand. The county rate sits in MCL 207.504, and the state act names the seller as the person who owes the tax in MCL 207.523.

Combined transfer tax by price, from the Kalamazoo County fee schedule rates
Price usedCounty taxState taxSeller pays
$100,000$110$750$860
$242,000$266.20$1,815$2,081.20
$350,000$385$2,625$3,010

The middle row starts from the Census median value of $241,800 and rounds up to $242,000. A chart on the county website covers other prices, and the site links exemption lists for both taxes.

Which Kalamazoo County deeds need a tax certificate?

If the grantor "warrants" or "defends" the title in the deed, the treasurer must clear taxes first. The county's list names warranty and covenant deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments with warranty wording, and master deeds, including amendments that add property to a condominium. The rule comes from MCL 211.135.

A house inside the City of Kalamazoo adds a step. The seller gets a city certificate from the City Treasurer at Kalamazoo City Hall, 241 W South Street, phone 269-337-8036, for $10, and the County Treasurer issues its own only after that.

A parcel with unpaid taxes cannot be cleared until the balance is paid at closing. Request a payoff figure early, because interest builds monthly on delinquent balances.

What must a paper show to be accepted in Kalamazoo County?

Layout is governed by MCL 565.201, and the county FAQ restates it as a checklist:

  • White copy paper, letter or legal size.
  • Black ink, 10 point type or larger.
  • A clear 2.5 inch strip across the top of page one, the document type printed on the first line below it, and half inch margins elsewhere.
  • A notary for the deed types the county lists, including warranty, quitclaim, executor, trustee and sheriff's deeds. Witnesses are no longer required.
  • Court documents bearing the court's certification and seal.

A rejected paper returns with a letter stating why, and you correct and refile it. Adding or removing a name on a deed takes a new deed, and the office cannot draft one, so use an attorney or title agency.

Can I record a Kalamazoo County deed electronically?

Yes, through four certified vendors, which are Simplifile, Indecomm, ePN and CSC. Filings are processed on county business days, payment moves by ACH under each vendor's agreement, and vendors may add their own processing fees. Plats and master deeds with full size maps cannot be sent this way.

Michigan's statewide e-recording standards took effect on January 1, 2014, and the county follows them. Sellers rarely meet a vendor, because the title company submits the deed.

A Consumer E-Recording portal serves one time filers with affidavits, discharges, mortgages, certificates of trust, liens and releases. Deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are excluded, so a seller recording a deed should use the counter or a title company.

How do I search Kalamazoo County land records?

The Document Searches page on kalcounty.gov is the starting point. Its Deeds Search tool costs nothing for index searching, then $1 a page plus a processing fee to view, print or save an image. Tapestry EON, available since October 21, 2024, costs $8.75 per search, and Laredo is a monthly subscription aimed at frequent users like title professionals.

Staff can fetch your latest deed for $5 a property and $1 a page, with certification at another $5. Public workstations in the Administration Building let you search grantor and grantee names free, charging $1 a printed page. Name searches beat address searches, since recorded papers need no address.

Land record images reach back to 1831, though the complete index only starts in 1984. A title company search is the safer route for a long chain of title.

What happens to a Kalamazoo County deed when an owner dies?

Surviving owners do not need a new deed, the county says. Recording an official death certificate with this office shows the deceased owner's interest has ended, and the certificate becomes part of the title chain. Photocopies of death certificates are refused.

Heirs who plan to sell should ask the title company what authority it needs, because county staff cannot advise on that. A free fraud alert is also offered. Enter a personal or business name and you are told whenever a matching document is recorded, which helps protect an empty inherited house.

What do the numbers say about Kalamazoo County housing?

Renters take a bigger share here than in Jackson or Kalkaska counties, so many sellers are landlords. QuickFacts reports 263,795 residents in mid 2025, 116,117 housing units, and owners living in 64.5 percent of occupied homes for 2020 to 2024.

  • Middle home value: $241,800.
  • Household income, midpoint: $72,532 in 2024 dollars.
  • Gross rent, midpoint: $1,093 monthly.
  • Adults 25 and over holding a bachelor's degree: 41.3 percent.

Wikipedia lists 562 square miles of land, with I-94 crossing the middle of the county and US 131 through its west central part. Owners outside the city limits record here too but ask a township or village treasurer about local tax.

More questions about Kalamazoo County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the price of getting a deed on record in Kalamazoo County?

Thirty dollars a document. Transfer tax and treasurer certificates are billed separately, and a paper discharging several instruments adds $3 per extra one.

Is transfer tax my bill as a Kalamazoo County seller?

Yes, the seller does, at the Register of Deeds counter when the deed is recorded. The county charges $1.10 and the state $7.50 for every $1,000, after the price is rounded up to the next $500.

Does a house in the city of Kalamazoo need two tax certificates?

Yes. A parcel within city limits pays $10 for the city certificate first, then $5 for the county one.

Are witnesses required on a Kalamazoo County deed?

No. A notary is the requirement now, for warranty, quitclaim and most other deed types.

May I use a card for Kalamazoo County recording fees?

Yes, by calling the office at 269-383-8970 or paying at the counter at 201 West Kalamazoo Avenue. The county has no online payment portal for counter recordings.

Where do Kalkaska County deeds get recorded?

The Register of Deeds is housed in the Administration Building, 605 N. Birch Street, village of Kalkaska, MI 49646, phone 231-258-3315. Weekday administration hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and legal holidays are observed. The counter also processes passport applications by appointment only.

Wikipedia places Kalkaska County in northern Lower Michigan, within the Traverse City metropolitan area. Its 571 square miles hold more than 80 lakes and about 275 miles of streams and rivers. Marsh and the Pere Marquette State Forest account for a good deal of the land.

Cabins, lake lots and acreage anywhere in the county all record at this single office. The village of Kalkaska is both the county's only village and its seat.

What will the Kalkaska County office charge to file a deed?

Indexing and recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or any other instrument takes $30 for the whole paper, with no per page charge since October 1, 2016, the county says. A document discharging or assigning mortgages adds $3 per extra instrument number. See MCL 600.2567.

Warranty covenant deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments need a county treasurer tax certificate first. The county prices it at $5.00 per instrument for as many as five descriptions, then 20 cents for each further description, which matters when a sale spans several parcels.

  • Cards can be used through an online county payment page, with a paycode shown on the register of deeds page.
  • Plat books are sold at the counter for cash or check.
  • A free property fraud alert notifies you of any document recorded with your name in it.

What transfer tax comes out of a Kalkaska County sale?

Any deed worth $100 or more triggers both taxes, and the grantor bears them. The county share is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state share is $3.75 per $500. The county site carries a chart for looking up any price.

State the property value on the deed, or file a valuation affidavit, which costs nothing but must be noted on the deed. An exemption claimed under MCL 207.505 for the county or MCL 207.526 for the state has to be written on the deed too.

Sample Kalkaska County transfer tax at $4.30 per $500 (county $0.55 plus state $3.75)
Price usedNumber of $500 stepsCombined tax
$75,000150$645.00
$189,000378$1,625.40
$300,000600$2,580.00

The $189,000 row starts from the county's Census median home value of $188,900, rounded up to the next $500 step.

Which Kalkaska County deeds escape the tax?

The two transfer tax acts supply the exemptions, and the county posts both lists on its recording fees page. Both exempt security instruments, leases and deeds given by a government grantor, along with confirmation deeds, for example a quitclaim that fixes a flaw in title the grantee already holds.

Family transfers are treated differently. Only the state act exempts a deed from a parent to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The same MCL 207.526 also exempts foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, though a later resale by the foreclosing party is taxed.

Whichever exemption applies, put it in writing on the deed. If tax was paid on a deed that qualified, the state act lets the seller request a refund from the state treasury.

Does Kalkaska County take electronic filings?

Yes, for all document types except judgments, court orders, plats, surveys and other certified papers. The partner vendors are ePN, CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile, and Simplifile alone handles warranty deeds, land contracts and other treasurer certified papers.

Title professionals sign up for Laredo, the county's records search program, by sending the register of deeds a subscription agreement. Individual owners can use the fraud alert and the front counter.

A one time seller is usually best served when the title company or closing attorney e-records. To carry a paper deed instead, read the layout list below first, because a returned deed can delay closing.

What page layout will the Kalkaska County counter accept?

The state recording statute, MCL 565.201, binds this office like any other, and an instrument missing an item cannot be accepted. Homemade deeds tend to fail on these points:

  • 2.5 inches of open space atop page one, and half inch margins around the rest.
  • Dark print, 10 point type, on white paper no lighter than 20 pound.
  • A single phrase on the first printed line naming what is being recorded.
  • Names printed beneath every signature, and the notary's name beside the notary signature.
  • The grantee's address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • An attached English translation when part of the text is in another language.

The statute adds that anything already recorded is conclusively presumed to comply, so a deed that clears the counter stays on record even if a small slip went unnoticed.

How big is the Kalkaska County housing market?

This is a small market where nearly everyone owns. QuickFacts counts 18,693 residents in mid 2025, a gain of 4.2 percent over the April 2020 base, in 11,820 housing units. Owners live in 88.2 percent of occupied homes.

  • Middle home value, 2020 to 2024: $188,900.
  • Rent at the midpoint: $853 a month.
  • Share of residents past 65: 24.6 percent.
  • Mean trip to work: 29.7 minutes, longer than in Jackson or Kalamazoo counties.
  • Density: 32 people per square mile.

Per Wikipedia, US 131 cuts through the western part of the county, M-66 runs north to south in the west center, and M-72 crosses the middle from west to east.

What is the Kalkaska County setting for a house sale?

The area began as Wabassee County in 1840 and took its present name in 1843, according to Wikipedia. It was organized in its own right on January 27, 1871. Kalkaska sand, the Michigan state soil, is named for it, and elevation swings from 595 feet to about 1,246 feet, which makes it one of the more uneven counties in the Lower Peninsula.

Beyond the village of Kalkaska, the communities of Bear Lake, Manistee Lake, Rapid City and South Boardman are census designated places, and the county borders Antrim, Otsego, Crawford, Roscommon, Missaukee, Wexford and Grand Traverse counties. Buyers sometimes arrive from those neighbors, so the closing agent should settle early where each party will sign.

Census figures show 38 building permits in 2025, 4,120 jobs at employer firms in 2023, and 1,384 veterans. Employment slipped 5.9 percent between 2022 and 2023, a point worth knowing when you price a house for a local buyer.

What should I line up before closing on a Kalkaska County sale?

Pick up the certificate and any tax payoff figure from the county treasurer, and let the register of deeds look over your paperwork. Confirm the treasurer's hours and number before you head over, since schedules change.

Agree with your title company on who pays each of these, so nothing is paid twice:

  • The $30 deed filing charge.
  • The treasurer's certificate, $5 for a short parcel list.
  • Both transfer taxes, which land on the seller.

If the sale includes several parcels, count the descriptions early, because each one past five adds 20 cents to the certificate.

More questions about Kalkaska County, MI Register of Deeds

What does the Kalkaska County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?

Thirty dollars covers a whole document of any length. A paper assigning or discharging several mortgages adds $3 for each extra instrument number.

Does a Kalkaska County deed need a tax certificate?

It does when the deed has a warranty covenant, and for land contracts and their assignments. The treasurer charges $5.00 an instrument for up to five descriptions.

Who pays Kalkaska County transfer tax?

The seller does. Recording triggers 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state per $500 of price, unless an exemption stated on the deed applies.

Can I pay by card at the Kalkaska County Register of Deeds?

Yes. The register of deeds page links a county card payment service and gives a paycode to use. Treat the treasurer's tax certificate fee as a separate payment and ask that office how it takes payment.

What number do I call at the Kalkaska County Register of Deeds?

Dial 231-258-3315. The counter is at 605 N. Birch Street in Kalkaska and keeps weekday administration hours.

Who records deeds in Kent County

  • Kent County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30 per deed/mortgage/lis pendens/instrument (effective Oct 1, 2016); cash, check, money order (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

Kent County by the numbers

Kent County has about 658,844 residents and 267,071 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 4 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $265,700, 42% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $80,390, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 70% of occupied homes and renters in 30%.

Which office records Kent County deeds?

The building is at 300 Monroe Avenue NW, in the middle of downtown. Land contracts, liens and mortgages go through the same counter, under the Michigan Recording Act.

The office is careful about what it will not do. It does not supply blank deeds and it does not advise on how to prepare one. Anyone changing names on a deed can use a real property attorney, a title company or a blank form they fill in. It cautions that forms pulled from the internet may fall short of recording rules.

Why does the Kent County register of deeds see so many transfers?

Kent County is big. The county holds, by the July 2025 Census estimate, 675,232 people and 275,076 housing units across roughly 849 square miles of land. Records here start in 1836, the year the county was organized after being set off from Kalamazoo County in 1831.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.3%
  • Home value at the median: $289,900
  • Building permits in 2025: 2,398
  • People in the same house one year earlier: 87.9%

The Grand River runs through the county, and the land rises to 1,048 feet at Fisk Knob Park in Solon Township, so parcels range from river-valley city lots to rolling township acreage. All of them are recorded at one counter. Sellers should have the paperwork squared away before closing.

What are the recording fees in Kent County?

The base fee is $30 per document, and it has been in place since October 1, 2016. It covers deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and certified copies. The same fee schedule lists the add-ons you are most likely to meet when a house changes hands:

  • Assignments or discharges that cover several instruments add $3 per extra instrument, and the office asks you to limit these to 25 per document.
  • Deeds with a covenant of warranty, plus land contracts, need the treasurer's certification at $5 per deed (up to 25 parcels, 25 cents each beyond that). Write that check to the Kent County Treasurer, not the Register.
  • Copies are $1 per page. Searches start at $5, and certifying a document adds $5.
  • Pay with cash, a check or a money order. The check is written to the Kent County Register of Deeds.

Electronic filers pay the statutory recording fee to the county, and any e-recording vendor can add its own processing fee on top.

What transfer tax applies to a Kent County sale?

Add the two posted rates, $1.10 for the county and $7.50 for the state, and every $1,000 of price carries $8.60. Both come straight from Michigan's two transfer tax acts, MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Transfer tax on sample Kent County sale prices at the posted rates
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal
$150,000$165$1,125$1,290
$290,000$319$2,175$2,494
$400,000$440$3,000$3,440

The $290,000 row is near the Census median home value for Kent County, $289,900. The statute taxes each $500 or fraction of $500, so an odd price rounds the count up. There is no transfer tax on mortgages in Michigan.

Where does a Kent County deed get its tax certification?

That stamp comes from the Treasurer's Office, a separate counter from the Register of Deeds. Deed certifications are one of the few transactions the treasurer still takes in person, at the first-floor counter of the Administration Building during weekday business hours, 8 am to 5 pm.

Plan the order of events around that. A seller who learns at the last minute that taxes are open must first pay the treasurer, then collect the certification, and only after that bring the deed to the recording counter. The county's online delinquent tax search lets you check a parcel before you start, and the payment options page covers e-check, card, phone and mail payments for any balance.

Who owes the transfer tax, and how is an exemption claimed?

The seller, or grantor, owes it. Write the full price into the deed, or attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit. No fee applies to the affidavit so long as the deed mentions it.

Exemptions must be written on the deed itself. The state's list in MCL 207.526 includes a parent deeding to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds, land contracts that have not yet passed title, and court orders that set no price. If land lies in two counties, state the price for each part.

Can you get any of the state transfer tax back?

Possibly, for a seller who held a principal residence exemption and sold at a price close to the property's earlier assessed value. MCL 207.526(u) exempts a conveyance of property that carried the principal residence exemption when the state equalized value is no higher than the value set at the first tax day after the home was built or acquired, and the sale was an arm's-length price.

Kent County's transfer tax page lists what a refund claim needs: the state refund application, copies of the recorded deeds showing the transfer tax stamp and proof of the sales price, and proof of the SEV from the local municipality. Copies of deeds come from the online deed search or from the office itself.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Kent County?

Yes, through approved e-recording vendors, within a fixed window. Electronic documents are processed on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, skipping county holidays, and the fee is collected by ACH through the vendors.

Kent reserves the right to reject any electronic filing that fails the Michigan Recording Act, and a party whose documents violate the state standards is cut off until further notice. The county lists CSC eRecording, ePN, Simplifile and File and Go as the vendors it works with, and each vendor sets its own pricing. Recorded documents return to the submitter in electronic form. An individual seller will usually leave this step to the closing office.

What should a Kent County seller settle before the deed goes in?

Settle the property tax first, because the register of deeds cannot take a warranty deed without a treasurer's certificate. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate depends on a clean five-year tax record. Any open balance is settled by closing, and the Kent County Treasurer will quote it.

Check that the names on the deed match the owners of record. If a parcel's owner is unknown, the office suggests asking Equalization or the local assessor for the tax roll name, which may not match the true owner, and then searching recorded documents under it. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor the transfer notice under MCL 211.27a.

More questions about Kent County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the recording fee for a deed in Kent County?

Recording is $30 a document, under a schedule dated October 1, 2016. Budget a further $5 for the treasurer's tax certification on a warranty deed, plus any vendor charge if a filer submits electronically.

How high is the Kent County transfer tax?

It is $8.60 per $1,000 of price in total, split $1.10 county and $7.50 state. A $250,000 sale produces $2,150, owed by the seller unless the deed states an exemption.

Does the Kent County Register of Deeds help write a deed?

No. The office does not supply blank deeds or offer advice on preparing them. It sends people to an attorney, a title company or a blank form.

Will Kent County take a warranty deed while taxes are delinquent?

Not a warranty deed. State law requires a treasurer's certificate that taxes for the previous five years are paid. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excepted.

How do I order a certified copy from Kent County?

Visit the office in person, by letter, or through its online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.
