  • Recording fee $30 per document under MCL 600.2567 plus $3 per additional instrument (third-party michiganofficialrecords.com, not official) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Lake County?
We buy Lake County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where is the Lake County, Michigan Register of Deeds?

Look for Suite 200 at 800 Tenth Street in Baldwin, the county seat. The clerk and the register of deeds share that one office, so every deed for Lake County land goes across the same counter.

  • Monday to Thursday: 8:30 am until 5:00 pm
  • Friday: 8:30 am until 4:00 pm
  • Phone (231) 745-2725, fax (231) 745-8632

Equalization has its own suite in the same address, Suite 230, with a phone at (231) 745-2723. It maintains property descriptions and helps with assessment questions.

What kind of county is Lake County for a property seller?

Lake County is rural, seasonal and low-priced. About 567 square miles of land hold an estimated 13,182 residents (Census, July 2025), which was close to 21 people per square mile in 2020. Wikipedia notes that the Legislature created it in 1840 as Aischum County, and it took the Lake name in 1843 for its many lakes.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value (2020-2024): $133,900
  • Owner-occupied rate: 82.0%
  • Residents 65 and older: 28.6%
  • Mean commute to work: 34.0 minutes
  • Housing units in 2020: 13,315, with 61.9% vacant

A vacancy share that high means many parcels sit empty for long stretches, so an owner selling one may live far from Baldwin. Call the office with the parcel number to learn what it needs before you mail anything.

How do you pay Lake County recording fees?

Bring or mail a check, money order or cash payment to the clerk's office, because recording fees cannot be paid online. The county's web payment page covers copies, vital records and cremation permits, and the register of deeds page carves out recordable land record fees as the exception.

State law sets the amounts. The amounts in MCL 600.2567 are $30 per recorded document however many pages it runs, $1 per copied page, $5 to certify a recording, and a $5 floor on a records search. Statute lets a charter county adopt another schedule, so phone the office to verify the total first.

What will the transfer tax be on a Lake County sale?

Two layers apply in Baldwin as in the rest of Michigan. The county layer is 55 cents per $500 because Lake County has fewer than 2,000,000 residents (MCL 207.504), and the state layer is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525).

What the statutory rates produce on sample Lake County prices
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal
$60,000$66$450$516
$133,900$147.40$1,005$1,152.40
$250,000$275$1,875$2,150

The middle price is the Census median for the county, which rounds up to 268 units of $500. Since the seller bears the tax, the instrument has to show the full value, or a valuation affidavit has to go with it, and any exemption has to be written on it.

What gets a deed rejected at the Lake County register of deeds?

The clerk's office sends back non-compliant instruments with a checklist, and the checklist cites the Michigan statute for each problem. Most are fixable before you submit.

  • Original ink signatures, with each name printed or typed below, matching the notary block.
  • A street number or post office address for every grantee.
  • The drafter's name and address.
  • One statement of the recordable event on line one of page one, in black ink, 10-point type or larger, over a 2.5 inch blank top margin (half an inch on the other margins).
  • Paper no smaller than letter size and no longer than legal.
  • At most four sequential digits of any Social Security number.
  • An attached English translation for any foreign-language text.

Other triggers include a survivor deed with no recorded death certificate, an uncertified court order, a trust document that is not recorded as its own instrument, and a missing date in the acknowledgment.

Where do Lake County owners find assessment forms and parcel data?

The Equalization Department posts them, and it is the first stop for questions that are not about recording. The department runs annual sales and appraisal studies on every class of real property, and it uses them to equalize values across the county's 15 local units of government. State law (MCL 211.34) frames that work around an assessment level of 50% of true cash value.

Its page links to the state forms an owner is most likely to need: the principal residence exemption and homestead form, a request to rescind a PRE, the disabled veterans exemption, and the property transfer affidavit. It also links the Michigan Treasury property tax estimator, which lets you compare millage rates across local units. A seller can use that tool to show a buyer what the tax on the parcel is likely to look like.

Annual apportionment and equalization reports for Lake County are posted on the same page, with years back to 2015 for apportionment, so a buyer or heir can see how the county's values were adjusted from year to year. Equalization also keeps a map of subdivisions for all 83 Michigan counties, and its advice for using that tool is to type only the first two letters of the subdivision name.

Does Lake County offer a land records fraud alert?

Yes. The register of deeds describes itself as the beta test site for a fraud alert program that notifies subscribers when land record activity matches their name. Mail your name, email, phone number, mailing address and parcel ID (if known) to Lake County Register of Deeds, Attn: Fraud Alert, 800 10th Street, Suite 200, Baldwin, Michigan 49304.

An owner who lives elsewhere and holds a cabin or vacant land can use that alert as an early warning that someone has recorded a document against the parcel. The same page links to online land record searches, which you can use to review a parcel's recorded deeds before a sale.

What should a Lake County seller settle before recording?

Deal with taxes first. A deed that carries warranty covenants will not record in Lake County without the county treasurer's certificate under MCL 211.135, which speaks to liens and the last five years of tax. Request it from the Lake County treasurer well ahead of closing.

Equalization covers the 15 local units in the county and about 27,000 real property parcels, with permanent parcel numbers in use since 1987, so keep the number handy when you phone. After closing, the buyer has 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessing office (MCL 211.27a), and next year's taxable value is reset. Whether the buyer finances or pays cash, the steps in this guide are the same.

More questions about Lake County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the recording fee at the Lake County register of deeds?

The base fee is $30 for each recorded document, and a discharge or assignment that covers extra instruments costs $3 more per instrument. Take payment to the clerk's office as a check, money order or cash, since the online payment page excludes recording fees.

When can I visit the Lake County register of deeds?

Monday through Thursday it runs 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, and on Friday it closes at 4:00 pm. Go to Suite 200, 800 Tenth Street, Baldwin, or call (231) 745-2725.

Who owes Lake County real estate transfer tax?

The seller. Together the two rates are $4.30 per $500 of value, and a deed gets no exemption unless it says so on its face.

Why would the Lake County register of deeds return my deed?

Usually for a formatting or signature problem: no original signatures, no drafter name and address, a missing grantee address, the wrong margins or paper size, or no statement of total value. The office sends back a checklist of the reasons with the instrument.

Can I search Lake County land records online?

Yes. The register's page links to online land records and describes a fraud alert program you join by mail with your details and parcel ID.

The Lapeer County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Lapeer County

  • Lapeer County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Hours 8am-4:30pm Mon-Fri; County Complex Building, 255 Clay St (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Recording $30.00 per document; cash, check, money order (credit card inside) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page not searched/opened
  • Millage rates not researched

Lapeer County by the numbers

Lapeer County ranks 23 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 88,703 people in 36,980 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $229,100, the median home value sits 22% above the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Lapeer County reports $76,228. Owner-occupancy is 86%, so renters hold about 14% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1978, about 45 years ago.

How do I reach the Lapeer County Register of Deeds?

Staff serve the public weekdays, opening at eight and closing at half past four. The office page carries a Location Directions link for the street address, and every deed, mortgage and discharge touching Lapeer County land is filed there. Its mission statement promises prompt handling of papers that satisfy the Michigan Recording Act.

Payment can be cash, a check or money order made out to Lapeer County Register of Deeds, or a card used at the counter itself. Title companies and attorneys who file in volume are pointed to Simplifile for electronic submission, and that vendor's help line is 800.460.5657.

A homeowner bringing in a deed should have it signed in dark ink, with each signer's name printed or stamped under the signature, the buyer's street address shown, and the drafter's name and business address on the page.

What are the recording charges at the Lapeer County office?

The flat charge is $30 for each document, however long it runs. A sale adds transfer tax and, for most warranty forms, a tax certificate. The office publishes every figure on one sheet.

ItemChargeAuthority named on the sheet
Entering and recording one document$30.00MCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3.00MCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00MCL 211.135
County transfer tax$1.10 per thousand dollarsMCL 207.504
State transfer tax$7.50 per thousand dollarsMCL 207.525
Copy of a real estate record$1.00 a pageOffice schedule
Certifying a document$5.00 eachOffice schedule
Fixture filing on the standard form$30.00Office schedule

Source: Lapeer County Register of Deeds, Schedule of Fees.

Which Lapeer County deeds must the treasurer certify first?

The schedule singles out warranty deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments and any deed containing a covenant of warranty. Each one has to be certified by the County Treasurer ahead of recording.

The certificate costs $5, so allow time for that stop ahead of the recording counter. If your paper is some other kind of instrument, ask the treasurer's office whether it also requires one. If the parcel carries unpaid back taxes, talk with the treasurer about what must be cleared before a certificate is issued.

What will a Lapeer County seller owe in transfer tax?

Combined, the two rates come to $8.60 for every thousand dollars of value. Picture a $250,000 house: the county takes $275, the state takes $1,875, and the seller hands over $2,150 at recording.

The instrument must show the full value of the land and buildings, or carry an attached affidavit that gives it. In MCL 207.504 the county rate is written as 55 cents per $500 or fraction, the same thing as the $1.10 per thousand on the local sheet. The Transfer Tax page on the county site links two exemption lists. The county statute, MCL 207.505, excuses several kinds of paper:

  • anything where the money involved is under $100;
  • a mortgage or other security paper, and its later assignment or release;
  • leases, plus land contracts while legal title stays with the seller;
  • a spouse-to-spouse conveyance that sets up or ends ownership by the entireties;
  • a quitclaim that merely fixes a defect in a title already held;
  • a court order moving title with no dollar amount attached.

What happens to the tax bill once the deed is recorded?

Nothing changes automatically. The County Treasurer's FAQ says that office cannot take a name off a bill, so the new owner or the seller has to carry the deed or other proof of transfer to the assessor in the township, city or village where the property lies.

Until the assessor updates the record, the old name may keep receiving the July 1 and December 1 bills from the local treasurer. A bill that goes unpaid after March 1 moves to the county as delinquent, with the 4% administration fee and interest attached, so buyers and sellers should settle who is watching the mailbox before the closing date. Mortgage lenders sometimes miss a payment, and the treasurer's position is that the owner remains responsible for confirming the bill was paid.

Why might a Lapeer County deed be turned away?

A register may not receive a paper that skips the formatting rules in MCL 565.201. The usual causes are small and fixable before you arrive.

  • A printed name that differs from the name in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Pages with too little white space: the first page needs about two and a half inches clear at the top.
  • Type under 10-point, or ink that is not black on white stock.
  • Full Social Security numbers left visible, when only the last four digits may show.
  • No English translation attached to a foreign-language document.
  • A first line that fails to name the one recordable event the paper evidences.

After a paper is accepted, the law presumes it complies, and a register cannot reject a conforming instrument because of its content.

What other fees can a Michigan register of deeds charge?

MCL 600.2567 allows extras that the Lapeer sheet does not itemize. A name search can be billed at fifty cents for each year covered, with a $5 floor, and any other filing or lookup is $1 per paper.

  • $5 of each $30 recording fee is set aside for the county's automation fund.
  • The statute counts a page as one side of a sheet 8.5 inches wide and 11 to 14 inches long.
  • Foreclosure deeds and forfeiture certificates that a treasurer files can be settled after the sale on a delayed schedule instead of at the counter.

Phone the office before a research trip and ask how a search request would be priced.

How do I guard against deed fraud in Lapeer County?

Enroll in the free email alert offered by the office. Every filing made in a name you list sends a message, so a forged deed or loan against your house gets noticed early.

The office page announces the signup at the top, and a one page form sits on the county website. Sellers should also confirm that the name on their title matches the name they plan to sign, because a mismatch with the acknowledgment is one of the statute's own grounds for refusal.

What is Lapeer County like for sellers?

Lapeer County is one of five counties on the Thumb of Michigan, and it is more rural than Oakland County next door. It spans 663 square miles, with 20 of them water. The Flint River's headwaters sit in Columbiaville.

  • I-69 crosses the county from east to west, while M-24 is the north-south route through the City of Lapeer.
  • M-53 serves Imlay City, and M-90 passes through North Branch.
  • Sanilac, Tuscola, St. Clair, Genesee, Macomb and Oakland counties surround it.

The census counted 52,317 residents in 1970, 70,038 in 1980 and 87,904 in 2000. By 2020 it was 88,619, with an estimate of 89,516 for 2025.

More questions about Lapeer County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing fee for a deed in Lapeer County?

Thirty dollars per document, however many pages. A warranty deed adds a $5 certificate from the County Treasurer, and the seller owes transfer tax at $1.10 plus $7.50 for every thousand dollars of value.

What are the office hours for the Lapeer County Register of Deeds?

Monday to Friday, opening at eight and closing at half past four. The Location Directions link on the office page gives the street address.

Is a credit card accepted at the Lapeer County Register of Deeds?

Yes, at the counter only. The office also takes cash, checks and money orders, and checks are written to Lapeer County Register of Deeds.

Who covers transfer tax in a Lapeer County sale?

The seller. The deed shows the total value or has a valuation affidavit attached, and the exemptions under MCL 207.505 apply to the county portion.

Can I be warned if someone records a deed in my name?

Yes. The office runs a free email service that alerts you to any filing under a name you enter.

Who records deeds in Leelanau County

  • Leelanau County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Official office for recording instruments transferring/encumbering property; self-service records on vendor domain tylerhost.net (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Leelanau County?
We buy Leelanau County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where is the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?

The office is at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, in Suttons Bay, and its phone number is 231-256-9682. Email goes to rod@leelanau.gov. The county seat moved from Leland to a site in Suttons Bay Township in 2008.

The Register of Deeds is a constitutional office that dates to Michigan's first constitution in 1835, and Leelanau County has had fifteen registers since 1863. Records go back to that year. Documents received after 4:30 p.m. are held until the next business day, so a deed dropped off late in the afternoon waits for the next business day.

The office records instruments that transfer or encumber real property, and it cannot judge whether a document is legally sufficient or what its author intended. Michigan is a race-notice state, so papers are recorded in the order they are first presented, and first in time is first in line.

What should a seller know about Leelanau County's geography?

The whole of Leelanau County is the Leelanau Peninsula, a triangle of land about 30 miles long that reaches into Lake Michigan from the western Lower Peninsula and is about 25 miles wide at its base. The county's total area is 2,532 square miles, but only 347 of them are land, because 86% of the area is water.

It has the second highest share of water of any county in the country. Lake Leelanau is the largest inland lake, Glen Lake lies inside the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, and North and South Manitou Islands lie within the county line. Part of Traverse City falls inside Leelanau, and Elmwood Charter Township, on the southeastern edge, is the most urbanized piece. The villages are Empire, Northport and Suttons Bay, and ten civil townships cover the rest, including Leland, Glen Arbor, Solon and Centerville. The 2020 census counted 22,301 people, up from 21,708 in 2010.

Leelanau became its own organized county in 1863 and touches other Michigan counties by land only at Grand Traverse and Benzie. Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore was established in 1970. The Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians occupies scattered areas within Suttons Bay Township. Every deed for any of this ground is filed in the Suttons Bay office.

What makes a deed recordable in Leelanau County?

The office accepts only documents with original signatures, and it does not allow digital recording. It has kept the wet ink requirement on purpose, because it has stopped fraud attempts that way.

  • A court document must be certified by the court. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the same applies to a death certificate.
  • Under MCL 565.201 each signer's name is printed, typed or stamped beneath the signature, and the signature is in black or dark blue ink.
  • The notary's name appears on the same page near the signature.
  • Each grantee's street address, or post office address, appears on a deed.
  • The drafter's name and business address appear on instruments signed after January 1, 1964.

The office does not supply forms or give legal help. For drafting it points people to an attorney or title company, and it does not run title searches.

What does recording cost in Leelanau County?

State law sets recording at $30 for any document, whatever its length, and the office accepts cash, checks, debit cards and credit cards. One check can cover recording for several documents, along with transfer tax, a tax certificate and any copy fees.

ChargeAmountWhere it comes from
Recording any document$30.00MCL 600.2567
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00MCL 600.2567
Copy, in office or online$1.00 per pageRegister of Deeds page
Certified recorded document$5.00MCL 600.2567
Card convenience fee on $1 to $50$2.00Register of Deeds page
Card convenience fee above $50.012.95%Register of Deeds page

Source: Leelanau County Register of Deeds and the Michigan Legislature.

How do I work out transfer tax on a Leelanau County sale?

Counties of this size levy 55 cents per $500 of value, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. Any leftover fraction counts as a whole $500 unit. Take a $400,000 price: $440 goes to the county, $3,000 to the state, $3,440 overall, due from the seller when the deed is filed.

Leelanau's own guidance adds several points. The deed has to show the total consideration. A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit may be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says so. If land straddles two counties, the price is divided between the parcels and each county is paid its share. Stamps must be purchased in the county that holds the land. An easement is taxable, and a foreclosure instrument carries county tax based on the stated sale price.

Exemptions listed in MCL 207.505 include transfers for under $100, instruments given as security, leases, land contracts that have not yet passed title, spousal conveyances creating a tenancy by the entireties and corrective quitclaims.

How do I search Leelanau County land records?

Use the county's Self Service site, the two public workstations in the Suttons Bay office, or the vault. Names go in last name first with no punctuation, and the search needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year.

  • The free search shows index information only, and each image costs $1.00 per page.
  • Subscription passes run $5 for 15 minutes, $15 for a day, $200 a month and $1,100 for six months.
  • A parcel number search requires the county prefix 45 and the dashes, as in 45-000-000-000-00, and only documents that list the number turn up.
  • Online, only deed records are available before January 1, 1972. Other older records are searched in the office.
  • The historical grantor and grantee indexes went online in October 2025.

Try spelling variants, such as Richard, Rick and Dick, because the office records names exactly as written on each document.

What happens to the record after a payoff, a death or a sheriff's sale?

The office only records, so it does not issue a replacement deed after any of these events. Your original deed stays the deed to the property.

  • After a mortgage payoff, the lender sends a discharge or satisfaction of mortgage. No new deed follows, because the deed was delivered when you bought.
  • When a co-owner dies, bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee. It shows that the deceased person no longer holds an interest.
  • A sheriff's deed is recorded when it is submitted after the auction closes. The office is not the place to redeem; the attorney named on the sheriff's deed handles that.
  • If you have lost your deed, a recorded copy is available at the office, and copy fees apply.

How can Leelanau County owners watch for property fraud?

Subscribe to Fraud Notify, which costs nothing. It sends an email whenever a filing appears under a name you register, and the office has reported several attempts to list owners' property fraudulently that were stopped once owners were told.

If you see a neighbor's lot offered for sale, ask the owner. The office also warns about mail that looks official and charges for copies of your own deed. A 2016 Michigan law set rules for such mailings, and a copy from the office is $1.00 a page.

More questions about Leelanau County, MI Register of Deeds

How can I phone the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?

231-256-9682. The office is in Suttons Bay at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, and also takes questions by email at rod@leelanau.gov.

Does Leelanau County record deeds electronically?

No. The office requires original wet ink signatures and does not allow digital recording, to make deed fraud harder.

What total transfer tax applies to a Leelanau County sale?

The two rates add up to $4.30 per $500 of value, 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state. The seller pays when the deed is recorded.

Will Leelanau County record a copy of a death certificate?

Only a certified one. The office will not record a true copy, and it does not issue a new deed afterward, because it only records.

Where can I obtain a copy of my Leelanau County deed?

Go to the Suttons Bay office, ring 231-256-9682 or use the Self Service website. Each page costs $1.00.

Lenawee County ranks 21 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 98,823 people in 43,747 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $181,100, the median home value sits 3% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Lenawee County reports $67,013. Owner-occupancy is 79%, so renters hold about 21% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1969, about 54 years ago.

Who keeps property records for Lenawee County land?

The Register of Deeds in Adrian, the county seat, receives, records and digitally stores every legal document that affects real estate in Lenawee County. That covers deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens, surveys and land corners. Staff check each item against Michigan's recording rules, record it, and send the original back by U.S. mail to whoever presented it unless instructed otherwise.

Lenawee was carved from Monroe County in 1822 and organized in 1826. It spans roughly 750 square miles of land, counted 99,423 people in 2020 and hosts Adrian College and Siena Heights University. Whether a house stands near Adrian, in Tecumseh or on a farm road in a rural township, the deed goes to this one county office, because Michigan hands assessing, zoning and building rules to individual cities and townships and leaves deed recording with the county.

The 2020 census counted 43,577 housing units in the county, with 11.5 percent vacant and 77.3 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners. One local habit shows up in addresses: in the townships, north-south roads are called highways and east-west roads are called roads, so a newcomer reading a map has to watch which word follows the road name. The legal description in the deed gives the exact boundaries.

The office supplies no forms, and its employees are barred from advising on or helping complete a document. Content and intent are the preparer's responsibility, so closings usually run through a title agent or a lawyer.

What fees apply when Lenawee County records a document?

Recording runs $30.00 per document, whether it is one page or twenty, according to the county's answers to common questions. A page copy at the counter is $1.00. The counter takes checks, cash and cards, and cards carry an access fee.

Charges published by the Lenawee County Register of Deeds
ItemChargeSource
Recording a document$30.00 flatCounty FAQ
Counter copy$1.00 per pageCounty FAQ
Escrow account to view and print online$100.00 to openCounty FAQ
Deed copy direct from the officeAs little as $2.00Register of Deeds page

Owners sometimes receive letters from commercial services offering certified copies of their deeds by mail for as much as $83.00 each. The county flags these and points out that the identical record is available from its own counter for as little as $2.00. Check the county page before paying a mailer.

Which mistakes get a Lenawee County deed bounced?

The county posts 17 statutory requirements and treats them as a minimum, since some instruments carry extra rules. These are the ones that most often matter on a home sale:

  • Signatures must be original, with names typed or printed beneath, and those names must agree with the notary block (MCL 565.201).
  • Page one needs a 2.5 inch blank band across its upper edge, and all remaining edges need half an inch.
  • Use black ink in at least 10-point type on white 20-pound paper that is at least letter size and no longer than legal.
  • The first printed line has to state the recordable event, and one instrument may evidence only one event.
  • Include the grantee's street or post office address, plus drafter identification with a name and address.
  • A Michigan-signed deed needs acknowledgment by a judge, a court clerk or a notary public.
  • Social Security numbers may appear only as the final four digits.

A deed that says "survivor" must be backed by a certified death certificate that is recorded with it or already of record and cited by liber and page. A court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

Is transfer tax owed on a Lenawee County house sale?

On nearly every sale for money, yes. Michigan's state transfer tax attaches to deeds given for consideration. Under MCL 207.523, the seller is the liable party, and the money is paid to the county treasurer for the parcel's location. A separate county transfer tax comes from Act 134 of 1966. Phone the Register of Deeds for the combined figure on your price. Closing agents ordinarily subtract it from the seller's proceeds.

The statutes also list transfers that escape the tax. A few that touch home owners:

  • Deeds with consideration under $100.
  • Gifts of a home by an individual to a child or grandchild (state exemption, MCL 207.526).
  • Court orders that move title without naming a price.
  • Corrective quitclaim deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Land contracts, until legal title actually passes.
  • Mortgage foreclosures and the deeds that replace them.

Whichever exemption applies has to be cited correctly in the deed itself, so run the citation past your closing agent.

How can I search land records in Adrian and around Lenawee County?

The county offers an online search with two doors. A text search reads typed or legible text and works on a phone. A second tool serves experienced users and searches by name, recorded date, and liber and page; it runs best on a computer in Chrome or Edge with pop-ups allowed. Results are for information, and document images must be purchased.

Sellers can use the name search to see what stands against the property before listing: the vesting deed, open mortgages, an old lien that was paid but never discharged, or a death certificate that was never recorded. Buyers' title agents run the same search, so a problem found early costs less time.

Anyone worried about deed fraud can enroll in the free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or by phone at 1-800-728-3858. It sends a notice whenever a document carrying the owner's name is recorded.

Where does recording fit in a Lenawee County sale?

It comes last. At closing the title agent collects the signed, notarized deed, pays the recording fee and any transfer tax, and sends the package to the county. Until the deed is recorded and indexed, the sale is not visible in the public record.

Property tax enters the same week. The year after a transfer, the new owner's taxable value is uncapped, and the buyer files a property transfer affidavit with the local assessor. Challenging an assessment starts at the March Board of Review in your city or township and can continue to the Michigan Tax Tribunal, per the county's equalization answers. Owners who need more time on summer taxes are sent by the county treasurer's page to the state's deferment rules.

A house with deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate behind it can sell for cash with no lender repair list. The recording steps are identical in every case, and the $30.00 fee is the same for a one-page quitclaim as for a long deed with exhibits. After the office indexes the instrument, request the recorded deed and its recording details from your closing agent after indexing.

More questions about Lenawee County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is recording in Lenawee County?

The county lists $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. Transfer tax is a separate charge that depends on the sale price.

Can Lenawee County staff draft my deed?

No. Staff do not provide forms and cannot advise on or complete a document for you. Hire a title agent or attorney to draft it.

Who pays Lenawee County transfer tax?

The seller, under MCL 207.523, with payment due to the county treasurer for the property's location. Settlement statements normally show it as a seller charge.

What is the cheapest way to obtain a deed copy?

Ask the county office itself. A counter copy is $1.00 per page, and the office says a deed can run as little as $2.00, versus as much as $83.00 from commercial mailers.

Why would a Lenawee County deed be rejected?

Typical causes are photocopied signatures, narrow margins, a missing drafter address, names that differ from the notary block, or type that is too small. Compare the document against the county's 17-point list.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording requirements: only original signed document may be scanned for e-Recording via accredited service (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Online deeds search charge $1.00/page plus fee (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Livingston County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 195,143 people and 79,520 housing units in Livingston County, which ranks 10 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $331,100, which is 77% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $101,315; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 13% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 87% owner-occupied.

Where is the Livingston County Register of Deeds office?

The office sits in the Historical Courthouse at 200 E Grand River Ave, Howell, the county seat. Call (517) 546-0270. The counter opens weekdays at 8:00 a.m. and shuts at 4:30 p.m., with county holidays off.

Most documents never reach the counter. Title companies and attorneys send them electronically through four certified vendors: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A few instruments cannot go that way, including deeds that come with valuation affidavits, plats, and master deeds with large drawings. Those must be brought in or mailed on paper.

Livingston County sits in southeast Michigan along I-96, US 23 and M-59, with 585 square miles of area and a 2020 census population of 193,866. Roughly 86 percent of occupied homes belong to their residents, which keeps deeds flowing through this office steadily. The Census Bureau counted Brighton, Howell and nearby South Lyon as one contiguous urbanized area, and employers such as Tribar, PepsiCo and Citizens Insurance anchor the local economy. Sellers outside those towns, in the rural townships, record at the same counter. The county is laid out in 16 townships of 36 one-mile sections each, which is why legal descriptions on a Livingston deed read as a section number plus a starting corner.

Which fees does the Livingston County office charge?

Every recording carries a flat $30.00 charge, and $4 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. If one instrument assigns or discharges several earlier records, each reference past the first adds $3.

Livingston County Register of Deeds fee schedule from the county FAQ
ServiceFee
Recording a document$30.00 flat
Each extra liber and page cross-reference$3.00
Tax certification, first 25 parcel numbers$5.00, then $0.20 per added number
Fixture filing$30 per document
Copy of a recorded page$1.00 ($2.00 for plat or condo drawings)
Certifying a copy$5.00, all pages must be bought
Tract index use, unless it is your own property$10 per hour

Recording fees and transfer tax are never put on a charge account. Pay with cash, check or card; a card adds a service fee.

How does the office calculate transfer tax?

If a deed states a price, the office takes transfer tax the moment it records. The county describes the total as .086 of the amount, meaning $8.60 per $1,000: $1.10 per $1,000 to the county and $7.50 per $1,000 to the state. The grantor normally bears it. Before the math, the price rounds up to the next $500 step, so $100,000.01 is treated as $100,500.

Applied to a $300,000 price, the total is $2,580. Land that straddles two counties needs the price divided by county on the deed itself.

Exemptions exist. A deed may be exempt from the state share alone or from both shares, never from the county share by itself, and the exemption cited must fit the facts on the page. Mistakes the office sees:

  • Claiming the family-gift exemptions when a trust is the grantor; an individual has to be the grantor.
  • Assuming a church is automatically exempt.
  • Assuming a sheriff's deed escapes county tax. It is always exempt from the state portion, but exempt from the county portion only when the mortgage is federally backed.
  • Citing the under-$100 exemption while the deed shows a $5,000 price.

What does a tax certification cover?

A tax certification is a Treasurer's sticker showing that taxes are paid up and that the legal description matches the township tax roll. It is part of what makes a warranty deed a warranty deed. The county requires it before recording warranty deeds, any deed with "warrant" in the conveyance line, land contracts, assignments of land contract (except those given as collateral), master deeds, and master deed amendments that add property to a condominium.

For a mailed document, enclose the $5.00 and the office gets the certification for you. An e-recorded document that needs one goes through the document router so both departments receive it. The county treasurer's page lists tax clearance of deeds among its duties, so a seller with unpaid taxes learns of it at this stage at the latest.

How do copies, searches and corrections work here?

Searching the index by name is free online. Viewing a page costs $1 plus a convenience fee that covers card processing, and a link arrives immediately. Certified copies, death certificates, tax liens, condo master deeds and documents over 75 pages are mailed after purchase. Records are imaged and indexed back to November 7, 1980 (liber 1000), with earlier books imaged or kept in hard copy.

  • You cannot change a signed, notarized or recorded deed. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed signed by the current owners.
  • When a joint tenant or spouse dies, recording the death certificate shows the survivor as sole owner without a new deed.
  • An enhanced life estate (ladybird) deed becomes proof of ownership once both death certificates are recorded.
  • Paying off a mortgage produces a discharge, not a new deed.
  • A rejected document comes back with a letter listing the reasons, and it can be corrected and resubmitted.

Paper filings by mail or at the counter must come with a return envelope or $3 for postage. Giving an email address instead brings the recorded copy back at no charge, usually the same day.

Can the Livingston County office tell me when my house was built?

No. Deeds describe land and a legal description and rarely say whether a building stood on it, so the office points owners to the city or township assessor. The Howell Carnegie Library reference desk, at (517) 546-0720, can search its archives, and the county Plat Books for 1875, 1895 and 1915 show homesteads and, in 1875, the houses in the towns.

Staff offer one rough method for older homes: a deed whose price is far below a mortgage recorded the same day often marks an owner who was about to build. Name indexes go back to the first recorded documents in 1836 and 1837, and the grantor and grantee indexes reflect documents listed in the tract index. For a sale, a seller who wants proof of a renovation or a permit should ask the local building department instead.

What should a seller verify before the sale closes?

Have the closing agent pull the recorded chain: vesting deed, recorded death certificate if any, mortgage discharges and liens. The Register of Deeds says it cannot verify ownership, since unrecorded land contracts or deeds can affect it, and its staff do not run title searches or give a guarantee. Title companies do that work and can also check probate court records the recorder lacks.

Per the county Equalization Department, the buyer owes the local assessor a property transfer affidavit within 45 days or faces $5 a day in fines, up to $200, and the home's taxable value is uncapped the next year. A seller who knows the taxes will jump for the buyer can say so up front, because it affects what the buyer can afford.

Back taxes, estate paperwork and repair needs are the usual reasons owners ask for a cash sale. Recording works the same whoever the buyer is.

More questions about Livingston County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the Livingston County recording fee?

The flat fee is $30.00 per document, including $4 for the state survey and remonumentation fund. Extra cross-references cost $3 each, and transfer tax is separate.

Who bears transfer tax here?

Usually the seller, who is the grantor. It is collected at recording: $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, using a price rounded up to a $500 step.

Can I record a photocopy of a deed?

No. Only documents with original signatures can be recorded, and even electronic services must scan originals. Court orders, death certificates and surveys must be certified versions.

How do I put a family member on my deed?

The current owners must sign a new deed conveying the property to everyone who should hold title. A signed or recorded deed cannot be altered, and a lawyer or title agent can draft the new one.

Does the office run title searches?

No. The office does not do title searches or furnish abstracts and cannot guarantee results. Title companies perform and insure searches, while the office teaches the public how to use its index.

Where do Mackinac County deeds get filed?

The county's Register of Deeds works from the first floor of the Mackinac County Courthouse at 100 S. Marley in St. Ignace, and the phone line is (906) 643-7306. The County Treasurer is one floor up (second floor, Room 30, phone (906) 643-7318), and the Equalization Department sits in the Courthouse Annex, Room 120, at (906) 643-7310. A seller who needs a deed filed, a tax certificate and a parcel record can finish all three errands in one courthouse complex.

The county is mostly water. Of its 2,101 square miles, 1,079 are lake, because Mackinac County has shoreline on both Lake Huron and Lake Michigan at the Straits of Mackinac. The 2020 census counted 10,834 people. St. Ignace is the seat and the northern end of the Mackinac Bridge, and Mackinac Island is the other city. Naubinway is a census-designated place, and the Sault Tribe holds two small territories, one near St. Ignace and one in Clark Township.

Getting around shapes how people sell here. I-75 and US 2 serve the mainland, ferries run from St. Ignace and Mackinaw City to Mackinac Island, and M-185 around the island bans all motor vehicles except emergency and service vehicles. The nearest scheduled airline service is at Chippewa County International in Sault Ste. Marie or Pellston Regional. Owners who live far from the courthouse should use the mail option below.

Can a Mackinac County deed be sent in by mail or e-recording?

Yes to both. Per the register's recording page, nobody has to appear in person, and documents with the right fee can go by mail, UPS or FedEx. Electronic filers can route through CSC E-Recording Solutions, Simplifile or EPN E Recording Partners Network, each with its own price list.

Staff offer a service most counties skip: they will look over a draft before you submit it. The office cannot write a private legal document or advise you, but it will check a draft against the recording rules. That can save a round trip across the Straits. Other handy points from the office's notes:

  • Include a self-addressed return envelope so the original comes back sooner.
  • In a deed the grantor is the seller and the grantee is the buyer.
  • Copy the legal description from the prior deed or a new survey, and avoid the shortened version printed on a tax statement unless someone has verified it.
  • Blanket assignments and blanket releases are accepted.
  • Forms are sold at office supply stores or available online, and a local title company may supply one.

What fees apply at the Mackinac County register?

One flat charge covers any document up to any length. Under MCL 600.2567 that is $30.00, in force since October 1, 2016. The office's fee page notes that $4 of it goes to the state survey and remonumentation fund. A deed with a warranty clause also needs a treasurer's certificate for $5.00, and the register suggests a single $35.00 check. If you mail the deed, its staff pick up the certificate for you.

Mackinac County Register of Deeds charges, from the office's fee pages
What you are buyingPrice
Filing a deed, mortgage or other instrument$30.00
Each extra instrument released in one document$3.00
Tax certificate for a warranty clause$5.00
Certifying a copy$5.00
Plain copy$1.00 a page
Name search$0.50 a year searched, $5.00 floor
State or federal tax lien search$3.00 a name

A certified copy must reproduce the whole document. The fee page also mentions a 2016 push by the state's registers of deeds to stop private companies from selling deeds to residents at inflated prices. The office's own rate is the page price above.

How much transfer tax will a Mackinac County seller owe?

Seller-side transfer tax runs $4.30 for every $500 of price, rounded up for any leftover amount. That is the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) plus the state's $3.75, which the register lists in its FAQ. The statute puts the burden on the grantor.

Try an $820,000 Straits-view property: 1,640 units of $500, so $902 to the county and $6,150 to the state, or $7,052 combined. A modest $140,000 mainland house comes to $1,204. The deed must state the full price on its face, or a valuation affidavit goes with it at no filing charge, and the deed must say the affidavit is attached. Tax stamps are bought where the land sits, and land in two counties needs a stated split.

Exemptions appear on the register's county and state exemption pages and in MCL 207.526. Gifts to children and grandchildren, foreclosure transfers and court-ordered transfers are among them. An exemption has to be written on the face of the deed, so settle it with your closing agent before signing.

What if the house is behind on a mortgage or taxes?

Mackinac County's register and treasurer jointly run a foreclosure prevention page, and it explains a ranking that surprises many owners: a tax foreclosure takes precedence over a mortgage foreclosure. Once a mortgage foreclosure starts, the office says the owner keeps control of the property for 6 months, or 12 months if the parcel is larger than 3 acres, and can refinance or sell during that time.

The page also offers a set of practical steps:

  • Call the lender early and read every letter it sends.
  • Look for a HUD-approved housing counselor, since counseling is free or low cost.
  • Contact the Michigan State Housing Development Authority about its Save the Dream program.
  • Do not pay a company that promises to stop a foreclosure, and never sign a paper that appoints someone to act for you.

On the tax side, the County Treasurer collects delinquent property taxes for the local units and handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties under Public Act 123. The Equalization Department hosts a property and delinquent tax search and a list of each local unit's assessor and treasurer. A sale that pays off the balance before the redemption window ends is one way out.

What does a recorded deed change for property tax in Mackinac County?

The register notifies the assessor of recorded transfers each month, and the new owner must also file with the local assessor within 45 days under MCL 211.27a. A transfer of ownership resets the following year's taxable value to the state equalized value. Moves to a spouse, and residential moves to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild with no commercial use, do not count.

The statute counts a rental of fewer than 15 days in a year as non-commercial, which matters for a cottage that sees a few weekend guests. Longer rentals fall outside that carve-out. Ask the assessor for the parcel's current taxable value before you list.

The register also processes passport applications Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., which is useful to know if a seller who is relocating needs travel documents at the same visit.

More questions about Mackinac County, MI Register of Deeds

Is it $30 or $35 to file a deed in Mackinac County?

It is $35.00 when the deed contains a warranty clause, made up of the $30.00 filing fee and the $5.00 treasurer's certificate, and $30.00 when it does not. Each extra instrument released in one document adds $3.00.

Who writes the deed for a Mackinac County sale?

A title company or attorney should draft it. Register staff cannot draft private legal documents, though they will review a draft for compliance with the recording rules before you submit it.

What is the combined transfer tax rate for a Mackinac County home?

The combined rate is $4.30 per $500 of price or fraction. A $300,000 sale gives 600 units, so $330 to the county and $2,250 to the state, for $2,580 in total.

Who runs the foreclosure auction in Mackinac County?

The County Treasurer, at 100 S. Marley, Room 30, handles the summer auction of foreclosed properties. Call (906) 643-7318, or use the property and delinquent tax search on the Equalization Department page.

How long can an owner stay after a Mackinac County mortgage foreclosure?

Six months, or twelve months if the parcel has more than 3 acres, according to the county's foreclosure prevention page. During that window the owner can refinance or sell.

Households here earn a median $76,399; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 25% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 75% owner-occupied.

Where does the Macomb County Register of Deeds operate?

The register works inside the county Clerk's office at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens, MI 48043, staffed on weekdays until 4:15 p.m. after an 8 a.m. start. The phone is 586-469-7953 and the email is registerofdeeds@macombgov.org. An online booking tool lets you reserve a visit, and the same page links a land records search, a status page for documents already submitted, and a mail-in request for certified copies.

Macomb is a charter county on the eastern edge of Michigan. It touches Lake St. Clair, borders Detroit to the south, and had 881,217 residents in 2020, the third largest population in the state after Wayne and Oakland. Its 27 cities, townships and villages include Warren, Sterling Heights, St. Clair Shores, Roseville, Eastpointe, Fraser, Utica, Romeo and Armada, with the largest share of people living south of M-59 (Hall Road). I-94 and I-696 cut across the southern part, and Selfridge Air National Guard Base sits at Mount Clemens.

With that many parcels, return times stretch. The office's FAQ says to expect recorded documents back roughly 6 to 8 weeks after the recording date, so cite a correct RETURN TO name and address on page one.

What do deeds and searches cost in Macomb County?

Flat pricing applies: $30 for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified court paper, whatever its page count. A document that releases several instruments adds $3 each after the first. The county says $4 of each fee goes to the state survey fund, with exceptions for fixture filings, liens, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers.

Searches and copies are priced separately, and the schedule includes oddities such as large-format plats and Uniform Commercial Code filings. Plat copies run $3.50 at 11 by 17 inches and $4.50 at 18 by 24, with $2.50 postage if mailed. Fixture filings and UCC terminations are $30 each, the same as a deed. A UCC search is $12 per debtor name, made up of $6 for the name search and $3 each for state and federal tax lien certificates, and a copy of a UCC filing is $2 a page. Personal property financing statements filed after July 1, 2001 go to the state UCC office and do not show up in the register's searches, so the register's results cover fixture filings and similar land-based items.

Macomb County Register of Deeds charges from the county recording fee page
ServiceCharge
Record a deed or mortgage$30
Release or assign extra instruments$3 each after the first
Real estate search, mail or in person$5 minimum
Copy of a real estate record$1 a page
Certified copy$5 a record
UCC search$12 per debtor
Plat copy, 11 by 17$3.50

Which Macomb County deeds need a treasurer's certificate?

Anything carrying a warranty clause. The register's fee page says warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant clause, land contracts and assignments of land contract need certification from the County Treasurer before recording. Since July 1, 2015 the certificate costs $5 for up to five legal descriptions and $0.20 for each extra description. The authority is MCL 211.135.

The Treasurer, at 586-469-5190, confirms that tax is paid up for the five years before the deed date. The Land File office at 586-469-5313 supplies legal descriptions, and the register's FAQ lists the same number plus the local assessor as free sources for a taxpayer's name and address. Questions on transfer tax go to 586-469-5309.

Quitclaim deeds without a warranty covenant skip the certificate. Macomb also posts its own quitclaim form on the register's page, along with a construction lien claim form and a sheriff's deed payoff request. The county says it supplies these forms without any warranty about their legal effect.

Is the register's first-page cover sheet really needed?

It is when page one fails the margin rule. The county's recording requirements say a first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin and a half inch on all other sides. If it falls short, attach a cover page that states the document's title. This matters for older deeds that crowd the top edge.

The county also stresses a few other points:

  • Names typed or stamped under original signatures must match the notary's acknowledgment.
  • A deed must show each grantee's address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Instruments signed before April 16, 2017 had to state the marital status of male grantors.
  • Court orders are recorded only if certified and sealed by the court clerk.
  • A death certificate cannot be attached to another document since September 18, 2018.

Statutory sources are in MCL 565.201, and the county offers a link to common document problems.

How do I change who is on a Macomb County deed?

To add a person, record a quit claim deed, typed or in black ink, signed and notarized. The cost is $30. The register advises hiring an attorney if the goal is to avoid probate. To drop a deceased owner, record a certified copy of the death certificate for $30. The survivorship wording on the deed decides whether probate is still needed.

A paid-off mortgage does not produce a new deed. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage for recording, and the deed you received at purchase stays your title. Lost your copy? A recorded copy is just as good as the original, and you can ask in person, by mail or through the online search.

After any ownership change, the new owner must report it to the local assessor within 45 days. MCL 211.27a treats most deed transfers as a trigger to reset taxable value, with carve-outs for spouses and for residential transfers among close family.

How does a payoff letter work after a Macomb County sheriff's sale?

Someone entitled to redeem after a sheriff's sale can ask the register for a payoff letter for $25, paid with the request form. It is ready after 2 business days, and the form can be mailed or dropped off. The state statute behind it is MCL 600.3240, which lets registers in counties of 750,000 to 1,500,000 people determine the amount using only recorded affidavits, and it frees the county of liability for an incorrect figure.

Redemption itself follows a short checklist:

  • Pay by certified or cashier's check, delivered by 4 p.m. on the last working day of the redemption period.
  • Expect a $5 care and custody fee, already included in a figure from the register.
  • Receive the office's letter confirming that funds arrived.
  • Leave the redemption certificate to the sheriff's deed holder, who drafts and records it.

The register also offers a Fraud Notify alerts system. Owners who sign up are warned when a document is recorded under their names, a safeguard worth having when a house is vacant or being sold.

More questions about Macomb County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the recording charge at the Mount Clemens register of deeds?

It is $30 per document regardless of length. A warranty deed adds the $5 treasurer certificate for up to five legal descriptions, and extra descriptions are $0.20 each.

How soon do recorded Macomb County deeds come back?

Roughly 6 to 8 weeks from the recording date, according to the county's FAQ. A correct RETURN TO name and address on the document helps it reach the right person.

Where can I see whether a Macomb County document has been recorded?

Use the status of recorded documents page on the register's site, or call 586-469-7953. The land records search lets you request copies, and search and copy fees apply.

What does Macomb County charge in transfer tax?

The county rate is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. On a $310,000 sale, 620 units give $341 to the county and $2,325 to the state, or $2,666 combined. Call 586-469-5309 for details.

Can I mail a deed to the Macomb County register?

Yes. The county's FAQ says a completed quit claim deed can be mailed in or brought in for recording, and certified copy requests are accepted through the U.S. Mail.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

The Manistee County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Manistee County

  • Manistee County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30 for all documents regardless of pages (since Oct 1, 2016) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Documents can be mailed for filing; in-person delivery not necessary in most situations (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Manistee County?
We buy Manistee County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

How do I reach the Manistee County Register of Deeds?

The register works from the county courthouse at 415 Third Street, Manistee, MI 49660, and the phone is 231-723-2146. Weekday hours split around lunch: morning window 8:30 to noon, afternoon window 1 to 4. The Treasurer (231-723-3173) and Equalization Department (231-723-5957) share the street address and stay open until 5, so a seller can collect a deed certification and a parcel record in a single trip.

The county is built around Lake Michigan. Of 1,281 square miles, 738 are water, and 25,032 people lived here in 2020. Manistee, the only city, is the seat, and the villages are Bear Lake, Copemish, Eastlake, Kaleva and Onekama. US 31 passes through the city and Bear Lake, M-22 follows the shore through Onekama and Arcadia, and M-55 and M-115 cross inland. The county was organized in 1855 and has a state historical marker for the 1871 Great Fire.

Staff keep the records but will not run title for anyone. The office makes simple searches that reach back 20 years and sends anyone needing a full title search to a title company. A document handed in goes through a seven step recordation process, which usually takes one to two business days.

Do I have to come to the courthouse in Manistee to record a deed?

No. A May 2020 notice on the register's page says mailing completed documents to Register of Deeds, 415 3rd Street, Manistee, MI 49660 is acceptable and legal in almost every situation. Call 231-723-2146 first if you want the cost confirmed. The office accepts every form of payment, and it returns copies to other parties once copy fees are paid and an addressed, stamped envelope is supplied.

E-recording began on December 14, 2017. Manistee's business rules for electronic filers are:

  • Documents are handled between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excepted.
  • Payment goes through ACH, under each vendor's agreement.
  • A vendor that submits documents breaking the Michigan eRecording Standards can lose submission access.
  • The register may reject an electronic document that fails the recording act.
  • Changes to these rules are posted 90 days before they take effect.

The vendors may charge their own processing fees, but the register itself collects only the fees written into law.

What does recording and copying cost in Manistee County?

The county's fee page lists $30 as the flat recording charge, with a $3 extra for each additional instrument released in one document. Copy pricing has its own shape here: $7 buys a two page real estate record copy and each added page is $1. The office requires payment before it releases anything.

Manistee County recording, copy and search charges from the Fees and Requirements page
ServiceCharge
Recording, any length$30
Record copy, first two pages$7
Added pages or extra copies$1 a page
Plat copy$2 a page
Certifying a complete copy$5
Name search$0.50 per year, $5 minimum
Tax lien certificate, state or federal$3 per name
UCC-11 certificate$6 per name
Tax certificate for a warranty deed$5

Online access is a pay for view site covering 1978 forward, and a separate search tool covers 1856 through 1991. The vault is open to the public for those who prefer to dig through the books.

Why does a warranty deed in Manistee County go to the Treasurer first?

Manistee's routing is unusual. You hand a warranty deed, a land contract, an assignment with a warranty clause or a condominium master deed to the County Treasurer for certification, and the Treasurer forwards it to the register with the fees. The register does not send papers back to the Treasurer, and an uncertified instrument is returned to whoever sent it. The legal basis is MCL 211.135, and the certificate costs $5.

The Treasurer's office also keeps tax histories on real property, handles Principal Residence Exemption audits, and bills or refunds for board of review changes. That makes it the right stop for a payoff question. If a quitclaim deed has no warranty covenant, the statute does not require the certificate.

The county posts a property foreclosure timeline for tax delinquency under Public Act 123. For 2024 taxes, summer bills went out July 1, 2024. City summer taxes were due August 20, township and village summer taxes September 14, and winter taxes February 14, 2025. Unpaid township and city taxes moved to the County Treasurer on March 1, 2025 with a 4% fee and 1% monthly interest, and foreclosure for those 2024 taxes lands in 2027.

How does a tax foreclosure play out in Manistee County?

After forfeiture on March 1 of the second year, the 2024 timeline stacks on several charges:

  • $175 for the title search, $60 for recording and $7.10 for notice.
  • Interest at 1.5% a month, applied back to the prior year.
  • $45 for a site inspection in June.
  • $50 for publication in December.

Notice runs in the Manistee News Advocate twice in January, and the Treasurer holds a show cause hearing. The circuit court enters judgment in February. Taxes can be paid through March 31, 2027, and foreclosure becomes final the next day.

Tax-foreclosed property in the county goes to an online auction run by a contractor, Title Check, LLC. The county says the auction happens once a year, typically in August or September. The 2026 schedule opened with the minimum bid auction on August 27, then a re-offer round with sealed bids due September 25 and a no reserve round with sealed bids due October 30.

A former owner can file a Notice of Intention to Claim Interest in Foreclosure Sales Proceeds (Form 5743), due July 1 in the foreclosure year under the 2024 timeline, and later a court motion to claim remaining proceeds. A seller with unpaid taxes should settle them before forfeiture, while a normal sale is still possible.

What changes in property tax after a Manistee County sale?

The Equalization Department keeps the tax rolls up to date for transfers, principal residence and agricultural exemptions, and uncapping. It does not set or change an individual assessment, since its role is to survey classes of property across the city and townships. Under MCL 211.27a, a transfer of ownership lifts taxable value to the state equalized value for the following year, so a buyer's first bill can exceed what the seller paid. The buyer reports the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days.

Transfer tax is separate and falls on the seller. The register's FAQ states $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, with a $100 floor. On a $265,000 sale that is 530 units, which means $291.50 county and $1,987.50 state, or $2,279 together. The register points to the legislature's exemption lists for transfers that owe nothing, such as family transfers of the kinds those lists cover.

Check the exemption wording with your title company before the deed is signed, since an exemption has to be claimed on the document.

More questions about Manistee County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the total cost to file a warranty deed in Manistee County?

Plan on $35, which is the $30 recording charge plus the $5 treasurer certification. A document that releases several instruments adds $3 for each one after the first.

When is the Manistee County courthouse register office closed during the day?

The lunch hour, noon to 1 p.m., is the gap. Doors are open for the morning and afternoon windows listed above, weekdays only.

Can Manistee County staff find the owner or run a title for my house?

Staff can do simple searches back 20 years, but they will not run a full title. For that you need a title company, and the office says it cannot give legal advice.

How is the Manistee County tax auction run?

It is online and held once a year, usually in August or September, through Title Check, LLC. The county's 2026 schedule had a minimum bid round on August 27 and later re-offer and no reserve rounds.

What is the transfer tax on a $200,000 Manistee County sale?

It is $1,720: $220 for the county at $0.55 per $500 and $1,500 for the state at $3.75 per $500. The seller owes it unless the deed is exempt.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

The Marquette County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Marquette County

  • Marquette County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • 234 W. Baraga Avenue, Marquette, MI 49855; 906-225-8415; Mon-Fri 8-5 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • All documents cost $30.00 to record regardless of pages (includes remonumentation and automation fees) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Public document search has $8.75 per search fee (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Marquette County?
We buy Marquette County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Marquette County by the numbers

Marquette County has about 66,430 residents and 33,553 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 30 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $202,000, 8% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $64,675, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 71% of occupied homes and renters in 29%. The median home was built in 1971, about 52 years ago.

Where do you take a deed in Marquette County?

Deeds go to the Register of Deeds at 234 W. Baraga Avenue, Marquette, MI 49855, and the counter phone is (906) 225-8415. The county posts weekday hours of 8 to 5. Documents sent through an e-recording vendor can be submitted around the clock, though staff work them between 8 and 4.

The county site traces the office to Michigan's first constitution, in 1835, and spells out why order matters. Michigan runs on a race-notice rule, so whichever buyer records first outranks a later claimant. Documents are processed in the sequence presented, and that is the reason closings tend to record on funding day.

Three desks at the Baraga Avenue courthouse touch most house sales here:

  • The Register of Deeds, for the deed itself, mortgage releases and copies
  • The County Treasurer, at (906) 225-8425, for tax history and delinquent real property bills
  • Equalization and Tax Roll, at (906) 225-8405, for ownership records and parcel maps

What kind of county is Marquette for someone selling a home?

Marquette County is big and thinly settled. It holds 1,808 square miles of land, the most of any Michigan county, with Lake Superior along its north edge and the Huron Mountains inside it. About 47 percent of its 3,425 total square miles is water. The three cities are Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee, and Northern Michigan University, founded in 1899, sits in the county seat.

The Census Bureau counted 66,017 residents in April 2020 and estimated 68,064 by July 2025, which makes this the most populous county in the Upper Peninsula. Federal survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show owners valuing a typical house at $216,500, with 69.6 percent of homes lived in by their owners. Typical gross rent was $949 a month, and a typical household earned $65,429.

The Marquette Iron Range, the Cliffs Shaft Mine and the Jackson Mine are among the ten state historical markers in the county. Parcels near the range towns can have long chains of ownership, so ask your title company how far back it will search.

Which townships and cities make up Marquette County?

Twenty-two local units assess property inside the county, and the county's townships page lists them. Assessing, bills and zoning questions start with the unit where the parcel sits, not with the Baraga Avenue offices.

  • Cities: Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee
  • Townships, A to M: Champion, Chocolay, Ely, Ewing, Forsyth, Humboldt, Ishpeming, Marquette and Michigamme
  • Townships, N to W: Negaunee, Powell, Republic, Richmond, Sands, Skandia, Tilden, Turin, Wells and West Branch

Wikipedia's climate table for the county puts January highs near 21 degrees Fahrenheit and lows near 10, with July highs near 68. Allow for that when scheduling a showing or an inspection.

What does a deed filing cost at the Marquette County courthouse annex?

Page count does not matter: one deed is $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. The state remonumentation charge and the register's automation charge are baked into that amount, so the window adds nothing else for the recording.

Charges at the Marquette County recording counter, from the register's schedule of fees
ServiceAmount
File a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Each extra instrument released within one paper$3.00
Treasurer's certificate attached to a warranty deed$5.00
Certified copy stamp$5.00
Ordinary copy, per sheet$1.00
Plat copy, per sheet$2.00
Clerk-run name search$0.50 a year, $5.00 minimum
Copy of a record made before 1983 (county FAQ)$7.50 tract fee added

Transfer tax is separate and applies to any taxable deed. Payment at the counter can be cash, check or card, with a processing charge on cards.

Which part of a Marquette County sale price goes to transfer tax?

The burden sits with the grantor, whoever signs the property over. Marquette County's transfer tax page adds that the deed must state the total consideration. If the price is kept off the deed, a valuation affidavit fills the gap, and the office files it free provided the deed notes that one exists.

Under MCL 207.525 the state portion is $3.75 for each $500 step of the price, with any remainder counted as another step. Take $200,000: 400 steps, so $1,500 for the state alone. Call the office for the county's per-step amount before you finalize a net sheet.

MCL 207.526 exempts some deeds if the grantor says so in the text. Sellers lean on these most:

  • Consideration below $100
  • A deed from an individual to a child or grandchild
  • Transfers following foreclosure, or a deed given to avoid it
  • A land contract that has not yet delivered legal title
  • A corrective quitclaim that only repairs a title flaw

Why would the Marquette County Register of Deeds send a deed back?

Usually the cause is a defect under MCL 565.201. Staff cannot prepare a deed or give legal advice, and only original signatures are recorded, which rules out faxes and photocopies. A "true copy" of a court order is also refused, since the court itself must certify it.

Defects that get a deed returned:

  • Signer names printed under the signatures that disagree with the notary block
  • No mailing address for the buyer, or no name and address for whoever prepared the deed
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue, or type under 10 point
  • Less than 2 1/2 inches of clear space at the top of page one
  • An opening line that names more than one recordable event
  • Full Social Security numbers left on the page

Anything that is not in English needs an English translation attached.

What does the Marquette County Treasurer check before a deed is accepted?

For warranty deeds and land contracts, the treasurer must vouch that the parcel's taxes were paid in each of the five years leading up to the deed (MCL 211.135). Plain quitclaims escape the rule. The treasurer works from the Courthouse Annex, same street address, weekdays 8 to 5, at (906) 225-8425.

On March 1 each year the townships and cities pass their unpaid real property bills up to the county treasurer, and the county then collects them. Debit and credit cards are taken on those delinquent accounts. An owner who is behind can pay before asking for the certificate, or have the title company settle the balance from sale proceeds.

The treasurer's office also sells county plat books and issues tax histories, handy when a buyer wants to see past billing on a parcel.

How can I search or file Marquette County records without driving to Baraga Avenue?

Online, the index and images start with deeds dated January 1, 1980 and with mortgages and miscellaneous papers dated January 1, 1983. Earlier books can be read only at the office.

E-recording runs through CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile, the four vendors the county names. Some document types cannot go this way, so title companies check with their vendor first, and any rejection is returned electronically.

The register's fraud page cautions about outside companies charging $50 or more for a certified deed copy that the county sells for as little as $1 a page. Owners may also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert service.

What happens to the Marquette County tax bill after the sale closes?

Recording the deed sets off a taxable value reset. MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessor, and the following year's taxable value becomes the state equalized value. The register reports recorded transfers to assessors at least once a month.

The Equalization office studies the county's 22 assessing districts and recommends equalized values to the Board of Commissioners. Its page says it prepares about 50,000 tax statements a year, keeps ownership maps, and warns owners when a defective deed has been recorded. The printed assessment roll sells for $0.15 a page with a $35 minimum.

Before closing, call (906) 225-8405 for a tax code number or parcel map, and ask the local unit what the next bill is likely to be.

More questions about Marquette County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is a flat deed filing in Marquette County?

$30.00 whatever the page count, which already covers the state survey and automation portions. Each additional instrument released in the same paper is $3.00.

Who has to pay the transfer tax in Marquette County?

The grantor, which in a sale is the seller. The state takes $3.75 for each $500 step of the price and the county adds its own amount. A deed to a child or grandchild may be exempt if it says so.

Can I mail a photocopy of my signed deed to the Marquette County recorder?

No. Only originals with live signatures are recorded, and court orders need the court's certification. Phone (906) 225-8415 first to check the paperwork.

Does my Marquette County warranty deed need a certificate from the treasurer?

It does, along with land contracts. The treasurer confirms the preceding five years of taxes are paid, and the fee sheet lists $5.00 for the certification. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

How old are the Marquette County records I can search online?

Deeds from January 1, 1980 and mortgages and miscellaneous papers from January 1, 1983. For older books, visit the office on Baraga Avenue.
