What is on file at the Mason County Register of Deeds?

Everything that moves title to land in the county, or burdens it, ends up on file here. The county page describes the register as an elected officer on a four-year term, and it quotes MCL 565.551, which obliges the office to give the public reasonable facilities to examine and copy the records.

The register also leads the county plat board, a three-seat panel that reviews proposed subdivisions before they reach the state. The clerk acts as its secretary and the treasurer holds the third seat.

The counter keeps three separate schedules, all skipping legal holidays:

  • General business, 9 to 5
  • Accepting documents for the record, 9 to 4:30
  • Passport applications, 9 to 3

Ask the office for its street address and direct phone line before you send a package.

What is Mason County like, and who is selling homes there?

Ludington serves as county seat and is the biggest city. The county was created in 1840 under the name Notipekago and took its present name in 1843. Of 1,242 square miles, only 495 are land, with the rest under Lake Michigan and inland water. US 10 runs through the middle of the county by way of Scottville and Custer, US 31 meets it close to Ludington, and M-116 follows the lakeshore to Ludington State Park. A piece of the Manistee National Forest falls within the boundary, and Manistee, Lake, Newaygo and Oceana counties are the land neighbors.

The Census Bureau estimated 29,040 residents for 2025, almost unchanged since 2020. Federal survey figures for 2020 through 2024 sketch an older, owner-heavy county:

  • Homeowners report a typical value of $219,600
  • 78.3 percent of homes are lived in by owners
  • Rent for a typical unit comes to $896
  • 28.8 percent of residents have passed 65
  • A typical household earns $64,748

The West Shore Educational Service District, based in Ludington, supports the local school districts, and the county also has a charter school, Gateway to Success Academy, plus Covenant Christian School and Ludington Area Catholic School.

What will the Mason County recorder's counter charge for a deed?

Filing one deed, mortgage or lis pendens is a $30.00 transaction. When a single paper discharges or assigns several instruments, each extra one costs $3.00. Ordinary copies are priced at $1.00 per page, plats at $2.00, and a certification stamp at $5.00.

If staff run a name search for you, the price is 50 cents for every year covered, never less than $5.00, and a state or federal tax lien certificate search costs $3.00 a name. The fee page on the county site shows a February 2018 revision date, so ring the office to verify a figure before you cut the check.

Images and indexes reach back to June 23, 1840 and are online now. Heavy users can buy a prepaid subscription, and occasional users can pay by card per search. The county cautions that its index is a working tool that may contain mistakes and is not a certified search.

How big is the transfer tax bill on a Mason County sale?

The county's table stacks $3.75 of state tax and $0.55 of county tax on each $500 of price, which makes $4.30 per slice. The grantor owes it on any deed given for $100 or more.

Mason County combined transfer tax at three sale prices, pulled from the county's published table
Price up toStateCountyTotal
$50,000$375.00$55.00$430.00
$75,000$562.50$82.50$645.00
$100,000$750.00$110.00$860.00

The pattern continues beyond the table's top row. A $200,000 sale has 400 slices and owes $1,720, while a $250,000 sale has 500 slices and owes $2,150. For a price that lands between rows, use the county's table.

Separate exemption pages cover the county share and the state share. If one applies, say so on the deed itself. Foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, and land contracts that have not yet passed title are on the exempt list.

What must a deed show before the Mason County Register of Deeds accepts it?

The register publishes the full text of MCL 565.201 as its standard. The short version for a modern deed: legible names under the signatures, the notary's name printed nearby, grantee addresses, and a preparer's name and business address.

Format rules run alongside those. Leave a clear strip about 2 1/2 inches deep at the top of the first sheet, print in 10 point or larger, and stay between letter and legal size. A single recordable event belongs on the first line. A translation must accompany foreign-language text, and most of a Social Security number has to be blanked.

Once the register accepts and records a deed, the law treats it as conforming. A compliant deed cannot be refused because of what it says, so closing agents proof the document before it is presented.

Who certifies taxes on a Mason County deed, and what else does that office do?

The county treasurer. Per the treasurer's page, the office signs off on deeds ahead of recording, confirming nothing is delinquent for the five years before the instrument date, and it hands out tax abstracts on request. Under MCL 211.135 that certificate goes with warranty deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments.

Counter hours are weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax line is 231 843-8411. Each March 1 the township and city rolls come to the county in a step called settlement, and unpaid real property tax becomes the treasurer's to collect. Village taxes are handled on a different timetable.

Since 2004 Mason County has chosen to run its own tax foreclosures, so the treasurer's staff run title searches, mail notices and sell tax-delinquent parcels instead of the state. The county also opted in to principal residence exemption audits, which means any exemption claimed in error is pursued from the same office.

The board of commissioners has long authorized the treasurer to buy every delinquent real property tax bill. Townships, villages, cities, school districts and special authorities therefore get their full levy in the budget year, and the county recovers the money later as delinquent taxes are paid, sometimes by issuing short-term notes against them.

Which Mason County office handles parcel splits and address changes?

That falls to Equalization, which keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5 and answers at 231-845-6288. The department issues addresses for every unit except Ludington and Scottville, splits and combines tax parcels, takes mailing address updates and supplies aerial and tax maps. Its page also links the county parcel GIS layer, the apportionment report and the yearly equalization report.

Splits come up when a buyer wants only part of a lot or a lakeside piece is being divided. The register records the new deed, and equalization then revises the parcel records.

The register's page also offers owners a free Property Fraud Alert sign-up.

More questions about Mason County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the Mason County deed filing price?

Thirty dollars for each document, with $3.00 more for every additional instrument it releases. Copies are $1.00 a page and certification is $5.00.

What time does Mason County stop taking deeds for the record?

Recording ends at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, half an hour before the front office closes at 5. A deed handed in late can slide to the next business day, so title agents aim for earlier in the afternoon.

What would transfer tax be if a Mason County house sold for $200,000?

It would come to $1,720: $1,500 for the state and $220 for the county. The seller pays unless the deed states an exemption.

Does a Mason County warranty deed need anything from the treasurer?

Yes. The county treasurer must certify that no taxes are delinquent for the previous five years before the register records it. A quitclaim without warranty language is excused under MCL 211.135.

How far back do Mason County online land records go?

Images and indexes are online from June 23, 1840 to the present. The county calls its index a working index, so check any key detail against the recorded document.

Who records deeds in Mecosta County

  • Mecosta County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • $3.00 added per additional instrument assigned/discharged; copies $1/page; plat copies $2/page; search 50 cents/yr min $5 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Selling in Mecosta County?
We buy Mecosta County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Mecosta County by the numbers

Mecosta County ranks 41 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 40,321 people in 21,045 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $169,900, the median home value sits 9% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Mecosta County reports $57,774. Owner-occupancy is 76%, so renters hold about 24% of occupied homes.

Where does a Mecosta County deed get mailed or dropped off?

Recording packages are accepted by mail or courier at 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307, and the county page names USPS, UPS and FedEx as options. The phone is (231) 592-0148. Call first to learn the counter's recording hours.

The register maintains the real estate record for every parcel in Mecosta County. Indexing is complete back to January 1, 1968, and every document back to 1859 has been scanned and tagged by liber and page. Index books, including oil and gas, are imaged on the Countyfusion site, and a second public search runs through Vanguard at mecosta.mi.publicsearch.us.

The same office accepts passport applications for its own set of hours and a separate acceptance charge of $35. That service has no connection to a home sale.

What is Mecosta County like for a seller?

The county spreads over 571 square miles, 555 of them dry land, and holds more than 100 lakes, rivers and streams. The Muskegon River passes through Big Rapids, the county seat and largest city, where Ferris State University is located. County government was organized in 1859. Local government is made up of 16 townships, the city of Big Rapids and four villages: Barryton, Mecosta, Morley and Stanwood.

Federal estimates count 42,320 people in mid-2025, a 4.9 percent gain on the 2020 base, spread over 21,490 housing units. The 2020 to 2024 survey found owners living in 76.9 percent of homes and pegged a typical house at $178,900, lower than in Marquette or Mason County.

Wherever the parcel sits, the deed is filed in Big Rapids, while assessing and collection stay with the township, village or city. Work out which local unit covers the parcel before asking for a payoff or tax certificate.

Schools are served by the Mecosta-Osceola Intermediate School District, based in Big Rapids, and the county has a charter school, Crossroads Charter Academy, along with Brockway Christian Academy, St. Michael Elementary and St. Peters Lutheran School.

What does the Mecosta County Register of Deeds charge for recording and copies?

Recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or similar instrument costs $30.00 here. The county explains that the amount includes the statutory fee under MCL 600.2567a plus a $5.00 contribution to the automation fund. A document releasing several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra one.

Mecosta County Register of Deeds price list, copied from the county's fee section
ItemPrice
Deed or mortgage recording$30.00
Tax certificate with a warranty deed, up to five descriptions$5.00 per instrument
Each description beyond five$0.20
Copy of a land record, each page$1.00
Copy of a plat, each page$2.00
Name search$0.50 per year, $5.00 minimum
Certifying a record copy$5.00

The office also records fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral under the Uniform Commercial Code. All other personal property filings belong with the Secretary of State.

How is transfer tax worked out on a Mecosta County sale?

Two levies add together here. Mecosta County charges 55 cents per $500 slice of value and the state charges $3.75 per slice (MCL 207.525), with any partial slice counted as whole. A deed valued at $100 or more is taxable, and MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor.

Take a $175,000 house: 350 slices, $1,312.50 to the state and $192.50 to the county, $1,505.00 combined. The Register of Deeds office collects both amounts alongside the recording fee, and the act calls for payment inside 15 days of delivering the deed.

The deed has to carry the property's full value. Alternatively, attach a valuation affidavit and add a line on the deed saying it is on file, which costs nothing to file. Claim any MCL 207.526 exemption on the deed's face, for instance for a parent-to-child transfer or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

What makes the Mecosta County Register of Deeds reject a document?

An eleven-point checklist on the county page, drawn from Michigan statutes, governs what gets filed. These are the points that most often cause trouble:

  • Names printed under the signatures that differ from the notary acknowledgment
  • A missing grantee address, or no name and address for the drafter
  • A notary block with no commission expiration date
  • A deed naming a surviving owner without a certified death certificate on record
  • A court order lacking the clerk's certification and seal
  • Type under 10 point, or less than 2 1/2 inches of clear top margin
  • An opening line naming more than one recordable event
  • No statement of total property value and no affidavit

Stock should be white and 20-pound, from letter to legal size. Run through the list before mailing, since a rejected package costs days.

Does a Mecosta County deed need a tax certificate?

A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract and an assignment of a land contract all do. The certificate comes from the county treasurer and shows taxes paid for the five years before the instrument date, under MCL 211.135. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

The county treasurer's page describes how unpaid taxes move toward forfeiture and foreclosure, so a seller carrying old bills should ask for a payoff figure before closing. Mecosta County's companion property tax guide covers the summer and winter due dates, the March 1 delinquency date and the appeal calendar.

What do UCC filings and lien searches cost at the Mecosta County office?

The register records only the real-estate side of Uniform Commercial Code work: fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral. A standard-form filing with two debtor names and up to 100 pages is $30.00. Extra charges apply for a non-standard form ($7.00), for filings over 100 pages ($12.00) and for each debtor name past two ($10.00).

  • UCC search, per name: $6.00
  • State or federal tax lien certificate, per name: $3.00
  • Copy of a UCC filing, per page: $2.00
  • Copy of a state or federal tax lien, per page: $1.00

The county notes that its UCC search results cover personal property filings only through June 30, 2001. Real estate filings made after July 1, 2001 appear in the real estate index. Searches are done as time allows and carry no guarantee.

How old are the land records in Big Rapids and the surrounding villages?

The county was set off in 1840 and organized in 1859. The plat of the Village of Big Rapids was recorded on November 3, 1859, and French's addition (Glen Elm) followed on May 9, 1860. The state legislature authorized the City of Big Rapids in April 1869.

Railroads shaped the villages. The Grand Rapids and Indiana line crossed the Little Muskegon River in June 1869, creating the Village of Morley, and construction of the next stretch in late July 1869 brought the Village of Stanwood into existence. The register's documents back to 1859 are imaged, which helps when an old lot line or easement turns up in a title search.

Where can I look up Mecosta County parcels and maps?

The Equalization page links a land records portal and a map viewer, and it carries tax maps for each of the 16 townships: Aetna, Austin, Big Rapids, Chippewa, Colfax, Deerfield, Fork, Grant, Green, Hinton, Martiny, Mecosta, Millbrook, Morton, Sheridan and Wheatland. Its document center also lists the millage rates and a property tax estimator.

Lining up the parcel number on a tax map with the legal description on the deed is a quick way to catch a wrong lot before closing. The Vanguard support line, listed on the register's page, is (888) 608-1808.

More questions about Mecosta County, MI Register of Deeds

What is Mecosta County's charge for filing a deed?

Thirty dollars per instrument, plus $3.00 for each additional instrument released in the same paper. Page copies are $1.00 each.

What would a $175,000 Mecosta County sale owe in transfer tax?

$1,505.00 in total, split into $1,312.50 for the state and $192.50 for the county. The seller carries it unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

What address takes Mecosta County recording packages?

400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. Phone (231) 592-0148 beforehand to confirm paperwork and payment.

Is an uncertified court order good enough for Mecosta County recording?

No. The clerk of the court must certify and seal it. A plain copy is sent back.

How old are the Mecosta County records that can be searched?

The full index starts January 1, 1968, and papers from 1859 onward are scanned and tagged by liber and page. Countyfusion and Vanguard are the two public portals.

Who records deeds in Midland County

  • Midland County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Register of Deeds is constitutional office recording documents for all real property; transfer tax information and recording info pages exist (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Statewide: recording fee $30.00 per document (MCL 600.2567) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Selling in Midland County?

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Midland County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 83,641 people and 37,048 housing units in Midland County, which ranks 24 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $184,300, which is 2% below the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $77,538; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 22% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 78% owner-occupied.

Where do Midland County deeds get recorded?

The Register of Deeds sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street in Midland, MI 48640, and answers at (989) 832-6820. Recording runs on weekdays, opening at 8 a.m. and closing to new documents at 4 p.m. The vault, where the older books live, opens a half hour later.

A deed that shows up after the 4 p.m. cutoff waits for the next business day, and it queues in the order received as long as cash or a check came with it. The staff take in warranty and quit claim deeds, land contracts, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats. Drafting and legal advice are outside their role, so a deed still unwritten is a job for an attorney or a title company.

Which fees does the Midland County office list?

A single $30.00 charge covers any document of any length, and the state remonumentation and automation charges are already inside it. The county's own sheet lists a handful of extras.

Fees on the Midland County Register of Deeds sheet
ItemAmount
Recording one document$30.00
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3.00 per instrument beyond the first, added to $30.00
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00 for up to 5 legal descriptions, then $1.00 each
Plain copy$1.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 plus $1.00 per page

Accepted payment includes cash, checks payable to the Register of Deeds, and cards at the counter, where the card processor tacks on a charge that the office says is generally about $1.50. The office also takes e-recording from qualified submitters, though anything needing a raised court seal or a death certificate has to be brought in on paper.

Which Midland County deeds need a tax certificate first?

Four kinds of instruments, according to the county's recording page, cannot be recorded until the treasurer issues a certificate:

  • A warranty deed, or any deed that includes a covenant of warranty.
  • A land contract.
  • A land contract assignment containing a warranty clause.
  • A master deed for a site condominium.

Order the certificate ahead of closing day. A bare quit claim deed is absent from the list. To see whether a parcel's taxes are current, the county's online lookup offers what the treasurer's counter would show, in the county's words.

What does transfer tax come to under the Midland County chart?

Columns in the county's chart show $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500, so $4.30 together. At a $100,000 price the columns read $750, $110 and $860. Payment is required from a value of $100 upward, subject to the exemption sheets the office links.

The parties may omit the price from the deed by attaching a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit. A different form, the Property Transfer Affidavit, goes to the assessor for the City of Midland or for the township that holds the parcel, and state law allows the buyer 45 days.

In what order does a Midland County closing move?

A title company runs most of these steps, but the order helps a seller see where the money and paper go.

  • Request a treasurer's tax certificate when the deed contains a warranty covenant.
  • Have the deed notarized. The recorder's staff cannot do it, and the County Clerk in the same County Services Building charges a small fee.
  • Remit both transfer taxes to the county treasurer inside 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523(3)).
  • Record the deed, pay the $30.00, and reach the counter ahead of the 4 p.m. close.
  • Leave the buyer to file the Property Transfer Affidavit with the City of Midland or the township assessor within 45 days.

Recorders also pass a list of recorded transactions to local assessors at least monthly under MCL 211.27a(10).

How old are the records the office holds?

The collection begins in 1855, the year the county was established. Books and microfilm cover the whole run, scanned images with computer indexing start in 1968, and online images reach back to 1950. Searches run through Fidlar-hosted tools called Tapestry EON and Laredo, and recorded papers are public, so anyone can request copies.

The index for 1958 to 1968 is available in an Adobe search format, and entries older than 1958 turn up in the Simple Search option. The office says back-indexing continues, so an older chain of title may need a visit or a call. The county's recording page also links a property fraud alert and a reporting form, which is worth raising with the office when an inherited parcel still carries a relative's name.

What does the ground and water situation look like for sellers?

By Census Bureau measure the county holds 517 square miles of land and two incorporated cities, Midland, the county seat, and Coleman. The Tittabawassee River runs through Edenville Township and past the village of Sanford. In May 2020 the Edenville and Sanford dam failures forced evacuations across parts of the city, the village and several townships, so a seller near the river should expect buyers to ask about flood history. Dow Chemical dates to 1890 in the city of Midland, per the county history.

Service lines vary by location. The city of Midland provides water and sewer to its residents and a few neighboring townships, while parcels beyond municipal water rely on private wells and septic systems. Winters are cold and snowy, with January highs near freezing. Out in the townships, collect well and septic records before listing.

What else do buyers weigh in Midland County?

Buyers looking at a Midland County house tend to ask about the surroundings as well as the structure. The county's profile points to a few answers:

  • Scheduled flights leave from MBS International Airport near Freeland, and Flint's Bishop International Airport is the other option.
  • No regular public bus service exists. Dial-A-Ride covers trips inside the city, and County Connection serves the rest of the county, both for a fare.
  • The Pere Marquette Rail-Trail follows a former rail corridor, with more than 20 miles of riding according to the county's website.
  • Grace A. Dow Memorial Library serves the city and most townships by contract, and Coleman Area Library covers Coleman, Geneva and Warren townships.

The Midland County Educational Service Agency supports the county's districts with special education, early education and career programs. Ask the district office for the boundary that applies to your address, since township lines and school lines differ.

How does Midland County's housing stock compare in the Census data?

The Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 83,754 people living among 37,723 housing units. Renters pay about $1,016 a month, and they occupy roughly 22 percent of homes, which leaves 78.1 percent in owner hands. A 2020-2024 survey values the middle owner-occupied house at $195,400 and puts household income at $77,705. Only 128 building permits were issued in 2025.

Population has crept up 0.3 percent since the April 2020 base. Nine in ten residents lived at the same address a year earlier, a sign of long tenure. Commutes average 23.7 minutes, and 36.6 percent of adults aged 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree.

More questions about Midland County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the street address for Midland County deeds?

220 W Ellsworth Street, Midland, MI 48640, phone (989) 832-6820. Recording closes at 4 p.m. on weekdays, and papers received later are recorded the next business day.

What is the price to file a deed there?

$30.00 for any document, regardless of length. A treasurer's tax certificate for a warranty deed adds $5.00 for up to five legal descriptions.

Does Midland County take e-recorded deeds?

Yes, from qualified submitters, including documents that need tax certification. Paper is still required for documents that need a raised court seal or a death certificate.

Can the register's staff notarize or draft a deed?

No. The office does not write legal documents, and its own staff do not notarize what they record, since that would create a conflict of interest. The County Clerk's office next door has a notary available for a small fee.

What would a $100,000 sale owe in transfer tax?

$860 in total: $750 to the state and $110 to the county, according to the county's chart. A $200,000 sale would owe $1,720 at the same rates.

Monroe County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 155,001 people and 66,300 housing units in Monroe County, which ranks 15 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $215,700, which is 15% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $75,272; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 19% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 81% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1973, about 50 years ago.

When can you record a deed in Monroe County?

Monroe County's deeds office takes recordings Monday through Friday between 8:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. A real property document that arrives after 3:00 p.m. is handled on the next working day, so the practical cutoff for same-day posting is an hour earlier than the closing time. Ask the office for its current counter location and e-recording instructions before sending a courier.

Most sellers never visit. Their title agent carries the deed in and pays the charge from the closing funds.

What does Monroe County charge for recording?

Every instrument, whether a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens, costs a flat $30 however long it runs. The amount already includes the Michigan remonumentation and automation fees. The county accepts cash, checks and credit cards, and a card adds 3 percent, with a floor of $2.

Monroe County Register of Deeds charges that sellers meet
ServiceFee
Deed or mortgage, any page count$30
Each added instrument assigned or discharged in one document$3 on top of the flat fee
Certifying a recorded document$5
Real estate copy, per page$1
Tax certificate for a warranty deed, up to 5 descriptions$5, then $0.20 per extra description
State tax lien search certificate$1

UCC copies run $2 per page, and a recorded plat copy on letter paper is $1. One exception removes the $3 add-on: a document that moves from the State of Michigan or a local government to a Land Bank Authority.

How is transfer tax computed in Monroe County?

The county's fee page prices the state tax at $7.50 per $1,000 and the county tax at $1.10 per $1,000 of total consideration, so $8.60 combined. Applied to $228,900, the Census median for owner-occupied homes, that is roughly $1,969: $1,717 state and $252 county, before rounding up to the next $500 step.

State law makes the seller liable, with payment due at the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. MCL 207.526 exempts several kinds of deeds, among them gifts to children and grandchildren, deeds that simply confirm title, and foreclosure transfers. The county treasurer's office issues the certificate that warranty deeds, master deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments with a covenant of warranty must show under MCLA 211.135.

Can you look up a Monroe County deed by street address?

No. The office searches by name only and asks for a grantor or grantee plus an approximate year. Its staff cannot trace ownership from a street address. A person who lacks the owner's name can obtain the names on the tax roll from the County Equalization Department or a city assessor, though the roll may list someone other than the true owner.

That rule matters when a relative's house is being sold. Before asking a title company to search, collect these items and have the search check for any lis pendens or lien:

  • The earlier deed or deeds in the family.
  • Probate papers, if an estate owned the house.
  • The exact spelling of every owner's name, with the approximate year of each transfer.

Tax lien searches are priced separately: $1 for a state tax lien certificate and $6 per name for a federal one.

Does the office handle commercial filings that touch a house sale?

The fee page also covers Uniform Commercial Code filings, which can surface in a title search. A standard form filing and a termination of a filing each cost $30, and the schedule lists fixture filing fees as not applicable. Its UCC section marks standard-form debt filings, assignments, amendments, continuations and partial releases as not accepted, and the notes say the information on UCC searches runs only through June 30, 2001, because realty-related filings after July 1, 2001 are recorded in the real estate index alone.

The practical lesson is to search the real estate index, not the personal property files, when checking for a lien on a house.

What sets Monroe County apart as a place to sell a house?

It is the only Michigan county touching Lake Erie, and the shoreline is the state's lowest ground at 571 feet. The Census Bureau measures about 549 square miles of land. The River Raisin and Sandy Creek drain it. French settlers reached Frenchtown on the Raisin in the 1780s, and the county was carved out in 1817.

A few features color what buyers see:

  • The city of Monroe is both county seat and largest city, and Dundee drew attention in 2001 when a large Cabela's store opened there.
  • Nine public school districts operate within the county, and its district-of-choice policy lets a family enroll in any district with room.
  • Industry marks the lakeshore. The Port of Monroe is still heavily industrial, and the Enrico Fermi nuclear station sits in Frenchtown Charter Township near the water.
  • Monroe County Community College is the only higher education campus in the county.
  • Lake Erie Transit runs eight fixed routes in and around the city of Monroe.

Tornadoes are uncommon, about 30 since 1950, and the latest with significant damage hit Dundee Township in June 2010.

Do the county's boundary quirks affect any deeds?

A few do, which is why a legal description matters more here than a street address. The Toledo War settlement of 1836 left a sliver of Monroe County, the Lost Peninsula in Erie Township, separated from the rest of Michigan by the state line, and most of that land is a marina. A 1973 agreement then ran the line through tiny Turtle Island in Lake Erie, giving Erie Township the Michigan half.

Lakeshore and river parcels raise their own questions about bottomland and easements. If your house touches Lake Erie, the River Raisin or Sandy Creek, hand the title company your survey and any earlier easements at the start, so the exceptions on the title commitment are known well before the buyer's deadline.

How do the Census figures describe Monroe County homes?

The Bureau's 2025 estimate is 156,004 people in 67,494 housing units. Owners hold 81.7 percent of homes. Half of owner-occupied houses sit above $228,900 in the 2020-2024 data, and renters pay a median $1,059. Household income has a median of $77,335. Commuters travel 26.2 minutes on average, and building permits totaled 191 in 2025. Density was 281.8 people per square mile in 2020.

The county has 63,029 households averaging 2.45 people. Nine in ten residents stayed at the same address over the prior year, 23.3 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 9.7 percent of residents are in poverty. Set beside Midland County, the middle Monroe County house is worth about $33,500 more, and owners make up 3.6 points more of the households.

More questions about Monroe County, MI Register of Deeds

What hours does the Monroe County deeds office keep?

Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Anything real property related that comes in after 3:00 p.m. is recorded or filed the following working day.

How much is the flat charge for a deed there?

$30 per document regardless of length. Extra instruments assigned or discharged add $3 each, and certifying a copy adds $5. Plain copies of real estate records are $1 a page, and the warranty deed tax certificate is a separate charge.

Does the office search by property address?

No. It cannot search ownership by address and needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year. The Equalization Department or a city assessor can supply the name on the tax roll.

Which transfer tax rates does the county list?

$1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, based on total consideration. A $200,000 sale comes to $1,720, with $1,500 to the state and $220 to the county.

How can I pay at the counter?

Cash, checks and credit cards are accepted. A card carries a 3 percent fee with a $2 minimum, so a check costs less on a large closing.

Montcalm County by the numbers

Montcalm County has about 67,174 residents and 28,046 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 28 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $172,100, 8% below the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $64,892, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 82% of occupied homes and renters in 18%.

Where does Montcalm County keep its land records?

Every Montcalm County deed lands in one place, the register of deeds in Stanton at 211 W. Main St. (box 368, Stanton, MI 48888). Treasury's statewide directory lists 989-831-7337 and regofdeeds@co.montcalm.mi.us. Phone ahead for counter hours and for the electronic filing rules, since staff set both.

Voters moved the county seat from Greenville, the seat since 1840, to Stanton in 1860. Stanton is tiny, 1,348 residents in 2020, and it occupies the point where Day, Evergreen, Sidney and Douglass townships touch. A parcel in any township of the county, from Carson City to Vestaburg, is recorded here.

What do Greenville and Stanton tell a seller about the market?

Greenville is the largest city, with 8,816 residents in 2020. It lies 16 road miles southwest of Stanton and about 33 miles northeast of Grand Rapids, which explains why Montcalm is counted in the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. The Flat River runs through town, and Baldwin, Manoka and Como lakes sit inside the city limits. Greenville built its name on refrigerator manufacturing, and it was the birthplace of the Meijer store chain. The Electrolux plant closed in 2006, a loss that affected 2,700 employees and their families.

Around the city, farms grow potatoes, corn and Christmas trees and run dairy herds. The Fred Meijer Heartland Trail ends in Greenville after 41 miles from Alma, and the Flat River Trail loops the city. A house near a lake or trail often draws a buyer who wants the recreation, so mention those features in your listing.

The city's roots go back to 1844, when a settler built a sawmill on the Flat River, and Danish immigrants followed. Ranney Refrigerator Company opened in 1892 and earned Greenville the label Refrigerator Capital of the World. Hendrik Meijer opened his first grocery there in 1934. Stanton, by comparison, is a government town whose ZIP code, 48888, is shared with parts of Ferris, Belvidere and Pine townships.

Carson City, a city of 1,120 in the southeast, was platted in 1866 and lies along M-57, 20 miles by road from Stanton. Its students attend Carson City-Crystal Area Schools.

  • Greenville's Lafayette Street downtown district was placed on the National and State Register of Historic Places in 2008.
  • The Danish Festival fills the third weekend of August.
  • The Montcalm County 4-H Fair is held in Greenville each summer.

What do the Census figures show for Montcalm County?

Rural living dominates: 84.6% of residents are outside urban areas, spread across 705 square miles of land. The 2020 count of 66,614 grew to an estimated 69,406 by July 2025, and 20.1% are 65 or older.

Owners live in 83.1% of occupied housing. Half of owner-occupied homes were worth under $185,500 in 2020 to 2024 figures, rent at the median ran $869 and median household income reached $67,344. A one-way trip to work averages 30.7 minutes, and the Census tally for 2025 shows 201 building permits.

Connectivity matters to remote buyers: 83.9% of households have a broadband subscription, and 88.5% of adults have finished high school. About 16.0% hold a bachelor's degree, and 14.2% of residents live in poverty.

Families choose among eight public districts: Carson City Crystal Area, Central Montcalm, Greenville, Lakeview, Montabella, Tri County Area and Vestaburg, with the Montcalm Area ISD coordinating services. Montcalm Community College anchors higher education.

What will the recording fee be in Montcalm County?

Section 2567 of the Revised Judicature Act prices recording at a flat $30.00 a document. If one paper assigns or discharges multiple instruments, each beyond the first costs another $3.00. Copying runs a dollar a page, and a certificate on a recorded paper is $5.00.

Money is due with the paper. An electronic filing gets one extra business day. Charter counties alone may set other amounts, so confirm the Stanton figures before mailing a check.

How much transfer tax would a Montcalm County seller pay?

Both taxes fall on the grantor. Michigan takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 block of value, with a partial block counted whole, and payment reaches the county treasurer inside 15 days of handing over the deed. The table prices a sale at the Montcalm median.

Transfer tax on a $185,500 Montcalm County sale (rates in MCL 207.504 and 207.523; median value from Census QuickFacts)
StepResult
$500 blocks in $185,500371
State share$1,391.25
County share$204.05
Seller's combined bill$1,595.30

Family handovers get special treatment. The state act excludes a deed from a parent to a child or grandchild, and it excludes foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu. The county act has no family exclusion, so the county share can still apply. Whichever exemption fits, write it on the deed itself.

What should I check on a deed before bringing it to Stanton?

MCL 565.201 gives the register grounds to refuse a paper, and a refusal costs a trip across the county. Hand your closing agent this short list before anyone signs.

  • Dark ink signatures, with every signer's name printed beneath and spelled as the notary spelled it.
  • Each grantee's mailing address, plus the preparer's name and address.
  • Roomy margins: 2.5 inches at the top of page one, half an inch around the rest.
  • One recordable event named on the opening line.
  • Letter or legal size sheets in 10-point type or larger.

Anything in a foreign language travels with an English translation, and a Social Security number has to be masked down to four digits.

How does a sale change taxes for the next owner?

Between sales, Michigan lets taxable value rise by no more than 5% or inflation, whichever is smaller. A transfer ends that protection, and the next owner's value jumps to state equalized value. A close relative who keeps a residence non-commercial can inherit without the jump.

Assessing is a city and township job in Michigan, not a county one, so your local assessor handles the paperwork even though the deed goes to Stanton. The new owner reports the transfer within 45 days.

Sellers who claimed the homestead exemption rescind it on Form 2602 within 90 days of moving out. Late filing runs $5 per day to a $200 limit, and the exemption ends December 31. New occupants file Form 2368 by June 1 or November 1.

What if the Montcalm County house is inherited or worn out?

It can still sell. An heir signs through the personal representative, and a certified death certificate gets recorded when the deed names a survivor. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands skips lender appraisals and repair demands.

Before choosing a closing date, ask the county treasurer where the parcel stands on taxes, because any delinquent balance is cleaned up first. If you cannot reach the person named on the deed, a title company can tell you what paper the register will need.

More questions about Montcalm County, MI Register of Deeds

Which office records a deed for a house near Greenville?

Stanton's register of deeds, even for a Greenville address, because Montcalm County has a single recording office at 211 W. Main St. Treasury's directory lists 989-831-7337.

What transfer tax applies at a $185,500 price?

$1,595.30 in total: $1,391.25 to the state and $204.05 to the county, paid by the seller. Prices round up in $500 steps before the rates apply.

Will the register review my deed form?

Staff check that a paper meets recording standards and then record it. Drafting is outside their role, so bring a finished deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

How far is Stanton from Greenville?

About 16 miles by road. Carson City is roughly 20 miles from Stanton, so sellers in the south and west should allow time for an in-person filing.

What happens to the homestead exemption when I sell?

It has to be rescinded on Form 2602 with the local assessor within 90 days of moving out. A late filing is charged $5 per day up to $200.

When can I visit the Montmorency County register of deeds in Atlanta?

Deeds for the county go to 12265 M-32 West in Atlanta, mailing box 789, ZIP 49709. Phone 989-785-8079. The posted window is Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the county site adds that the counter stays staffed at midday.

The register is the constitutional recording officer for anything that transfers or burdens land here, including mineral interests along with surface interests. Each paper gets an exact receipt time, a liber and page, and a line in the entry book. Originals are scanned and sent to microfiche for off-site archive storage, and a tract index lets a searcher start from the legal description rather than a name.

The same staff chair the county plat board and take passport applications. Abstractors, title companies, mortgage lenders, oil and gas land agents and township assessors all rely on this counter, and the office describes itself as the starting point of the county's tax base.

What is Montmorency County like for a home seller?

Montmorency sits in Northern Michigan on the Lake Huron side, drained by the Thunder Bay River toward Alpena. The land area is 547 square miles, and most of it is state forest on the Grayling outwash plain, with jack pine barrens and lakes left by glaciers. The Legislature created the county in 1840 under an Ojibwe chief's name, renamed it in 1843 and organized it in 1881, and Hillman, the first seat, yielded to Atlanta in 1891.

Only 9,153 people lived here in 2020, which makes it the second-smallest Lower Peninsula county. The Census Bureau's estimate for July 2025 is 9,842, up 7.5%. A third of residents are 65 or older, and the average household has 1.92 people. The 2020 census counted 8,930 housing units with 51.6% of them vacant, a share that goes with a tourism economy of cabins, lake lots and trail traffic.

Atlanta itself is an unincorporated community of 720, 46 miles west of Alpena and 32 miles east of Gaylord. It calls itself the Elk Capital of Michigan and hosts a winter rally race. Hillman, a village of 605, lies 15 miles east-northeast, and Atlanta Community Schools serves the center of the county.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $158,600.
  • Median household income: $49,756.
  • Median gross rent: $686.
  • Mean travel time to work: 26.3 minutes.

Townships are Albert, Avery, Briley, Hillman, Loud, Montmorency, Rust and Vienna, plus the Village of Hillman.

How does recreation shape sales in Montmorency County?

Trail access drives much of the local market. The county's ORV, ATV and snowmobile trails are described as some of the best in the state, and it is one of the few counties that let ATVs ride public county roads, which links fuel stops, food and lodging in Hillman, Atlanta and Lewiston. The county's newspaper of record is the Montmorency County Tribune. Buyers who hunt, fish or ride often care more about where a parcel touches state forest or a lake than about square footage.

Farming is a smaller piece of the economy, built around dairy products and dry beans. Tourism services and retail form most of the base, so a house near the Thunder Bay River or a lake lot can read as a rental or a weekend place to a buyer. A seller should state the road type, the water frontage and any recorded easement in the listing, then confirm each against the register's index before the contract is signed.

Which forms and helpers does the Montmorency County register list?

The county page carries downloads for a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, an affidavit of affixture for a mobile home, a notice of intention to maintain mineral rights and a principal residence exemption form. It also posts fee sheets for statutory charges, copies and searches, commercial code filings, recording standards and transfer tax, with separate sheets for county exemptions, state exemptions and valuation.

For a cabin, hunting parcel or acreage, three items come up most.

  • A deed that repeats the legal description exactly, because the tract index runs on it.
  • A recorded survey when a boundary matters. The page lists several surveyors and independent searchers in the region.
  • Mobile home or mineral paperwork, when either appears in the chain of title.

Title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord are also listed. One of them can draft the deed and order the search that a buyer will want, which the register's staff cannot do.

What does the Montmorency County register charge?

Michigan's judicature act sets $30.00 as the base recording charge, with $3.00 more for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges. Searches by name run 50 cents a year with a $5.00 floor. A county that is not chartered cannot go above the state schedule, so the sheet on the county site is the number to follow.

The county page also posts separate sheets for copies and searches and for uniform commercial code filings. Phone 989-785-8079 if you plan to mail a check and want the total confirmed.

How much transfer tax will a Montmorency County seller owe?

On a sale at the county median the combined bill lands near $1,367. The state takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 of price or part of it, and the county treasurer receives payment within 15 days.

Transfer tax on a Montmorency County sale at the median home value (rates from MCL 207.504 and 207.523; value from Census QuickFacts, 2020-2024)
StepResult
Price$158,600
$500 blocks, rounded up318
State$1,192.50
County$174.90
Seller's total$1,367.40

A deed for under $100, a land contract that keeps title with the seller until paid in full, and a corrective quitclaim all sit outside both taxes. For a parcel that crosses a county line, split the price and pay each county its share.

What happens to the tax bill after a cabin or house sells?

A sale resets taxable value. Under MCL 211.27a the next year's figure moves up to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer informs the local assessor within 45 days. A cabin held for decades can carry a taxable value far below that number, so the new owner may see a jump. A parent, child, sibling or grandchild who keeps a residence non-commercial is excepted, and so is a surviving spouse.

An inherited property counts as a transfer when it passes by will or intestacy to anyone outside those groups. Ask the township assessor which rule fits before you decide on a price. The Montmorency County treasurer can report the parcel's tax status before you set a closing date.

If the seller took the homestead exemption, it must be rescinded on Form 2602 within 90 days of the house ceasing to be the owner's home.

More questions about Montmorency County, MI Register of Deeds

Is the Montmorency County register of deeds open at lunchtime?

Yes. The county site says the office stays open during lunch hours, with a weekday window of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone is 989-785-8079.

What is the combined transfer tax on a $158,600 house?

$1,367.40, split as $1,192.50 to the state and $174.90 to the county. The seller owes it, and the price is rounded up to the next $500 before the rates apply.

Can the office prepare my quit claim deed?

No. It records and indexes. The county page offers quit claim and warranty deed forms, but a title company or attorney should confirm which one fits your transfer.

How do I find out whether mineral rights were severed?

Ask a title company to search the chain of title. The register records mineral interests apart from surface interests, and the county page lists a notice form for keeping mineral rights.

Which county page lists Atlanta-area title companies?

The register of deeds page lists title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord, as well as surveyors and independent searchers in the area.

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Muskegon County by the numbers

Muskegon County ranks 12 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 175,378 people in 74,969 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $180,900, the median home value sits 4% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Muskegon County reports $63,495. Owner-occupancy is 78%, so renters hold about 22% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1968, about 55 years ago.

How do I reach the Muskegon County register of deeds?

Suite A102 at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Muskegon, MI 49442, is where Muskegon County deeds are filed, and 231-724-6271 reaches the staff. Business hours run 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Anything to be recorded must arrive by 4:30 p.m. The county calls itself the official recorder and depository of land documents since 1859, the year it was organized out of Ottawa County.

The shelves hold mortgages, liens, surveys, plats, land contracts, condominium filings and financing statements as well as deeds. Transfer tax for both the state and the county is collected at this counter when the deed goes on record.

Writing or advising on a deed is off limits, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from legal advice. The county points owners to title companies, real estate lawyers or off-the-shelf forms that satisfy the state's recording standards.

Can I file by mail, in person or online in Muskegon County?

Counter, mail and online all work, provided the paper has original signatures. Photocopies and faxes come back unrecorded.

Electronic filing goes through CSC, EPN, Indecomm or Simplifile. Some document types stay on paper.

  • Master deeds, and amendments that change a legal description and bring large drawings.
  • Plats.
  • Property transfer affidavits, which go to the equalization department instead.

Your title company can tell you whether it files through one of these vendors.

The office adds two free protections. Home Security Search lets an owner look up records under their own name, and Fraud Guard emails you when your name shows up on a document headed for recording in the county. Both suit a landlord or an owner who holds property for years.

What does the register charge, line by line?

The county's schedule took effect October 1, 2016. Of the $30 recording charge, $4 supports the state survey and remonumentation program. A warranty deed, land contract or other deed with a covenant of warranty also needs a treasurer's tax certificate.

Muskegon County register of deeds charges (source: the county Schedule of Fees page)
ItemCharge
One deed, mortgage or other instrument$30
Each further instrument assigned or discharged in the same document$3
Treasurer's tax certificate$5
Copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2
Certification$5 a document
Minimum search charge$5

Paying by check with a certificate takes two checks: one to the register of deeds covering recording and transfer tax, and one for $5 to the Muskegon County Treasurer.

What does a Muskegon County seller owe in transfer tax?

Selling triggers two taxes on the grantor: $3.75 to the state and $0.55 to the county for each $500 block of price, partial blocks counted whole. At the county's $198,300 median home value that is 397 blocks, which produces $1,488.75 for the state, $218.35 for the county and $1,707.10 in all.

Troubled sales get special treatment, and the county FAQ spells it out. A sheriff's deed always escapes the state tax and only sometimes escapes the county tax. The state act also exempts deeds given in foreclosure or in place of it, and both acts exempt a corrective deed and a spousal conveyance that makes or ends a tenancy by the entirety. Whatever exemption applies, put the wording on the face of the deed.

Which pre-closing steps matter for a Muskegon County seller?

Start with the treasurer's stamp, which shows the parcel's taxes are current. A warranty deed cannot be recorded without it, so any unpaid balance is settled by closing.

The loan is next. A payoff leads the lender to record a discharge, and no new deed is issued. Copies of the discharge or of your deed can be bought at the counter or through the online record search.

  • Pull the current deed so the legal description is copied word for word.
  • List every owner by exact name, since a missing owner means a missing signature.
  • Record a certified death certificate or proof of death if the deed names a survivor.
  • Get the clerk's certification and seal on any court order.

Removing or adding a name takes a new, notarized deed, not an amendment. Recording a certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a fresh deed. A title company or attorney should prepare the paper.

What does the Muskegon County map look like?

Water outweighs land in Muskegon County: 961 of 1,460 square miles are lake, which leaves 499 square miles of ground. Muskegon Lake, fed by the Muskegon River, is Michigan's only deep water port on Lake Michigan, and White Lake and Mona Lake add more shoreline. The river's name comes from an Ojibwa word for marsh. The urban southwest corner holds Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores.

The 2020 census found 175,824 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 177,901. Owners live in 78.1% of housing units. Median home value stands at $198,300 against median rent of $1,028, and the mean trip to work takes 21.6 minutes. Builders took out 451 permits in 2025.

Property forms live with the county equalization department. A new owner sends the transfer affidavit to the city or township assessor, and the principal residence exemption lifts up to 18 mills of school operating tax. Poverty and disabled veteran relief are requested at the local assessor. The county assesses for some of its cities and townships, and the rest do their own.

How do Muskegon, Norton Shores and the lakeshore affect a house sale?

Muskegon city, the county seat, had 38,318 residents in 2020 and wraps around a harbor on Lake Michigan, 42 miles northwest of Grand Rapids. Winters bring heavy lake-effect snow, which is why buyers of older houses ask about roofs and porches. Some neighborhoods began as separate villages: Bluffton, a lumbering village from 1862, was annexed by Muskegon in 1889.

Norton Shores, with 25,030 residents, sits south of the city between Lake Michigan and Mona Lake, and it holds forested dunes in Hoffmaster State Park. Norton Township was split from Ottawa County in 1859, Roosevelt Park began as a 1926 subdivision and became a city in 1946, and Norton Shores incorporated in 1968. Mona Shores Public Schools serves that area. Muskegon Public Schools dates to 1860, and Muskegon Community College hosts programs from several universities.

Downtown Muskegon stretches nearly two miles along the south shore of Muskegon Lake. A convention center opened there in 2021, the Saturday farmers market draws more than 10,000 visitors in summer, and the lumber barons' Hackley and Hume mansions form a historic district. Michigan's Adventure amusement park lies a few miles north of the city.

Beaches, bike trails along Muskegon Lake and a Lake Express ferry to Milwaukee shape how buyers value a lakeside address, and Pere Marquette Beach is the largest free public beach on Lake Michigan's eastern shore. A cottage-style house near Pere Marquette Beach or Mona Lake often draws different offers than a mid-century house inland, and a seller should pin down the parcel's legal description and township before listing.

More questions about Muskegon County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the last time of day a deed can be recorded in Muskegon County?

4:30 p.m. on weekdays. The office itself stays open to 5 p.m., at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Suite A102.

Can a scanned or photocopied deed go on record?

No. Only papers with original signatures are accepted, and a court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

Why might I need two checks at the register of deeds?

The treasurer's $5 certificate for a warranty deed is paid to the Muskegon County Treasurer, separately from the $30 recording fee and any transfer tax.

What would the seller owe in transfer tax on a $198,300 sale?

The total is $1,707.10: $1,488.75 to the state and $218.35 to the county. Any exemption has to be stated on the deed.

How does a co-owner come off a deed?

By a new, notarized deed that is then recorded. Staff cannot draft it, so use a title company or attorney. A certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a new deed.

Fees

Selling in Newaygo County?

Newaygo County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 50,414 people and 24,781 housing units in Newaygo County, which ranks 36 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $178,300, which is 5% below the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $61,931; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 14% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 86% owner-occupied. The median home was built in 1978, about 45 years ago.

What is the Newaygo County register's address and schedule?

Look for the red-roofed Administration Building in downtown White Cloud, across the street from the post office. The register works from 1087 Newell Street (mail to box 885, ZIP 49349), answers at 231-689-7246 and keeps a fax line at 231-689-7271. Doors are open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday.

White Cloud became the seat of a county created in 1840 and organized in 1851. Deed records are indexed back to 1910, and the books themselves reach 1840, so an old family parcel often has a paper trail worth pulling before a sale. The office takes deeds, mortgages, land contracts, trusts and other papers about real property. It supplies no abstracts, forms or notary service, and it cannot tell you when a house was built because it handles land records only.

How does paper or electronic recording work in Newaygo County?

Photocopies and faxes are turned away. Only an original with live signatures is recorded, and a self-addressed stamped envelope gets the recorded paper back to you. Fees are collected on the spot and cannot be billed. You can pay with cash, check, debit or credit, though cards add a $3.50 charge on $100 or less and 3.5% above that.

E-recording follows the Michigan eRecording Standards that took effect January 1, 2014. The county handles e-filed documents from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, takes ACH payment and warns that the filing vendor may bill extra. Providers named on the page are CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile.

  • Left out of e-recording: court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys.
  • On paper, a court document or death certificate must be certified, since a plain true copy is refused.
  • A sheriff's deed goes on record within 20 days of the sale, so call the sheriff's office for sale details before bringing it in.

How is Newaygo County transfer tax worked out?

The county's own examples show the arithmetic. Shorthand on the page is $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, applied after a price is rounded up to the next $500.

Newaygo County transfer tax examples (first two rows from the register's FAQ; third row computed with the same rates on the Census median home value, 2020-2024)
Price usedStateCountyTotal
$100,000$750.00$110.00$860.00
$100,000.01, treated as $100,500$753.75$110.55$864.30
$186,700, treated as $187,000$1,402.50$205.70$1,608.20

The grantor pays. A deed has to state total consideration, with any exemption written beside it, or both taxes are collected. Exchanges are taxed on the actual value of each parcel, and land lying in two counties gets a price split with tax paid to each. Stamps are bought only where the parcel is located, and filing a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit costs nothing.

What can a free search of the Newaygo County records show?

Grantor and grantee name searches cost nothing, and you can use the books yourself even though staff will not run searches for you. A tract index search starts from a legal description, which the county equalization department or your township can supply. A parcel number works too.

Everything recorded is public, so a buyer's title agent will see your deed, any mortgage discharge and any recorded survey. The register has a survey of your lot only if someone recorded one, and it knows lot dimensions only for recorded subdivisions and site condominiums. A deed describes the land, not the buildings on it. A new street address comes from the equalization department, not this office.

A fraud alert signup page on the county site suits owners of land they seldom visit.

What does the Newaygo County housing market look like?

West Michigan's Newaygo County covers 862 square miles, 813 of them land, with more than 230 natural lakes, 350 miles of rivers and streams and three big dams, Croton, Hardy and Newaygo. Over half the county lies within the Manistee National Forest, and the county operates parks, including a marina at Hardy Dam.

Census figures put the 2020 population at 49,978 and the July 2025 estimate at 51,622, up 3.3%. Owners occupy 86.5% of homes in a stock of 25,455 units. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $186,700 in 2020 to 2024, the median renter paid $904 and the median household earned $63,304. People spend an average 30.6 minutes commuting, and 111 building permits were issued in 2025.

Three towns anchor the map. Fremont, a city of 4,516, is home to Gerber and holds the National Baby Food Festival each July. Newaygo, population 2,471, sits on the Muskegon River, which once floated logs to Muskegon mills. White Cloud has 1,479 residents, lies on the White River and is a recognized Trail Town on the North Country Trail. The Newaygo County Regional Educational Service Agency in Fremont serves the public districts.

  • Tourism leads the economy, followed by farming and small manufacturing.
  • The register keeps plat books, which matter for lake lots in platted subdivisions.
  • Confirm the township before advertising a lake property, because the township assessor holds the tax record.

Which Newaygo County features do buyers ask about?

Summer cottage residents are common here, and anglers come for steelhead in spring and salmon in fall. Camping, hunting, cross-country skiing, cycling, birding and ORV riding fill the Manistee National Forest, so a listing that sits near public land should say so. Hardy Dam, completed early in the twentieth century, is the largest earthen dam east of the Mississippi. Croton and Newaygo dams were built in the same period.

Jobs help explain demand. Gerber, the county's largest employer, has roughly 1,300 workers, and in White Cloud the county government, the public schools and North American Refractories are named as major employers. A feed mill that opened in the White Cloud Industrial Park in 2018, plus an airport with a 2,917-foot runway, adds to a small but active commercial base.

Fremont's history gives a sense of the area's age. Settlers arrived in 1855, Dutch families followed in the 1870s, and a forest fire in 1871 did heavy damage to the lumber mills. Check the dates on your own paperwork before you list. A seller with an old parcel near Fremont or Newaygo may find early plats and deeds in the register's books, which reach back to 1840.

What changes for taxes once a Newaygo County house sells?

Expect the buyer's taxable value to rise. Michigan resets it at the next assessment to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer has 45 days to notify the assessor. Close relatives who keep a residence non-commercial are excepted.

Ask the Newaygo County treasurer for a tax statement, and for the certification that has to be stamped before a warranty deed can be recorded.

More questions about Newaygo County, MI Register of Deeds

When does the Newaygo County register of deeds close for the day?

The counter is open until 5 p.m. on weekdays. E-recorded documents are processed between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., so a late file waits for the next business day.

What is the transfer tax on a $100,000 house in this county?

$860.00, composed of $750.00 for the state and $110.00 for the county. The seller pays it, and any price is rounded up to the next $500 first.

Is there a charge for paying by card at the counter?

Yes: $3.50 on payments up to $100, and 3.5% of the payment above that. Cash and check carry no surcharge, and recording fees cannot be billed.

Can a sheriff's deed or death certificate be e-recorded here?

No. The e-recording rules exclude court documents, death certificates, sheriff's deeds and surveys, so those arrive on paper, certified where required.

Will the register record a photocopy of my signed deed?

No. Only originals with live signatures are accepted, and a court document needs the court's certification.

Oakland County by the numbers

Oakland County has about 1,272,294 residents and 557,978 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 2 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $320,400, 71% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $95,296, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 72% of occupied homes and renters in 28%.

Which office files deeds for Oakland County land?

The combined Clerk/Register of Deeds handles them. Land record questions can go to the office by phone at 248-858-0597 or by email to deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov. Walk-in service is weekdays only, from 8:30 a.m. through the late afternoon. Almost 100 employees work in the combined office, which serves roughly 1.2 million residents and ranks among the biggest in Michigan.

Oakland County dates to 1820, and the office keeps documents from that period. Michigan counties rarely merge the two offices, but Oakland did so in 1958. Staff record more than 140,000 real estate documents every year.

The county has 530,460 households and 569,537 housing units. Census data shows 89.1% of residents kept the same address through the prior year, and median monthly owner costs are $1,998 with a mortgage against $778 without. Mortgages and discharges therefore pass through the recording counter next to deeds.

The public record spans deeds, mortgages, foreclosure records and personal property filings. The Oakland County Super Index supplies copies of recorded documents from 1964 forward, except subdivision plats. As of November 3, 2025 the office stopped recording UCC filings apart from land records, so land record fees cover them.

Not every records request belongs at the deeds counter. The Register of Deeds does not issue birth certificates or other vital records, and it does not take UCC filings for utility transfers. The wider Clerk's office keeps circuit court documents, military discharge forms and birth, death and marriage records for the county, so route those questions to the Clerk instead of the land records staff.

What does the Oakland County register collect when a deed is filed?

One deed carries a flat $30 charge, whatever its length. Of that, $4.00 is the state survey and remonumentation charge. The same $30 base amount appears in Michigan's fee statute, MCL 600.2567.

What the Oakland County register collects
ItemCharge
Deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Extra liber and page cited in a discharge or assignment$3.00
Photocopy, per sheet$1.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 per document
Treasurer's certificate for a warranty deed$5.00
Transfer tax, county portion55 cents for each $500 of price
Transfer tax, state portion$3.75 for each $500 of price

A deed carrying a warranty covenant, along with every land contract, needs the county treasurer's tax certification before it is recorded. If you mail a document in, the register will obtain the certificate and attach revenue stamps for you, and the $5 certificate fee goes into your payment.

How much does transfer tax add to an Oakland County sale?

Any written transfer of real property worth $100 or more is taxed. Oakland's county rate works out to $1.10 for every $1,000 of price and the state rate to $7.50. A claimed exemption must be explained on the document.

Using the county's $343,600 median home value, the county portion is about $378 and the state portion about $2,577, which makes roughly $2,955. Michigan's two transfer tax acts, as summarized by the Oceana County register, place the tax on the seller or grantor, so plan for it on the seller's side of the closing statement.

  • Put the full property value on the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it.
  • Print any claimed exemption on the document.
  • Find out from the closing agent who buys the stamps and when they are paid.

What must an Oakland County document contain before recording?

Recording depends on meeting the signature and format rules of MCL 565.201, Michigan's recording statute. Staff examine each one and record only those that pass, and a validation unit checks the legal description before the cashier takes the document.

  • Signatures are original, with the signer's name typed or printed below.
  • The names in the notary block match the names under the signatures.
  • Any instrument that conveys or encumbers real estate shows the grantee's name and address.
  • A document signed in Michigan carries a notary acknowledgment listing the notary's county of commission and expiration date.
  • Black ink, type of at least 10 points, and white paper of 20-pound weight, sized from letter to legal length.
  • An unprinted band of 2.5 inches opens the first page, with half an inch left clear elsewhere.
  • The first printed line names the recordable event.
  • Total property value is given on the document or an affidavit.

When a document names a survivor, a certified death certificate or proof of death must go with it. A court order has to carry the court clerk's certification and seal. Older instruments follow the rules of their day: male grantors' marital status was required before April 6, 2017, and two witnesses before March 2002.

Can Oakland County documents be recorded electronically?

Yes. Four registered providers connect to the register: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and HopDox. UCC documents and mortgage foreclosure documents cannot be e-recorded.

The county also runs MiPropDocs for documents that do not transfer ownership. It accepts affidavits, association liens and discharges, claims of lien, certificates of trust, discharges, lis pendens, mortgages, notices of commencement, releases and satisfactions of mortgage. Deeds cannot use it, so a house transfer still goes through a provider account or on paper.

Paper filings remain open to anyone. Bring the original to the counter or mail it with payment. Copy the legal description from the prior deed word for word, since the validation step reviews it.

How do the register and the county treasurer work together on a sale?

The tax certificate is where the two offices meet. The treasurer confirms the parcel is paid up before a warranty deed goes on record, and the register will not file the deed without the stamp. To price a delinquent balance in advance, buy an official statement through the county's Property Gateway.

Tax foreclosure reaches the register too. It collects redemption money for sheriff deeds and clerk deeds, checks the person redeeming has a stake in the parcel, and passes the funds to the treasurer, who holds them in trust until the paperwork is finished and a check can go to the grantee. Anyone who inherited a house with unpaid taxes should read the Oakland County property tax guide before listing, since the county's foreclosure calendar runs on fixed dates.

How soon does a recorded deed come back?

A document carried to the counter returns in roughly two weeks. One sent by mail takes two to four. A document that came through a title company usually returns about two weeks after recording. Originals are indexed and then mailed back.

Copy requests move faster. Counter customers get five pages as a courtesy, and bigger orders are usually ready within a day or two, for pickup or mailing. The office can quote a foreclosure payoff and takes redemptions on sheriff deeds and clerk deeds from parties with a stake in the land. Money for a redemption is receipted and held by the treasurer until paperwork is complete.

More questions about Oakland County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is the Oakland County recording fee?

$30 per document, whatever its length. The $4.00 state survey and remonumentation charge is part of that. A discharge that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per extra reference.

Is a tax certificate required for a warranty deed in Oakland County?

Yes. Warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a warranty clause need the county treasurer's certification, at $5.00, before the register records them.

How far back do the county's online records reach?

To January 1, 1964, apart from subdivision plat maps. Call the Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597 about anything older.

Are UCC statements still filed separately in Oakland County?

No. After November 3, 2025 they are handled with land records, and the land record recording fees apply.

Which party owes transfer tax on a house sale?

The seller or grantor, under the Michigan acts, paid with the recording. Combined county and state tax in Oakland County is about $8.60 per $1,000 of the sale price.
