Where are Oceana County deeds recorded?

Deeds for Oceana County property are filed with the Register of Deeds, whose office is inside the Hart courthouse. Reach it at (231) 873-4158 or write to P.O. Box 111, Hart, MI 49420. Voters elect the register to a four-year term, and the post makes that person the official keeper of the county's land records.

Behind the counter sits an index of everything recorded, plus the original plats for each subdivision. Local governments call on the office for liber and page numbers, instrument numbers and parcel descriptions taken from those plats. UCC financing statements may be filed there as well, and the register chairs the County Plat Board that signs off on new subdivisions.

You can request copies or file a document in person or by post, as long as the fee is enclosed. Enclose a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself. Adding a daytime phone number lets staff call about a defect instead of returning the paper. The department page also links an online official records search.

What is Oceana County, Michigan, like for a property seller?

Oceana is a rural West Michigan county on the Lake Michigan shore, with Hart serving as seat and largest incorporated community. Michigan created it in 1840 and organized it in 1855. Of its 1,306 square miles, 794 are water and 512 are land.

The economy began with logging, as timber moved down the White River, and turned to farming. Asparagus is the signature crop, enough that the county bills itself the Asparagus Capital of the World, and Hart hosts the National Asparagus Festival. Part of the Manistee National Forest lies within the borders.

Before settlement, the land belonged to the Ojibwe, and in the 1850s the federal government moved about 1,400 Odawa here from Ionia County. Population climbed from 496 in 1840 to a peak of 26,873 in 2000, and the 2020 count was 26,659, so the county has been steady for twenty years.

  • US 31 follows the western side, passing Rothbury, New Era, Shelby, Mears, Hart and Pentwater.
  • M-20 crosses the south from US 31 near New Era toward Hesperia.
  • M-120 climbs north from the Muskegon and Newaygo corner to meet M-20 at Hesperia.
  • Shoreline road B-15 runs from the south county line up to Pentwater.

Mason, Lake, Newaygo and Muskegon counties adjoin it on land. Recording and transfer tax stamps belong to the county holding the parcel, so make sure the property lies in Oceana before you send a deed here.

What do the latest Census figures show for Oceana County housing?

QuickFacts puts Oceana County at 27,177 people for July 2025 and 16,115 housing units. Of 10,419 households, owners hold 84.5%, and the typical owned home is worth $190,100. Rent at the median is $759 a month, and owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,280.

Nearly a quarter of residents, 24.9%, are over 65, and 15.8% identify as Hispanic or Latino. Only 136 building permits were issued during 2025. Prices here sit far below the Detroit suburbs, so the dollar cost of transfer tax and other percentage-based charges is lower even though the rates match.

Stability stands out: 91.8% of people had not changed addresses in the prior year, and the county has 1,554 veterans. Broadband reaches 83.1% of households, which affects how comfortably a seller can handle e-signing and electronic recording from home.

What does the Oceana County register charge for recording?

State law, at MCL 600.2567, fixes recording at $30 for any document regardless of length. A charter county may set a different schedule by ordinance, so phone the Oceana office for the price list before you mail a check.

Fees a Michigan register of deeds may charge, MCL 600.2567
ServiceAmount
Record one document$30.00
Each extra instrument covered by an assignment or discharge$3.00
Page of a copy$1.00
Certification of a recorded document$5.00
Grantor/grantee search, each year covered$0.50, with a $5.00 floor
Filing or looking up any other paper$1.00

Pay when you hand over the document. Electronic submissions have one business day after receipt, and the statute gives government agencies and tax foreclosure filings separate payment schedules.

How much transfer tax applies when an Oceana County house sells?

Two Michigan acts tax a deed's value, and the register's page cites MCL 207.505 for the county share and MCL 207.526 for the state share. Transfers worth $100 or more owe both: 55 cents per $500 block to the county and $3.75 per block to the state, counting any partial block as a full one. The seller or grantor is the taxpayer.

The fraction rule shows up in a sale at the county's $190,100 median. That value breaks into 381 blocks of $500, because the last $100 counts as a whole block. County tax is $209.55, state tax is $1,428.75, and the pair comes to $1,638.30. Swapping two properties triggers tax on each deed, measured by the true value of what each deed conveys.

  • State the full consideration on the deed, or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit alongside it.
  • The affidavit costs nothing to file, but the deed must say it is being filed.
  • Write any exemption you claim on the instrument.
  • A parcel lying in two counties pays each county on its share of the price.

Which rules does a deed have to meet for Oceana County?

The register publishes a checklist built on Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201 and neighboring sections. A document that misses a point gets returned, so read the list before you sign.

  • Signatures are originals, and typed, stamped or printed names appear below them.
  • Notary names match the signature names exactly.
  • A grantee address, by street or post office box, appears on each deed or assignment.
  • The drafter's name and address are on the document.
  • A Michigan judge, court clerk or notary acknowledges anything that conveys or burdens real estate.
  • A survivor clause needs a certified death certificate or other proof of death.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the court clerk.

The page layout has its own checks. Keep the top 2.5 inches of the first sheet blank and half an inch clear on every other edge. Print in black on white stock that weighs 20 pounds or more, in type of 10 points or larger, and use sheets between letter and legal size. The first line of print must name the recordable event in a single statement.

Can Oceana County deeds be recorded electronically?

Yes, through Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile or Indecomm Global Services. Sign up with one provider to begin. The register answers e-recording questions at (231) 873-4158.

A title company closing your sale can say whether it files through one of these services. For a family transfer or a paper deed, deliver the original to the courthouse or mail it with the fee and a return envelope.

More questions about Oceana County, MI Register of Deeds

What number reaches the Oceana County Register of Deeds?

(231) 873-4158. The office sits in the Hart courthouse, and the post office box is 111, Hart, MI 49420.

Will the register accept a deed sent by post?

Yes, with enough fees enclosed. Add a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, and a phone number so staff can resolve any question about the paperwork.

What does recording one document cost in Oceana County?

State law sets $30 per document, whatever the page count. Because a county schedule can differ, confirm the figure with the office before you send payment.

Is there a fee to file the transfer valuation affidavit?

No. The deed has to state that the affidavit is being filed, and the affidavit has to disclose the total consideration.

Who owes the Michigan transfer tax when an Oceana County house sells?

The seller or grantor does, according to the register's page. The county levy is 55 cents and the state levy is $3.75, each applied to every $500 of value.

What we confirmed on the official page

Where is the Osceola County recording office?

The Register of Deeds sits on the first floor of the main courthouse at 301 W. Upton Avenue in Reed City, MI 49677. Call (231) 832-6113, fax (231) 832-6115, or write register@osceolacountymi.gov. The counter runs 9 to 5 on weekdays, holidays excepted, and the public computers shut off fifteen minutes early, at 4:45.

Reed City took over as county seat in 1927. Osceola began organized government in 1869 with Hersey as its seat, and before that the land was attached in turn to Ottawa, Mason, Newaygo and Mecosta counties. The register still holds books that go back to 1853, long before the county governed itself.

Beyond taking deeds, the office keeps a tract index for every parcel by legal description and its register chairs the county Plat Board. Staff will not draft a deed or answer legal questions. A seller who needs a document prepared should hire an attorney or ask the title company at closing.

What does Osceola County charge for recording and copies?

A deed costs a flat $30 to record, whether it runs one page or twenty. Cash, cards, checks and money orders are all accepted, with checks written to Register of Deeds. Card users pay an extra processing charge on top.

Fees posted by the Osceola County Register of Deeds (osceola-county.org)
ServiceCharge
Recording a deed or mortgage$30.00 flat
Releasing or assigning several instruments in one paper$3.00 for each beyond the first
Photocopy of a recorded paper$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 more
Plat copy$2.00 a page
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00 for five descriptions, then $0.20 each
Document sent by email$7.00
Staff name search$5.00 a name plus $0.50 a year
Staff search of the tract index$50.00 an hour

The treasurer's certificate fee rides along in the same payment to the register, so a closing agent writes one check for both.

How much transfer tax comes due on an Osceola County sale?

The county publishes the combined figure as $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state. Behind those numbers sit MCL 207.504 (55 cents per $500) and MCL 207.525 ($3.75 per $500). A deed shows the sale price on its face, or an affidavit of value travels with it.

Try a $150,000 sale, which is near the county's median home value of $155,400. The state takes $1,125, the county takes $165, and the buyer's title agent collects $1,290 at the counter. A $90,000 cabin comes to $774. If a sale bundles furnishings with the house, list the two values apart so only the real property is taxed.

Exemptions differ between the two taxes, and the state list is longer. Points that matter to Osceola sellers:

  • Family transfers from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild skip the state tax, with no matching county exemption.
  • Lender foreclosures and deeds in lieu are exempt from the state tax, and the county tax is exempt when the loan is government backed.
  • A price under $100 owes neither tax.
  • A court-ordered transfer owes neither tax unless the court sets a price.
  • A land contract owes nothing until title passes at final payment.

List any exemption on the face of the deed. The register at (231) 832-6113 can tell you how the office likes it phrased.

What makes Osceola County reject a deed?

A short checklist from MCL 565.201 governs what the register can take, and a miss on any line can bounce the deed. Look for these:

  • Margins: a clear 2.5 inches at the top of page one, half an inch elsewhere.
  • Print: black ink, 10-point type or bigger, on white 20-pound paper that is letter or legal size.
  • Names: each signer printed below the signature and spelled like the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Addresses: the grantee's street address and the drafter's name and business address.
  • Privacy: the first five digits of any Social Security number removed.

Tax proof is its own hurdle. The county's fee page says warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts need a certificate from the County Treasurer. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate covers liens and five years of paid taxes. A quitclaim without covenants of warranty skips it.

Can I search Osceola County land records myself?

Yes. The county's online search covers 1988 forward, and images of every document can be called up by liber and page back to 1853. Handwritten grantor and grantee books run to 2003, and courthouse terminals show names from 1988. Browsing names is free.

Searching by legal description through the tract index costs $50 an hour, a rate the Board of Commissioners set, and staff do not do title or mineral searches. Mailed search requests get done as time allows, aiming for three days. If you need an answer the same day, call a title company.

The county's Fraud Notify service emails you when anything is recorded under your name. That helps an owner of a vacant, inherited or seasonal house spot a forged deed early. GIS parcel maps are linked from the same page.

In what order should an Osceola County seller line up the paperwork?

A sale in Osceola County moves faster when the courthouse steps happen in a sensible order. A seller working with a buyer from outside the area can hand this sequence to the closing agent:

  1. Pull the current deed from the online search or the public terminal in Reed City and check the legal description against the parcel map.
  2. Order the treasurer's certificate, because a warranty deed cannot be recorded without one.
  3. Have the deed drafted on compliant paper with the sale price or an affidavit of value.
  4. Calculate the state and county transfer tax, and note any exemption on the face of the deed.
  5. Bring or mail one payment payable to Register of Deeds covering the $30 recording charge, the tax and the treasurer's fee.
  6. Sign up for Fraud Notify so that any later filing under your name reaches your inbox.

Each step is cheap on its own, and the Reed City counter handles most of them in a single visit.

What is the Osceola County housing market like?

Osceola County spreads over 573 square miles of rolling hills in Northern Michigan. Half of it was cleared for farms and towns, and the rest is still wooded, with Rose Lake the largest of many small lakes. The Muskegon and Manistee river systems drain it. Evart and Reed City are the cities, and the villages are Hersey, LeRoy, Marion and Tustin. US 10 and US 131 are the main roads, joined by M-61, M-66 and M-115.

The Census Bureau counted 22,891 people in 2020 and estimates 23,516 for 2025. For 2020 to 2024 it puts the middle home value at $155,400, owner occupancy at 83.7%, monthly rent at $807 and household income at $58,267. The 2025 permit count was zero, so the housing supply is mostly older stock.

The county's own site carried a notice on flooding between April 10 and 21, 2026, with a fact sheet on U.S. Small Business Administration disaster loans. An owner whose house took water should read it before pricing a sale. Ask the Osceola County Treasurer for a payoff figure before choosing a closing date, since a warranty deed will not record until the certificate is in hand.

More questions about Osceola County, MI Register of Deeds

Is recording in Osceola County priced by the page?

No. The charge is $30 for the document, however many pages it has, with $3 more for each extra instrument a single paper releases or assigns.

Will Osceola County email a recorded deed?

Yes, for $7.00. Counter copies run $1.00 a page, and a certified copy adds $5.00.

Do I need a treasurer's certificate for a quitclaim deed in Osceola County?

Usually not. The county names warranty deeds and land contracts as the papers that need it, and MCL 211.135 excuses conveyances with no covenants of warranty.

What transfer tax would a $200,000 Osceola County house owe?

It would be $1,720: $1,500 to the state and $220 to the county, before any exemption.

How do I reach the Osceola County Register of Deeds?

Call (231) 832-6113 or email register@osceolacountymi.gov. The office is at 301 W. Upton Avenue in Reed City and keeps weekday hours.

Where and how do I file a deed in Mio?

Oscoda County has one office for both the Clerk and the Register of Deeds. It works out of the Government Administration Building at 311 South Morenci Avenue in downtown Mio, MI 48647. Phone 989-826-1110, fax 989-826-1136, or email countyclerk@oscodacountymi.com. Mailed items go to PO Box 399.

Doors are open on weekdays from half past eight until half past four, with a break at noon for an hour, and the office shuts on most federal holidays. Walk-ins are fine. Documents arrive in three ways:

  • Over the counter in Mio.
  • By regular mail to the box, with a stamped return envelope so the original comes home.
  • By courier, UPS or FedEx, to the street address.

Title agents based elsewhere can send files through CSC Ingeo, EPN (E-Recording Partners) or Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates cannot go that route, so ask first.

What fees apply at the Oscoda County register?

The county's Register of Deeds page lists no prices, so the numbers below are the state's schedule in MCL 600.2567. Phone 989-826-1110 for the exact total, including any card or vendor surcharge, before a check goes in the mail.

State fee schedule for registers of deeds, MCL 600.2567(1), Michigan Legislature
ServiceFee

The county's page also says copies must be taken in paper form, and phone photos of records are not allowed.

What transfer tax does a Mio-area sale pay?

Two taxes ride on every deed. The state charges $3.75 per $500 of price (MCL 207.525), and the county charges 55 cents per $500 (MCL 207.504). A part-block rounds up. The price must be shown on the deed itself or in an attached affidavit.

Picture a $125,000 sale, near the $125,500 middle home value the Census Bureau lists for Oscoda County. That is 250 blocks. The state portion is $937.50, the county portion is $137.50, and $1,075 is due together. A $60,000 cabin lands at $516.

Exemptions the two laws share, and one they do not:

  • Price under $100.
  • Transfers ordered by a court with no price attached.
  • Boundary straightening with no money paid.
  • Quitclaims that only repair a flaw in title already held.
  • Family deeds from parent to child or grandchild, which excuse the state tax and nothing more.

Put the exemption in writing on the deed.

What do the Oscoda County land records offer owners?

The archive reaches into the late 1800s. Anything from 1985 forward is electronic, and older material is on microfiche. New filings show up online within five days. Each one is time stamped, checked, numbered, indexed and scanned.

All real estate records are public, and anyone may search them in the office or online. Searches go by the property owner's name, and several public computers sit in the office. The staff do not run title searches. They send people to a title company or a private searcher. The county's view is that ownership follows whatever documents the office has recorded, so a seller with an old unrecorded deed in a drawer should file it before listing.

Online tools come in three flavors. Fidlar Laredo is a subscription program with a software download, popular for heavy searching. Fidlar Tapestry bills as you go and spans several Michigan counties. A free direct search link also exists on the county page.

Property Fraud Alert costs county landowners nothing and starts at 1-800-728-3858 or propertyfraudalert.com/mioscoda. It alerts you right away when a paper is recorded against your parcel. The county page adds that the Youngblood Law, House Bills 5598 and 5599, signed in November 2024, makes filing a fraudulent document with any Michigan register of deeds a felony.

What must a deed show before the Mio office accepts it?

The office drafts nothing and keeps no legal forms. It recommends an attorney or title company, and for do-it-yourselfers it names MichiganLegalHelp.org and eforms.com as starting places. Staff cannot say how a deed should be prepared.

MCL 565.201 governs the page itself: dark ink signatures with printed names, the grantee's address, the drafter's name and address, and a 2.5 inch clear top margin on the first page. MCL 211.135 governs tax proof. Before a warranty deed records, the county treasurer certifies that no liens or tax titles are held and that five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim without warranty covenants is excused. Get the certificate from the Oscoda County Treasurer and carry it with the deed to Mio.

What is selling a house in Oscoda County like?

Oscoda County is the only county in Michigan with no incorporated city or village. Mio, the seat, is a census-designated place in the Au Sable River valley, where M-33 and M-72 meet. The south half lies in the Huron National Forest, much of it on the Grayling outwash plain of sandy ridges, jack pine and hardwoods. Neighbors include Montmorency, Alpena, Alcona, Iosco, Ogemaw, Roscommon, Crawford and Otsego counties. The legislature created the county in 1840 and its government formed in 1881. The name is a Schoolcraft coinage thought to mean pebbly prairie.

The 2020 census counted 8,219 people, the fewest of any Lower Peninsula county. The Bureau estimates 8,723 for July 2025, up 6.1% from 2020. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a middle home value of $125,500, owner occupancy of 87.2%, and monthly rent of $681. Household income is $49,515, and about one in three residents is 65 or older. Only 44.1% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and the average commute is 29.1 minutes.

The Census Bureau's snapshot of residents adds useful context for anyone pricing a house here:

  • 16.8% of people under 65 live with a disability, and 16.5% of residents are in poverty.
  • 81.4% of households have a broadband subscription, so remote-work buyers should confirm service at a given address.
  • 85.9% of adults 25 and older finished high school, and 15.6% hold a bachelor's degree.
  • 90.5% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

With no city or village government anywhere in the county, the county offices in Mio are the nearest local government for every parcel. Oscoda County Park is listed as a good vantage point over the area. The work economy is small: the Bureau counts 176 employer establishments with 1,335 jobs in 2023, up 6.2% from 2022, and 2022 retail sales of $72.2 million. Housing units total 7,792 against 3,788 households, which shows how many homes sit empty or are used seasonally. The Bureau tallied 24 building permits in 2025. Before listing a cabin or woodland home, search the owner's name at the register and ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate, since both steps affect closing speed.

More questions about Oscoda County, MI Register of Deeds

Where is the Oscoda County register's office?

It is at 311 South Morenci Avenue in Mio, MI 48647. Letters go to PO Box 399, and the main number is 989-826-1110.

Does Oscoda County take deeds by mail?

Yes. Send the original to the PO Box, or ship by UPS or FedEx to the street address, and include a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return.

Which e-recording vendors does Oscoda County use?

CSC Ingeo, EPN and Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates are excluded, so call before sending one.

What does a $100,000 Oscoda County sale owe in transfer tax?

It is $860: $750 for the state and $110 for the county, if no exemption fits. A partial $500 block counts as a full one, so a price just over a block boundary adds to the bill.

Does the Mio office search titles?

No. It is a recording office and refers people to title companies or private searchers, though you may search names yourself in the office or online.

Who records property documents in Otsego County, Michigan?

Find the Otsego County Register of Deeds at 225 W Main Street, Gaylord, MI 49735. Call 989-731-7550 or fax 989-731-7519. By the county's own description, this office keeps every record of a transfer or encumbrance of land in Otsego County.

Staff time stamp each paper, assign liber and page numbers and index it on computer. The computerized index and images start on March 5, 1864, and every record can be pulled and copied in the office within minutes. Images are also sold online.

The office works with the county Equalization Department to keep ownership current, using tax identification numbers or owner names. It does not run searches for the public. Anyone who wants a search done on their behalf should call a title insurance company or a land records data company, or sit at the Gaylord counter and look for themselves.

What does recording cost in Gaylord?

The Gaylord office charges $30 for each document it records, with every page included. The county says that rate took effect October 1, 2016. The table below comes straight from the county's fee and copies pages.

Otsego County Register of Deeds fees, from otsegocountymi.gov
ServiceFee
Recording a document, all pages$30
Each extra instrument a document assigns or discharges$3
Copies of recorded instruments$1 per page
Certification of a document$5
Real estate record search$5 per name
State or federal tax lien certificate$3 per name
U.C.C.-11 certificate$6 per name

Per the county, $4 of the fee is routed to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund, a share that is skipped for fixture filings, state, federal and MESC liens, state deeds and plats. For mailed copy orders, phone 989-731-7551 first so staff can fix the page count and price. Payment is due when the service is performed, and checks are made out to Otsego County Register of Deeds.

How do transfer tax and exemptions work in Otsego County?

The clerk's staff collect transfer tax at the moment of recording, and the county's page cites MCL 207.505(5) and MCL 207.526(6) for it. Either print the full consideration on the deed or file a real estate transfer valuation affidavit, at no charge. An exempt transfer should say so on its face.

The rates are $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county per $500 or fraction. They come from MCL 207.525 and MCL 207.504. A sale at $220,000, matching the $219,700 middle home value reported for Otsego County, is 440 blocks of $500. State tax is $1,650 and county tax is $242, so $1,892 is due at recording unless an exemption applies.

Exemptions that matter to homeowners:

  • Consideration below $100 removes the tax under both acts.
  • A deed from a mortgage foreclosure skips the state tax, and one given on a government-backed loan skips both. The state exemption does not carry over to the lender's later sale of the property.
  • Deeds within a family, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, are exempt from the state tax only.
  • A land contract owes nothing until the buyer finishes paying and legal title passes.
  • A deed that moves a boundary line with no money paid is exempt from both.

Mineral rights transfers and leases are exempt too, but they come up rarely in a house sale.

Can I e-record or search Otsego County land records online?

Yes. Otsego County offers electronic recording for people who file many documents at once. It is a secure, verified-user service, and you register through an approved provider before you start. The county names Simplifile, at simplifile.com, and CSC, at cscglobal.com/service/erecording.

Online, the office sells images of recorded documents. Searching the real estate record at the office costs $5 per name, and certificate searches for state tax liens, federal tax liens and U.C.C.-11 filings carry the per-name fees in the table above.

Freedom of Information requests go on a completed FOIA Request Form sent by email to the county's FOIA coordinator or faxed to 989-731-7529. A deed copy does not need a FOIA request, since recorded instruments are available at $1 per page.

What paperwork should a deed carry before it reaches the Gaylord counter?

The Gaylord office applies two statutes. MCL 565.201 governs how the paper looks, and MCL 211.135 governs proof that taxes are paid. A deed that misses either can be refused.

  • Legible black or dark blue signatures, with each signer's name printed below and matching the notary's wording.
  • The grantee's mailing address, plus whoever drafted the instrument with a business address.
  • Black type of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, between letter and legal size, and a clear 2.5 inches at the top of page one.
  • A single opening line naming the one recordable event, such as a warranty deed or a mortgage discharge.
  • Social Security numbers masked down to the last four digits, unless a law demands more.

With a covenant of warranty in the deed, the county treasurer must certify there are no tax liens or titles on the parcel and that five prior years of taxes are paid. A city, village or township treasurer certifies the local side. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants, a sheriff's deed and a deed made under a court judgment are excused.

How does the Otsego County setting shape a house sale?

Otsego County spans 526 square miles of Northern Michigan, which makes it the fifth smallest in the state by total area. Gaylord is the only city and also the seat, with Vanderbilt as the lone village. Unincorporated communities include Elmira, Johannesburg, Waters, Sparr and the lakeside settlement of Otsego Lake. The county began as Okkuddo County in 1840, became Otsego in 1843, and organized in 1875.

Water shapes the housing stock. The county has more than 370 lakes, mostly in the south, and Otsego Lake is the largest at 1,972 acres. The headwaters of the Au Sable, Black, Manistee, Pigeon and Sturgeon rivers are here. I-75 bypasses Gaylord on the west and M-32 runs east and west through it.

The 2020 census counted 25,091 residents, and the Bureau's 2025 estimate is 26,080, a gain of 3.9%. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a $219,700 middle home value, 77.2% owner occupancy and a $1,008 monthly rent. Median household income is $68,183. The county has 14,976 housing units but 11,231 households, so housing units outnumber households by about 3,700. Building permits numbered 25 in 2025, and retail sales per resident in 2022 were $39,474, far above the other three counties in the same release.

The Census Bureau counts 846 employer establishments in Otsego County in 2023, with 9,372 jobs and a $448 million annual payroll. Retail sales topped $1 billion in 2022, and health care and social assistance receipts reached $213 million. Households with a broadband subscription make up 91.3%, and 26.3% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. A buyer who works remotely can find service, but should confirm it at the address.

Owners of lake or woodland parcels can ask the Equalization Department for the parcel's tax identification number, and the Treasurer for the tax certificate, before choosing a closing date.

More questions about Otsego County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the Otsego County recording fee?

Gaylord charges $30 a document with all pages included, and adds $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

Is there a filing fee for Otsego County's transfer valuation affidavit?

None. The county collects nothing for the affidavit, which you can use instead of printing the value on the deed.

How far back do Otsego County's computer records go?

They start on March 5, 1864. The office keeps both the index and the images on computer from that date to the present.

What do Otsego County copies cost?

Each page is $1, and a certification adds $5. For mail orders, ring the office first for an exact quote.

Will Gaylord staff search a title for me?

No. The office says search services are not provided, and it points people to a title insurance company or a land records data company. You can search the records in person at the Gaylord office.

Ottawa County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 298,614 people and 116,173 housing units in Ottawa County, which ranks 7 of 41 mi counties here. Median home value is $291,200, which is 55% above the middle county in this mi set. Households here earn a median $87,144; the middle mi county is at $65,004. 22% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 78% owner-occupied.

Which Ottawa County office records my deed, and where is it?

Ottawa County runs its recording desk from West Olive, at 12220 Fillmore Street, West Olive, MI 49460. The Register of Deeds pages list Room 146 as the recording office, and the county's locations page shows a combined vital records and deeds counter in Room 130 of the same building, so phone ahead at (616) 994-4510 to learn which window takes your deed. The email is register@miottawa.org and the fax is (616) 994-4521.

A second site, the Research Library, is at 414 Washington Avenue, Room 115, in Grand Haven, the county seat. Its direct line is (616) 846-8109. Weekday service at both sites starts at 8 am and ends at 5 pm, though Grand Haven shuts for an hour after noon. Since January 1, 2026 the vital records and deeds offices close from 8:00 to 9:30 am on the third Monday of each month.

A big county needs several doors. Ottawa County counts 296,200 residents, and the Clerk and Register of Deeds operates five locations. Only West Olive and Grand Haven handle deeds, while Holland and Hudsonville are vital records sites.

How does recording work in Ottawa County?

Ottawa County records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt, as long as it meets the recording requirements. A fax or photocopy of a deed is turned away, because originals with live signatures are all it accepts. Court papers must be certified by the court, and a death certificate must be certified by the Clerk's office before it can be recorded.

Professional filers use electronic recording. The county's software lets it record warranty deeds and other documents that need a tax stamp, and it accepts submissions from four approved companies, including Indecomm, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. Contact each firm about eligibility and pricing. The county's business rules say the office collects only the fees set by state and local law, and vendors may add processing charges.

A one-time filer can use the Consumer E-Recording portal for affidavits, liens, certificates of trust, mortgages, discharges, lis pendens, notices of commencement and releases. Deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are barred from the consumer portal, so a seller has to deliver the deed in paper or through a title company.

At the counter you can pay in cash, by check or by card. Recording by card adds a 3% convenience fee, and copy orders can also draw on an escrow account.

What are the recording and copy fees in Ottawa County?

Michigan sets the base amounts in MCL 600.2567, and Ottawa County posts its own online and card terms in its FAQ and document search pages. Searching the index is free, and the county asks $1 per page, plus a convenience fee, to view, print or save an image.

Ottawa County fees from the Register of Deeds FAQ and document search, and the state schedule in MCL 600.2567
ItemAmount
Recording one document, any length$30
Extra instrument assigned or discharged in the same document$3 each
Searching the online indexNo charge
Viewing, printing or saving an image online$1 per page plus a convenience fee
Certified copy$5 under the state schedule
Card payment when recording3% added

The county's FAQ says documents are not obtained through Freedom of Information requests, since every record in the office is public or covered by statute and copy fees are fixed by state law. Anyone can obtain a copy of your deed once it is recorded.

How much transfer tax will an Ottawa County seller pay?

Two statutes stack here: MCL 207.525 levies $3.75 per $500 for the state, and MCL 207.504 levies 55 cents per $500 for the county, which is the rate for any county under 2,000,000 people. Any remainder under $500 is treated as a full block.

The median owner-occupied home in Ottawa County is valued at $323,400, the highest of the four counties in this release. On a $325,000 sale there are 650 blocks of $500. State tax comes to $2,437.50 and county tax to $357.50, a total of $2,795 at recording. The deed needs to show the value or carry an affidavit.

You can often avoid the tax with an exemption written on the deed. The common ones for homeowners are:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • Mortgage foreclosure deeds, including deeds in lieu, under the state act.
  • Gifts down the family line, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which the state act alone excuses.
  • A spouse's deed that makes or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A deed whose only job is to cure a flaw in title the grantee already holds.

The county site links both a County Exemptions sheet and a State Exemptions sheet on its Document Recording page.

What do I need to prepare before recording an Ottawa County deed?

The office does not draft documents, supply forms or give legal advice, and it does not furnish abstracts of title. It suggests an attorney, title company or real estate agent for help. It cannot say when a house was built or whether a survey exists either, since it only holds land records, and most property has never had a survey recorded.

Ottawa County explains its top margin rule this way: a state law effective April 1, 1997 requires 2.5 inches at the top and half an inch on the other sides, to leave room for recording stamps. MCL 565.201 contains that rule. Witnesses are no longer required on documents, though most documents still need a notary.

Papers that need a tax certificate from the Treasurer's office:

  • Warranty deeds.
  • Land contracts and assignments of land contracts.
  • Master deeds and amendments to master deeds.

MCL 211.135 backs that requirement and excuses quitclaim deeds without covenants of warranty. If a house is in mortgage foreclosure, the Register of Deeds takes redemption payments, though you may redeem straight through the lender or its lawyer. After the redemption period runs out, only the lender can help.

The county also offers Property Fraud Alerts. Owners sign up to be told when a document is recorded that affects their property.

What is selling a house in Ottawa County like?

Ottawa County is in West Michigan on 24 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. Its 1,631 square miles include 1,068 of water, so only 563 are land. The Grand River, the longest in Michigan, crosses the county and empties into the lake at Grand Haven. Holland is the largest city, and the others include Zeeland, Hudsonville, Coopersville and Ferrysburg. Grand Valley State University is in Allendale and Hope College is in Holland. The county was authorized in 1831 and organized in 1837.

School districts that serve the county include Grand Haven Area Public Schools, Holland City School District, West Ottawa, Zeeland Public Schools, Hudsonville Public School District, Spring Lake Public Schools, Jenison Public Schools and Allendale Public School District.

The Census Bureau counted 296,200 people in 2020 and estimates 308,459 in July 2025, up 4.1%. For 2020 to 2024 it lists a median home value of $323,400, an owner-occupied rate of 79.3%, median gross rent of $1,211 and median household income of $90,502. The Bureau recorded 1,411 building permits in 2025, many more than in the three northern counties.

More questions about Ottawa County, MI Register of Deeds

Where does a deed get recorded in Ottawa County?

Bring it to the recording office at 12220 Fillmore Street in West Olive, or let a title company e-record it. Phone (616) 994-4510 to confirm the room. The Washington Avenue site in Grand Haven is the research library.

Can I record a photocopy or fax of a deed in Ottawa County?

No. Staff record only papers bearing original signatures.

How quickly does Ottawa County record a deed?

The county says it records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt when it meets the recording requirements. A title company or lender decides when the original reaches you.

Can I use the Ottawa County consumer e-recording portal for my deed?

No. The portal excludes deeds and other documents that transfer ownership, as well as UCC documents and foreclosure papers. It handles items like mortgages, discharges and notices of commencement.

What would a $400,000 Ottawa County sale owe in transfer tax?

The bill is $3,440 with no exemption: $3,000 to the state and $440 to the county.

Where do I take a deed in Roscommon County?

Take it to the Roscommon County Register of Deeds, 500 Lake Street in the village of Roscommon, ZIP 48653. The county lists 989-275-5931 for the office and 989-275-8640 for its fax. The recording page gives no counter hours, so a short call saves a wasted trip, especially for owners driving in from Houghton Lake, Prudenville or St. Helen.

The county covers 580 square miles, of which 60 are water. Houghton Lake is the largest inland lake in Michigan, Higgins Lake is the other big water body, and part of the Au Sable State Forest falls inside the boundary. Crawford, Oscoda, Ogemaw, Gladwin, Clare, Missaukee and Kalkaska counties surround it. Interstate 75 clips the northeast, US 127 follows the western edge of both lakes, and M-18 and M-55 cross near the middle. Founded in 1840 as Mikenauk County, it took the Roscommon name in 1843 and was organized in 1875.

The county's Online Services page links a public record search, a separate sign-in for title companies and law offices, BS&A parcel and tax data, and a GIS parcel map. Pull the prior deed and the legal description there before anything is drafted. Houghton Lake State Airport sits in Roscommon Township and the Blodgett Memorial Airport in Markey Township, which gives a sense of how spread out the parcels are.

What are the recording charges at the Roscommon office?

Filing is a flat $30 for each document, whether it is a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens. If one document releases or assigns several earlier instruments, add $3 for each additional one. The register's fee page also flags a state fee change effective October 1, 2016, and it lists these extras:

  • Photocopies at $1 a page, plus $5 when certified.
  • Faxed copies at $2 plus $1 a page.
  • Mailed copies at $5.
  • Emailed copies at $2 plus $1 a page.

E-recording is limited. The county takes no certified documents electronically except death certificates, so a signed deed arrives at the counter or by post. Ask the office how the check should be made out and whether to enclose a prepaid return envelope.

Which Roscommon County documents need a treasurer's certificate first?

The register will not file a warranty deed, a deed with any warranty covenant, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract, a condominium master deed or a covenant deed until the County Treasurer has issued a tax certificate. The treasurer's fee is a separate $5 payment for up to 25 parcel descriptions, with 20 cents for every description after that, made out to the County Treasurer.

The rule comes from MCL 211.135. A certificate has to show no tax liens or tax titles on the parcel and that the preceding five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim deed with no warranty falls outside the section, and that is why many family transfers skip it.

Roscommon County sale paperwork, compiled from the register's fee page and the cited statutes
StepOfficeCost or timing
Tax certificate for a warranty deedCounty Treasurer$5 for up to 25 descriptions
State transfer tax, when it appliesCounty TreasurerDue within 15 days of delivery
Recording the deedRegister of Deeds$30 for the document

Who owes Michigan transfer tax when a Roscommon County house sells?

The seller carries this tax, and the treasurer's office takes the payment. Under the state act the money falls due a little over two weeks after the deed changes hands, and it attaches to deeds and sale contracts made for consideration (MCL 207.523). A county levy of $0.55 for each $500 band of value also applies where the population is below two million (MCL 207.504). The deed has to show its full value on its face, or an affidavit giving that value is attached. A deed that mixes real and personal property can state the two values separately so only the land is taxed.

Plenty of conveyances owe nothing. The state act exempts transfers under $100, deeds to a son, daughter or grandchild, transfers by foreclosure or deed in lieu, court orders that name no price, and quitclaim deeds that fix a defect in title (MCL 207.526). A seller who paid and later decides the sale qualified can ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

How does a recorded sale change the tax bill?

Two notices reach the assessor. The office passes recorded transfers to local assessing officers at least monthly, and the buyer sends the assessor a transfer form no later than 45 days after closing. After a transfer, the taxable value is reset to state equalized value for the following year (MCL 211.27a). A cabin held since the 1970s can therefore carry a much higher bill under its next owner.

The county's housing numbers explain why this comes up often. The 2020 census counted 23,069 housing units for 23,459 residents, and 50.5% of those units were vacant, the mark of a seasonal market. Owners occupied 81.5% of the homes that had year-round residents. The median age was 56.6.

Assessing is done by the townships and the village, so valuation questions belong with the local assessor named on the bill. The county treasurer issues certificates and takes transfer tax, and the Register of Deeds files the instrument itself.

What does the population history say about Roscommon County land?

The county had 1,459 residents in 1880 and 2,055 in 1930, then grew fast after the war to 16,374 in 1980 and a peak of 25,469 in 2000. The 2020 count was 23,459. A county that added about 6,500 residents between 1970 and 1980 has parcels with long chains of deeds, so a title search can run back many owners.

Seasonal events keep the lakes busy: Tip-up-Town on Houghton Lake each January, the Bluegill Festival in St. Helen each summer, and Historical Village Days in August. The Michigan Shore-to-Shore Trail also passes through.

Where a property was bought on a land contract, remember that the contract and the later deed are separate instruments. A land contract needs the treasurer's certificate, and under MCL 211.27a its taxable value resets for the year after the contract is signed, with no second reset once the deed is on file.

What should a Roscommon County seller check before closing?

Start with the parcel record on the county's search page, and confirm the owner of record, the legal description and any open mortgage. Then run through this list:

  • Decide whether the deed will carry a warranty covenant, because that triggers the certificate.
  • Request the certificate and the transfer tax amount from the treasurer ahead of closing.
  • State the full value on the deed, or prepare the valuation affidavit.
  • Phone 989-275-5931 for counter hours and how to submit the original.

A buyer's title agent will flag any lien, prior mortgage or unreleased discharge that shows in the record search, so clear those first.

More questions about Roscommon County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the fee to file a deed in Roscommon County?

It is $30 per document, with $3 more for each extra instrument that one document assigns or discharges. Copies cost $1 a page and certification adds $5.

Is a treasurer's certificate needed for a quitclaim deed here?

Usually not, since a quitclaim deed with no warranty is outside MCL 211.135. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts need the certificate from the County Treasurer.

Can a Roscommon County deed be e-recorded?

Mostly no. The county accepts no certified documents electronically apart from death certificates, so deeds go to the counter or through the mail.

Whose job is the transfer tax on a Roscommon County sale?

The seller covers it, and the county treasurer takes the payment inside the same short window. Conveyances to a son, daughter or grandchild, foreclosures and transfers under $100 are exempt.

Which phone number reaches the Roscommon County Register of Deeds?

Call 989-275-5931, or fax 989-275-8640. The office is at 500 Lake Street in Roscommon.

What is the address and schedule for the Saginaw County Register of Deeds?

Find it in the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602. The county's page shows weekday service from 8:00 until a quarter to five, with holidays off. Dial (989) 790-5270 to reach staff or send faxes to (989) 790-5278. The page still carries an old note about a lunch closing that ended in November 2022, so confirm the counter schedule by phone before a trip downtown.

The register is an elected keeper of every real property record in the county, keeps the index, and holds the original subdivision plats. Cities and townships call on it for liber and page references. Drafting and legal questions are off the table, and the quitclaim deed form page says so plainly.

Saginaw County spans 816 square miles, with the city of Saginaw as its seat. In 2020 it had 190,124 people and 85,953 housing units. Vacancy ran 8.7%, and 70.5% of the occupied homes belonged to their residents.

What will filing a document cost at the Saginaw office?

The recording charge is $30 a document under MCL 600.2567, however many pages it runs. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments picks up $3 per extra instrument. The fee page adds:

  • Page copies at $1, with a $5 certification per document.
  • Counter searches at $5 apiece.
  • A free public workstation inside the office.
  • Tax certification, which the County Treasurer handles.

Payment can be cash, check, money order, American Express, Discover, Mastercard or Visa, and cards add a fee. The checklist prices the Treasurer's certificate at $5 for the first five parcel descriptions, then $1 more per description. Before queueing at the register, stop at the Treasurer in Room 107 to learn if your instrument needs one.

Which formatting slips cause a Saginaw County rejection?

Saginaw County posts a long checklist built on Michigan's recording statutes. Each line carries a statute number, and a paper that fails any of them may come back unrecorded. These lines apply to deeds signed after April 1, 1997.

Saginaw County recording checklist, summarized from the register's quitclaim deed page
ItemWhat the checklist requires
Paper and typeWhite paper of at least 20 pounds, legible, in 10-point type or larger
Page sizeAt least 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14
Margins2.5 inches clear at the top of page one and half an inch on every other side
Title lineFirst line names the single recordable event the paper evidences
SignaturesOriginal, in black or dark blue ink, with the name printed beneath
Notary blockDated acknowledgment, printed notary name and commission expiration
Legal descriptionPlat caption and lot number, or quarter section, section, town and range if unplatted

More lines follow. A street or post office address for the grantee is required, as is the drafter's name and address. Anyone signing after September 12, 2017 must black out the first five digits of a Social Security number, and foreign-language text needs a translation stapled behind it.

What does a Saginaw County deed say about transfer tax?

The checklist states a rate of $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Either the deed itself shows total consideration or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit goes in with it. Where nothing is owed, the deed cites the exemption instead.

State law makes the seller responsible, with payment to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). MCL 207.526 exempts a handful of transfers, for example a land contract that leaves title with the vendor, a boundary line adjustment with no payment, a mineral rights conveyance, and a spouse's conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety.

A few papers need extra proof. If a deed names a survivor, the death certificate must be certified and either recorded separately or cited by liber and page. A court order arrives certified and sealed by the clerk. A release or assignment points back to the original liber and page or document number.

Which Saginaw County places and roads shape local sales?

Saginaw County grew along the Saginaw River. A footpath that became the Saginaw Trail was authorized in 1819 and reached the city of Saginaw in 1841, one of Michigan's earliest roads. Today I-75 and I-675 pass through the area, with US 23, M-13, M-46 and M-47 linking the western suburbs to the airport at Freeland. Organized in 1835, the county includes the cities of Saginaw, Frankenmuth and Zilwaukee plus dozens of townships.

Saginaw Valley State University occupies part of Kochville Township, while Delta College serves residents from neighboring Bay County. Parcels can sit in one of about twenty school districts, from Saginaw Public Schools and Saginaw Township Community Schools to Frankenmuth, Chesaning Union and Birch Run Area Schools.

Saginaw County is part of a three-county metro area with Midland and Bay City. Residents had a median age of 41.3 in 2020. Michigan law leaves assessing and building permits with cities and townships, so a Saginaw County buyer or seller often deals with three offices: the township or city assessor, the county treasurer and this register.

What does the Saginaw County Treasurer add to a deed transfer?

Tax questions go to Room 107 in the same courthouse, open weekdays from eight to five. That office takes over delinquent real property tax, manages the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund, and its head chairs the Land Bank Authority that handles tax foreclosed parcels. Without that certificate, state law keeps most warranty deeds off the record (MCL 211.135).

Back taxes can be paid at the counter, mailed to 111 S. Michigan Avenue or paid on the web around the clock. The web payment runs through an outside vendor that adds an access fee on the total. A card payment that is later reversed voids the payment, and the fees and interest reapply back to the original date. The Treasurer's page also describes a class action settlement, Fox v. Saginaw County, over surplus proceeds from tax foreclosure auctions between 2013 and 2020. Its claim deadline of July 16, 2026 has passed, so former owners who still have questions should contact the settlement administrator named on the county page.

How should a seller prepare for filing in Saginaw County?

Work through these steps in order:

  • Look up the current deed and legal description on the office workstation.
  • Learn from the Treasurer if a certificate applies, and pay for it apart from recording.
  • Show the price on the deed or prepare the valuation affidavit, and carry the tax payment.
  • Compare margins, ink, notary block and grantee address with the checklist.
  • Phone ahead about card fees and counter hours, and carry $30 per document.

After closing, the register passes transfers along to local assessors, and the buyer files a separate form with the assessor inside 45 days. Taxable value then resets to the state equalized value for the next year (MCL 211.27a).

More questions about Saginaw County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the charge for recording at the Saginaw office?

Thirty dollars a document, plus $3 for every extra instrument one document assigns or discharges. Copies run $1 a page and certification costs $5.

Will staff draft my deed?

No. Staff cannot prepare documents or offer legal advice. The quitclaim deed page sells access to a blank form for $5 plus an access fee, and sends owners to an attorney for legal help.

How is the Saginaw County transfer tax stated?

The checklist gives $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Sellers owe it, and an exempt transfer cites its exemption on the instrument.

Who issues the tax certificate?

The Saginaw County Treasurer issues it, and the register does not. The checklist fee is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 per description past that.

What number do I call for the register?

Call (989) 790-5270. The office is in the courthouse, 111 S. Michigan Avenue, and faxes go to (989) 790-5278.

The Sanilac County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Sanilac County

  • Sanilac County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Accepts cash, check, money order, credit/debit cards; $3 per additional instrument assigned/discharged; tax certificate required for warranty deeds (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Sanilac County?

Sanilac County by the numbers

Sanilac County has about 40,574 residents and 21,751 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 40 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $162,200, 13% below the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $59,074, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 82% of occupied homes and renters in 18%. The median home was built in 1970, about 53 years ago.

Who records deeds in Sanilac County, Michigan?

Any paper that changes or burdens title to land in this county is filed with the recorder in Sandusky. Deeds, mortgages, land contracts, easements, liens, plats, surveys and court orders about real estate all get indexed there, using one uniform system and fees fixed by state law.

Drafting is outside its job: staff will not write a deed or give legal advice, so have an attorney or title agent prepare yours. Once a document exists, the office answers practical questions at (810) 648-2313, and the county's department page links to forms, fee schedules and requirements.

A weekly land transfer list is posted on the same site, naming the parties and the section and township for each deed that cleared that week. The county spans 963 square miles of land, the most of any Lower Peninsula county, so those sections range from farm acreage in the Thumb to cottages near the Lake Huron shore.

What will recording a Sanilac County deed cost?

Expect $30 to put a deed on record, plus $8.60 in transfer taxes per $1,000 of price. The table gathers the amounts a seller meets most often.

What the Sanilac County fee schedule charges around a sale
ItemAmountAuthority
Base charge to record a deed or mortgage$30 whatever the lengthMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Surcharge per additional instrument in an assignment or discharge$3MCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Treasurer's tax certificate$5County fee schedule
County transfer tax$1.10 per $1,000MCL 207.504
State transfer tax$7.50 per $1,000MCL 207.525
Paper copies from the land records$1 a page, $5 to certifyCounty fee schedule

Try a $160,000 house: 160 thousands at $8.60 is $1,376 in transfer tax, and the recording fee and treasurer's certificate bring the government total to $1,411.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Sanilac County sale?

The seller does. State law puts the tax on the grantor and gives 15 days after delivery of the deed to pay the county treasurer, though at the Sanilac counter it is collected as the deed is recorded.

Put the full value of the land on the face of the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it. A sale that bundles a house with furniture or equipment is taxed on the real estate alone when the two values are written separately.

Some deeds owe no tax. The state exemptions include:

  • a transfer for under $100;
  • family transfers from a parent to a child and from a grandparent to a grandchild;
  • a court-ordered transfer with no price set by the order;
  • a land contract, until title actually passes.

The county act has no family exemption, so a gift deed can skip the state share and still owe the county share. A deed with neither a price nor an exemption cited is returned.

What formatting does a deed need before the office accepts it?

MCL 565.201 sets the intake checklist, and the county reposts it on its real estate information page. In short, signatures need dark ink with printed names beneath them, the grantee's address and the drafter's details belong on the page, and page one needs a 2.5 inch clear top margin and a first line naming the type of recordable event.

Social Security numbers must be cut back to their last four digits, and non-English text needs a translation attached. A deed that clears every point cannot be refused for its content, while one that misses a point is sent back and the closing waits.

Do Sanilac County warranty deeds need a tax certificate?

A warranty deed does. The treasurer must certify the property's tax status first for $5. Land contracts, assignments of them and any deed containing a warranty covenant follow the same path.

The county's schedule lists no such step for a plain quit claim deed. A quit claim hands over whatever the grantor owns with no promise about title, which suits relatives and estate cleanups but leaves a paying buyer exposed, so market-price buyers usually ask for a warranty deed.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey lists $168,300 as the median home value in Sanilac County. Transfer tax on a sale at that price runs about $1,450, a number to subtract when you compare offers.

How do I pay, and where can I look up recorded documents?

The office takes cash, checks, money orders and debit or credit cards, with checks payable to the Sanilac County Register of Deeds. Card payers at the counter show photo ID, and an online payment location exists for remote payers.

Searching costs nothing at rod.sanilaccounty.net, where guest users can look through an index that begins in 1801. Page images come as PDFs at $1 a page, with a $5 charge on every order.

The office also runs a free property fraud alert. Enroll a parcel and the owner is told whenever something new is recorded against it, which helps with a farm field or lake cabin that nobody checks for weeks.

Which forms does the Sanilac County office post for sellers?

The county's forms page carries three downloads: a warranty deed form, a quit claim deed form and an agricultural property affidavit form. The affidavit matters on farmland, where a buyer may need to state that qualified agricultural property will stay qualified agricultural property after the sale.

A separate packet covers manufactured homes. A seller whose home is a mobile or manufactured unit on owned land should ask the office about the Affidavit of Affixture, which the county lists beside the recording requirements and the transfer tax exemption statutes.

The same office is a U.S. passport acceptance facility, so a family selling a house and moving abroad can handle a passport application in the same trip. Hours and appointment rules change, so phone (810) 648-2313 before driving to Sandusky.

How has the Sanilac County housing market changed over time?

The county has shrunk slowly since 2000. It reached 44,547 residents that year, fell to 43,114 in 2010 and to 40,611 in 2020, and its median age in 2020 was 45.3 with 22.0 percent of residents aged 65 or older. By 2020 to 2024 that older share had risen to 25.2 percent in the Census Bureau's survey.

The Census Bureau counts 17,516 households and 21,972 housing units in Sanilac County, so there are roughly 4,450 more homes than households. That gap fits a county known for lakeshore cottages and for houses that sit empty after a death or a move to town.

  • Households average 2.28 people.
  • 91.0 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.
  • Workers face a mean commute of 28.6 minutes.
  • 16.5 percent of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree.

The county was carved out of St. Clair County and unorganized territory in 1822, and it lost land in 1840 when Huron and Tuscola counties were created. Port Sanilac was once called Bark Shanty, after a bark-covered shed used for making shingles.

What is Sanilac County like for sellers?

Sanilac County fronts Lake Huron in the Thumb, with Huron County above it, Tuscola and Lapeer to the west, and St. Clair below. Organized in 1849, it counted 40,611 residents in 2020 and an estimated 40,083 in 2025.

Its four cities are Sandusky, Croswell, Marlette and Brown City, while Lexington, Port Sanilac and Carsonville see seasonal visitors. Six state highways cross it, M-19 through M-90, and level, rich soil keeps farming at the center of many parcels.

  • Share of homes occupied by their owners: 82.6 percent.
  • Monthly cost for owners with a mortgage: $1,226.
  • Median rent: $807.
  • Median household income: $58,863.
  • New building permits in 2025: 74.

Local families and lake-home shoppers make up much of the buyer pool, and an inland farmhouse reaches a different audience than a cottage at the shore.

More questions about Sanilac County, MI Register of Deeds

Where is the Sanilac County Register of Deeds?

The office is in Sandusky, the county seat, and its phone number is (810) 648-2313. It records deeds and mortgages and does not prepare documents.

How much does a deed cost to record in Sanilac County?

The base charge is $30 for each document. A warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer's certificate, and transfer tax runs $8.60 per $1,000, so a $200,000 sale owes the seller $1,720 in tax.

Can I search Sanilac County land records without an account?

Yes. The guest login at rod.sanilaccounty.net searches the index at no cost, and page images are $1 each plus a $5 order fee.

Which forms does the county offer for a farm or family sale?

The forms page lists a warranty deed, a quit claim deed and an agricultural property affidavit. Have an attorney check any form against your facts before you sign.

How far back do the online Sanilac County land records go?

The index at rod.sanilaccounty.net starts in 1801. Searching is free for guests, and image copies are $1 per page plus a $5 fee per order.

The Shiawassee County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Shiawassee County

  • Shiawassee County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30.00; $3.00 each additional liber and page for discharges/assignments; $5 tax certificate on warranty deeds (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Shiawassee County?
We buy Shiawassee County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Shiawassee County by the numbers

Shiawassee County has about 68,061 residents and 30,272 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 27 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $164,600, 12% below the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $64,464, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 79% of occupied homes and renters in 21%. The median home was built in 1969, about 54 years ago.

What does the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds do?

Corunna's courthouse holds the land records for every parcel in the county. Incoming papers are checked against the state recording act, numbered, timed and indexed, and the originals are stored for safekeeping. A question about who owns a given parcel gets answered from this office's books.

Michigan's 1835 constitution created the recording office in each county. Shiawassee's books start in 1836, a year before the county itself was organized. From 1954 on, records are scanned into the computer system, and all of it can be searched by liber and page. The address is the Circuit Courthouse, 208 N. Shiawassee Street, first floor, Corunna, MI 48817. Phone 989-743-2216 or write rod@shiawassee.net.

The county's boundaries were first drawn in 1822, carved out of Oakland and St. Clair counties and named for the Shiawassee River. For years it was attached to neighboring counties for revenue and court matters. Only after Michigan became a state in 1837 did the state authorize a county government of its own.

When is the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds open?

The counter is staffed on weekdays, 8:00 a.m. until noon, then 1:05 p.m. until 5:00 p.m. The search room closes a little earlier in each half of the day. Because a county holiday page asks visitors to phone and book an appointment, call ahead before carrying in a closing package.

Recording is paid in cash or by check made out to the Register of Deeds. Card payment covers copies and searches, with a $1.00 convenience fee when you print from the website.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Shiawassee County?

Recording one instrument costs $30.00. A deed that carries a warranty clause also needs a $5.00 tax certificate under MCL 211.135. The treasurer issues it from the second floor of the courthouse (989-743-2224). Land contracts, their assignments and condominium master deeds need the same certificate.

Shiawassee County Register of Deeds fees. Source: Shiawassee County fee schedule and FAQ pages.
ItemFee
Recording one instrument$30.00
Mortgage discharge or assignment, each added liber and page$3.00
Tax certificate$5.00
Plat, fixture filing (real estate only) or UCC$30.00 each
Copies$1.00 a page, $5.00 more to certify
Tract index search$70.00 an hour, $35.00 minimum
State or federal lien search$3.00 per name

How does the Michigan transfer tax work in Shiawassee County?

Recording a sale deed triggers a county tax under MCL 207.505 and a state tax under MCL 207.526. Shiawassee's schedule gives multipliers of .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county and tabulates the amounts in $500 bands. The first band, $100.00 up to $500, shows $3.75 state and $0.55 county.

  • Liability rests with the grantor.
  • The deed face shows total consideration and any claimed exemption.
  • A parcel crossing a county line splits the price between the two counties.
  • Stamps are sold only in the county of the land.
  • A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit carries no filing fee.

Which transfers are exempt from the transfer tax?

The county's excerpt of MCL 207.505 excuses a list of transfers, including those priced under $100, mortgages and other security papers, leases, and spousal deeds that create or end a tenancy by the entireties. Relatives retitling a house commonly look at two items on that list: a corrective quitclaim, and a joint tenancy formed with someone who already owned the land. Ask the staff which subsection belongs on your deed.

What makes a Shiawassee County deed recordable?

The office posts a piece of Act 103 of 1937 (MCL 565.201) with its acceptance tests. Staff need the original paper with original signatures, a typed name under each signature, the grantee's address, a 2.5 inch blank band at the top of page one, and the drafter's name and address. The first five digits of any Social Security number must be removed.

A deed of unplatted land must also repeat the right-to-farm statement from MCL 560.109, warning that nearby farms may produce noise, dust and odors, which matters in a county where 59.8 percent of residents lived in rural areas in 2020. When a spouse dies, the survivor brings a certified death certificate. No replacement deed is issued, since the office only records.

What else does Shiawassee County list for sellers and buyers?

Sheriff's sales are held Wednesday mornings at 10:00 a.m. in the 35th Circuit Court lobby, and bidders need a certified check for the full opening bid. The office also links a property fraud alert service. Michigan leaves assessing and zoning to cities and townships, and the County Equalization department (989-743-2263) works across the county's 21 units of local government, fielding questions on valuation, millage and exemption status.

The county covers 541 square miles. The Shiawassee River passes through Corunna, the county seat, and Owosso, the largest city. Durand, Laingsburg, Perry and part of Ovid are the other cities. I-69 enters near the southwest corner and leaves east of Durand, where Amtrak's Blue Water train stops, and M-21 serves Corunna and Owosso. The 2010 population center of Michigan fell in Bennington Township.

What do Census figures say about Shiawassee County housing?

The 2025 estimate is 67,681 residents, against 70,648 in 2010. In the 2020 count, residents had a median age of 43.3 and 27,889 households. Of 30,231 housing units that year, 7.7 percent were vacant. For 2020 through 2024, the Census Bureau counts 28,126 households and says owners occupy 80.1 percent of homes. Only 71 building permits were issued in 2025.

The median value for a home lived in by its owner is $171,600. Median rent is $899, and median household income is $67,404. At 128 people per square mile and a 27.8 minute average commute, most parcels sit outside a city street grid.

The local economy is small and spread out. The Census Bureau counted 1,202 employer establishments in 2023 with 14,259 jobs and a payroll of about $655 million, and 4,579 businesses with no employees in 2024. Retail sales reached roughly $1.18 billion in 2022. Residents are settled: 92.3 percent lived in the same house a year earlier, and 92.7 percent of adults finished high school.

Which other county pages help a Shiawassee seller?

The Register of Deeds site links several pages worth reading before a closing:

  • A property fraud alert signup.
  • Sheriff sale information.
  • The county transfer tax exemption excerpt and the state exemption form.
  • The Michigan Homeowner Assistance Fund program at MSHDA, a starting point for owners who are behind on a mortgage.

The county treasurer collects and distributes tax roll levies for schools, townships, cities and villages, and its site includes a page for paying delinquent taxes online. Ask the treasurer for the balance on your parcel before you sign a purchase agreement, since the tax certificate on a warranty deed depends on those taxes being current.

More questions about Shiawassee County, MI Register of Deeds

What will it cost me to put a sale deed on record in Corunna?

The filing charge is $30.00 per paper. If the deed has a warranty clause, add the $5.00 certificate from the treasurer next door, plus the state and county transfer taxes calculated on the price.

Is the buyer or the seller responsible for transfer tax in Shiawassee County?

The seller carries it. The county's posted schedule applies .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county against the price on the deed.

Will the office accept a scanned or photocopied deed?

No, it wants the signed original. Once it is on record, anyone can order a plain copy at $1.00 a page or a certified copy for an extra $5.00.

If my husband or wife died, do I receive a fresh deed?

No. Take a certified death certificate and the filing fee to the courthouse so the record shows the deceased owner is off the title. Your existing deed continues to apply.

How do I reach the Shiawassee County deeds office?

Go to the first floor of the Circuit Courthouse at 208 N. Shiawassee Street, Corunna, MI 48817, or dial 989-743-2216. The holiday page asks visitors to book an appointment.
