Tuscola County by the numbers

Tuscola County ranks 34 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 53,071 people in 24,005 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $136,900, the median home value sits 27% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Tuscola County reports $62,847. Owner-occupancy is 85%, so renters hold about 15% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1970, about 53 years ago.

Where do I take a deed or mortgage for recording in Tuscola County?

Find the Register of Deeds in Suite 400 of the Purdy Building, 125 W. Lincoln Street, Caro, MI 48723. It opens at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, with a lunch closure from noon until 1:00 p.m., and it shuts for holidays. Call 989-672-3840 or write to registerofdeeds@tuscolacounty.org.

You can walk a document in or send it by post. A mailed packet needs the exact fee and a stamped return envelope. Cash, money orders and checks are all taken. Checks must print both the account holder's name and the bank's name and address, and they cannot be stale-dated. An incorrect amount gets the whole request rejected, so count twice before sealing the envelope.

Caro is the county seat and Vassar is the second city. Tuscola County lies in Michigan's Thumb, about 914 square miles in all with 12% water, and the Tuscola Area Airport serves it along with highways M-15, M-24, M-25, M-46, M-81 and M-138. The county was created in 1840 and organized in 1850.

What are the recording charges in Tuscola County?

A single $30.00 charge covers entering and recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified copy or other instrument. Papers that discharge or assign several older records add to it.

Tuscola County Register of Deeds fee schedule, taken from the office's Fees for Copies and Recording page
ServiceCharge
Recording one instrument (deed, mortgage, lis pendens and similar)$30.00 flat
Every extra liber and page assigned, discharged, indexed or posted$3.00 extra
Photocopy, real estate record$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 a document
Tax lien search certificate, state or federal$3.00 a name

Four dollars of every recording fee funds the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation program. Fixture filings, lien documents, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers skip that portion. Copies are paid for at the time of purchase, and a mailed order must name the liber and page. Tuscola County also records fixture filings at $30.00, while UCC filings go to the Secretary of State instead of Caro.

Why must a warranty deed visit the Treasurer before it is recorded?

The fee page cites MCLA 211.135 for a rule that taxes must be shown paid before some papers reach the recorder. Three types go to the Tuscola County Treasurer first: warranty deeds, land contract assignments with a warranty clause, and condominium master deeds. The Treasurer's certification costs $5.00 per document.

When the stamped document returns, send it on to Caro in recording order with the exact fee. The Treasurer, at the same street address, answers certification questions at 989-672-3890.

Sellers carrying unpaid tax feel this step most. Settle early with your title company or closing attorney who will order the certificate, since each mailed round trip adds days to a closing.

Which paperwork mistakes get a Tuscola County recording returned?

Staff compare each submission with the list on the office's Recording Requirements page, which starts from MCL 565.201. A document that misses any item comes back to the sender.

  • Original signatures, each with the signer's name typed or printed beneath it. Fax and photocopy versions are refused.
  • An acknowledgement by a notary, judge or court clerk on any paper that conveys or burdens Michigan land.
  • A mailing address for every grantee, plus the name and address of whoever drafted the paper.
  • Black print of 10 points or larger on white paper between letter and legal size, leaving a blank 2 1/2 inches atop page one and 1/2 inch on other margins.
  • No more than four sequential Social Security digits anywhere on the page.
  • One recordable event per instrument, named on the first line of print.

Court orders and death certificates are recordable only as certified copies, and a survivor deed needs the death certificate recorded or referenced by liber and page. Staff do not draft deeds, answer legal questions or hand out blank forms.

What transfer tax is owed on a recorded Tuscola County deed?

Recording a sale brings two charges. The county's is in MCL 207.504: 55 cents per $500 of value, with any leftover under $500 counted as a full unit, for counties below 2,000,000 people. The state's is in MCL 207.525, at $3.75 for each $500 or fraction.

Value must appear on the face of the deed or in an attached affidavit. Tuscola's Recording Requirements page says the whole consideration is taxed unless the paper cites a valid exemption.

  • Both acts exempt consideration under $100, security instruments, leases and certain land contracts.
  • The state act, MCL 207.526, adds conveyances from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, plus foreclosure transfers.
  • The county act's list, MCL 207.505, lacks the family exemption. Ask the office how the county share applies when a parent deeds a house to a child.

How can I search or monitor Tuscola County land records?

Online indexes start in December 1988, and the vault holds land records back to 1852 for visitors. Every index is by grantor and grantee name. No search by street address or parcel number exists, and the office cannot tell you a build date, because it keeps land records only.

Copies of recorded documents are open to anyone, since recording makes them public. Residents can sign up for Property Alert, an email notice whenever a paper under their name is recorded. The office calls it an alert, not fraud prevention, and a common name will trigger false alarms. If an alert shows a document you do not recognize, phone the office.

Staff run only simple searches for a small fee and cannot say who owns a parcel. An attorney or title company reaches that conclusion.

What if the property taxes on a Tuscola County house are behind?

The Tuscola County Treasurer works with delinquent owners to head off foreclosure, and its page lays out three paths: keep the property, sell it, or let foreclosure proceed. Forfeiture comes first and is not foreclosure. During it, the county adds a title search fee of at least $175 plus recording costs, and interest climbs to 18% a year (1.5% monthly), reaching back to the start of the delinquency.

A year after forfeiture, foreclosure follows. The owner's interest and every lien are wiped out, redemption ends, and the parcel is prepared for auction. The county says listings usually appear in early August for its August and October auctions. For a bill you dispute, or for a Principal Residence, veteran or poverty exemption, call your township assessor.

A 2025 Census estimate counts 52,680 people over about 805 square miles of land. Homeownership is high at 86.4%, and the 2020 to 2024 median value was $149,500. Households earn a median of $63,811, and workers travel 29.6 minutes on average.

More questions about Tuscola County, MI Register of Deeds

What will a Tuscola County recording cost me?

Expect $30.00 flat per instrument, with $3.00 more for each extra liber and page. Transfer tax comes on top, figured on the total consideration unless the document states an exemption.

Does a Tuscola County warranty deed need a tax certificate first?

Yes. Send the document to the Tuscola County Treasurer first with the $5.00 certification fee, then submit the stamped document to the Register of Deeds with exact recording fees. The Treasurer's phone is 989-672-3890.

Can a Tuscola County deed be found by street address?

No. Indexing is by name only. Search by grantor or grantee, or bring the liber and page, with online indexes starting December 1, 1988.

Who may order a copy of a Tuscola County deed?

Anyone may. Each page costs $1.00, certifying a copy adds $5.00 per document, and a mailed order needs a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Which transfer tax rates apply to a Tuscola County sale?

The county charges 55 cents and the state $3.75, each for every $500 of value. The value comes from the instrument or an attached affidavit.

The Van Buren County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

  • Van Buren County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

Fees

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page not searched/opened

Van Buren County by the numbers

Van Buren County has about 75,681 residents and 37,243 housing units in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, number 26 by population among the 41 mi counties we cover. The median owner-occupied home is worth $189,900, 1% above the median of the mi counties covered. Median household income is $66,902, against $65,004 for the middle mi county. Owners live in 80% of occupied homes and renters in 20%.

Where do you take a deed in Van Buren County?

Paperwork for Van Buren County land goes to the Register of Deeds in Suite 102 at 219 E. Paw Paw Street, Paw Paw. The county's online records portal gives the counter schedule as weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5:00 in the afternoon, closed on holidays. Call (269) 657-8242 with questions.

The office dates back to Michigan's first constitution of 1836 and says it processes more than 430 document types. It accepts originals bearing real signatures and court papers that carry a certification. Photocopies and faxes are refused.

Clerks read each paper against state requirements, scan and index it, then hand the original back to the sender. The county FAQ promises a turnaround of one to two days for a compliant paper. When a title company runs your closing, that company gets the original first, so ask them when it will be passed along to you.

What will the Van Buren County recording counter charge you?

A single flat price covers any length of deed or mortgage. The table follows the county's fee page, and the figures agree with MCL 600.2567.

Charges at the Van Buren County Register of Deeds, taken from the county fee page
ServicePriceCounty page note
Record a deed or mortgage$30.00Pages do not change the price; $4.00 of it funds the state survey and remonumentation program
Each added instrument in an assignment or discharge$3.00Charged per instrument
Photocopies$1.00 a pageBy fax, email or mail
Certified copy$5.00Per document
Tax certificate from the treasurer$5.00Fold it into one payment

Walk-in and mailed recording payments must be cash or a check written to Register of Deeds. A card is accepted only for copies bought online. Mail a stamped return envelope with your package so the original finds its way back.

When does a Van Buren County deed need the treasurer's stamp first?

Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments that carry a warranty promise must arrive with a county treasurer's tax certificate. Both the fee page and the FAQ say so. The rule traces to MCL 211.135, which wants proof that five years of taxes before the instrument date are paid and a statement on tax liens or tax titles. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants escape it.

  • Get the certificate before you head to Paw Paw; the recording desk will not take a warranty deed without it.
  • Budget $5.00 for it in addition to the $30.00 recording price.
  • Any unpaid tax usually comes out of your proceeds, so ask the county treasurer for the figure early enough to plan the closing date.

How does transfer tax work on a Van Buren County house sale?

The seller pays when value reaches $100.00. Van Buren's page prints a county rate of $0.55 and a state rate of $3.75, each applied to every $500 or fraction of $500. These tie back to MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Show the full price on the deed or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which is free. For swaps, each deed is taxed on its own property's real value. A parcel that straddles county lines needs a price per parcel and a payment to each county.

Delivery of the deed starts a 15-day clock for paying the county treasurer under MCL 207.523. The county page adds that a sale later found exempt can be refunded through the state Treasury, provided the form goes in within four years of payment.

Some transfers are exempt under MCL 207.526, such as these:

  • Gifts from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child.
  • Gifts from a grandparent to a grandchild.
  • Corrective deeds that confirm title the buyer already has.
  • Court orders that move property with no stated price.

What does the Van Buren County office ask for with each type of document?

Every paper needs a date and a legal description. Beyond that, the county's requirements page spells out extras by document type, and two stand out for sellers dealing with a distressed property.

  • A sheriff's sale or foreclosure by advertisement comes with the auction sale amount, a signed and notarized auctioneer statement, a Soldiers and Sailors affidavit if it applies, the newspaper publication notice, an affidavit of posting, a redemption period statement and an affidavit of redemption.
  • A tax deed or similar paper carries the $5.00 treasurer certificate.
  • Releases and assignments cross-reference the original by liber and page.
  • A land patent must be an original or certified copy.

General rules track MCL 565.201. Names are typed under signatures and match the notary block, every party's address appears, the drafter is identified and the notary acknowledgment is complete. Leave 2 1/2 inches clear at the top of page one, use 10-point type or bigger and keep sheets to 8.5 by 14 inches at most. The county lists wrong fees, missing drafter names, handwritten names and partial notary certificates as the usual causes of rejection.

A certified death certificate must back any deed that names a survivor. The office cannot draft documents or give legal advice, so see a lawyer or title agent for wording.

How do you search Van Buren County deed records?

The Register of Deeds portal at deeds.vanburencountymi.gov lets anyone search the index and buy images one document at a time. A BS&A property search from the county site also lists the liber and page in each legal description, and the sale history section can fill in gaps.

Paying for an older record depends on its volume. Liber 924 or lower is paid through the county's GovPayNow link. Liber 925 and higher is bought from the searchable index and downloads right after payment. Online copy orders may take up to two working days, and big orders on the portal may take up to 48 hours. Recorded papers are public, so anyone can request a copy of any deed.

What is Van Buren County like for a home seller?

Water covers 482 of the county's 1,090 square miles, and the rest is 607 square miles of farmland, small towns and lakeshore. Paw Paw is the seat, a courthouse whose cornerstone was laid in 1901 after a $35,000 bond vote. Bangor, Gobles, Hartford and part of South Haven are cities, while Decatur, Lawton, Mattawan, Lawrence, Bloomingdale and Paw Paw are villages. Antwerp and Almena townships, beside Kalamazoo County, are turning suburban.

Visitors come for Van Buren State Park, the Kal-Haven Trail and Lake Michigan beaches, and many inland lakes are ringed by year-round homes and cottages. Highways include I-94, I-196, US 31 and M-40, and an Amtrak Pere Marquette stop serves the county.

The county's population stood at 48,395 in 1960 and 75,587 in 2020. Census estimates put it at 76,071 for 2025. Among 30,622 households, 80.6 percent own, 22.5 percent of residents are 65 or older and 23 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Owner-occupied homes are valued at $206,500 at the median, household income is $68,114 and gross rent runs $870. Zoning and building permits come from the township or city, so call local hall about those.

More questions about Van Buren County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the recording price in Van Buren County?

$30.00 per instrument, whatever the page count. Add $3.00 for each further instrument assigned or discharged. Certified copies and treasurer tax certificates cost $5.00, and photocopies cost $1.00 a page.

Does the Van Buren County Register of Deeds take credit cards?

Only for copies ordered online. Anything you file, along with the transfer tax, must be paid in cash or by check made out to Register of Deeds.

Who owes transfer tax on a Van Buren County sale?

The seller, when the property's value is $100.00 or more. County tax is $0.55 and state tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of $500.

How fast does the Van Buren County office record a deed?

Within one to two days of receipt, if the paper meets the requirements. Wrong fees, missing drafter names, handwritten names and incomplete notary certificates get it sent back.

Is a treasurer's certificate needed for a Van Buren County quitclaim deed?

No. Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments with a warranty covenant need it. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants is excused under MCL 211.135.

Who records deeds in Washtenaw County

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30 per document; $3 added per additional instrument assigned/discharged (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • eRecording accepted, same fees/requirements; county may reject noncompliant e-docs (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Washtenaw County?
We buy Washtenaw County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Washtenaw County by the numbers

Washtenaw County ranks 6 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 368,394 people in 158,115 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $353,000, the median home value sits 88% above the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Washtenaw County reports $87,156. Owner-occupancy is 62%, so renters hold about 38% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1978, about 45 years ago.

What records does Washtenaw County hold in its deed office?

Anyone researching land in Washtenaw County ends up at the Register of Deeds. Its files include deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records, along with other real and personal property papers. The register works inside the joint Clerk / Register of Deeds department, and inspection is open to all comers.

The office's main page links to recording rules, record searches and requests, eRecording, a fee schedule and a transfer tax explainer. Copies bought through the online land record search need a login.

Recording finishes a sale, because the buyer is shielded from later claimants only once the deed is on file. Closings usually pass the signed deed to a title company, which can tell you the recording date and supply a recorded copy for your files.

Can Washtenaw County take a deed filed electronically?

Yes. Electronic filings come in through vendors approved by the Register of Deeds, a route lenders and title agents rely on. An owner who signs outside a title closing usually files on paper, mailing it or visiting the counter in Ann Arbor.

Read the recording requirements page before you send anything; a paper with layout defects comes back unrecorded. The fee schedule page states what the county charges for each service.

  • Keep the original signed deed in hand until the county accepts it.
  • Ask which payment types the office takes for your kind of filing.
  • Request your recorded deed before listing, so the buyer's title agent has the legal description early.

What do state statutes set for Washtenaw County recording and transfer tax?

Michigan statutes supply the baseline figures for any register of deeds, and Washtenaw's fee schedule page shows how the county applies them. Each charge below is paired with its section; read the text itself at the Michigan Legislature site.

Statutory charges that frame a Washtenaw County deed filing
ChargeRateSection
Placing a paper in the land records$30.00 whatever its length600.2567(1)(a)
Extra instrument within one discharge or assignment$3.00 each600.2567(1)(b)
Record copies$1.00 per sheet600.2567(1)(c)
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00600.2567(1)(d)
County share of transfer tax55 cents per $500 or part of $500 where the county has fewer than 2,000,000 people207.504
State share of transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or part of $500207.525

Who pays transfer tax in a Washtenaw County sale, and what avoids it?

Sellers carry this one. MCL 207.523 makes the grantor liable and sets a 15-day window, running from delivery of the deed, for payment to the county treasurer. Washtenaw's explainer adds a rule that trips people up. Collection is automatic unless the deed qualifies and states the reason on its face.

Any exemption you plan to claim therefore belongs in the document itself. MCL 207.526 lists the categories, including:

  • Spouses who set up or end a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A parent or grandparent deeding to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild.
  • A boundary line fix with no money changing hands.
  • A joint tenancy where one of the co-owners already holds title.
  • A deed delivered through foreclosure or in place of it.

A payer who later learns that an exemption applied can request a refund from the state Treasury department under subsection (4) of the section on liability.

Does a Washtenaw County warranty deed need a tax certificate?

Usually. MCL 211.135 has registers of deeds ask for treasurer certificates whenever a deed or land contract is presented. They disclose tax liens or tax titles and confirm that the five years of tax before the instrument date were paid.

Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excused, as are sheriff's deeds and a few other kinds. A Washtenaw seller using an ordinary warranty deed should plan on the certificate first.

If back tax is owing, the Washtenaw County Treasurer can quote a payoff figure. Settle it by closing and the certificate issues, so the deed can be filed without a stall.

How should a Washtenaw County deed be formatted?

Format rules are in MCL 565.201, and a register must refuse any paper that breaks them. Check these before anyone signs.

  • The first printed line states the single recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Black ink, white paper of 20-pound weight or heavier, type of at least 10 points.
  • 2 1/2 inches blank above the text on page one and half an inch on every remaining edge.
  • Grantee addresses, with the drafter's name and business address.
  • Any Social Security number cut to its last four digits.
  • An English translation stapled to anything partly in another language.

The office also enrolls people in Fraud Guard alerts, which warn you when a paper is recorded under your name. It is a sensible precaution while a house sits listed or vacant. Two other county pages cover older paperwork: discharging prohibited deed restrictions, such as covenants that discriminated by race or religion, and the Michigan Construction Lien Act, which matters if contractors recently worked on the house.

What is the story behind Washtenaw County?

Michigan's territorial government defined the county in 1822 and organized it in 1826. French traders built the first lasting settlement at Ypsilanti around 1809. The University of Michigan moved to Ann Arbor in 1839, a consolation after the city lost its bid for the state capital, and Eastern Michigan University began as a normal school in Ypsilanti in 1849. Early settlers drained swamps for farms, and parts of the Waterloo Recreation Area still look as they did then. Greek Revival buildings and township names reflect the 1820s and 1830s enthusiasm for Greece.

The university is the largest employer in a July 2020 list, followed by Trinity Health, federal jobs, Ann Arbor Public Schools, the Toyota Technical Center, Faurecia, Eastern Michigan University, IHA Health Services and the State of Michigan. Domino's Pizza, Thomson Reuters and NSF International also make the top fifteen.

The county spans 722 square miles, 706 of them land, and borders Livingston, Oakland, Wayne, Monroe, Lenawee, Jackson and Ingham counties. Ann Arbor is the seat. Chelsea, Dexter, Manchester, Saline, Ypsilanti and the northern slice of Milan are the other cities, with Barton Hills a village and Whitmore Lake a census community. Main roads are I-94, US 23, US 12, M-14, M-17 and M-52, and the county runs 10 parks and a recreation center.

What do the numbers say about Washtenaw County homes?

Census estimates put Washtenaw County at 370,214 people in 2025 living in 165,103 housing units. Owners occupy 61.6 percent of homes, and the middle owner-occupied value is $374,100, about double Wayne County's. Typical household income is $89,180 and typical gross rent is $1,463. Bachelor's degrees or higher belong to 58.7 percent of adults. Around 79 percent of residents stayed at the same address over the prior year, 13.1 percent were born abroad and the mean commute is 23.5 minutes.

The county counts 8,322 employer establishments with 158,858 jobs for 2023, and health care and social assistance took in about $8.7 billion in 2022. Population density reaches 527 per square mile. Zoning, building permits and assessing belong to local units, so ask the city or township about any open permit before you list.

More questions about Washtenaw County, MI Register of Deeds

Does Washtenaw County take electronic deed filings?

Yes. Lenders and title companies commonly file through eRecording vendors that the Register of Deeds has approved.

Who is responsible for transfer tax in a Washtenaw County sale?

The seller. Michigan sets 55 cents for the county plus $3.75 for the state on each $500 of value, and the county treasurer must receive payment within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Does my Washtenaw County deed have to name a transfer tax exemption?

Yes. According to the county's explainer, the tax is collected unless the instrument is exempt and the exemption appears on the face of the deed, so write out the statutory reason before signing.

What tax paperwork goes with a Washtenaw County warranty deed?

Certificates from the county treasurer showing no tax liens or titles and five prior years of paid taxes. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excused.

Where can I confirm the Washtenaw County recording fee?

Check the Register of Deeds fee schedule page, which covers recording, copies, searches, transfer tax and tax certificates. State law sets the starting recording charge at $30.00 per document.

title: Wayne County, MI Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Wayne County, MI Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Michigan
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Wayne County, MI Register of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Wayne County, MI Register of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Wayne County, MI Register of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Wayne County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Wayne County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

The Wayne County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Wayne County

  • Wayne County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $26.00 plus $4.00 state survey/remonumentation fee = $30.00 per document (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Online land records: credit card account, $6 for 15 min search or $24 for 60 min; $2/page copies (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Wayne County?
We buy Wayne County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • County equalization office page/contact not searched or opened (time-box)

Wayne County by the numbers

Wayne County ranks 1 of 41 mi counties in this guide by population, at about 1,773,767 people in 796,119 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $170,200, the median home value sits 9% below the mi county median for this guide. The mi county median income is $65,004, and Wayne County reports $59,521. Owner-occupancy is 64%, so renters hold about 36% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1956, about 67 years ago.

Where does a Wayne County seller take a deed to be recorded?

Recording happens at the Wayne County Register of Deeds, 400 Monroe, 7th floor, in the Greektown neighborhood of downtown Detroit. The Treasurer's deed certification desk is in that building too, on the 5th floor.

Since October 1, 2025 the office no longer takes walk-ins. The office now serves people by appointment, and nobody can wait on the floor for a cancellation. The day's first slots begin at 8:00 AM and the last begin at 3:50 PM. A 20 minute slot handles up to five documents, while a 45 minute slot is reserved for high volume customers filing five to 25. One person per appointment may enter. The scheduling help line is 313-224-5860, and the recording help line is 313-224-5851.

Mailing documents in is also allowed. Recorded papers come back the way they arrived. An agent who hand delivered them must collect them in person, and mailed ones return to the address typed on the document, which is often the attorney's or the title agent's, not the buyer's.

What are the Wayne County recording fees?

The county's fee schedule changed on January 1, 2026, the first rise since 1996. For a deed, mortgage or similar instrument the charge is $26.00 plus a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee, which adds up to $30.00 for each document no matter how many pages it runs.

Charges listed on the Wayne County Register of Deeds and Treasurer pages
ServiceCharge
Recording a deed or mortgage$26.00 plus $4.00 state fee
Property search at the office$5.00 (waived for your own home with proof)
Search by mail$15.00 per address
Copies$2.00 per page
Certifying a recorded document$10.00 each
Online account, 15 minutes$6
Online account, 60 minutes$24
Treasurer's deed certification$5.00 per document, up to 25 parcel numbers

The county itself cautions that its charges differ from other counties, so a figure quoted elsewhere may not apply.

How does Wayne County collect transfer tax at recording?

The Register states the formula: $0.55 per $500 of consideration for the county, $3.75 per $500 for the state, which the office also expresses as $8.60 per $1,000. The tax is collected when the deed is filed unless an exemption is noted on it, and accepted forms are cash, check or money order, payable to that office.

Exemptions are listed in MCL 207.526 and, for the county tax, MCL 207.505. A deed claiming one must cite the statute and subparagraph. Typical examples seen in a house sale:

  • consideration below $100
  • a gift deed running down to a son, daughter or grandchild
  • a deed issued in foreclosure or instead of foreclosure
  • a land contract whose title has not yet passed to the buyer
  • a court order with no stated price

Sellers who held a principal residence exemption should also read subsection (u) of the state act. It excuses certain arm's-length sales where the state equalized value never rose above the first value set after the home was built or bought, and a refund can be requested when tax was paid on such a sale.

What kinds of payment does the Wayne County counter accept?

Debit and credit cards work at the counter when the cardholder shows matching ID. So do money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks, corporation checks and law firm checks. Two card brands, American Express and Discover, are refused. Personal checks are turned away at the window yet welcome in the mail, and cards cannot be used for mailed filings.

Each document needs its own check for fees plus any tax. The office is strict about amounts:

  • Underpaying returns both document and check.
  • An overpayment above $25.00 also returns everything.
  • An overpayment of $25.00 or less is kept and not refunded.
  • Several documents on one check travel as a group, and if one fails, all come back.

Title companies handle this routinely. A seller recording a family transfer alone should work out the exact figure first.

What does a deed need to be accepted in Wayne County?

The county posts a checklist and a list of common rejection reasons. The main points are original signatures with names typed, printed or stamped under them, a notary acknowledgment on any real estate deed signed in Michigan, plus the preparer's name and address.

  • Pages meet the office's size, margin, ink and type rules, with a deep blank top margin on page one.
  • The document's title sits on the first line, and the parcel number and street address are shown.
  • A full legal description appears, including plat liber and page or condominium details where they apply.
  • Any Social Security number has its first five digits removed or hidden.
  • A death certificate is an original certified by the clerk, and a court order is certified and sealed.

The register does not furnish blank forms and cannot give legal advice. An attorney is the office's recommendation for drafting.

Why must the Wayne County Treasurer certify a deed first?

MCL 211.135 bars the register from recording until a treasurer's certificate shows the parcel's taxes current for the prior five years. Wayne County requires the Treasurer's stamp on warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and their assignments.

Only originals can be certified. Make a separate appointment with the Treasurer, or send the original by UPS, FedEx or USPS with a check payable to the Wayne County Treasurer and a stamped return envelope. The Treasurer sends it back and you forward it for recording. A document listing more than 25 parcels pays $5.00 plus 20 cents per extra parcel.

Unpaid tax is the usual snag. By the Treasurer's account, a bill left unpaid at the local office past the end of February is delinquent from March 1 and then payable only to the county. After a full year it is forfeited, the interest climbs to 1.5% a month, and a $175 foreclosure fee plus $30 in recording charges join the balance.

What does the size of Wayne County mean for recording?

Wayne is Michigan's most populous county, created in 1796. Detroit holds the county seat as its biggest city, and the southern communities are called Downriver. The Register calls the office the library of land records for nearly 900,000 parcels, filed by liber and page back to 1703.

Census figures for July 2025 show 1,769,038 residents on 611.84 square miles of land and 814,793 housing units. For 2020 to 2024, 64.8% of homes are owner-occupied, the middle value for an owned home is $178,500, and median household income is $60,539. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 3,922.

At that volume, appointments fill up. Reserve one early when a closing depends on a recorded deed, and ask the title company which of your documents need Treasurer certification beforehand.

How can you find or copy a recorded Wayne County deed?

You can use the land records website, visit the office, or request a search by mail. The website is open around the clock. A free name search shows a list of recorded documents by grantor or grantee but not the documents themselves. A paid On-Demand Account adds searches by address, legal description, parcel number or liber and page, and printing costs $2 per page. Certified copies are not sold online.

Lobby kiosks allow self-service searching. Veterans and current military personnel can get a search of their own property and its copies at no charge with credentials, though businesses are excluded. A mailed request needs a short description, a check payable to the Wayne County Register of Deeds, and the address 400 Monroe, 7th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226. The county's pages give two different start years for online images, so ask which years your search needs before buying a session.

More questions about Wayne County, MI Register of Deeds

What does Wayne County charge for one recorded document?

The charge is $30.00, made up of $26.00 plus the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. A warranty deed also needs Treasurer certification at $5.00. The current schedule began January 1, 2026.

Can I just show up at 400 Monroe to record a deed?

No. Since October 1, 2025 service is by appointment only. Choose record, search or kiosk on the county's calendar, or call 313-224-5860 for help booking.

How much transfer tax does Wayne County print per $500?

The county prints $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, or $8.60 per $1,000. The seller pays at recording unless the deed cites an exemption.

Will the Register of Deeds write my deed for me?

No. The office provides no blank documents and may not give legal advice. It points owners to an attorney who can prepare a deed that meets the recording rules.

What gets a Wayne County deed sent back?

A photocopied signature, no stated price or exemption, wrong margins or type size, a thin legal description, or no treasurer certification. Rejected papers return with the check so you can fix and refile.

The Wexford County register of deeds records Michigan deeds and mortgages.

Who records deeds in Wexford County

  • Wexford County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Recording fee $30.00 (includes remonumentation and automation fees); track index $50/hr (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Fees

Selling in Wexford County?
We buy Wexford County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where is the Wexford County Register of Deeds located?

Find the office at 437 E. Division St., Cadillac, on the second floor of the older section of the courthouse. Letters go to P.O. Box 303, Cadillac, MI 49601, and the telephone is (231) 779-9455. The main entrance and parking lot sit behind the building.

Directions from the county: drive east on Harris Street from downtown Cadillac, go four blocks, and look to the left. Cadillac is Wexford's largest city and county seat, though it had to win the title. The seat started in Sherman, moved to Manton in 1881, and returned to Cadillac after a countywide vote in April 1882.

Mailed filings are accepted when sent with the fees and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for the return. State law does not permit recording a photocopy, so the sheet you send must be the original with original signatures.

What fees does the Wexford County office list?

Every document costs $30.00 to record, however many pages it has. That number folds in the Michigan remonumentation fee and the Register's automation fee, and it has been the statewide figure since October 1, 2016. Cash, checks and credit cards are taken, and checks are written to Register of Deeds.

  • Tax certification, $5.00, is required on every warranty deed and land contract.
  • A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per instrument beyond the base $30.00.
  • A fixture filing costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $1.00 a page, and certifying a document is $5.00.
  • Name searches cost $5.00 each plus $0.50 per year. UCC searches are $6.00 a name, and state, federal, MESC or judgment searches are $3.00 a name.
  • A track index request is $50 an hour, or $25 for half an hour.
  • Emailing a request adds a $3.00 convenience fee.

The counter also sells fill-in-the-blank quit claim, warranty and mineral deeds and non-construction liens for $5.00 each. Staff do not draft legal papers or answer questions about how to word them, and the office suggests hiring an attorney for any deed.

How much transfer tax applies to a Wexford County sale?

The county publishes a table that splits each $500 price band into a state share and a county share. A single check payable to the Wexford County Register of Deeds can cover transfer tax, tax certification and recording together.

First three price bands in the Wexford County transfer tax table, as printed by the county
Sale price bandStateCountyTotal
$100.01 to $500$3.75$0.55$4.30
$500.01 to $1,000$7.50$1.10$8.60
$1,000.01 to $1,500$11.25$1.65$12.90

Each further $500 band repeats the same pair of amounts. The printed table ends at $100,000, so for a typical home price ask the counter staff for the exact tax before writing the check. An exemption has to be cited on the deed itself, drawing on MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax.

What must a deed contain to be recorded in Wexford County?

The county posts seventeen numbered rules with statute citations, and each deed is checked against them. The ones that matter most:

  • Names typed or printed under the original signatures must match the names in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Each deed or assignment gives the grantee's street or post office address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Page one leaves 2.5 inches blank at the top and every page keeps a half inch around the other edges. Ink is black, type is at least 10 point, and the paper is white, at least 20 pound, and between letter and legal size.
  • The first line of print identifies what the paper does, such as a warranty deed.
  • If the deed claims survivorship, a certified death certificate or proof of death is recorded already or referenced by liber and page.
  • A court order carries the clerk's certification and seal.

Unplatted land adds two required statements. One says whether the right to make further divisions under the Land Division Act is being conveyed, and the other is the Michigan right to farm notice about nearby agricultural operations.

Does Wexford County accept electronic recording?

For most paper types, yes. Court certified documents and anything needing tax certification are excluded, so warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, their assignments, plats and condominium documents must still be filed on paper.

The county's e-recording rules give a processing window of 8:30 A.M. to 4:30 P.M., Monday to Friday, except county holidays. Payment goes by ACH under vendor agreements, and only fees set by state and local statute reach the county, while vendors can add their own charges. A submission that breaks the Michigan Recording Act can be rejected. A filer who violates the state's e-recording standards is cut off until further notice. Four vendors are named: CSC eRecording, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm.

Were any Wexford County records lost in the 2024 cyber incident?

Yes, a small share. A cyber incident on November 5, 2024 kept the office from recovering under 5% of documents first recorded between August 14, 2024 and October 30, 2024. Anyone who sent papers for recording in that stretch is asked to call and learn whether theirs survived or must be recorded again. A seller who closed in those months should make the call before listing.

The online land records search is hosted through the county website, and the office says its holdings go back to 1864. Duplicate microfilm sits in underground storage in Grand Rapids. Once a document is recorded, anyone may request a copy for $1.00 a page. The office will fax prepaid copies but will not email them.

It also runs a Fraud Notify service that watches for recordings under a name or business name. Ask the office how to enroll.

How does Michigan law connect taxes to a Wexford County deed?

MCL 211.135 keeps a warranty deed from being recorded until a treasurer's certificate shows the prior five years of tax paid, which is what the $5.00 certification line buys. Any balance owed on the parcel therefore has to be settled by closing.

The Register's FAQ covers family situations too. If a spouse dies and both names were on the deed, bring a certified death certificate and the fee; no new deed is issued, because the office only records. A paid-off mortgage produces a discharge from the lender, not a deed. The county cautions that adding or removing a name affects divorce, borrowing, taxes and probate, and urges an attorney's advice first. Once the sale closes, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor a transfer notice (MCL 211.27a).

What does the Wexford County housing stock look like?

Forest dominates Wexford County, which sits in the Northern Lower Peninsula and holds much of the Manistee National Forest. Briar Hill, at 1,706 feet, is the Lower Peninsula's highest point. The Legislature created the county in 1840 as Kautawaubet County, renamed it in 1843, and it organized in 1869.

Census figures put the July 2025 population at 34,445, across 564.93 square miles of land with 16,924 housing units. For 2020 to 2024, 80.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, the middle value of an owned home is $170,400, and median household income is $61,085. Permits for 191 buildings were issued in 2025. Many parcels are rural, so the land division and farm notice statements above come up more often here than in a platted city lot.

More questions about Wexford County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the per-document recording charge in Wexford County?

It is $30.00, which includes the Michigan remonumentation and Register of Deeds automation fees. Warranty deeds add $5.00 for tax certification, and discharges covering several instruments add $3.00 for each.

Can a warranty deed go through e-recording in Wexford County?

No. Warranty deeds and land contracts need tax certification, so they go in on paper: the original, with original signatures, delivered or mailed with fees and a stamped return envelope.

Will Wexford County staff advise me on wording my deed?

No. The office prepares no legal documents and gives no legal advice. It sells blank fill-in forms for $5.00 and recommends an attorney.

How can I learn the owner of a Wexford County parcel?

Ask the County Equalization Department or the assessor for the city, township or village. They give the name on the tax roll, which may differ from the owner, and that name opens a search of the Register's records.

Do I get a new deed after paying off a Wexford County mortgage?

No. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage to be recorded. Your deed remains the one from purchase, and a recorded copy costs $1.00 per page.
